use.how: Predicate or attributive, about a person stuck between choices: 他一直犹豫不决；别再犹豫不决了。 Often mildly critical.

near.diff: 优柔寡断 is an indecisive character; 犹豫不决 is being undecided about a particular choice right now.

cards.cue: In the shop, your friend keeps picking up one phone, then the other, for an hour without choosing either. What state is he in?

ctx.s: 两件衣服都很好看，她站在镜子前{犹豫不决}。
ctx.en: Both dresses looked good, and she stood in front of the mirror unable to choose.

ctx.s: 别再{犹豫不决}了，机会可不等人。
ctx.en: Stop dithering; opportunities don't wait for anyone.

ctx.s: “你到底去不去？”“我还在{犹豫不决}，明天告诉你。”
ctx.en: "Are you going or not?" "I still can't make up my mind; I'll tell you tomorrow."

ctx.s: 他对要不要接受这份工作一直{犹豫不决}，结果错过了截止日期。
ctx.en: He couldn't decide whether to accept the job and ended up missing the deadline.

ctx.s: 看着菜单上几十道菜，我{犹豫不决}，最后让朋友帮我点。
ctx.en: Faced with dozens of dishes on the menu, I couldn't decide, so I let my friend order for me.

ctx.s: 面对两所大学的录取通知，他{犹豫不决}了整整一个星期。
ctx.en: With offers from two universities, he wavered for a whole week.

bad.s: 他{犹豫不决}地答应了我们的邀请。
bad.en: (meant: he accepted our invitation hesitantly)
bad.why: It means not deciding at all, so it cannot describe how someone agreed; say he hesitated a little before agreeing.

bad.s: 这个问题很{犹豫不决}，大家讨论了很久。
bad.en: (meant: this question is hard to decide)
bad.why: It describes a person who cannot decide, not the issue; say the question is hard to decide.

cards.mean: without the slightest hesitation
cards.lit: not hesitating in the slightest

use.how: Adverbial before a verb, usually with 地: 他毫不犹豫地答应了。 Describes one quick, firm action or choice.

near.diff: 不假思索 is acting or answering without thinking at all; 毫不犹豫 is acting firmly, with no doubt about what to do.

cards.cue: When her old friend asked for help moving house, she said yes before he had even finished asking. How did she answer?

ctx.s: 看到孩子掉进水里，他{毫不犹豫}地跳了下去。
ctx.en: Seeing the child fall into the water, he jumped in without a moment's hesitation.

ctx.s: 老板给了她一个出国的机会，她{毫不犹豫}地答应了。
ctx.en: Her boss offered her a chance to work abroad, and she accepted at once.

ctx.s: “如果再选一次，你还会学医吗？”“会，我会{毫不犹豫}地再选一次。”
ctx.en: "If you could choose again, would you still study medicine?" "Yes, I'd choose it again without hesitation."

ctx.s: 医生说手术有风险，她还是{毫不犹豫}地在同意书上签了字。
ctx.en: The doctor said the operation was risky, but she signed the consent form without hesitating.

ctx.s: 另一家公司开出高薪挖他，他{毫不犹豫}地拒绝了。
ctx.en: Another company offered him a big salary to poach him, and he turned it down flat.

ctx.s: 只要朋友有需要，他总是{毫不犹豫}地伸出援手。
ctx.en: Whenever a friend needs him, he always helps without a second thought.

bad.s: 他想了三天，最后{毫不犹豫}地决定了。
bad.en: (meant: after three days of thought, he made a firm decision)
bad.why: Three days of thinking is hesitation, which contradicts the idiom; say he finally made up his mind.

bad.s: 他很{毫不犹豫}，做事从不拖泥带水。
bad.en: (meant: he is a decisive person)
bad.why: It is an adverbial for a single action and cannot be modified by a degree word like 'very' as a character trait; say he is decisive.

cards.mean: to know when to stop
cards.lit: stop when it is just enough

use.how: Predicate, usually advice or a warning: 玩笑要适可而止。 Said of drinking, joking, criticising, playing, anything that harms when overdone.

near.diff: 见好就收 is quitting while you are ahead after a gain; 适可而止 is not overdoing something.

cards.cue: Everyone laughed at your first joke about Li's haircut, but you keep making more and he is getting upset. What should you have done?

ctx.s: 酒可以喝，但要{适可而止}。
ctx.en: Drinking is fine, but know when to stop.

ctx.s: 开玩笑要{适可而止}，你看他都快生气了。
ctx.en: Don't push the joke too far; look, he's about to get angry.

ctx.s: “再玩一局吧！”“{适可而止}吧，明天还要上班呢。”
ctx.en: "One more round!" "Let's call it a night; we have work tomorrow."

ctx.s: 批评孩子要{适可而止}，说得太多反而没用。
ctx.en: When you scold a child, don't overdo it; too much talking only backfires.

ctx.s: 减肥是好事，但节食也应该{适可而止}，别把身体搞坏了。
ctx.en: Losing weight is good, but don't take dieting too far and ruin your health.

ctx.s: 双方争论了很久，主持人提醒大家{适可而止}。
ctx.en: The two sides had argued for a long time, and the host reminded everyone to leave it there.

bad.s: 我的作业做到一半就{适可而止}，明天再做。
bad.en: (meant: I stopped my homework halfway and will finish tomorrow)
bad.why: It means not overdoing something that harms in excess, not pausing an unfinished task.

bad.s: 这场雨下了一天，终于{适可而止}了。
bad.en: (meant: the rain finally stopped after a whole day)
bad.why: It implies a person's judgment and self-control; it is not used for things that simply stop.

cards.mean: completely safe, with no chance of failure
cards.lit: in ten thousand tries, not a single miss

use.how: Predicate, or after 确保/力求/为了, about a plan, arrangement or safety measure: 这样就万无一失了；为了万无一失……

near.diff: 万无一失 says a plan cannot go wrong; 有备无患 is the reason for preparing in case something does.

cards.cue: Before the product launch, the manager checks every detail three times because she wants to be absolutely sure nothing can go wrong. What does she want?

ctx.s: 我在两个地方都放了备用钥匙，这样就{万无一失}了。
ctx.en: I've left spare keys in two places, so nothing can go wrong now.

ctx.s: 婚礼的每个细节我们都检查了三遍，应该{万无一失}。
ctx.en: We've checked every detail of the wedding three times; it should be foolproof.

ctx.s: “你觉得这个计划怎么样？”“听起来不错，但不一定{万无一失}。”
ctx.en: "What do you think of the plan?" "Sounds good, but it's not necessarily foolproof."

ctx.s: 为了{万无一失}，他又把文件备份到了另一台电脑上。
ctx.en: To be completely safe, he backed the files up onto another computer as well.

ctx.s: 这次手术风险很高，医生们反复讨论，力求{万无一失}。
ctx.en: The operation was high-risk, so the doctors discussed it again and again to leave nothing to chance.

ctx.s: 世界上没有{万无一失}的投资，任何投资都有风险。
ctx.en: There's no such thing as a risk-free investment; every investment carries risk.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜{万无一失}，每道都好吃。
bad.en: (meant: every dish in this restaurant is good)
bad.why: It is about a plan or arrangement being safe from failure, not praise for quality.

bad.s: 我{万无一失}地准备了考试。
bad.en: (meant: I prepared thoroughly for the exam)
bad.why: It is not a manner adverb for how you prepared; say you prepared thoroughly so that nothing could go wrong.

cards.mean: extremely urgent, imminent
cards.lit: pressing right up against the eyebrows and eyelashes

use.how: Predicate or attributive, about a deadline, problem or task that is very close and pressing: 考试迫在眉睫；迫在眉睫的问题。

near.diff: 燃眉之急 is a noun for the urgent need itself (解燃眉之急); 迫在眉睫 describes how close and pressing something is.

cards.cue: It is Friday night, your thesis is due on Monday morning, and the conclusion is still unwritten. How close is the deadline?

ctx.s: 考试{迫在眉睫}，他却还在玩游戏。
ctx.en: The exam is just around the corner, and he's still playing games.

ctx.s: 离交论文只剩两天，截止日期已经{迫在眉睫}。
ctx.en: Only two days left before the paper is due; the deadline is right on top of us.

ctx.s: “你还不着急吗？”“当然急，比赛已经{迫在眉睫}了。”
ctx.en: "Aren't you worried yet?" "Of course I am; the match is almost here."

ctx.s: 老城区的水管已经严重老化，全面更换{迫在眉睫}。
ctx.en: The water pipes in the old town are badly worn, and replacing them all is now urgent.

ctx.s: 随着人口老龄化加剧，养老问题变得{迫在眉睫}。
ctx.en: As the population ages, the question of elderly care has become pressing.

ctx.s: 公司的资金只够维持一个月，寻找新投资人成了{迫在眉睫}的任务。
ctx.en: The company has only a month's funding left, so finding new investors has become an urgent task.

bad.s: 他是一个{迫在眉睫}的人，做什么都很急。
bad.en: (meant: he is an impatient person)
bad.why: It describes an approaching event or problem, never a person's character; say he is impatient.

bad.s: 我昨天{迫在眉睫}地赶到了机场。
bad.en: (meant: I rushed to the airport yesterday)
bad.why: It is not an adverb for hurrying; it says something urgent is close at hand. Say you rushed to the airport.

cards.mean: changing fast with each passing day
cards.lit: new every day, different every month

use.how: Predicate or attributive, about technology, a city or the times constantly renewing: 科技日新月异；日新月异的变化。 Not used of a person's skills.

near.diff: 突飞猛进 is a sudden rise in a level or skill; 日新月异 is a continuing stream of new things replacing old ones.
翻天覆地 is one total transformation compared with before; 日新月异 is change that keeps coming, day after day.

cards.cue: Every few months there is a new phone, a new app, a new gadget, and last year's model already looks old. How is technology changing?

ctx.s: 现在的手机{日新月异}，去年的新款今年就过时了。
ctx.en: Phones change so fast now that last year's new model is already out of date.

ctx.s: 这座城市{日新月异}，每次回来都能看到新的高楼。
ctx.en: This city changes constantly; every time I come back there are new tower blocks.

ctx.s: “你还在用这个老软件？”“没办法，技术{日新月异}，我跟不上。”
ctx.en: "You're still using this old software?" "I can't help it; technology changes so fast I can't keep up."

ctx.s: 在这个{日新月异}的时代，我们必须不断学习新知识。
ctx.en: In this fast-changing age, we have to keep learning new things.

ctx.s: 网上的流行语{日新月异}，父母常常听不懂孩子在说什么。
ctx.en: Internet slang changes so fast that parents often can't understand what their kids are saying.

ctx.s: 通了高铁以后，这个小镇的面貌{日新月异}。
ctx.en: Since the high-speed railway arrived, the little town has been changing with every passing day.

bad.s: 我的汉语水平{日新月异}，老师很满意。
bad.en: (meant: my Chinese is improving fast)
bad.why: It is for things that keep renewing, like technology or a city; for one person's rapidly rising level, use an idiom of leaps and bounds.

bad.s: 他今天的心情{日新月异}，一会儿高兴一会儿难过。
bad.en: (meant: his mood keeps swinging today)
bad.why: It describes renewal and progress, not fickle ups and downs; say his mood is changeable.

cards.mean: sweeping, earth-shaking (change)
cards.lit: to turn the sky over and overturn the earth

use.how: Mostly attributive in 发生了翻天覆地的变化, comparing a place, life or system with how it was before. Also a predicate: 变化翻天覆地.

near.diff: 日新月异 is change that keeps coming day after day; 翻天覆地 is a total transformation, the before and after unrecognisable.

cards.cue: When your grandmother was young her village had dirt roads and no electricity; now it has paved streets, shops and internet. How has it changed?

ctx.s: 这些年，我的家乡发生了{翻天覆地}的变化。
ctx.en: My hometown has changed beyond recognition over these years.

ctx.s: 有了孩子以后，他们的生活发生了{翻天覆地}的变化。
ctx.en: Once they had a baby, their lives were turned completely upside down.

ctx.s: “你们村现在怎么样？”“变化可大了，跟以前比真是{翻天覆地}。”
ctx.en: "How is your village these days?" "It's changed enormously; compared with before, it's a whole new world."

ctx.s: 互联网给人们的购物方式带来了{翻天覆地}的改变。
ctx.en: The internet has completely transformed the way people shop.

ctx.s: 新老板上任后进行了{翻天覆地}的改革，几乎所有部门都重组了。
ctx.en: The new boss carried out a sweeping overhaul; almost every department was reorganised.

ctx.s: 那场大病之后，他对金钱和家庭的看法发生了{翻天覆地}的转变。
ctx.en: After that serious illness, his views on money and family were completely turned around.

bad.s: 我把桌子挪了一下，房间{翻天覆地}了。
bad.en: (meant: I moved the desk and the room looks different)
bad.why: It is for sweeping, total change; a small rearrangement makes it absurd unless meant as a joke.

bad.s: 科技每天都{翻天覆地}，新产品层出不穷。
bad.en: (meant: technology changes every day)
bad.why: It is one total transformation, not continual daily novelty, which needs an idiom of constant renewal.

cards.mean: never changing; rigid
cards.lit: once formed, it does not change

story.text: The Book of Rites, discussing punishment, explains that a penalty carried out on the body is final: once it is done it cannot be changed or undone. For that reason, it says, a ruler must give his whole mind to a case before passing sentence. The phrase 'once formed, it cannot be changed' later came to describe anything fixed and never altered.

use.how: Attributive or predicate, very often negated: 计划不是一成不变的。 Said of one rule, plan or habit staying fixed over time.

near.diff: 千篇一律 says many works or things are all alike; 一成不变 says one thing stays the same over time.

cards.cue: Your manager tells the team the project schedule can be adjusted if circumstances change; it was never meant to be set in stone. What does she say about the plan?

ctx.s: 计划不是{一成不变}的，可以根据情况调整。
ctx.en: The plan isn't fixed; it can be adjusted as things develop.

ctx.s: 他每天的生活{一成不变}：上班、下班、睡觉。
ctx.en: His days never change: go to work, come home, sleep.

ctx.s: 世界上没有{一成不变}的事物。
ctx.en: Nothing in the world stays the same forever.

ctx.s: “这条规定能改吗？”“规定也不是{一成不变}的，我们可以讨论。”
ctx.en: "Can this rule be changed?" "Rules aren't set in stone either; we can discuss it."

ctx.s: 这家餐厅的菜单十年来{一成不变}，老顾客却越来越少。
ctx.en: The restaurant's menu hasn't changed in ten years, and its regulars keep dwindling.

ctx.s: 用{一成不变}的眼光看待孩子，是很多父母的误区。
ctx.en: Seeing a child through a fixed, unchanging lens is a mistake many parents make.

bad.s: 这些新房子的样子{一成不变}，看起来都一样。
bad.en: (meant: the new houses all look the same)
bad.why: It means one thing staying the same over time; many things that all look alike call for the idiom meaning 'formulaic'.

bad.s: 他把计划{一成不变}了。
bad.en: (meant: he froze the plan)
bad.why: It describes a state and cannot take an object or the ba construction; say instead that the plan stayed unchanged.

cards.mean: to keep up with the times
cards.lit: to advance together with the times

use.how: Predicate, often after 要 or 需要: 教育要与时俱进。 Said of people, institutions or ideas that update themselves to fit the present; also used playfully.

near.diff: 日新月异 describes things themselves changing fast; 与时俱进 praises someone actively adapting to change.

cards.cue: Your seventy-year-old grandmother now pays for everything by phone and sends voice messages to the family group. How do you praise her for not falling behind?

ctx.s: 奶奶现在也用手机付款了，真是{与时俱进}啊！
ctx.en: Grandma pays by phone now too. She really moves with the times!

ctx.s: 学校的教材应该{与时俱进}，不能总用老内容。
ctx.en: School textbooks should be updated, not stuck with the same old content.

ctx.s: “你怎么也开始做短视频了？”“要{与时俱进}嘛。”
ctx.en: "Since when do you make short videos?" "Got to keep up with the times."

ctx.s: 一家公司如果不能{与时俱进}，很快就会被市场淘汰。
ctx.en: A company that can't keep up with the times will soon be pushed out of the market.

ctx.s: 这家老字号在保留传统味道的同时，也在包装上{与时俱进}。
ctx.en: While keeping its traditional flavour, the old brand has modernised its packaging.

ctx.s: 法律条文需要{与时俱进}，才能应对网络时代的新问题。
ctx.en: Laws need to evolve with the times to deal with the new problems of the internet age.

bad.s: 时间{与时俱进}，转眼就到年底了。
bad.en: (meant: time flies; it's suddenly the end of the year)
bad.why: It means adapting to a new era, not time passing by; to say time flies, simply say time passes quickly.

bad.s: 他的病情{与时俱进}，越来越严重了。
bad.en: (meant: his illness got worse over time)
bad.why: It is praise for adapting to the present, not something growing worse as time goes on.

cards.mean: to see someone in a new, better light
cards.lit: to rub one's eyes and look at someone again

story.text: Lü Meng, a general of Wu, was a soldier with little learning until Sun Quan urged him to read. Later the statesman Lu Su visited him, talked with him and was astonished at how much he now knew, saying he was no longer the old Lü Meng of Wu. Lü Meng replied that when a scholar has been away for three days, you should rub your eyes and look at him anew.
story.source: 《三国志·吴书·吕蒙传》裴松之注引《江表传》

use.how: Usually 让/令人刮目相看 or 对某人刮目相看: 他的进步让大家刮目相看。 Said when someone once underrated shows real improvement.

near.diff: 另眼相看 is treating someone specially, better or worse; 刮目相看 is raising your opinion after someone has improved.

cards.cue: The quiet intern everyone overlooked gave the best presentation of the quarter, and the whole team now thinks of her differently. How do you describe their reaction?

ctx.s: 他这次考了全班第一，老师都对他{刮目相看}。
ctx.en: He came top of the class this time, and even the teachers saw him differently.

ctx.s: 半年不见，你的中文进步这么大，真让人{刮目相看}！
ctx.en: Half a year and your Chinese has improved so much. I'm impressed!

ctx.s: “你会做饭了？”“别小看我，今天就让你{刮目相看}。”
ctx.en: "You can cook now?" "Don't underestimate me. Today you'll see me in a new light."

ctx.s: 这支没人看好的球队连赢三场，令所有人{刮目相看}。
ctx.en: The team nobody rated won three in a row and made everyone think again.

ctx.s: 她暗下决心：总有一天要让那些看不起她的人{刮目相看}。
ctx.en: She quietly vowed that one day the people who looked down on her would have to think again.

ctx.s: 这家小公司凭一款新产品打开了市场，让同行{刮目相看}。
ctx.en: With one new product the small company broke into the market, and its rivals took notice.

bad.s: 他一直都是最优秀的学生，大家对他{刮目相看}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone admires him)
bad.why: It needs a change of opinion after improvement; it is not plain admiration for someone always at the top.

bad.s: 他偷了东西以后，邻居们都对他{刮目相看}。
bad.en: (meant: after the theft the neighbours saw him differently)
bad.why: It only means seeing someone in a better light, never a worse one.

cards.mean: monotonously alike, formulaic
cards.lit: a thousand pieces of writing, all to one pattern

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 这些电影千篇一律。 Criticises many works, designs or products that all follow the same dull pattern.

near.diff: 大同小异 simply says things are mostly alike; 千篇一律 complains that they are all the same and boring.
一成不变 is one thing never changing over time; 千篇一律 is many things all made to one formula.

cards.cue: You watched five new romantic comedies this month and every one had the same plot, the same jokes and the same ending. How do you complain about them?

ctx.s: 这些网红餐厅的装修{千篇一律}，没什么特色。
ctx.en: These trendy restaurants all have the same décor; none has any character.

ctx.s: 为什么现在的城市看起来都{千篇一律}？
ctx.en: Why do cities all look the same these days?

ctx.s: 学生的作文开头{千篇一律}，都是“今天天气很好”。
ctx.en: The students' essays all open the same way: "The weather was nice today."

ctx.s: 评委说：“你们的设计太{千篇一律}了，能不能有点新意？”
ctx.en: The judge said: "Your designs are all so formulaic. Can't you show something new?"

ctx.s: 很多求职信内容{千篇一律}，招聘人员看两行就放下了。
ctx.en: So many cover letters read the same that recruiters put them down after two lines.

ctx.s: 景点卖的纪念品{千篇一律}，到哪儿都是一样的钥匙扣和明信片。
ctx.en: The souvenirs at tourist spots are all alike: the same key rings and postcards everywhere.

bad.s: 我和我的双胞胎哥哥长得{千篇一律}。
bad.en: (meant: my twin brother and I look exactly alike)
bad.why: It criticises many works or products sharing one dull formula; two people who look alike are simply exactly the same.

bad.s: 我们的产品质量{千篇一律}，每一件都很好。
bad.en: (meant: our products are consistently high quality)
bad.why: It is a complaint about dull sameness, never praise for consistent quality.

cards.mean: completely different
cards.lit: as sharply apart as if cut, not the same

use.how: Predicate or attributive, often with 和/与……: 两人的性格截然不同。 Contrasts two things that differ sharply.

near.diff: 大相径庭 is more bookish and mostly said of views, results or expectations; 截然不同 fits any sharp contrast.

cards.cue: Two sisters grew up in the same house, but one is loud and adventurous and the other quiet and cautious. How do you describe their personalities?

ctx.s: 这对双胞胎的性格{截然不同}，一个外向，一个内向。
ctx.en: The twins have completely different personalities: one outgoing, one introverted.

ctx.s: 南方和北方的早餐习惯{截然不同}。
ctx.en: Breakfast habits in the south and the north are entirely different.

ctx.s: “电影和原著一样吗？”“不一样，两者的结局{截然不同}。”
ctx.en: "Is the film like the book?" "No, the two endings are completely different."

ctx.s: 同一件事，从不同角度看，可能会得出{截然不同}的结论。
ctx.en: Look at the same event from different angles and you may reach opposite conclusions.

ctx.s: 搬到乡下以后，他过上了和以前{截然不同}的生活。
ctx.en: After moving to the countryside he lived a life utterly unlike his old one.

ctx.s: 两家公司对远程办公的态度{截然不同}：一家鼓励，一家禁止。
ctx.en: The two companies take opposite views of remote work: one encourages it, the other bans it.

bad.s: 这件衣服和那件有点{截然不同}。
bad.en: (meant: this shirt is a bit different from that one)
bad.why: It already means utterly different, so it cannot be softened with 'a bit'; just say the two are a little different.

bad.s: 他{截然不同}了自己的想法。
bad.en: (meant: he completely changed his mind)
bad.why: It describes a contrast between two things and cannot take an object; say he completely changed his mind.

cards.mean: evenly matched, about equal
cards.lit: neither one above nor below the other

use.how: Predicate with two compared subjects, or 跟……不相上下: 两人的成绩不相上下。 Said of ability, level, quality or amount.

near.diff: 势均力敌 is for opposing sides in a fight or contest; 不相上下 compares the level of any two things.

cards.cue: Two job candidates have nearly identical experience and interview scores, and the manager cannot say which one is stronger. How does she describe them?

ctx.s: 他们俩的中文水平{不相上下}。
ctx.en: Their Chinese is about the same level.

ctx.s: “你和你哥谁更高？”“我们俩{不相上下}，差不多一样高。”
ctx.en: "Who's taller, you or your brother?" "We're about even, pretty much the same height."

ctx.s: 这两款手机的价格和性能都{不相上下}，很难选。
ctx.en: The two phones are about equal in price and performance, so it's hard to choose.

ctx.s: 这次期末考试，两个班的平均分{不相上下}。
ctx.en: In this term's final exams, the two classes' average scores were about the same.

ctx.s: 论做菜的手艺，她跟她妈妈已经{不相上下}了。
ctx.en: When it comes to cooking, she's now every bit as good as her mother.

ctx.s: 两位候选人的经验{不相上下}，最后是面试决定了结果。
ctx.en: The two candidates had equal experience, so in the end the interview decided it.

bad.s: 这两种颜色{不相上下}，我分不清。
bad.en: (meant: the two colours look the same and I can't tell them apart)
bad.why: It compares which of two is higher or better, not how alike they look; colours you can't tell apart simply look the same.

bad.s: 他{不相上下}地打量着我。
bad.en: (meant: he looked me up and down)
bad.why: Despite its 'up and down' characters, it is a predicate comparing two parties, never an adverb for how someone looks at you.

cards.mean: just right, to exactly the right degree
cards.lit: reaching exactly the right point

use.how: Predicate, or complement after 得: 盐放得恰到好处。 Praises an amount, degree or timing that is exactly right.

near.diff: 适可而止 advises stopping before going too far; 恰到好处 praises something that hit the right degree.

cards.cue: The chef added just enough chili to give the soup warmth without burning your mouth. How do you praise the seasoning?

ctx.s: 这道菜咸淡{恰到好处}。
ctx.en: This dish is seasoned just right.

ctx.s: “这件衣服大小怎么样？”“{恰到好处}，不松也不紧。”
ctx.en: "How's the size?" "Just right, not loose and not tight."

ctx.s: 她的妆化得{恰到好处}，自然又精神。
ctx.en: Her make-up is just right: natural and fresh.

ctx.s: 演讲中他开的那个玩笑{恰到好处}，一下子让气氛轻松了。
ctx.en: His joke in the speech was perfectly judged and instantly relaxed the room.

ctx.s: 老师的批评{恰到好处}，既指出了问题，又没伤他的自尊。
ctx.en: The teacher's criticism struck the right balance: it named the problem without hurting his pride.

ctx.s: 这部电影的配乐用得{恰到好处}，从不抢画面的风头。
ctx.en: The film's score is used just right and never upstages the pictures.

bad.s: 我昨天的考试{恰到好处}，考了满分。
bad.en: (meant: I did perfectly in yesterday's exam)
bad.why: It praises a degree that is neither too much nor too little, not an outstanding result.

bad.s: 我们{恰到好处}在车站遇见了老同学。
bad.en: (meant: we happened to run into an old classmate at the station)
bad.why: It is a predicate praising the right degree, not an adverb meaning 'by chance'; for that, use a plain word for 'happen to'.

cards.mean: very few, hardly any
cards.lit: sparse and scattered, not even a few

use.how: Predicate, said of countable people or things: 来的人寥寥无几。 Stresses how few there are, often with disappointment.

near.diff: 屈指可数 can stress rarity with respect (few true experts); 寥寥无几 simply stresses how sparse something is.
微不足道 says something is too small to matter; 寥寥无几 counts how few people or things there are.

cards.cue: On a rainy Monday morning the huge shopping mall has only a handful of shoppers wandering around. How do you describe the crowd?

ctx.s: 下大雨了，街上的行人{寥寥无几}。
ctx.en: It's pouring, and there's hardly anyone on the street.

ctx.s: “报名的人多吗？”“{寥寥无几}，才三四个。”
ctx.en: "Have many signed up?" "Hardly any, just three or four."

ctx.s: 讲座开始时，台下的听众{寥寥无几}。
ctx.en: When the lecture began, there were only a handful of people in the audience.

ctx.s: 新店门口冷冷清清，进去的顾客{寥寥无几}。
ctx.en: The new shop is deserted; hardly any customers go in.

ctx.s: 到了深夜，还亮着灯的窗户已经{寥寥无几}。
ctx.en: By late night only a few windows were still lit.

ctx.s: 这种老手艺，如今会做的人已经{寥寥无几}了。
ctx.en: Hardly anyone today still knows this old craft.

bad.s: 我杯子里的水{寥寥无几}了。
bad.en: (meant: there's hardly any water left in my cup)
bad.why: It counts people or things, not an uncountable amount like water; just say there isn't much left.

bad.s: 他的贡献{寥寥无几}，没人注意到。
bad.en: (meant: his contribution was too small to notice)
bad.why: It counts how few people or things there are; a contribution too small to matter calls for the idiom meaning 'trivial'.

cards.mean: too trivial to be worth mentioning
cards.lit: so slight it is not worth speaking of

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 一点微不足道的小事。 Said of something small or unimportant, often modestly about one's own help.

near.diff: 无关紧要 says something does not affect the outcome; 微不足道 says it is too small or slight to be worth mentioning.

cards.cue: Thanked on stage for organising the charity event, a volunteer insists that her part was tiny compared to everyone else's. How does she put it modestly?

ctx.s: 这点钱对他来说{微不足道}。
ctx.en: That bit of money means nothing to him.

ctx.s: “谢谢你帮我！”“一点{微不足道}的小忙，不用客气。”
ctx.en: "Thanks for helping me!" "It was a tiny favour, don't mention it."

ctx.s: 跟大家的努力相比，我做的事情{微不足道}。
ctx.en: Compared with everyone's effort, what I did hardly counts.

ctx.s: 在宇宙面前，人类显得多么{微不足道}啊！
ctx.en: Before the universe, how insignificant humans seem!

ctx.s: 别小看这些{微不足道}的细节，客户往往就是因为它们才选择我们。
ctx.en: Don't dismiss these tiny details; clients often choose us because of them.

ctx.s: 调查发现，一个看似{微不足道}的小错误造成了很大的损失。
ctx.en: The investigation found that a seemingly trivial mistake caused heavy losses.

bad.s: 他是公司里{微不足道}的人物，每个决定都要经过他。
bad.en: (meant: he is a key figure; every decision goes through him)
bad.why: It means trivial, the opposite of what was meant; someone every decision must pass through is an influential figure.

bad.s: 来参加聚会的人{微不足道}，只有三个。
bad.en: (meant: very few people came to the party)
bad.why: It says something is too slight to matter, not that a number is small; for very few guests use the idiom meaning 'hardly any'.

cards.mean: holding a pivotal position; very influential
cards.lit: one lift of the foot tips the weight one way or the other

story.text: In the wars that followed the fall of Wang Mang, Dou Rong held the Hexi region in the northwest, between rival powers. Liu Xiu, Emperor Guangwu of Han, wrote to him that with Gongsun Shu holding Shu and Wei Ao holding Tianshui, and Shu and Han at war, the decision lay with Dou Rong: whichever way he lifted his foot, left or right, would tip the balance. Dou Rong chose to side with Han.

use.how: Mostly 举足轻重的人物/地位/作用 or 在……中举足轻重. Said of a person, group or factor whose weight can decide an outcome.

near.diff: 至关重要 says something is crucial to get right; 举足轻重 says someone or something has the weight to sway the outcome.

cards.cue: In a tight committee vote, everyone knows the one undecided member will settle the result, so both sides are courting her. How do you describe her vote?

ctx.s: 他在公司里是个{举足轻重}的人物。
ctx.en: He's a very influential figure in the company.

ctx.s: “这个项目谁说了算？”“李经理的意见{举足轻重}，先问他吧。”
ctx.en: "Who has the final say on this project?" "Manager Li's opinion carries the most weight, so ask him first."

ctx.s: 她的一票在这次投票中{举足轻重}。
ctx.en: Her single vote could decide this ballot.

ctx.s: 父母的态度在孩子选专业时往往{举足轻重}。
ctx.en: Parents' attitudes often weigh heavily when a child chooses a major.

ctx.s: 这座港口在国际贸易中起着{举足轻重}的作用。
ctx.en: This port plays a pivotal role in international trade.

ctx.s: 作为行业里{举足轻重}的大公司，它的一举一动都受到关注。
ctx.en: As one of the industry's most influential companies, its every move is watched.

bad.s: 这件事{举足轻重}，大家不用太在意。
bad.en: (meant: this matter is trivial, don't worry about it)
bad.why: It means carrying great weight, the opposite of trivial, so it clashes with telling people not to worry about it.

bad.s: 他{举足轻重}地走进了会议室。
bad.en: (meant: he walked into the meeting room with heavy steps)
bad.why: Despite the foot in it, it describes influence, not the way someone walks, and is never used as an adverb of manner.

cards.mean: to put a finger right on the crux of the matter
cards.lit: one jab of the needle and blood shows

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 他的话一针见血；一针见血地指出问题。 Said of a remark or analysis that names the real problem in few words.

near.diff: 直言不讳 is about frankness, saying things bluntly; 一针见血 is about accuracy, hitting the very heart of the problem.

cards.cue: After two hours of a meeting circling the problem, the intern says one sentence that names its real cause. How was her remark?

ctx.s: 他的评论{一针见血}，说到了问题的关键。
ctx.en: His comment was spot on; it went right to the heart of the problem.

ctx.s: 老师{一针见血}地指出了我作文里最大的问题。
ctx.en: The teacher pinpointed the biggest problem in my essay.

ctx.s: “你不是没时间，是不想做。”妈妈的话{一针见血}。
ctx.en: "It's not that you don't have time, you just don't want to do it." Mum hit the nail on the head.

ctx.s: 开了两个小时会，新来的实习生一句话就{一针见血}：问题出在价格上。
ctx.en: After a two-hour meeting, the new intern nailed it in one sentence: the problem was the price.

ctx.s: 这篇书评写得{一针见血}，把小说最大的毛病说透了。
ctx.en: The review is razor-sharp; it lays bare the novel's biggest flaw.

ctx.s: 能{一针见血}地看出问题所在，是一个好经理必备的本领。
ctx.en: Being able to see straight to the core of a problem is a skill every good manager needs.

bad.s: 他讲了三个小时，{一针见血}地分析了每一个细节。
bad.en: (meant: he analysed every detail thoroughly for three hours)
bad.why: It praises a short, sharp remark that hits the key point, not a long, exhaustive analysis of every detail.

bad.s: 他{一针见血}地骂了我一顿，我很伤心。
bad.en: (meant: he scolded me cruelly and hurt me)
bad.why: It praises insight into the crux of a matter; it does not mean hurtful or harsh words.

cards.mean: too complicated or painful to sum up in a few words
cards.lit: hard to say it all in one word

use.how: Predicate, often as a sighing reply: 唉，一言难尽。 Said of one's own experiences or a tangled affair, hinting at hardship.

near.diff: 说来话长 only says the story is long to tell; 一言难尽 hints the matter is tangled or painful, often with a sigh.

cards.cue: An old friend asks how your last three years went; there was a lost job, a divorce and a move, and you just sigh. What do you say?

ctx.s: “你最近怎么样？”他苦笑着摇摇头：“唉，{一言难尽}。”
ctx.en: "How have you been?" He gave a wry smile and shook his head: "Oh, where do I start."

ctx.s: 这几年的经历，真是{一言难尽}。
ctx.en: What I've been through these past few years is hard to put into words.

ctx.s: 那段婚姻带给她的痛苦，真是{一言难尽}。
ctx.en: The pain that marriage caused her is more than words can say.

ctx.s: 她创业的辛苦{一言难尽}，只有她自己知道。
ctx.en: The hardships of starting her business are beyond a few words; only she really knows.

ctx.s: 两家公司之间的恩怨{一言难尽}，我们改天再聊吧。
ctx.en: The history between those two companies is too tangled to explain now; let's talk another day.

ctx.s: 他望着窗外，叹了口气说：“这里面的事，{一言难尽}啊。”
ctx.en: He looked out of the window and sighed: "There's more to it than I can tell you."

bad.s: 他说话总是{一言难尽}，很啰嗦。
bad.en: (meant: he is always long-winded)
bad.why: It describes a matter too tangled to sum up, not a person who talks too much.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜好吃得{一言难尽}。
bad.en: (meant: the food is indescribably delicious)
bad.why: It hints at complication or hardship, never at delight beyond words.

cards.mean: to tell everything in full, holding nothing back
cards.lit: one, five; one, ten: counting off by fives, every item tallied

use.how: Adverbial before 说, 讲, 告诉 or 交代, often with 地: 他一五一十地说了。 Said of recounting what happened, in full and truthfully.

cards.cue: After the vase broke, your little brother sat your mother down and told her exactly what happened, step by step, leaving nothing out. How did he tell her?

ctx.s: 他把事情的经过{一五一十}地告诉了我。
ctx.en: He told me exactly how it all happened, from start to finish.

ctx.s: 别着急，你{一五一十}地说，到底发生了什么？
ctx.en: Calm down and tell me everything: what actually happened?

ctx.s: 孩子回家后，把学校里的事{一五一十}讲给妈妈听。
ctx.en: When the child got home, he told his mother everything that had happened at school.

ctx.s: 面对警察，他把那天晚上看到的情况{一五一十}说了出来。
ctx.en: In front of the police, he recounted everything he had seen that night.

ctx.s: “你都跟老板说了？”“嗯，我{一五一十}全交代了。”
ctx.en: "You told the boss everything?" "Yes, I came clean about all of it."

ctx.s: 回到家，她把在医院听到的话{一五一十}地转告了丈夫。
ctx.en: When she got home, she passed on to her husband every word she had heard at the hospital.

bad.s: 这本书我{一五一十}地读完了。
bad.en: (meant: I read the book cover to cover)
bad.why: It is used for telling or reporting what happened in full, not for reading or doing something thoroughly.

bad.s: 他说话{一五一十}，很有条理。
bad.en: (meant: he speaks in an organised way)
bad.why: It is an adverbial for recounting a particular matter in full, not a description of someone's speaking style.

cards.mean: with a dead-serious, earnest air (often comically so)
cards.lit: as proper as a volume of the classics

use.how: Adverbial with 地 or attributive with 的: 一本正经地说；一本正经的样子。 Describes a person's serious manner, often comic against a trivial topic.

near.diff: 装模作样 says the manner is put on to fool people; 一本正经 just describes a serious, earnest manner, sincere or deadpan.

cards.cue: Your friend tells an absurd made-up story with a perfectly straight face, and for a minute everyone believes him. How did he tell it?

ctx.s: 他{一本正经}地问我：“猫会不会做梦？”
ctx.en: He asked me in all seriousness: "Do cats dream?"

ctx.s: 看他那{一本正经}的样子，大家都忍不住笑了。
ctx.en: Seeing how solemn he looked, everyone burst out laughing.

ctx.s: 小女孩{一本正经}地给布娃娃上课。
ctx.en: The little girl was giving her dolls a lesson with the utmost seriousness.

ctx.s: 他{一本正经}地胡说八道，我们差点儿信了。
ctx.en: He talked complete nonsense with a perfectly straight face, and we almost believed him.

ctx.s: “你别笑，我是{一本正经}地跟你说这件事。”
ctx.en: "Don't laugh, I'm telling you this in all seriousness."

ctx.s: 主持人{一本正经}地宣布：“今天会议的主题是午饭吃什么。”
ctx.en: The host announced with a dead-serious face: "Today's meeting is about what to have for lunch."

bad.s: 他工作很{一本正经}，从来不出错。
bad.en: (meant: he is meticulous at work and never makes mistakes)
bad.why: It describes a serious manner or expression, not careful, accurate work.

bad.s: 这个会议很{一本正经}。
bad.en: (meant: the meeting is very formal)
bad.why: It describes a person's manner, not the formality of an event such as a meeting.

cards.mean: having nothing at all to one's name
cards.lit: there is not one thing that one has

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 我一无所有；一无所有的穷学生。 Said of a person or family with no money or possessions, sometimes of life without love or health.

near.diff: 倾家荡产 is the act of losing a whole fortune; 一无所有 is the state of having nothing, whether lost or never had.

cards.cue: A man arrived in the city at nineteen with no money, no friends and no job. Describe what he had at that time.

ctx.s: 刚来北京的时候，我{一无所有}。
ctx.en: When I first came to Beijing, I had nothing.

ctx.s: 一场大火之后，他们家变得{一无所有}。
ctx.en: After the fire, their family was left with nothing.

ctx.s: 他从一个{一无所有}的穷学生，变成了公司老板。
ctx.en: He went from a penniless student to the boss of a company.

ctx.s: “你什么都没有，凭什么娶我女儿？”“我现在是{一无所有}，但我会努力的。”
ctx.en: "You have nothing; what makes you think you can marry my daughter?" "I have nothing now, but I'll work hard."

ctx.s: 就算{一无所有}，我们还有彼此。
ctx.en: Even if we have nothing, we still have each other.

ctx.s: 有人说，没有健康，再有钱也等于{一无所有}。
ctx.en: Some say that without your health, however rich you are, you really have nothing.

bad.s: 我对这件事{一无所有}。
bad.en: (meant: I know nothing about this)
bad.why: It is about possessions, not knowledge; knowing nothing about a matter takes the idiom ending in zhi, to know.

bad.s: 这个房间很{一无所有}。
bad.en: (meant: the room is very empty)
bad.why: It cannot take hen (very), and it says a person owns nothing, not that a place is empty.

cards.mean: completely unaware of a matter or its facts
cards.lit: there is not one thing that one knows

use.how: Predicate, usually 对……一无所知: 我对这件事一无所知。 Said of not knowing the facts of a matter, event or person.

near.diff: 一窍不通 is having no grasp of a skill or field, like music or computers; 一无所知 is not knowing the facts of a matter.

cards.cue: Your company was sold last week, and you only found out today from the news; nobody had said a word to you. How much did you know before?

ctx.s: 我对这件事{一无所知}。
ctx.en: I know nothing about this.

ctx.s: 在看到新闻之前，他对公司被卖的事{一无所知}。
ctx.en: Until he saw the news, he had no idea the company had been sold.

ctx.s: “你知道他们要搬家吗？”“我{一无所知}，没人告诉我。”
ctx.en: "Did you know they're moving?" "I had no idea; nobody told me."

ctx.s: 我们对这个人的过去几乎{一无所知}。
ctx.en: We know almost nothing about this man's past.

ctx.s: 那个邻居说，他对那天晚上的事{一无所知}。
ctx.en: The neighbour said he knew nothing about what happened that night.

ctx.s: 很多人吃了几年的药，却对它的副作用{一无所知}，这很危险。
ctx.en: Many people take a medicine for years yet know nothing about its side effects, which is dangerous.

bad.s: 我{一无所知}这件事。
bad.en: (meant: I know nothing about this)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; the matter must come before it, introduced by dui (about).

bad.s: 他钢琴弹得{一无所知}。
bad.en: (meant: he can't play the piano at all)
bad.why: It is about not knowing facts, not lacking a skill, and cannot be a complement after de; having no skill at all calls for a different idiom.

cards.mean: to feel like old friends at the first meeting
cards.lit: meeting once, it is as if they were old acquaintances

use.how: Predicate, with two people as subject: 我们一见如故。 Said only of people meeting for the first time who instantly get on like old friends.

near.diff: 一见钟情 is falling in love at first sight; 一见如故 is instant friendship, a mutual feeling of old acquaintance.

cards.cue: At a conference you meet a stranger who loves the same books and grew up in your hometown; within an hour you are talking like childhood friends. How did you two get on?

ctx.s: 我们俩{一见如故}，聊了一整晚。
ctx.en: We hit it off right away and talked all night.

ctx.s: 第一次见面，他们就{一见如故}，后来成了最好的朋友。
ctx.en: They clicked the first time they met and later became best friends.

ctx.s: “你们认识很久了吧？”“没有，上个月才认识，不过{一见如故}。”
ctx.en: "You must have known each other for ages." "No, we only met last month, but it felt like we'd always been friends."

ctx.s: 两位老人在公园里{一见如故}，从此每天一起下棋。
ctx.en: The two old men took to each other at once in the park, and from then on played chess together every day.

ctx.s: 她和新同事{一见如故}，很快就无话不谈。
ctx.en: She and her new colleague got on like old friends and were soon telling each other everything.

ctx.s: 在火车上和一位陌生人{一见如故}，是这次旅行最难忘的事。
ctx.en: Striking up an instant friendship with a stranger on the train was the most memorable part of the trip.

bad.s: 他对她{一见如故}，马上就爱上了她。
bad.en: (meant: he fell in love with her at first sight)
bad.why: It is about friendship felt by both sides; falling in love at first sight is a different idiom.

bad.s: 我们是老同学，十年没见了，今天{一见如故}。
bad.en: (meant: old classmates reunited felt as close as ever)
bad.why: It is only for people meeting for the first time; old friends meeting again are already old friends.

cards.mean: one's every move
cards.lit: every lift of a hand and every movement

use.how: Noun phrase, usually after a possessor: 他的一举一动。 Often the object of 注意, 关注, 盯着 or 模仿, about someone being watched or copied.

cards.cue: On her first day, the new teacher feels the whole class watching how she walks, gestures and writes on the board. What of hers are they watching?

ctx.s: 孩子会模仿父母的{一举一动}。
ctx.en: Children copy their parents' every move.

ctx.s: 明星的{一举一动}都受到媒体的关注。
ctx.en: Everything a celebrity does is watched by the media.

ctx.s: 第一天上班，我觉得老板在注意我的{一举一动}。
ctx.en: On my first day at work, I felt the boss was watching my every move.

ctx.s: “你为什么总看着我？”“我在学你做菜，你的{一举一动}我都要记住。”
ctx.en: "Why do you keep watching me?" "I'm learning to cook from you; I need to remember every move you make."

ctx.s: 他的{一举一动}都很得体，看得出家教很好。
ctx.en: Everything he does is so proper; you can tell he was raised well.

ctx.s: 猫躲在沙发后面，紧紧盯着小鸟的{一举一动}。
ctx.en: The cat hid behind the sofa, tracking the little bird's every movement.

bad.s: 他{一举一动}地走进了教室。
bad.en: (meant: he walked into the classroom step by step)
bad.why: It is a noun phrase meaning someone's every action, not an adverbial describing how one moves.

bad.s: 这个计划我们要{一举一动}完成。
bad.en: (meant: we must finish the plan in one go)
bad.why: It means a person's every movement, not doing something in a single move; for that use a word meaning in one go.

cards.mean: hopelessly bad; an utter shambles
cards.lit: all collapsed and muddled

use.how: Predicate or degree complement after 得: 考得一塌糊涂。 Says a result, situation or performance is hopelessly bad; also of crying uncontrollably.

near.diff: 乱七八糟 is about disorder and mess; 一塌糊涂 says something turned out hopelessly badly, not just untidily.

cards.cue: You didn't study, the exam was hard, and when the results came back you had your worst score ever. How did you do?

ctx.s: 这次考试我考得{一塌糊涂}。
ctx.en: I made a complete mess of this exam.

ctx.s: 他把这次谈判搞得{一塌糊涂}，公司丢了最大的客户。
ctx.en: He made such a mess of the negotiations that the company lost its biggest client.

ctx.s: “比赛怎么样？”“别提了，我们输得{一塌糊涂}。”
ctx.en: "How was the match?" "Don't ask; we got thrashed."

ctx.s: 看到电影的结局，她哭得{一塌糊涂}。
ctx.en: At the end of the film, she cried her eyes out.

ctx.s: 新经理上任半年，公司的业绩就差得{一塌糊涂}。
ctx.en: Six months after the new manager arrived, the company's results were dreadful.

ctx.s: 我的发音{一塌糊涂}，老师听了直摇头。
ctx.en: My pronunciation is hopeless; the teacher just kept shaking her head.

bad.s: 他是一个{一塌糊涂}的人，总是忘记带钥匙。
bad.en: (meant: he is a scatterbrained person who always forgets his keys)
bad.why: It describes how badly something turned out, not a person's character; it cannot label someone as forgetful or careless.

bad.s: 他{一塌糊涂}了这个项目。
bad.en: (meant: he messed up the project)
bad.why: It is not a verb and cannot take an object; it goes after de, as in ba xiangmu gao de yitahutu (made a shambles of the project).

cards.mean: without saying a word
cards.lit: not one word is sent out

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 他一言不发地走了。 Said of someone who stays silent on an occasion when they could or should speak.

near.diff: 哑口无言 is being left with no answer, usually after losing an argument; 一言不发 is simply keeping silent, often by choice.

cards.cue: Throughout the whole family quarrel, your father sat in the corner drinking his tea and didn't say a single thing. What did he do?

ctx.s: 他坐在那里，{一言不发}。
ctx.en: He sat there without saying a word.

ctx.s: 整个会上，经理{一言不发}，只是听大家说。
ctx.en: The manager didn't say a word throughout the meeting; he just listened.

ctx.s: “你怎么{一言不发}？是不是不高兴了？”
ctx.en: "Why aren't you saying anything? Are you upset?"

ctx.s: 被老师批评以后，他{一言不发}地走出了教室。
ctx.en: After being told off by the teacher, he walked out of the classroom without a word.

ctx.s: 吃饭的时候，爸爸一直{一言不发}，气氛有点儿紧张。
ctx.en: Dad didn't say a word all through dinner, and the atmosphere was a bit tense.

ctx.s: 记者问了好几个问题，那位演员却{一言不发}，转身离开了。
ctx.en: The reporters asked several questions, but the actor said nothing, turned and walked away.

bad.s: 这个婴儿还小，{一言不发}。
bad.en: (meant: the baby is too young to talk)
bad.why: It implies choosing silence when one could speak; it is not for someone who cannot talk yet.

bad.s: 他{一言不发}地告诉我，他明天要走了。
bad.en: (meant: he quietly told me he was leaving tomorrow)
bad.why: It means saying not a single word, so it cannot describe the manner of telling someone something; for speaking softly use xiaosheng (quietly).

cards.mean: to let one's mind run wild with idle or groundless thoughts
cards.lit: to think wildly and imagine at random

use.how: Used as a verb, very often in 别胡思乱想 to calm someone who is worrying for no reason. Said of a person's own wandering, anxious thoughts.

near.diff: 异想天开 is a fanciful, unrealistic idea or plan; 胡思乱想 is aimless, often anxious thinking with no basis.

cards.cue: Your friend lies awake picturing every way tomorrow's interview could go wrong. You tell her to stop and get some sleep.

ctx.s: 别{胡思乱想}了，早点睡吧。
ctx.en: Stop letting your imagination run away with you and get some sleep.

ctx.s: 我一晚上没回电话，妈妈一个人在家{胡思乱想}。
ctx.en: I didn't return her calls all evening, so Mum sat at home imagining the worst.

ctx.s: 体检结果还没出来，你先别{胡思乱想}，等医生说了再讲。
ctx.en: The test results aren't out yet, so don't go imagining things; wait for the doctor.

ctx.s: “他是不是不喜欢我了？”“你想多了，别{胡思乱想}。”
ctx.en: "Has he stopped liking me?" "You're overthinking it. Don't torture yourself with ideas like that."

ctx.s: 人一闲下来，就容易{胡思乱想}。
ctx.en: When people have nothing to do, their minds easily start to wander into worries.

ctx.s: 考试前一天晚上，她躺在床上{胡思乱想}，怎么也睡不着。
ctx.en: The night before the exam she lay in bed with her thoughts racing and couldn't fall asleep.

bad.s: 他是个科学家，每天在实验室里{胡思乱想}新发明。
bad.en: (meant: he spends his days imagining new inventions)
bad.why: It disparages idle, groundless thoughts; it cannot describe creative or productive thinking.

bad.s: 这个计划太{胡思乱想}了，根本行不通。
bad.en: (meant: this plan is too unrealistic)
bad.why: It is what a person does in their head, not a quality of a plan; a plan that is wildly unrealistic calls for yì xiǎng tiān kāi.

cards.mean: again and again, time after time
cards.lit: three turns and five times

use.how: Adverbial before a verb: 我三番五次提醒他。 Said of one person repeating the same act, often a request, warning or nuisance, usually with impatience.

near.diff: 接二连三 is about events following one another quickly; 三番五次 is about someone doing the same thing over and over.

cards.cue: You reminded your roommate again and again to lock the front door, and he still left it open last night.

ctx.s: 我{三番五次}提醒他带伞，他还是忘了。
ctx.en: I reminded him to take an umbrella time after time, and he still forgot.

ctx.s: 老板{三番五次}找他谈话，他才答应留下来。
ctx.en: Only after the boss talked to him again and again did he agree to stay.

ctx.s: 楼上的邻居{三番五次}在半夜放音乐，大家都很生气。
ctx.en: The upstairs neighbour keeps playing music in the middle of the night, and everyone is angry.

ctx.s: 你怎么又迟到了？我已经{三番五次}跟你说过了！
ctx.en: Late again? I've told you over and over!

ctx.s: 这家公司{三番五次}邀请她加入，都被她婉言谢绝了。
ctx.en: The company invited her to join again and again, and each time she politely declined.

ctx.s: 他{三番五次}地向物业反映，问题却一直没有解决。
ctx.en: He complained to the building management time after time, but the problem was never fixed.

bad.s: 地球{三番五次}地绕着太阳转。
bad.en: (meant: the earth keeps going round the sun)
bad.why: It is about a person repeating a deliberate act, not a regular natural cycle.

bad.s: 他每天早上{三番五次}地刷牙。
bad.en: (meant: he brushes his teeth every morning)
bad.why: It marks repetition beyond what is expected, usually requests or warnings, not a normal daily routine.

cards.mean: in just a few words
cards.lit: three words and two phrases

use.how: Adverbial or object about speaking: 三言两语就说清楚了, or negated: 不是三言两语能说清的. Said of how briefly something is or can be said.

near.diff: 一言难尽 says a matter is too complex or painful to tell at all; 三言两语 simply means a few words, which may or may not be enough.

cards.cue: Your colleague settled a long argument in the meeting with just a couple of short sentences. How did he do it?

ctx.s: 这件事很简单，{三言两语}就能说清楚。
ctx.en: This is simple; it can be explained in a couple of sentences.

ctx.s: 他{三言两语}就把哭闹的孩子哄笑了。
ctx.en: With just a few words he had the crying child laughing.

ctx.s: 这个问题很复杂，不是{三言两语}能讲明白的。
ctx.en: This problem is complicated; it can't be explained in a few words.

ctx.s: 经理只用了{三言两语}，就让会议回到了正题。
ctx.en: With only a few words the manager brought the meeting back on topic.

ctx.s: 临走前，她{三言两语}交代了几件事，就匆匆出门了。
ctx.en: Before leaving she gave a few quick instructions and hurried out the door.

ctx.s: 他在信里只写了{三言两语}，说自己一切都好。
ctx.en: He wrote only a few lines in the letter, saying that all was well.

bad.s: 他是个{三言两语}的人，从来不爱说话。
bad.en: (meant: he is a man of few words)
bad.why: It describes a brief utterance, not a person's character; for a quiet man of few words use chén mò guǎ yán.

bad.s: 这本书写得很{三言两语}，读起来很轻松。
bad.en: (meant: the book is concisely written)
bad.why: It is not an adjective and cannot take hěn; concise writing is jiǎnjié.

cards.mean: to think twice before acting
cards.lit: to think three times and then act

story.text: The Analects records that Ji Wenzi, a minister of the state of Lu, always thought three times before he acted. When Confucius heard of it he remarked: twice is enough. The phrase 'think three times, then act' became a saying that now simply advises careful thought before acting, though Confucius himself was hinting that Ji Wenzi overdid it.

use.how: Usually advice before a decision: 你要三思而行, 还是三思而行吧, or a habit: 做事总是三思而行. Also said in the full form 三思而后行.

near.diff: 深思熟虑 describes careful thought already given (经过深思熟虑); 三思而行 is advice to think before you act.

cards.cue: Your cousin wants to quit a stable job tomorrow, on impulse, to open a café. What do you advise before he hands in his notice?

ctx.s: 辞职是大事，你最好{三思而行}。
ctx.en: Quitting is a big step; you'd better think it over carefully first.

ctx.s: 爷爷常对我们说，凡事要{三思而行}。
ctx.en: Grandpa always told us to think things through before acting.

ctx.s: “我打算把房子卖了去创业。”“这么大的决定，还是{三思而行}吧。”
ctx.en: "I'm planning to sell the flat and start a business." "A decision that big, you should think twice."

ctx.s: 网上投资陷阱很多，大家一定要{三思而行}。
ctx.en: There are many online investment traps, so everyone should think carefully before acting.

ctx.s: 他年轻时吃过冲动的亏，从那以后做事总是{三思而行}。
ctx.en: He paid for being impulsive when he was young, and ever since he has always thought before acting.

ctx.s: 签合同之前，律师提醒她{三思而行}，别急着签字。
ctx.en: Before she signed the contract, her lawyer reminded her to think it over and not rush to sign.

bad.s: 经过{三思而行}，他终于做出了决定。
bad.en: (meant: after careful thought he finally decided)
bad.why: It is advice or a habit, not a noun for thought that can follow jīngguò; say jīngguò shēn sī shú lǜ.

bad.s: 他{三思而行}地把这本书看了三遍。
bad.en: (meant: he read the book carefully three times)
bad.why: The three is not a count of repeats; it means being careful before taking an action.

cards.mean: practically certain to succeed
cards.lit: of ten grabs, nine hold firm

use.how: Predicate or 是…的 about the likely outcome of an exam, deal or match: 这次比赛我们十拿九稳。 Also said of confidence that turns out misplaced.

near.diff: 万无一失 says nothing at all can go wrong, often of safety measures; 十拿九稳 is a confident forecast that something will succeed.
胸有成竹 is about having a ready plan in mind; 十拿九稳 is about the odds of the result.

cards.cue: Your team leads by twenty points with two minutes left, and a teammate says the win is as good as in the bag.

ctx.s: 这次考试我准备得很充分，及格是{十拿九稳}的。
ctx.en: I've prepared thoroughly for this exam; passing is a sure thing.

ctx.s: “这笔生意你有几成把握？”“放心吧，{十拿九稳}。”
ctx.en: "How sure are you of closing this deal?" "Don't worry, it's in the bag."

ctx.s: 以她的成绩，考上这所大学应该{十拿九稳}。
ctx.en: With her grades, getting into this university should be practically certain.

ctx.s: 他以为这场比赛{十拿九稳}，没想到最后输了。
ctx.en: He thought the match was a sure win, but in the end they lost.

ctx.s: 我们才领先一个球，现在说{十拿九稳}还太早。
ctx.en: We're only one goal ahead; it's too early to call it a sure win.

ctx.s: 教练觉得这场球{十拿九稳}，就让主力球员休息了。
ctx.en: The coach thought the game was a certain win, so he rested his key players.

bad.s: 这座桥修得{十拿九稳}，可以用很多年。
bad.en: (meant: the bridge is very solidly built)
bad.why: It forecasts the success of an attempt, not physical sturdiness; a solid bridge is jiēshi or láogù.

bad.s: 我对他的人品{十拿九稳}。
bad.en: (meant: I fully trust his character)
bad.why: It is about the likely outcome of an attempt, not about trusting a person; say xìndeguò, to trust.

cards.mean: absolutely true, every word of it (of a report or claim)
cards.lit: a thousand times true, ten thousand times certain

use.how: Predicate or a reply on its own, insisting that news, a fact or a claim is true: 这消息千真万确。

cards.cue: Your friend refuses to believe the shy new classmate won the speech contest. You were there and insist it really happened.

ctx.s: 这个消息{千真万确}，是我亲耳听到的。
ctx.en: This news is absolutely true; I heard it with my own ears.

ctx.s: “他真的要出国了？”“{千真万确}，机票都买好了。”
ctx.en: "Is he really going abroad?" "Absolutely, he's already bought the ticket."

ctx.s: 我说的每一句话都是{千真万确}的，你可以去查。
ctx.en: Every word I've said is true; you can check.

ctx.s: 起初没人相信她中了大奖，可这件事{千真万确}。
ctx.en: At first nobody believed she had won the big prize, but it was absolutely true.

ctx.s: 报道里说的那些事，难道都是{千真万确}的吗？
ctx.en: Is everything in that report really, completely true?

ctx.s: 调查结果表明，他当晚就在现场，这一点{千真万确}。
ctx.en: The investigation established beyond doubt that he was at the scene that night.

bad.s: 他是一个{千真万确}的人，从不撒谎。
bad.en: (meant: he is an honest person who never lies)
bad.why: It says a statement or fact is true, not that a person is honest; an honest person is chéngshí.

bad.s: 你放心，我明天{千真万确}会来。
bad.en: (meant: don't worry, I will definitely come tomorrow)
bad.why: It insists that a fact or report is true; it is not an adverb for a promise. To promise, say yídìng huì lái.

cards.mean: all sorts of strange and bizarre things
cards.lit: a thousand oddities and a hundred strange things

use.how: Attributive with 的 or predicate, about many things, shapes or questions that are odd: 千奇百怪的石头, 形状千奇百怪.

near.diff: 五花八门 stresses a great variety of kinds; 千奇百怪 stresses that the things are strange and odd.

cards.cue: On a reef dive you see fish shaped like boxes, needles and balloons, each odder than the last. How do you describe them?

ctx.s: 海底有很多{千奇百怪}的鱼。
ctx.en: There are all kinds of weird and wonderful fish on the seabed.

ctx.s: 这座山上的石头形状{千奇百怪}，有的像动物，有的像人。
ctx.en: The rocks on this mountain come in all sorts of bizarre shapes; some look like animals, some like people.

ctx.s: 孩子们总会问一些{千奇百怪}的问题，比如鱼会不会做梦。
ctx.en: Children are always asking the strangest questions, like whether fish dream.

ctx.s: 昨天夜里我做了好多{千奇百怪}的梦。
ctx.en: Last night I had a whole string of bizarre dreams.

ctx.s: 博物馆里的古代乐器长得{千奇百怪}，我根本看不出是怎么演奏的。
ctx.en: The ancient instruments in the museum come in such bizarre shapes that I couldn't tell how they were played.

ctx.s: “这家店卖什么？”“全是些{千奇百怪}的小玩意儿，好多我都叫不出名字。”
ctx.en: "What does this shop sell?" "All sorts of odd little gadgets; I can't even name half of them."

bad.s: 他这个人{千奇百怪}的，谁都不理。
bad.en: (meant: he is a strange man who ignores everyone)
bad.why: It describes a mass of many different odd things, not one person's eccentric character; an odd person is gǔguài.

bad.s: 这家超市商品{千奇百怪}，日用品一应俱全。
bad.en: (meant: the supermarket has a full range of goods)
bad.why: It implies the goods are bizarre; a full range of ordinary goods is yīng yǒu jìn yǒu.

cards.mean: one after another in quick succession
cards.lit: the second follows on, the third joins after

use.how: Adverbial, often with 地, before verbs like 发生, 传来, 出现: 事故接二连三地发生. Said of separate events, often bad ones, coming close together.

near.diff: 三番五次 is someone repeating the same act; 接二连三 is separate events following one after another.
络绎不绝 is a steady stream of people or vehicles; 接二连三 is a series of separate happenings.

cards.cue: Within one week your car broke down, your phone was stolen and your landlord raised the rent. How did the troubles arrive?

ctx.s: 好消息{接二连三}地传来，大家都很高兴。
ctx.en: Good news kept coming in, one piece after another, and everyone was delighted.

ctx.s: 最近家里{接二连三}地出事，妈妈都累病了。
ctx.en: One thing after another has gone wrong at home lately, and Mum has worn herself out.

ctx.s: 比赛刚开始，对方就{接二连三}地进了好几个球。
ctx.en: Right after kick-off the other side scored several goals in quick succession.

ctx.s: 这个路口{接二连三}发生车祸，交警决定加装红绿灯。
ctx.en: After one accident after another at this junction, the traffic police decided to put in lights.

ctx.s: “你今天怎么了？”“别提了，{接二连三}地出状况。”
ctx.en: "What's up with you today?" "Don't ask. One mishap after another."

ctx.s: 新店开张后，订单{接二连三}地涌来，员工忙得团团转。
ctx.en: After the new shop opened, orders poured in one after another and the staff were run off their feet.

bad.s: 他{接二连三}地爱了她二十年。
bad.en: (meant: he loved her without a break for twenty years)
bad.why: It is about separate events in quick succession, not one continuous state over a long time.

bad.s: 教室里学生{接二连三}，座位都坐满了。
bad.en: (meant: the classroom is packed with students)
bad.why: It describes events following in time, not a large number of people present at once.

cards.mean: all the streets and alleys of a town
cards.lit: big streets and small lanes

use.how: A place noun, as subject (大街小巷都…) or object of 传遍, 走遍, 穿过: 歌声传遍了大街小巷. Means everywhere in a town.

near.diff: 家喻户晓 means known in every household; 大街小巷 names the places, every street in town, where something is seen or heard.

cards.cue: During the festival, red lanterns hang over every road and lane in the city, from the main avenue to the tiniest alley.

ctx.s: 春节快到了，{大街小巷}都挂起了红灯笼。
ctx.en: Spring Festival is near, and red lanterns hang in every street and lane.

ctx.s: 这首歌一夜之间传遍了{大街小巷}。
ctx.en: Overnight this song could be heard on every street in town.

ctx.s: 我小时候常和朋友骑车穿过城里的{大街小巷}。
ctx.en: As a child I often rode my bike with friends through all the streets and alleys of the town.

ctx.s: 下了一夜大雪，{大街小巷}一片白茫茫。
ctx.en: After a night of heavy snow, every street and lane was a sheet of white.

ctx.s: 这座古城的{大街小巷}，你都走遍了吗？
ctx.en: Have you walked every street and alley of this old town?

ctx.s: 世界杯期间，{大街小巷}都在谈论足球。
ctx.en: During the World Cup, the whole town was talking about football.

bad.s: 我家门口有一条{大街小巷}。
bad.en: (meant: there is a street outside my house)
bad.why: It means all the streets of a town together and cannot name or count a single street.

bad.s: 她{大街小巷}地找了一整天小猫。
bad.en: (meant: she searched all over town for her kitten)
bad.why: It is a place noun and cannot be an adverb with de; make it the object of a verb such as zhǎobiàn, searched all over.

cards.mean: loving each other dearly
cards.lit: to be close to each other and love each other

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地, about family members, couples or a close group: 一家人相亲相爱. Warm, often in wishes.

cards.cue: At their golden anniversary, the grandchildren describe how Grandma and Grandpa have cherished each other all their lives.

ctx.s: 他们一家人{相亲相爱}，日子过得很幸福。
ctx.en: Their family love each other dearly, and they live a happy life.

ctx.s: 爷爷奶奶{相亲相爱}地过了一辈子。
ctx.en: Grandpa and Grandma spent their whole lives devoted to each other.

ctx.s: 祝你们两个以后{相亲相爱}，白头到老。
ctx.en: May you two always love each other dearly and grow old together.

ctx.s: 妈妈常说，兄弟姐妹要{相亲相爱}，互相帮助。
ctx.en: Mum always says brothers and sisters should love each other and help one another.

ctx.s: 看到小猫和小狗{相亲相爱}的样子，大家都笑了。
ctx.en: Seeing the kitten and the puppy so fond of each other made everyone smile.

ctx.s: 我们班的同学像一家人一样{相亲相爱}。
ctx.en: Our classmates are as close and caring as one family.

bad.s: 我和老板{相亲相爱}，合作得很好。
bad.en: (meant: my boss and I get on well)
bad.why: It implies family-like loving affection; colleagues who get on well are xiāngchǔ de hěn hǎo.

bad.s: 他上周末去{相亲相爱}了，见了一个女孩。
bad.en: (meant: he went on a blind date last weekend)
bad.why: A blind date is xiāngqīn alone; the full idiom is a state of mutual love, not an activity you go to.

cards.mean: close enough to talk about anything
cards.lit: there is nothing that is not talked about

use.how: Predicate or attribute describing a close relationship between people: 我们俩无话不谈。 Very often in 无话不谈的朋友.

near.diff: 推心置腹 is sincerely confiding in someone in a given talk; 无话不谈 describes a lasting closeness where any topic is open.
亲密无间 is closeness in general; 无话不谈 is specifically about being able to talk freely about everything.

cards.cue: Two friends from college still tell each other about their jobs, their worries and their love lives, holding nothing back. How would you describe them?

ctx.s: 我和表妹从小一起长大，一直{无话不谈}。
ctx.en: My cousin and I grew up together and have always told each other everything.

ctx.s: 他们是{无话不谈}的好朋友，彼此没有秘密。
ctx.en: They are close friends who share everything; they have no secrets from each other.

ctx.s: “你跟你妈妈关系怎么样？”“挺好的，我们母女俩{无话不谈}。”
ctx.en: "How do you get on with your mum?" "Really well. The two of us can talk about anything."

ctx.s: 刚认识的时候他很少开口，没想到半年后我们竟然{无话不谈}了。
ctx.en: When we first met he hardly spoke; I never expected that half a year later we'd be telling each other everything.

ctx.s: 父母都希望能和孩子{无话不谈}，可到了青春期往往很难做到。
ctx.en: All parents hope to be able to talk with their children about anything, but once the teenage years arrive that is often hard.

ctx.s: 小说里的两个女主角曾经{无话不谈}，后来却因为一场误会形同陌路。
ctx.en: The two heroines of the novel once shared everything, but a misunderstanding later made them like strangers.

bad.s: 他特别爱说话，在会上{无话不谈}。
bad.en: (meant: he is very talkative and talked at length in the meeting)
bad.why: It describes closeness between people who confide in each other, not one person being talkative.

bad.s: 我跟老板{无话不谈}了一个小时工作的事。
bad.en: (meant: I talked with my boss about work for an hour)
bad.why: It describes a relationship, not an act of talking with a duration and a topic; just say you chatted for an hour.

cards.mean: naturally, of its own accord
cards.lit: so of itself, and therefore so

use.how: Adverbial (自然而然地 or 自然而然就 + verb) or 是自然而然的事: something happens without effort or planning, e.g. 时间长了，自然而然就会了。

near.diff: 顺理成章 says a result follows logically from what came before; 自然而然 says it simply happens by itself, without effort or intent.
水到渠成 says success comes once the conditions are ripe; 自然而然 is broader: any change that happens without forcing.

cards.cue: You never took a lesson in the local dialect, but after years of living there you just found yourself speaking it. How did it happen?

ctx.s: 每天听中文歌，我{自然而然}就记住了很多词。
ctx.en: Listening to Chinese songs every day, I just picked up lots of words without trying.

ctx.s: 在一起工作久了，大家{自然而然}地成了朋友。
ctx.en: After working together for a long time, we naturally became friends.

ctx.s: “你是怎么学会做饭的？”“一个人在国外住，{自然而然}就学会了。”
ctx.en: "How did you learn to cook?" "Living alone abroad, I just picked it up."

ctx.s: 孩子看到父母每天读书，{自然而然}也会爱上阅读。
ctx.en: When children see their parents reading every day, they come to love reading too, all by themselves.

ctx.s: 天气一冷，人们{自然而然}地想吃火锅。
ctx.en: As soon as the weather turns cold, people naturally start craving hotpot.

ctx.s: 好习惯一旦养成，做起来就是{自然而然}的事，不再需要意志力。
ctx.en: Once a good habit is formed, doing it comes naturally and no longer takes willpower.

bad.s: 这里的风景很{自然而然}，没有高楼。
bad.en: (meant: the scenery here is very natural, with no tall buildings)
bad.why: It describes how something comes about without effort, not unspoiled nature, and it cannot be used as an adjective after 'very'.

bad.s: 你{自然而然}要来参加我的婚礼啊！
bad.en: (meant: of course you have to come to my wedding!)
bad.why: It does not mean 'of course' or express obligation; it describes a process happening by itself. Use the plain word for 'of course'.

cards.mean: strutting openly, without a care
cards.lit: to sway grandly and swing grandly as one walks

use.how: Adverbial before verbs of walking: 大摇大摆地走进来. Describes someone moving openly and self-importantly where they ought to be careful or ashamed; can be humorous about animals.

near.diff: 趾高气扬 is an arrogant, triumphant bearing in general; 大摇大摆 is the swaggering, unconcerned way someone walks somewhere.
明目张胆 is doing something wrong brazenly; 大摇大摆 pictures the swaggering walk itself.

cards.cue: A shoplifter walks out through the front door, slowly, swinging his arms, as if he owned the place. How does he leave?

ctx.s: 一只猫{大摇大摆}地走进厨房，一点也不怕人。
ctx.en: A cat strolled into the kitchen as if it owned the place, not the least bit afraid of people.

ctx.s: 他迟到了半小时，还{大摇大摆}地走进会议室。
ctx.en: He was half an hour late and still swaggered into the meeting room.

ctx.s: 小偷拿了东西，竟然从正门{大摇大摆}地走了出去。
ctx.en: The thief took the goods and actually strolled out through the front door.

ctx.s: “你看，那个人插了队，还{大摇大摆}地站到最前面去了！”
ctx.en: "Look, that guy jumped the queue and just strutted right up to the front!"

ctx.s: 没买票的人{大摇大摆}地进了场，保安居然没拦。
ctx.en: People without tickets sauntered into the venue, and the guards didn't even stop them.

ctx.s: 几只鸭子{大摇大摆}地横穿马路，司机们只好停车等着。
ctx.en: A few ducks waddled across the road without a care, and the drivers had to stop and wait.

bad.s: 新娘穿着婚纱，{大摇大摆}地走向舞台，非常优雅。
bad.en: (meant: the bride walked gracefully towards the stage)
bad.why: It pictures a swaggering, brazen walk, which clashes with grace and elegance.

bad.s: 他{大摇大摆}地把这件事告诉了大家。
bad.en: (meant: he openly told everyone about it)
bad.why: It describes walking or moving about with a swagger, not saying something openly or publicly.

cards.mean: late at night when all is quiet
cards.lit: the night is deep and people are still

use.how: Time setting at the head of a clause: 夜深人静的时候, 每当夜深人静. Describes the quiet late hours when others are asleep.

near.diff: 万籁俱寂 is total silence at any time and is more literary; 夜深人静 is specifically late at night with everyone asleep.

cards.cue: Everyone in the dorm is asleep and you can hear only the clock ticking; that is when you finally start writing. When do you write?

ctx.s: {夜深人静}的时候，我喜欢一个人听音乐。
ctx.en: Late at night when everything is quiet, I like listening to music on my own.

ctx.s: 每当{夜深人静}，她就会想起远方的家人。
ctx.en: Whenever the night grows late and still, she thinks of her family far away.

ctx.s: “你怎么总是半夜写作？”“{夜深人静}，没人打扰，最容易专心。”
ctx.en: "Why do you always write in the middle of the night?" "Late at night it's quiet and nobody bothers me, so it's easiest to focus."

ctx.s: {夜深人静}时，楼上突然传来一阵敲打声，把我吵醒了。
ctx.en: In the dead of night a sudden banging came from upstairs and woke me up.

ctx.s: 他白天上班，只能等到{夜深人静}才复习功课。
ctx.en: He works during the day, so he can only study once the night is late and quiet.

ctx.s: 小说开头写道：{夜深人静}，村口的老狗忽然叫了起来。
ctx.en: The novel opens: deep in the silent night, the old dog at the village entrance suddenly began to bark.

bad.s: 今天下午图书馆里{夜深人静}，大家都在看书。
bad.en: (meant: the library was very quiet this afternoon)
bad.why: It refers only to the late hours of the night, so it cannot describe a quiet library in the afternoon.

bad.s: 他这个人很{夜深人静}，不爱说话。
bad.en: (meant: he is a quiet person who doesn't talk much)
bad.why: It describes a time of night, not a person's character, and it cannot follow 'very'.

cards.mean: with all one's heart (serving or caring for others)
cards.lit: whole heart, whole mind

use.how: Adverbial before a verb (全心全意地照顾, 全心全意为……服务): someone devotes themselves without reservation to a person or a cause.

near.diff: 一心一意 is single-minded focus on one thing; 全心全意 stresses giving oneself entirely, typically to serving or caring for others.
尽心尽力 stresses doing one's utmost on a task; 全心全意 stresses wholehearted devotion without holding anything back.

cards.cue: A woman has looked after her paralysed father for ten years, putting his needs before everything of her own. How has she cared for him?

ctx.s: 妈妈{全心全意}地照顾生病的外婆。
ctx.en: Mum devotes herself completely to looking after Grandma, who is ill.

ctx.s: 这家小店的老板{全心全意}为顾客着想，所以回头客很多。
ctx.en: The owner of this little shop thinks wholeheartedly of his customers, so lots of them come back.

ctx.s: “你为什么辞职回老家？”“我想{全心全意}陪伴年迈的父母。”
ctx.en: "Why did you quit and move back home?" "I want to devote myself fully to being with my elderly parents."

ctx.s: 他退休后{全心全意}投入到志愿服务中。
ctx.en: After retiring he threw himself wholeheartedly into volunteer work.

ctx.s: 一个好医生应该{全心全意}为病人服务。
ctx.en: A good doctor should serve patients with complete devotion.

ctx.s: 她{全心全意}地爱着这个家，却很少考虑自己。
ctx.en: She loves her family with all her heart, yet seldom thinks of herself.

bad.s: 他{全心全意}地反对这个计划。
bad.en: (meant: he wholeheartedly opposes the plan)
bad.why: It describes devotion to serving or caring for someone, not the strength of an opinion; firm opposition needs a different word.

bad.s: 我{全心全意}了三年，终于考上了大学。
bad.en: (meant: I gave it everything for three years and finally got into university)
bad.why: It is an adverbial that must come before a verb; it cannot stand alone as the verb or be followed by a length of time.

cards.mean: to make irresponsible remarks about others behind their backs
cards.lit: to say three and speak four

use.how: Predicate, often 对某人说三道四 or 别说三道四: criticises careless gossip or judgments about matters that are not the speaker's business.

near.diff: 指手画脚 is bossily telling others what to do; 说三道四 is gossiping about them or passing careless judgment.
议论纷纷 is many people discussing something, not necessarily unfairly; 说三道四 always disapproves of the talk.

cards.cue: The neighbours keep gossiping about why your sister is still single, though it is none of their business. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 别人的家事，你别{说三道四}。
ctx.en: Other people's family matters are not for you to gossip about.

ctx.s: 她离婚以后，邻居们总在背后{说三道四}。
ctx.en: After her divorce, the neighbours kept talking about her behind her back.

ctx.s: “我穿什么是我的自由，轮不到你{说三道四}！”
ctx.en: "What I wear is my own business. It's not your place to pass comment!"

ctx.s: 网上有些人根本不了解情况，就对当事人{说三道四}。
ctx.en: Some people online don't know the facts at all, yet they still pass judgment on the people involved.

ctx.s: 你自己都没做过这份工作，凭什么对我{说三道四}？
ctx.en: You've never even done this job yourself, so what gives you the right to criticise me?

ctx.s: 他做事向来认真，从来不在乎别人{说三道四}。
ctx.en: He has always done things conscientiously and never cares about other people's gossip.

bad.s: 老师在课上{说三道四}，讲得很清楚。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher explained things point by point in class)
bad.why: It criticises irresponsible gossip; it never means explaining things in an orderly way.

bad.s: 他{说三道四}了我一顿。
bad.en: (meant: he gave me a scolding)
bad.why: It is not a direct scolding and takes no object; it is careless talk about someone, not a telling-off aimed at them.

cards.mean: beaming with delight
cards.lit: the eyebrows open out and the eyes smile

use.how: Predicate, complement (乐得眉开眼笑) or adverbial (眉开眼笑地说): happiness clearly visible on someone's face, at good news, a gift or praise.

near.diff: 喜出望外 is joy at unexpected good luck; 眉开眼笑 describes the beaming face, whether the joy was expected or not.
心花怒放 is inner elation; 眉开眼笑 is how happiness shows on the face.

cards.cue: Grandma opens the door and sees all her grandchildren standing there with a birthday cake. What does her face look like?

ctx.s: 收到礼物，小女孩{眉开眼笑}。
ctx.en: When she got the present, the little girl beamed with delight.

ctx.s: 听说下周放假，同学们一个个{眉开眼笑}的。
ctx.en: Hearing there's a holiday next week, every one of the students was all smiles.

ctx.s: 奶奶看到孙子回家，乐得{眉开眼笑}。
ctx.en: When Grandma saw her grandson come home, she lit up with joy.

ctx.s: “什么事这么开心？看你{眉开眼笑}的。”“我拿到奖学金了！”
ctx.en: "What are you so happy about? You're beaming." "I got the scholarship!"

ctx.s: 老板{眉开眼笑}地数着今天的营业额。
ctx.en: The boss, beaming, counted the day's takings.

ctx.s: 一提起他的新车，他就{眉开眼笑}，说个没完。
ctx.en: The moment his new car comes up, his face lights up and he can't stop talking.

bad.s: 这部电影很{眉开眼笑}，大家都看得哈哈大笑。
bad.en: (meant: this film is very funny)
bad.why: It describes a person's beaming face, not a film or anything else that is funny.

bad.s: 他冷冷地{眉开眼笑}了一下。
bad.en: (meant: he gave a cold little smile)
bad.why: It is open, wide delight; it cannot be cold or brief, so 'coldly' and 'for a moment' clash with it.

cards.mean: face streaming with tears
cards.lit: tears flow until they cover the face

use.how: Predicate, complement (看得泪流满面) or adverbial (泪流满面地说): someone cries openly with tears all over the face, from grief, being moved or relief.

near.diff: 热泪盈眶 is eyes brimming with tears, often from being moved; 泪流满面 is tears already streaming down the face.
痛哭流涕 is loud, bitter sobbing, often with regret; 泪流满面 describes the tears on the face and may be silent.

cards.cue: After ten years apart, a mother sees her son at the airport and cannot stop crying; her cheeks are soaked. How does she look?

ctx.s: 看完这封信，她已经{泪流满面}。
ctx.en: By the time she finished the letter, tears were streaming down her face.

ctx.s: 电影最后一幕，很多观众哭得{泪流满面}，纸巾都用完了。
ctx.en: At the last scene of the film, many in the audience cried until tears streamed down their faces and used up all their tissues.

ctx.s: “你怎么哭了？”“没事，听到这首歌，不知怎么就{泪流满面}了。”
ctx.en: "Why are you crying?" "It's nothing. I heard this song and somehow just burst into tears."

ctx.s: 比赛结束的那一刻，队员们抱在一起，哭得{泪流满面}。
ctx.en: The moment the match ended, the players hugged each other and cried until their faces were wet with tears.

ctx.s: 他{泪流满面}地向父母道歉，说再也不这样了。
ctx.en: With tears streaming down his face, he apologised to his parents and promised never to do it again.

ctx.s: 多年后重回故乡，老人站在村口，{泪流满面}，久久说不出话。
ctx.en: Back in his hometown after many years, the old man stood at the edge of the village, tears pouring down his face, unable to speak for a long time.

bad.s: 切洋葱的时候，我的眼睛有点{泪流满面}。
bad.en: (meant: my eyes watered a little while I was cutting onions)
bad.why: It means tears covering the whole face, so it cannot be 'a little' or describe watering eyes.

bad.s: 这个故事很{泪流满面}，你一定要看。
bad.en: (meant: this story is really moving, you must read it)
bad.why: It describes a person crying, not a story that moves people to tears.

cards.mean: too restless to sit or stand still
cards.lit: not at ease whether sitting or standing

use.how: Predicate or complement (急得坐立不安), or 让人坐立不安: restlessness from worry, anxiety or tense waiting.

near.diff: 忐忑不安 is inner nervous uncertainty; 坐立不安 is that worry showing as restlessness, unable to settle anywhere.
心神不宁 is a mind that cannot settle or concentrate; 坐立不安 stresses the restless body.

cards.cue: Your daughter should have been home at ten. It is midnight, her phone is off, and you keep sitting down and jumping up again. How are you?

ctx.s: 孩子还没回家，妈妈急得{坐立不安}。
ctx.en: The child still isn't home, and Mum is so worried she can't sit still.

ctx.s: 等考试成绩的那天晚上，我{坐立不安}，在屋里走来走去。
ctx.en: The night I was waiting for my exam results, I couldn't settle and kept pacing around the room.

ctx.s: “你看你{坐立不安}的，到底出什么事了？”
ctx.en: "Look at you, you can't keep still. What on earth has happened?"

ctx.s: 医生迟迟没有从手术室出来，家属们{坐立不安}。
ctx.en: The doctor still hadn't come out of the operating theatre, and the family were beside themselves with worry.

ctx.s: 老板说下午要找他谈话，这让他整个上午都{坐立不安}。
ctx.en: The boss said he wanted a word with him in the afternoon, which left him restless all morning.

ctx.s: 面试前半小时，她在走廊里{坐立不安}，一遍遍地看笔记。
ctx.en: Half an hour before the interview she couldn't settle in the corridor, reading her notes over and over.

bad.s: 这把椅子太硬了，我坐着{坐立不安}。
bad.en: (meant: the chair was so hard I couldn't sit comfortably)
bad.why: It describes restlessness from worry, not the physical discomfort of a hard chair.

bad.s: 我对这件事很{坐立不安}。
bad.en: (meant: I feel very uneasy about this matter)
bad.why: It cannot take 'very' or an object; make the worry the cause instead: this matter makes me restless.

cards.mean: red in the face (from anger, shame or effort)
cards.lit: the face red and the ears scarlet

use.how: Predicate or complement (吵得面红耳赤, 羞得面红耳赤): a flushed face from a heated argument, embarrassment, nerves or drinking.

near.diff: 脸红脖子粗 is colloquial and mostly about anger in an argument; 面红耳赤 also covers shame, nerves and drinking.

cards.cue: Two old friends argue about football so fiercely that both of them flush bright red to the ears. How did they argue?

ctx.s: 为了一点小事，两个人吵得{面红耳赤}。
ctx.en: The two of them argued over a trifle until they were both red in the face.

ctx.s: 被老师当众批评，他羞得{面红耳赤}。
ctx.en: Criticised by the teacher in front of everyone, he turned red with shame.

ctx.s: “你们俩别争了，都{面红耳赤}的，至于吗？”
ctx.en: "Stop arguing, you two. You're both red in the face. Is it really worth it?"

ctx.s: 她第一次上台演讲，紧张得{面红耳赤}，声音都在发抖。
ctx.en: Giving a speech on stage for the first time, she was so nervous she flushed bright red and her voice shook.

ctx.s: 会上大家为预算问题争得{面红耳赤}，最后也没有结论。
ctx.en: At the meeting everyone argued heatedly over the budget, and in the end they reached no conclusion.

ctx.s: 他才喝了两杯酒就{面红耳赤}了。
ctx.en: He'd had only two glasses and was already red in the face.

bad.s: 这个苹果{面红耳赤}的，看起来很好吃。
bad.en: (meant: this apple is nice and red, it looks delicious)
bad.why: It describes a person's face flushing from emotion, effort or drink; it cannot describe the colour of fruit or objects.

bad.s: 小宝宝的脸蛋{面红耳赤}，真可爱。
bad.en: (meant: the baby's rosy cheeks are so cute)
bad.why: It suggests anger, shame or strain, never a baby's healthy rosy cheeks.

cards.mean: staring fixedly, not taking one's eyes off
cards.lit: the eyeballs do not turn

use.how: Usually adverbial before 地看着 / 地盯着: 他目不转睛地看着屏幕。 Said of someone watching something visible with complete attention.

near.diff: 全神贯注 is full concentration on any task, even listening or working; 目不转睛 is only about the eyes staying fixed on something seen.

cards.cue: At the show the children never once looked away from the magician's hands as he slowly made the coin vanish. How were they watching?

ctx.s: 孩子们{目不转睛}地看着魔术师的手。
ctx.en: The children watched the magician's hands without taking their eyes off them.

ctx.s: 小猫蹲在鱼缸边，{目不转睛}地看着里面游来游去的金鱼。
ctx.en: The kitten crouched by the fish tank, eyes fixed on the goldfish swimming back and forth.

ctx.s: “你怎么一直{目不转睛}地盯着那幅画？”“我觉得它好像在对我笑。”
ctx.en: "Why do you keep staring at that painting?" "It feels like it's smiling at me."

ctx.s: 比赛只剩最后一分钟，全场观众都{目不转睛}地盯着球门，谁也不敢眨眼。
ctx.en: With one minute left in the match, the whole crowd kept their eyes glued to the goal, nobody daring to blink.

ctx.s: 他坐在电视机前{目不转睛}，连饭都忘了吃。
ctx.en: He sat in front of the TV staring at the screen, so absorbed he forgot to eat.

ctx.s: 她{目不转睛}地盯着屏幕，连眼睛都不敢眨，生怕错过自己的名字。
ctx.en: She stared at the screen without daring to blink, afraid of missing her own name.

bad.s: 我{目不转睛}地听着老师讲课。
bad.en: (meant: I listened to the teacher with full attention)
bad.why: It describes the eyes fixed on something seen; for listening attentively a different idiom of concentration is needed.

bad.s: 他学习一向{目不转睛}，所以成绩很好。
bad.en: (meant: he always studies with concentration)
bad.why: It is a moment of fixed staring at a particular sight, not a general habit of diligence.

cards.mean: so arrogant that no one else counts
cards.lit: there is nobody in his eyes

use.how: Predicate or attributive, often with 太 or 变得: 他太目中无人了。 Criticises someone who treats others as if they did not matter.

near.diff: 自以为是 is being sure one is always right; 目中无人 is ignoring and slighting other people altogether.

cards.cue: Since winning the award, the new star of the team ignores the coach, interrupts senior players and greets no one. How is he behaving?

ctx.s: 他考了第一名以后就{目中无人}，见了同学也不打招呼。
ctx.en: After coming first in the exam he became arrogant and doesn't even greet his classmates.

ctx.s: 这个新来的经理太{目中无人}了，跟老员工说话总是一副看不起人的样子。
ctx.en: The new manager is far too arrogant; he always talks down to the long-serving staff.

ctx.s: “别那么{目中无人}，人家跟你说话，你至少看人家一眼。”
ctx.en: "Don't be so arrogant; when someone talks to you, at least look at them."

ctx.s: 球队连赢了几场，有些队员开始{目中无人}，结果输给了一支弱队。
ctx.en: After a string of wins some players got cocky, and the team lost to a weak side.

ctx.s: 她说话的态度那么{目中无人}，难怪大家都不愿意跟她合作。
ctx.en: She talks to people with such disdain that it's no wonder nobody wants to work with her.

ctx.s: 一个人再有本事，也不能{目中无人}，把别人都不放在眼里。
ctx.en: However capable you are, you can't act as if no one else matters and look down on everyone.

bad.s: 他工作的时候非常专心，{目中无人}。
bad.en: (meant: he was so focused he didn't notice anyone around him)
bad.why: It means arrogance toward others, not being too absorbed to notice them.

bad.s: 老师夸我做事{目中无人}，我特别高兴。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher praised me for being independent)
bad.why: It is always a criticism; no teacher would use it as praise.

cards.mean: to whisper to one another
cards.lit: heads come together, mouths reach ears

use.how: Predicate for two or more people physically close, often where they should be quiet: 台下的人开始交头接耳。

near.diff: 窃窃私语 stresses talking secretly in low voices; 交头接耳 pictures people leaning heads together, often in a class, meeting or crowd.

cards.cue: As soon as the manager mentions layoffs, people around the meeting table lean toward their neighbours and start murmuring. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 上课的时候不要{交头接耳}。
ctx.en: Don't whisper to each other during class.

ctx.s: 考试时有两个学生{交头接耳}，被老师警告了。
