ctx.en: Two students whispered to each other during the exam and got a warning from the teacher.

ctx.s: “后排两位同学，你们{交头接耳}的，在说什么呢？”老师停下来问。
ctx.en: "You two in the back row, what are you whispering about?" the teacher stopped to ask.

ctx.s: 经理一宣布要裁员，会议室里的人就开始{交头接耳}。
ctx.en: The moment the manager announced layoffs, people in the meeting room started whispering to one another.

ctx.s: 新娘一出场，客人们纷纷{交头接耳}，夸她今天真漂亮。
ctx.en: When the bride appeared, the guests leaned over to each other, whispering how lovely she looked.

ctx.s: 电影院里，前排两个人一直{交头接耳}，影响了旁边的观众。
ctx.en: In the cinema two people in the front row kept whispering, disturbing everyone near them.

bad.s: 他一个人在房间里{交头接耳}。
bad.en: (meant: he was muttering to himself in his room)
bad.why: It needs at least two people leaning together; one person alone cannot do it.

bad.s: 我们俩在电话里{交头接耳}了一个小时。
bad.en: (meant: we chatted quietly on the phone for an hour)
bad.why: The image is heads physically close; it cannot describe a phone call.

cards.mean: to dance about with joy
cards.lit: the hands dance and the feet stamp

story.text: The Preface to the Book of Songs explains how poetry and dance arise from feeling: what stirs inside comes out as words; when words are not enough, one sighs; when sighing is not enough, one sings; and when singing is not enough, without knowing it the hands begin to dance and the feet to stamp.

use.how: Often after 高兴得 / 乐得, or adverbial with 地: 他高兴得手舞足蹈。 Describes visible, bodily excitement from joy.

near.diff: 欢天喜地 is a general air of great happiness; 手舞足蹈 shows the joy in waving arms and jumping feet.

cards.cue: Your little brother hears you're going to the theme park tomorrow and starts jumping, flapping his arms and spinning round the room. How is he reacting?

ctx.s: 听说明天去游乐园，弟弟高兴得{手舞足蹈}。
ctx.en: Hearing we were going to the theme park tomorrow, my little brother jumped about with joy.

ctx.s: 宝宝听到音乐，在床上{手舞足蹈}，逗得全家人都笑了。
ctx.en: When the baby heard the music she kicked and waved on the bed, making the whole family laugh.

ctx.s: “你看你，{手舞足蹈}的，是不是中奖了？”
ctx.en: "Look at you, bouncing around like that — did you win the lottery?"

ctx.s: 进球了！他在沙发上{手舞足蹈}地大喊大叫。
ctx.en: Goal! He leapt about on the sofa, shouting and waving his arms.

ctx.s: 收到录取通知书那天，她挥着信在厨房里{手舞足蹈}，把妈妈都逗笑了。
ctx.en: The day her acceptance letter came, she waved it about and danced round the kitchen, making her mother laugh.

ctx.s: 他一说起自己喜欢的球队就{手舞足蹈}，兴奋得停不下来。
ctx.en: Whenever he talks about his favourite team he gets so excited his arms and legs never stop moving.

bad.s: 她在舞蹈课上{手舞足蹈}，跳了一支芭蕾。
bad.en: (meant: she danced a ballet in dance class)
bad.why: It is excited, joyful flailing, not actual dancing; for real dancing just use the ordinary verb for dancing.

bad.s: 听说奶奶住院了，他急得{手舞足蹈}。
bad.en: (meant: he was so anxious he couldn't keep still)
bad.why: It expresses joy, not anxiety; for panic or restlessness other idioms are needed.

cards.mean: frank and outspoken by nature
cards.lit: a straight heart and a quick mouth

use.how: Describes a person's temperament, often as an apology or excuse: 我这个人心直口快，你别介意。 Says what one thinks at once, without malice.

near.diff: 直言不讳 is speaking frankly on a particular serious matter; 心直口快 is a personality that blurts out what it thinks.

cards.cue: Your grandmother always says exactly what she thinks the moment she thinks it — like telling you right away that you've put on weight. What kind of person is she?

ctx.s: 我这个人{心直口快}，说错了你别生气。
ctx.en: I'm the type who says what I think; don't be upset if I say something wrong.

ctx.s: 奶奶是个{心直口快}的人，看见我胖了就直接说出来。
ctx.en: Grandma is very outspoken; she saw I'd put on weight and said so straight away.

ctx.s: “他不是故意的，就是{心直口快}，想到什么说什么。”
ctx.en: "He didn't mean it; he's just blunt and says whatever comes into his head."

ctx.s: 她{心直口快}，有什么意见当场就说出来。
ctx.en: She's frank by nature; if she has an objection she voices it on the spot.

ctx.s: 小王{心直口快}，开会时一句话就点破了方案的问题，经理有点尴尬。
ctx.en: Xiao Wang is outspoken; in the meeting he pointed out the plan's flaw in one sentence, and the manager looked awkward.

ctx.s: 跟{心直口快}的朋友相处，至少不用猜他心里在想什么。
ctx.en: With a blunt friend, at least you never have to guess what he's really thinking.

bad.s: 他说话{心直口快}，一分钟能说两百个字。
bad.en: (meant: he talks very fast)
bad.why: The 'quick mouth' is not speech speed; it means saying what one thinks right away and frankly.

bad.s: 他{心直口快}，嘴上说好，心里却不同意。
bad.en: (meant: he agrees outwardly but disagrees inside)
bad.why: It means mouth and heart match; saying yes while disagreeing is the opposite.

cards.mean: fully convinced and accepting defeat
cards.lit: convinced in the heart and conceding with the mouth

use.how: Said by or of the one persuaded or defeated, often after 让…, 输得, 我就: 他讲得有理，我心服口服。

near.diff: 甘拜下风 is a modest admission of losing to a better rival; 心服口服 can also mean being won over by an argument or evidence.

cards.cue: You argued hard that you were right, but your friend calmly showed you the evidence, point by point, and now you have no objection left at all. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 他的解释很有道理，我{心服口服}。
ctx.en: His explanation makes perfect sense; I'm completely convinced.

ctx.s: 这场比赛我们输得{心服口服}，对手确实比我们强。
ctx.en: We lost this match fair and square; our opponents really were better.

ctx.s: “你要是能拿出证据，我就{心服口服}。”
ctx.en: "If you can show me the evidence, I'll admit you're right."

ctx.s: 老师没有批评他，只是把错误一条条讲清楚，让他{心服口服}。
ctx.en: The teacher didn't scold him; she just explained each mistake clearly until he fully accepted it.

ctx.s: 她一个月就把销售额翻了一倍，原来不看好她的人都{心服口服}了。
ctx.en: She doubled sales in a month, and the people who had doubted her were completely won over.

ctx.s: 光靠吓唬是没用的，要让孩子{心服口服}，得跟他讲道理。
ctx.en: Threats don't work; if you want a child to genuinely accept it, you have to reason with him.

bad.s: 老板逼我签字，我只好{心服口服}地签了。
bad.en: (meant: I reluctantly signed because my boss forced me)
bad.why: It means genuine, willing acceptance; giving in under pressure is the opposite.

bad.s: 这次我赢了，所以对结果{心服口服}。
bad.en: (meant: I won, so I'm satisfied with the result)
bad.why: It is said by the side that was persuaded or beaten, not by the winner.

cards.mean: perfectly content and satisfied
cards.lit: the heart is full and the wishes are satisfied

use.how: Adverbial with 地, or predicate often with 就…了: 有这些我就心满意足了。 A calm, complete contentment, not excitement.

near.diff: 心花怒放 is bursting, elated joy; 心满意足 is quiet contentment with nothing more to wish for.

cards.cue: After a big bowl of hot noodles on a cold night, your father leans back on the sofa, pats his stomach and wants nothing more. How does he feel?

ctx.s: 吃了一大碗热面条，他{心满意足}地躺在沙发上。
ctx.en: After a big bowl of hot noodles he lay back on the sofa, perfectly content.

ctx.s: 小猫吃饱了，{心满意足}地舔着爪子。
ctx.en: Its stomach full, the kitten contentedly licked its paws.

ctx.s: 只要每天能睡到自然醒，我就{心满意足}了。
ctx.en: As long as I can sleep until I wake up naturally every day, I'll be perfectly happy.

ctx.s: 孩子拿到了想要的玩具，再也不吵不闹，{心满意足}地跟着妈妈回家了。
ctx.en: Having got the toy he wanted, the child stopped fussing and went home with his mother, completely satisfied.

ctx.s: “就这么一点工资，你就{心满意足}了？”
ctx.en: "With a salary that small, you're already satisfied?"

ctx.s: 老人看着满屋子的儿孙，脸上露出{心满意足}的笑容。
ctx.en: Looking at the room full of children and grandchildren, the old man smiled with deep contentment.

bad.s: 听到中奖的消息，他{心满意足}地跳了起来。
bad.en: (meant: he leapt up with excitement at winning)
bad.why: It is calm contentment; jumping with excitement calls for an idiom of elation.

bad.s: 这件衣服太{心满意足}了，我马上就买了。
bad.en: (meant: this dress was so satisfying that I bought it at once)
bad.why: It describes how a person feels, not a thing that pleases; a dress cannot be content.

cards.mean: on a sudden whim
cards.lit: the heart's blood rises like a tide

story.text: In the Ming novel Investiture of the Gods, the immortals have a sign of coming events: when their heart's blood suddenly surges like a rising tide, they know something has happened in the world and work out by divination what it is. In everyday use the phrase came to mean a sudden impulse to do something.

use.how: Predicate or after 一时 / 全凭: 他一时心血来潮，报了个舞蹈班。 For an impulsive decision, often with light mockery.

near.diff: 突发奇想 stresses a strange, original idea popping up; 心血来潮 stresses acting on a sudden impulse, often without thought.

cards.cue: For no reason at all, your flatmate decided at midnight to dye her hair purple, and by morning it was done. Why did she do it?

ctx.s: 他{心血来潮}，半夜跑到楼下去跑步。
ctx.en: On a sudden whim he went downstairs in the middle of the night to go running.

ctx.s: 周末我{心血来潮}，把头发染成了紫色。
ctx.en: At the weekend I had a sudden urge and dyed my hair purple.

ctx.s: “你怎么突然要学钢琴？”“没什么，就是{心血来潮}。”
ctx.en: "Why do you suddenly want to learn the piano?" "No reason, it's just a whim."

ctx.s: 她做事全凭{心血来潮}，今天想开店，明天又想出国。
ctx.en: She does everything on impulse: today she wants to open a shop, tomorrow to move abroad.

ctx.s: 老板一时{心血来潮}改了方案，全组人只好加班重做。
ctx.en: The boss changed the plan on a whim, and the whole team had to work overtime redoing it.

ctx.s: 学外语不能靠一时的{心血来潮}，得每天坚持。
ctx.en: You can't learn a language on a passing impulse; you have to keep at it every day.

bad.s: 经过三个月的认真考虑，他{心血来潮}，决定换工作。
bad.en: (meant: after careful thought he decided to change jobs)
bad.why: It means a sudden, unconsidered impulse; months of careful thought contradict it.

bad.s: 听到这个坏消息，他{心血来潮}，气得说不出话。
bad.en: (meant: his blood boiled with anger)
bad.why: Despite the blood image it has nothing to do with anger; it means a sudden whim.

cards.mean: to have a fair idea of how things stand
cards.lit: there are figures in one's heart

use.how: Predicate, often 对…心中有数 or 做到心中有数: 这件事我心中有数。 Having a clear enough grasp of a situation to handle it.

near.diff: 胸有成竹 is having a ready plan and full confidence of success; 心中有数 is simply knowing roughly where things stand.

cards.cue: Before renovating, you add up the cost of every item so that you know roughly where the money will go and won't be caught out. What have you achieved?

ctx.s: 这件事大概是什么情况，我{心中有数}，你放心吧。
ctx.en: I have a fair idea of how this matter stands; don't worry.

ctx.s: 考试前把重点都复习一遍，就能{心中有数}了。
ctx.en: Go over the key points before the exam and you'll know where you stand.

ctx.s: “预算还剩多少，你{心中有数}吗？”
ctx.en: "Do you have a clear idea of how much budget is left?"

ctx.s: 装修前要把每一项花费都算清楚，做到{心中有数}。
ctx.en: Before renovating, work out every expense so you know exactly where things stand.

ctx.s: 老医生看了片子，{心中有数}，没多说就开了药。
ctx.en: The old doctor looked at the scan, knew what he was dealing with, and wrote a prescription without saying much.

ctx.s: 比赛还剩十分钟，教练看了看比分，对最后怎么打已经{心中有数}。
ctx.en: With ten minutes left, the coach glanced at the score and already had a clear idea of how to play the rest.

bad.s: 他{心中有数}，算术特别好。
bad.en: (meant: he is good at mental arithmetic)
bad.why: The 'figures' here are not maths; it means a clear grasp of a situation.

bad.s: 我对她{心中有数}，想跟她表白。
bad.en: (meant: I have feelings for her)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with affection; it means knowing how matters stand.

cards.mean: to know full well without saying it
cards.lit: the heart knows and the belly is clear

use.how: Predicate, often with 大家 / 都 / 自己: 谁对谁错，大家心知肚明。 For an awkward truth that is understood but left unspoken.

near.diff: 心照不宣 is two sides tacitly agreeing not to mention something; 心知肚明 is simply knowing it full well, even one person alone.

cards.cue: Your friend pretends to have no idea why you're upset with him, but you're sure he knows perfectly well and just won't admit it. What do you tell him?

ctx.s: 谁对谁错，大家都{心知肚明}。
ctx.en: Who was right and who was wrong — everyone knows perfectly well.

ctx.s: “你别装了，为什么生气你自己{心知肚明}。”
ctx.en: "Stop pretending; you know full well why I'm angry."

ctx.s: 他为什么突然请假，我{心知肚明}，只是不想说破。
ctx.en: I know perfectly well why he suddenly took leave; I just don't want to say it.

ctx.s: 这份礼物送得这么贵重，到底是什么意思，她{心知肚明}。
ctx.en: A gift that expensive — she knew perfectly well what it meant.

ctx.s: 价格明显偏高，顾客其实{心知肚明}，只是图个方便。
ctx.en: Customers know full well the prices are too high; they just pay for the convenience.

ctx.s: 经理嘴上说一切正常，其实他自己{心知肚明}，这个项目已经保不住了。
ctx.en: The manager says all is fine, but he knows full well the project can't be saved.

bad.s: 老师讲了两遍，我现在终于{心知肚明}了。
bad.en: (meant: after two explanations I finally understand)
bad.why: It is not about understanding a lesson; it means knowing an unspoken truth full well.

bad.s: 他{心知肚明}地向大家宣布了真相。
bad.en: (meant: he announced the truth to everyone)
bad.why: It is knowing without saying; announcing the truth contradicts it.

cards.mean: as if nothing had happened
cards.lit: as if there were no such matter

use.how: Mostly adverbial (若无其事地走开) or after 装作/表现得. Describes a person acting calm and normal after something that should affect them.

near.diff: 满不在乎 is genuinely not caring at all; 若无其事 is outward calm, often hiding what one feels or what one has done.

cards.cue: Your roommate broke your favourite mug, dropped the pieces in the bin and sat down to dinner chatting normally. How did they act?

ctx.s: 他打碎了杯子，怕被妈妈发现，就{若无其事}地继续看电视。
ctx.en: He broke the cup and, afraid Mum would find out, carried on watching TV as if nothing had happened.

ctx.s: 被老板批评后，她眼圈都红了，却还是{若无其事}地回到座位上工作。
ctx.en: After being told off by the boss her eyes were red, yet she went back to her desk and worked as if nothing had happened.

ctx.s: 你们昨天吵得那么凶，你今天怎么还能{若无其事}地跟他打招呼？
ctx.en: You two had such a big fight yesterday. How can you say hello to him today as if nothing happened?

ctx.s: “别担心，见到他我会装作{若无其事}的样子。”
ctx.en: "Don't worry, when I see him I'll act as if nothing has happened."

ctx.s: 明明心里很难过，她却表现得{若无其事}，还笑着安慰大家。
ctx.en: She was clearly hurting inside, yet she acted as if nothing was wrong and even smiled and comforted everyone.

ctx.s: 小偷把钱包塞进口袋，然后{若无其事}地走出了商店。
ctx.en: The thief slipped the wallet into his pocket and strolled out of the shop as if nothing had happened.

bad.s: 这里很安全，{若无其事}，你放心吧。
bad.en: (meant: it's safe here, nothing will happen, don't worry)
bad.why: It describes a person's calm manner after something happened, not a place or situation where nothing happens.

bad.s: 听说自己中了大奖，他激动得{若无其事}。
bad.en: (meant: hearing he had won the big prize, he was beside himself with excitement)
bad.why: It means looking calm and unaffected, so it cannot describe someone overcome with excitement.

cards.mean: both just as bad as each other; six of one, half a dozen of the other
cards.lit: half a jin and eight liang: in the old system a jin had sixteen liang, so both weigh the same

use.how: Predicate after two people or things compared: 你们俩半斤八两。 Says neither is better, usually that both are equally poor.

near.diff: 不相上下 is a neutral or admiring 'evenly matched'; 半斤八两 implies both are equally bad and is mocking.

cards.cue: Two brothers each blame the other for their messy room, but both are equally untidy. What do you tell them about each other?

ctx.s: 你们俩的字都写得不好看，{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: Neither of you has nice handwriting; you're as bad as each other.

ctx.s: 别笑他了，你的英语跟他{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: Stop laughing at him; your English is no better than his.

ctx.s: 这两家餐厅服务都很差，{半斤八两}，去哪家都一样。
ctx.en: Both restaurants have terrible service; there's nothing to choose between them, so either one will do.

ctx.s: “你说哥哥懒？你们俩{半斤八两}！”妈妈说。
ctx.en: "You say your brother is lazy? You're just as bad as each other!" said Mum.

ctx.s: 两个候选人都没什么经验，说起来是{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: Neither candidate has much experience; really, it's six of one and half a dozen of the other.

ctx.s: 这场比赛踢得太难看了，两个队谁也别笑谁，{半斤八两}。
ctx.en: It was an awful match; neither team can laugh at the other, they were as bad as each other.

bad.s: 两位钢琴家都弹得非常精彩，真是{半斤八两}。
bad.en: (meant: both pianists were brilliant and evenly matched)
bad.why: It mocks two parties as equally bad; it cannot praise two people as equally excellent.

bad.s: 这件衣服{半斤八两}，不贵也不便宜。
bad.en: (meant: this garment is so-so, average)
bad.why: It compares two parties with each other; it does not describe one thing as mediocre.

cards.mean: homeless, with nowhere to go
cards.lit: to have no home one can return to

use.how: Attributive (无家可归的人) or predicate, often after 让/使: 大火让很多人无家可归。 Said of people or animals with no home at all.

cards.cue: After the flood washed their houses away, the villagers had no roof over their heads and nowhere to go. What had they become?

ctx.s: 冬天到了，城里有一些{无家可归}的人需要帮助。
ctx.en: Winter has come, and there are homeless people in the city who need help.

ctx.s: 这家收容所专门照顾{无家可归}的猫和狗。
ctx.en: This shelter specialises in looking after homeless cats and dogs.

ctx.s: 志愿者每周给{无家可归}的老人送饭。
ctx.en: Volunteers bring meals every week to elderly people who have no home.

ctx.s: 他被房东赶了出去，一时{无家可归}，只好住在朋友家。
ctx.en: His landlord threw him out, and with nowhere to live for the moment he had to stay at a friend's.

ctx.s: 这场大火让几十户人家{无家可归}。
ctx.en: The fire left dozens of families homeless.

ctx.s: 小说讲的是一个{无家可归}的孩子在大城市里长大的故事。
ctx.en: The novel tells the story of a homeless child growing up in a big city.

bad.s: 我今天加班，{无家可归}，晚上很晚才回去。
bad.en: (meant: I'm working late and won't get home until late)
bad.why: It means having no home at all, not being away from home for a while.

bad.s: 家人都在南方，他一个人在北京，很{无家可归}。
bad.en: (meant: he is homesick and lonely)
bad.why: It means literally having no home, not a feeling of missing home, and cannot be graded with 'very'.

cards.mean: vanished without a trace
cards.lit: no shadow and no footprint

use.how: Usually a complement: 消失得/跑得/逃得无影无踪, or a predicate. Said of people, things or feelings that disappear completely.

near.diff: 一干二净 is doing something completely (forgot, ate, cleaned); 无影无踪 is something vanishing from sight with no trace left.
烟消云散 is mostly worries, anger or doubts melting away; 无影无踪 is mainly people or things vanishing from sight.

cards.cue: You put your phone on the café table, turned to order, and when you looked back it was simply gone, not a sign of it anywhere. What happened to it?

ctx.s: 我一转身，小猫就跑得{无影无踪}了。
ctx.en: The moment I turned around, the kitten had run off and vanished.

ctx.s: 太阳一出来，雾就消失得{无影无踪}。
ctx.en: As soon as the sun came out, the fog disappeared without a trace.

ctx.s: 刚才还在桌上的钥匙，怎么一下子就{无影无踪}了？
ctx.en: The keys were on the table just now; how have they vanished just like that?

ctx.s: 他借了钱以后就{无影无踪}，电话也打不通。
ctx.en: After borrowing the money he vanished without a trace, and his phone can't be reached.

ctx.s: 那艘小船越漂越远，最后在海面上消失得{无影无踪}。
ctx.en: The little boat drifted further and further away until it vanished without a trace on the sea.

ctx.s: 警察赶到时，那个骗子早已逃得{无影无踪}。
ctx.en: By the time the police arrived, the con man had long since disappeared without a trace.

bad.s: 这个房间{无影无踪}，什么家具都没有。
bad.en: (meant: this room is empty, there's no furniture)
bad.why: It says something has disappeared; it does not describe a place as empty.

bad.s: 他是个{无影无踪}的人，很少说话。
bad.en: (meant: he is a quiet, low-profile person)
bad.why: It is not a personality trait; it describes a disappearance.

cards.mean: quietly, without a word to anyone
cards.lit: no voice and no sound

use.how: Mostly adverbial: 不声不响地走了/做完了. Said of a person doing something quietly without telling or disturbing anyone.

near.diff: 不辞而别 is only leaving without saying goodbye; 不声不响 is doing anything quietly without announcing it.

cards.cue: Your colleague never mentioned it, then one day you learn she had quietly finished a master's degree at night. How did she do it?

ctx.s: 他{不声不响}地走进教室，坐在最后一排。
ctx.en: He slipped quietly into the classroom and sat in the back row.

ctx.s: 吃完饭，她{不声不响}地把大家的碗都洗了。
ctx.en: After the meal, she quietly washed everyone's bowls without a word.

ctx.s: 你怎么{不声不响}就辞职了？连我都不知道。
ctx.en: How could you just quit without telling anyone? Even I didn't know.

ctx.s: 平时{不声不响}的小李，这次竟然拿了全公司第一名。
ctx.en: Xiao Li, who usually keeps so quiet, actually came first in the whole company this time.

ctx.s: 这家小店{不声不响}地开了二十年，回头客特别多。
ctx.en: This little shop has quietly been open for twenty years and has lots of regulars.

ctx.s: 他{不声不响}地准备了一个生日惊喜，让女朋友感动得哭了。
ctx.en: He quietly prepared a birthday surprise that moved his girlfriend to tears.

bad.s: 图书馆里很{不声不响}，大家都在看书。
bad.en: (meant: the library is quiet, everyone is reading)
bad.why: It describes a person acting without a word to anyone, not a place being quiet.

bad.s: 听到这个噩耗，她{不声不响}地大哭起来。
bad.en: (meant: hearing the terrible news, she burst out sobbing)
bad.why: Loud sobbing contradicts it; it means making no sound and saying nothing.

cards.mean: ungrateful, not knowing what is good for one
cards.lit: not to know good from bad

use.how: Predicate, often 真不知好歹 or 别不知好歹. Reproaches someone who rejects or resents kindness or good advice.

near.diff: 恩将仇报 is actively harming a benefactor; 不知好歹 is failing to appreciate kindness, refusing or resenting it.

cards.cue: You stayed up late helping a friend fix his CV, and all he did was complain that you changed too much. What do you call him?

ctx.s: 我好心提醒你，你还生我的气，真是{不知好歹}！
ctx.en: I warned you out of kindness and you're angry with me? You really don't know what's good for you!

ctx.s: 别{不知好歹}了，老师批评你是为你好。
ctx.en: Don't be so ungrateful; the teacher criticised you for your own good.

ctx.s: “我请你吃饭，你还挑三拣四，怎么这么{不知好歹}？”
ctx.en: "I'm treating you to dinner and you're still picky? How can you be so ungrateful?"

ctx.s: 妈妈给他找了份好工作，他却嫌累不去，亲戚们都说他{不知好歹}。
ctx.en: His mother found him a good job, but he wouldn't go because it was tiring, and the relatives all said he didn't know what was good for him.

ctx.s: 他扶起摔倒的醉汉，那人却骂他多管闲事，真{不知好歹}。
ctx.en: He helped up a drunk who had fallen, and the man swore at him for meddling. How ungrateful.

ctx.s: 故事里，老仆人好心劝告少爷，那个{不知好歹}的少爷却把他骂了一顿。
ctx.en: In the story, the old servant gave the young master well-meant advice, and the ungrateful young master just gave him a scolding.

bad.s: 这孩子还小，{不知好歹}，分不清哪种蘑菇有毒。
bad.en: (meant: the child is too young to tell which mushrooms are poisonous)
bad.why: It reproaches someone for rejecting kindness, not an innocent inability to tell things apart.

bad.s: 这道题太难了，我{不知好歹}，不会做。
bad.en: (meant: this question is too hard, I don't know the answer)
bad.why: It is not about lacking knowledge; it is a reproach for ingratitude.

cards.mean: involuntarily, without meaning to
cards.lit: not up to one's own control

use.how: Adverbial before a verb: 不由自主地笑了/往后退. Says a movement or reaction happened on its own, before the person decided anything.

near.diff: 情不自禁 is a feeling welling up (joy, tears); 不由自主 covers any involuntary action, including bodily reflexes.
身不由己 is being forced by circumstances or others; 不由自主 is an automatic, unwilled reaction.

cards.cue: The bus braked hard and, before you could think, your whole body lurched forward. How did you move?

ctx.s: 一紧张，我就{不由自主}地咬指甲。
ctx.en: Whenever I get nervous, I bite my nails without meaning to.

ctx.s: 车突然刹住，大家都{不由自主}地往前一冲。
ctx.en: The bus braked suddenly and everyone lurched forward involuntarily.

ctx.s: 看到那条大狗，他{不由自主}地往后退了一步。
ctx.en: When he saw the big dog, he stepped back without thinking.

ctx.s: 冷风一吹，他{不由自主}地打了个哆嗦。
ctx.en: When the cold wind blew, he shivered involuntarily.

ctx.s: 听到有人叫自己的名字，他{不由自主}地回过头去。
ctx.en: Hearing someone call his name, he turned his head without thinking.

ctx.s: 他说话的时候，总是{不由自主}地摸鼻子。
ctx.en: When he talks, he always touches his nose without realising it.

bad.s: 我{不由自主}地报名参加了这个比赛。
bad.en: (meant: I signed up for the contest on my own initiative)
bad.why: It means involuntary, not 'by my own choice'; a deliberate decision is the opposite.

bad.s: 他的工作很{不由自主}，老板说什么他就做什么。
bad.en: (meant: he has no freedom at work, he does whatever the boss says)
bad.why: It describes a reflex action, not a lack of freedom at work, and cannot be graded with 'very'.

cards.mean: too many to count
cards.lit: its number cannot be counted

use.how: Usually a predicate after the thing counted: 游客不计其数。 Also 多得不计其数. Says a number is far too large to count.

near.diff: 成千上万 gives a scale, thousands upon thousands, and sits before a noun; 不计其数 says the number is beyond counting and usually follows it.

cards.cue: Asked how many fan letters the old singer received over his career, his manager just laughed: nobody could ever have counted them. How many?

ctx.s: 夏天的夜空里，星星{不计其数}。
ctx.en: In the summer night sky there are countless stars.

ctx.s: 这些年他帮助过的学生{不计其数}。
ctx.en: Over the years he has helped more students than anyone could count.

ctx.s: 春节期间，回家的旅客{不计其数}。
ctx.en: During the Spring Festival, countless travellers head home.

ctx.s: 网上关于减肥的文章{不计其数}，可真正有用的没几篇。
ctx.en: There are countless articles online about losing weight, but hardly any are actually useful.

ctx.s: 这家博物馆收藏的古书多得{不计其数}。
ctx.en: This museum holds more old books than can be counted.

ctx.s: 他说过的谎话{不计其数}，谁还会相信他？
ctx.en: He has told countless lies. Who would believe him now?

bad.s: 我们班的学生{不计其数}，一共三十个。
bad.en: (meant: our class has lots of students, thirty in all)
bad.why: Thirty is easily counted; it is only for numbers too large to count.

bad.s: 他{不计其数}地喜欢这本书。
bad.en: (meant: he likes this book enormously)
bad.why: It describes how many things there are; it is not an intensifier for feelings.

cards.mean: just as expected
cards.lit: not going beyond what was predicted

use.how: Usually at the start of a clause (不出所料，他又迟到了) or after 果然. Says something that has happened matched a prediction.

near.diff: 出乎意料 is the opposite: the outcome was a surprise.

cards.cue: Everyone guessed the lazy team member would miss the deadline, and on Friday he did exactly that. How do you begin telling the story?

ctx.s: {不出所料}，他又迟到了。
ctx.en: Just as expected, he was late again.

ctx.s: 天气预报说今天有雨，{不出所料}，下午就下起了大雨。
ctx.en: The forecast said rain, and sure enough, it poured in the afternoon.

ctx.s: 他平时从不复习，这次考试{不出所料}没及格。
ctx.en: He never revises, so predictably he failed the exam this time.

ctx.s: “我就知道他会答应，果然{不出所料}！”
ctx.en: "I knew he would say yes, and that's exactly what happened!"

ctx.s: 比赛结果{不出所料}，冠军还是去年那支队。
ctx.en: The result was as expected: the champions were the same team as last year.

ctx.s: 公司宣布涨工资后，{不出所料}，辞职的人少了很多。
ctx.en: After the company announced a pay rise, as everyone expected, far fewer people quit.

bad.s: 我没想到他会来，真是{不出所料}！
bad.en: (meant: I never thought he would come, what a surprise!)
bad.why: It means things went exactly as predicted, so it cannot express surprise.

bad.s: 明天考什么还{不出所料}，我心里没底。
bad.en: (meant: tomorrow's exam is unpredictable, I'm not sure)
bad.why: It confirms an outcome that has already happened as predicted; it does not mean unpredictable.

cards.mean: to talk on and on in a flood of words
cards.lit: surging like a flood that never stops

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 他滔滔不绝地讲着. Said of a fluent, unbroken stream of talk, neutral or admiring.

near.diff: 喋喋不休 is annoying, petty chatter and always critical; 滔滔不绝 is a fluent stream of words, often neutral or admiring.

cards.cue: Ask your uncle one question about his fishing trip and he talks for forty minutes without pausing for breath. How does he talk?

ctx.s: 一说到足球，他就{滔滔不绝}。
ctx.en: Once he starts on football, he talks on and on.

ctx.s: 两个老同学见了面，{滔滔不绝}地聊到半夜。
ctx.en: When the two old classmates met, they talked nonstop until midnight.

ctx.s: 你平时说话{滔滔不绝}，怎么面试时一句话都说不出来？
ctx.en: You normally talk a mile a minute. How come you couldn't get a word out in the interview?

ctx.s: 会上他{滔滔不绝}地讲了一个小时，各种数据张口就来。
ctx.en: At the meeting he spoke fluently for an hour, reeling off figures without a pause.

ctx.s: 记者只问了一个问题，他就{滔滔不绝}地回答了十几分钟。
ctx.en: The reporter asked just one question, and he answered in a flood of words for over ten minutes.

ctx.s: 老教授{滔滔不绝}地讲着古城的历史，学生们听得入了迷。
ctx.en: The old professor spoke at length about the ancient city's history, and the students listened spellbound.

bad.s: 我病了一个星期，咳嗽{滔滔不绝}。
bad.en: (meant: I've been ill for a week and can't stop coughing)
bad.why: It is only used for a flood of spoken words, not for coughing or other noises.

bad.s: 他{滔滔不绝}地说了一句“谢谢”。
bad.en: (meant: he said 'thank you')
bad.why: A single short phrase contradicts it; it describes a long, unbroken stream of talk.

cards.mean: a smooth, persuasive talker
cards.lit: able to speak and good at talking

use.how: Describes a person, as a predicate or before 的: 她很能说会道。 Usually admiring, sometimes hinting the talk outruns the substance.

near.diff: 花言巧语 is the deceptive talk itself and always criticises; 能说会道 describes a person's skill with words and is often praise.
口若悬河 is more literary and pictures a long, unstoppable flow of speech; 能说会道 is everyday and stresses persuasiveness.

cards.cue: Your cousin always has the right words ready and can talk a shop owner into a discount. How do you describe her?

ctx.s: 她从小就{能说会道}，大人都说她长大能当律师。
ctx.en: She has had a way with words since she was little; the adults all say she could become a lawyer.

ctx.s: 我们需要一个{能说会道}的人去跟客户谈。
ctx.en: We need someone who can really talk to go and negotiate with the client.

ctx.s: 别看他平时不爱说话，到了谈判桌上却特别{能说会道}。
ctx.en: He may not say much normally, but at the negotiating table he is a real talker.

ctx.s: 你这么{能说会道}，怎么不去做销售？
ctx.en: You're so persuasive, why don't you go into sales?

ctx.s: 那个推销员{能说会道}，没几分钟就让我妈买了一台净水器。
ctx.en: The salesman was such a smooth talker that within minutes he had my mum buying a water purifier.

ctx.s: 光{能说会道}没用，客户最后看的还是产品质量。
ctx.en: Being a good talker isn't enough; in the end the customer looks at the quality of the product.

bad.s: 这位科学家的论文写得{能说会道}。
bad.en: (meant: the scientist's paper is well written)
bad.why: It describes a person's skill in speaking, not the quality of a piece of writing.

bad.s: 他{能说会道}了三种外语。
bad.en: (meant: he can speak three foreign languages)
bad.why: It is not about knowing languages and cannot take an object; it describes being persuasive and fluent with words.

cards.mean: bold and confident, sure one is in the right
cards.lit: the reasoning is straight, so the spirit is strong

use.how: Mostly an adverbial with 地 before a verb of speaking or demanding: 理直气壮地说. Often used ironically of someone who is in fact in the wrong.

near.diff: 心安理得 is an inner feeling of being at peace with what one did; 理直气壮 is the bold, outward way one speaks or acts in a dispute.

cards.cue: You were overcharged and have the receipt to prove it. How should you go back to the shop and complain?

ctx.s: 这件事你没做错，可以{理直气壮}地跟他说。
ctx.en: You did nothing wrong here, so you can tell him so with your head held high.

ctx.s: 既然发票齐全，财务再拖，你就{理直气壮}地去问他们要。
ctx.en: Since all your receipts are in order, if the accounts office keeps stalling, go and demand the money from them with your head held high.

ctx.s: 店员说不能退货，她拿出购物小票，{理直气壮}地要求店长出来解释。
ctx.en: When the assistant refused a refund, she produced her receipt and firmly demanded that the manager come and explain.

ctx.s: 孩子被冤枉了，回答老师的时候声音不大，却很{理直气壮}。
ctx.en: The child had been wrongly accused; answering the teacher, he spoke quietly but with complete conviction.

ctx.s: 他迟到了一个小时，还{理直气壮}地怪我没提醒他。
ctx.en: He was an hour late and still had the nerve to blame me for not reminding him.

ctx.s: 钱是你借的，你凭什么说得这么{理直气壮}？
ctx.en: You're the one who borrowed the money; what gives you the right to sound so sure of yourself?

bad.s: 他在比赛中{理直气壮}，跑得特别快。
bad.en: (meant: he was full of energy in the race and ran fast)
bad.why: It is about the confidence of being in the right in a dispute, not physical energy or strength.

bad.s: 她第一次上台演讲，非常{理直气壮}，一点也不紧张。
bad.en: (meant: she was confident and relaxed in her first speech)
bad.why: It needs a question of right and wrong; calm confidence on stage is simply being self-assured, not this.

cards.mean: smooth, deceptive talk
cards.lit: flowery words and clever speech

story.text: Confucius warned in the Analects that clever words and an ingratiating face are seldom found with true goodness. Explaining that line to his students, the Song-dynasty scholar Zhu Xi said that such clever words are what people of his own day called by this phrase, an early record of the phrase often cited by dictionaries.

use.how: Used as a noun, often as the object of 听, 信, 用 or 被…骗: 别信他的花言巧语。 Always implies the words are meant to deceive.

near.diff: 甜言蜜语 is sweet, flattering talk, often between lovers and not always dishonest; 花言巧语 stresses that the fine words are a trick.
能说会道 describes a person who speaks well and can be praise; 花言巧语 is the deceitful talk itself and is always negative.

cards.cue: A stranger on the phone promises your grandmother huge returns if she transfers her savings today. What is she hearing?

ctx.s: 别信他的{花言巧语}，他上次也是这么说的。
ctx.en: Don't believe his fine talk; he said exactly the same thing last time.

ctx.s: 骗子用一番{花言巧语}，骗走了老人一辈子的积蓄。
ctx.en: With a stream of smooth lies, the con man cheated the old man out of his life savings.

ctx.s: 她早就看穿了那个推销员的{花言巧语}。
ctx.en: She saw through the salesman's slick patter long ago.

ctx.s: 你以为编几句{花言巧语}就能骗我把钱借给你吗？
ctx.en: Do you think a few made-up smooth words will trick me into lending you money?

ctx.s: 网上那些稳赚不赔的投资广告，全靠{花言巧语}吸引人。
ctx.en: Those online ads for no-risk investments draw people in with nothing but clever talk.

ctx.s: 法官没有被他的{花言巧语}打动，还是判他赔偿全部损失。
ctx.en: The judge was not swayed by his glib words and still ordered him to pay for all the losses.

bad.s: 老师的讲解{花言巧语}，我们都听懂了。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher's explanation was vivid and we all understood)
bad.why: It is always a criticism of deceptive talk, never praise for a lively or clear explanation.

bad.s: 他写给我的生日祝福全是{花言巧语}，我感动得哭了。
bad.en: (meant: his birthday message was full of beautiful words and moved me to tears)
bad.why: Using it says the words are insincere tricks, which contradicts being genuinely moved.

cards.mean: hesitant, hemming and hawing
cards.lit: swallowing and spitting out, again and again: words that keep getting stuck

use.how: Describes how someone speaks, as an adverbial or predicate: 吞吞吐吐地说, 说话吞吞吐吐. Implies they are reluctant or afraid to say something.

near.diff: 支支吾吾 is mumbling to dodge a question; 吞吞吐吐 is more general hesitation over something hard to say.
拐弯抹角 is talking fluently but indirectly; 吞吞吐吐 is halting, broken speech.

cards.cue: Your friend keeps starting a sentence, stopping and looking away, clearly afraid to tell you something. How is she talking?

ctx.s: 你别{吞吞吐吐}的，一句话断了好几次，到底想说什么？
ctx.en: Stop hemming and hawing; you have broken off that sentence several times. What are you trying to say?

ctx.s: 问他昨晚去哪儿了，他{吞吞吐吐}地说不清楚。
ctx.en: When asked where he went last night, he hesitated and couldn't give a straight answer.

ctx.s: 她{吞吞吐吐}了半天，才说出想借钱的事。
ctx.en: She hesitated for ages before finally saying she wanted to borrow money.

ctx.s: 你今天说话怎么{吞吞吐吐}的，是不是出什么事了？
ctx.en: Why are you so hesitant when you talk today? Has something happened?

ctx.s: 面试官一问到离职原因，他就变得{吞吞吐吐}起来。
ctx.en: As soon as the interviewer asked why he left his last job, he started to falter.

ctx.s: 医生说话有点{吞吞吐吐}，我心里一下子紧张了。
ctx.en: The doctor seemed reluctant to get the words out, and I suddenly felt nervous.

bad.s: 这台旧打印机{吞吞吐吐}，一张纸要印好久。
bad.en: (meant: the old printer is slow)
bad.why: It describes a person's hesitant speech, not a slow machine.

bad.s: 他吃饭{吞吞吐吐}，一碗面吃了半小时。
bad.en: (meant: he eats slowly)
bad.why: Despite the literal image of swallowing, it is only used about speaking, never about eating.

cards.mean: everyone is discussing it
cards.lit: discussion coming thick and fast from all sides

use.how: A predicate with a plural subject (大家, 人们, 网友们) reacting to some event: 消息传开后，大家议论纷纷。 Also 引得…议论纷纷.

near.diff: 七嘴八舌 is a group all talking at once in one noisy moment; 议论纷纷 is many people commenting on an event, often with differing views.
满城风雨 is a scandal that the whole town knows about; 议论纷纷 is simply widespread discussion and need not be scandalous.

cards.cue: The company suddenly announces a new boss, and for days the staff talk about little else in the corridors and group chats. How do you describe them?

ctx.s: 公司突然换了总经理，员工们{议论纷纷}。
ctx.en: The company suddenly changed its general manager, and the staff were all talking about it.

ctx.s: 这条新闻一发出来，网友们{议论纷纷}。
ctx.en: As soon as the news came out, people online were all discussing it.

ctx.s: 比赛结果公布后，观众{议论纷纷}，觉得裁判不公平。
ctx.en: After the result was announced, the audience was abuzz, many feeling the referee had been unfair.

ctx.s: 这几天小区里{议论纷纷}的，到底发生了什么事？
ctx.en: The whole estate has been abuzz for days; what on earth has happened?

ctx.s: 关于学校要不要取消午休，家长们{议论纷纷}，意见很不一致。
ctx.en: Parents are debating whether the school should drop the midday rest, and opinions are sharply divided.

ctx.s: 他俩突然一起出现在婚礼上，引得亲戚们{议论纷纷}。
ctx.en: The two of them suddenly turning up at the wedding together set the relatives talking.

bad.s: 我一个人在房间里{议论纷纷}。
bad.en: (meant: I was alone in my room thinking it over)
bad.why: It needs many people talking among themselves; one person alone cannot be said to do this.

bad.s: 老师上课讲得{议论纷纷}，很有意思。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher's lecture was lively)
bad.why: It describes many people discussing an event, not the style of one speaker.

cards.mean: left speechless, with no answer
cards.lit: a mouth gone mute, without a word

use.how: A predicate or result complement, usually after being challenged or refuted: 被问得哑口无言, 说得他哑口无言. About having no reply, not about awe.

near.diff: 张口结舌 is being tongue-tied from shock or nerves; 哑口无言 is having no answer to an argument or question.

cards.cue: In an argument, your brother is shown the bank statement proving he spent the money, and he has nothing left to say. How is he?

ctx.s: 她一句话就把他问得{哑口无言}。
ctx.en: With one question she left him without an answer.

ctx.s: 证据摆在面前，他{哑口无言}。
ctx.en: With the evidence laid out in front of him, he had nothing to say.

ctx.s: 孩子反问：“你自己不也天天玩手机吗？”爸爸一下子{哑口无言}。
ctx.en: The child shot back, "Don't you play on your phone every day too?" and Dad was suddenly stuck for a reply.

ctx.s: 你刚才不是很能说吗，现在怎么{哑口无言}了？
ctx.en: Weren't you full of arguments a minute ago? Why have you got nothing to say now?

ctx.s: 辩论赛上，对方一个问题就让我们队{哑口无言}。
ctx.en: In the debate, a single question from the other side left our team with no answer.

ctx.s: 面对记者的追问，那位发言人{哑口无言}，场面十分尴尬。
ctx.en: Pressed by reporters, the spokesperson could find no reply, and the moment was very awkward.

bad.s: 看到这么美的风景，我{哑口无言}。
bad.en: (meant: the scenery was so beautiful it left me speechless)
bad.why: It means having no reply to a challenge, not being lost for words with awe at something beautiful.

bad.s: 图书馆里很安静，大家都{哑口无言}地看书。
bad.en: (meant: everyone read quietly in the library)
bad.why: It is not about being quiet; it means being unable to answer after being challenged.

cards.mean: to embellish a story in the retelling
cards.lit: to add oil and add vinegar, as when seasoning a dish

use.how: A predicate or adverbial about retelling an event with invented details: 添油加醋地说, 经过别人添油加醋. The core of the story is real.

near.diff: 无中生有 is making up something that never happened; 添油加醋 starts from a real event and adds made-up details.
夸大其词 is overstating size or degree; 添油加醋 is adding colourful extra details when passing a story on.

cards.cue: Two neighbours had a short quarrel, but by the time the story has gone round the building it includes shouting, threats and a broken door. What has happened to the story?

ctx.s: 你照实说就行，别{添油加醋}。
ctx.en: Just tell it the way it happened; don't dress it up.

ctx.s: 这件事被他{添油加醋}地一说，听起来特别吓人。
ctx.en: The way he embellished it, the whole thing sounded terrifying.

ctx.s: 本来只是吵了两句，经过几个人{添油加醋}，就传成了打架。
ctx.en: It was only a brief argument, but after a few people embroidered it, the story became a fight.

ctx.s: 这些细节是真的，还是你{添油加醋}编出来的？
ctx.en: Are these details true, or did you make them up to spice the story up?

ctx.s: 有些自媒体为了流量，把普通的小事{添油加醋}，写成惊人的新闻。
ctx.en: Some online accounts embellish ordinary little incidents into shocking news just to get clicks.

ctx.s: 奶奶讲年轻时的故事，每次都要{添油加醋}一番，越讲越精彩。
ctx.en: Every time Grandma tells stories from her youth she adds a bit more, and they get better with each telling.

bad.s: 妈妈做菜时喜欢{添油加醋}，味道很好。
bad.en: (meant: Mum likes to add seasoning when she cooks)
bad.why: It is used only figuratively, about stories, never about actually seasoning food.

bad.s: 他把报告的数据{添油加醋}，修改得更准确了。
bad.en: (meant: he refined the data in the report to make it more accurate)
bad.why: It means distorting by adding false details, the opposite of making something more accurate.

cards.mean: vying with one another to be first
cards.lit: striving to be first and afraid of being last

use.how: An adverbial, usually with 地, describing a group rushing to do something: 孩子们争先恐后地举手。 Needs several people (or animals).

near.diff: 一拥而上 is a crowd surging forward all at once; 争先恐后 stresses each one trying to get ahead of the others.

cards.cue: The teacher asks who wants to try the problem on the board, and every hand in the class shoots up, each child trying to be picked first. How do they raise their hands?

ctx.s: 下课铃一响，孩子们{争先恐后}地跑出教室。
ctx.en: The moment the bell rang, the children raced each other out of the classroom.

ctx.s: 老师一提问，同学们{争先恐后}地举手。
ctx.en: As soon as the teacher asked a question, the students all scrambled to put their hands up.

ctx.s: 商场打折第一天，顾客们{争先恐后}地往里挤。
ctx.en: On the first day of the sale, shoppers jostled one another to get inside.

ctx.s: 这款手机有什么特别的，大家为什么{争先恐后}地抢购？
ctx.en: What's so special about this phone that everyone is falling over themselves to buy it?

ctx.s: 地震发生后，志愿者们{争先恐后}地报名去灾区帮忙。
ctx.en: After the earthquake, volunteers rushed to sign up to help in the disaster area.

ctx.s: 小鸡一看到米粒，就{争先恐后}地围了过来。
ctx.en: As soon as the chicks saw the grains of rice, they crowded round, each trying to get there first.

bad.s: 我一个人{争先恐后}地赶到了车站。
bad.en: (meant: I hurried to the station)
bad.why: It describes several people competing to be first; one person alone cannot do it.

bad.s: 这次考试他{争先恐后}，得了第一名。
bad.en: (meant: he worked hard and came first in the exam)
bad.why: It pictures a group scrambling at one moment, not one person's effort or achievement.

cards.mean: an eye for an eye
cards.lit: to pay back a tooth with a tooth

story.text: The phrase comes from the Chinese translation of the law of retaliation in the Hebrew Bible: eye for eye, tooth for tooth, rendered in Chinese as 'repay an eye with an eye, repay a tooth with a tooth'. In everyday Chinese the second half is now used on its own for hitting back in the same way one was hit.

use.how: A predicate or adverbial for retaliating in kind: 对他以牙还牙, 以牙还牙地骂回去. Only for paying back harm, never kindness.

near.diff: 针锋相对 is sharp opposition point against point, often in argument; 以牙还牙 is paying someone back with the same harm they did.

cards.cue: A rival shop slashes its prices to steal your customers, so you immediately cut yours by the same amount. What are you doing?

ctx.s: 他骂我，我也不能{以牙还牙}地骂回去。
ctx.en: He swore at me, but I can't just swear back at him.

ctx.s: 弟弟抢了哥哥的玩具，哥哥{以牙还牙}，把弟弟的饼干也拿走了。
ctx.en: The younger brother grabbed his brother's toy, so the older one paid him back by taking his biscuits.

ctx.s: 对手在比赛中故意犯规，我们也不应该{以牙还牙}。
ctx.en: Even if the other team fouls on purpose, we shouldn't retaliate in kind.

ctx.s: 她在网上被人写文章嘲笑，干脆{以牙还牙}，也写了一篇文章讽刺对方。
ctx.en: Mocked in an online article, she simply hit back the same way and wrote a piece ridiculing them.

ctx.s: 那家公司降价抢客户，我们只好{以牙还牙}，也推出了优惠。
ctx.en: That company cut prices to steal customers, so we answered in kind with discounts of our own.

ctx.s: 别人怎么对你，你就怎么对别人，这样{以牙还牙}真的能解决问题吗？
ctx.en: Treating people exactly the way they treat you: can tit-for-tat really solve anything?

bad.s: 朋友帮我搬家，我请他吃饭，算是{以牙还牙}。
bad.en: (meant: my friend helped me move, so I repaid him with dinner)
bad.why: It is only for paying back harm or hostility; repaying a kindness needs a different expression.

bad.s: 他对我很{以牙还牙}。
bad.en: (meant: he treats me harshly)
bad.why: It names an act of retaliation and cannot be used as an adjective after a degree word like 'very'.

cards.mean: to scrimp and save
cards.lit: to save on eating and be sparing in using

use.how: A predicate or adverbial about a person or family cutting their own living costs, often to save for something or someone: 父母省吃俭用供我上学。 Usually said with respect.

near.diff: 精打细算 is careful planning and calculation of spending; 省吃俭用 is denying oneself everyday comforts to save.
节衣缩食 is more written and suggests harsher deprivation of food and clothing; 省吃俭用 is the everyday phrase.

cards.cue: For years your parents ate the cheapest food and never bought new clothes so they could pay your university fees. What did they do?

ctx.s: 父母{省吃俭用}，供我读完了大学。
ctx.en: My parents scrimped and saved to put me through university.

ctx.s: 她{省吃俭用}了好几年，终于买了一台钢琴。
ctx.en: She went without for several years and finally bought a piano.

ctx.s: 刚工作那几年，我{省吃俭用}，午饭常常只吃一个馒头。
ctx.en: In my first years at work I scrimped so hard that lunch was often just one steamed bun.

ctx.s: 你工资不低，为什么连一件新衣服都舍不得买，这么{省吃俭用}？
ctx.en: You earn a decent salary; why won't you even buy yourself a new piece of clothing? Why skimp like this?

ctx.s: 这笔钱是妈妈{省吃俭用}攒下来的，你可不能乱花。
ctx.en: Mum saved this money by going without, so don't you dare waste it.

ctx.s: 爷爷奶奶一辈子{省吃俭用}，自己舍不得花钱，却总给孙子买东西。
ctx.en: Grandma and Grandpa lived frugally all their lives, begrudging themselves every penny but always buying things for their grandchildren.

bad.s: 公司为了{省吃俭用}，裁掉了一半员工。
bad.en: (meant: the company laid off half its staff to cut costs)
bad.why: It is about a person or family cutting their own living expenses, not a company cutting costs or staff.

bad.s: 这台空调很{省吃俭用}，一个月用不了多少电。
bad.en: (meant: this air conditioner is energy-efficient)
bad.why: It describes people cutting their own food and living costs, never a machine that uses little power; for that, say it saves electricity.

cards.mean: wishing you prosperity (a New Year greeting)
cards.lit: respectful congratulations, and may you make a fortune

use.how: Said on its own as a greeting, mostly at Spring Festival: 新年好，恭喜发财！ It wishes the listener wealth in the coming year.

near.diff: 万事如意 wishes that everything goes well and suits any occasion; 恭喜发财 wishes wealth and belongs mainly to the Lunar New Year.

cards.cue: On the first morning of the Lunar New Year, a child greets an uncle, hoping a red envelope will follow. What does the child say?

ctx.s: 大年初一，孩子们见到爷爷就说：“{恭喜发财}！”
ctx.en: On New Year's Day the children greet their grandfather: "Happy New Year, may you prosper!"

ctx.s: 春节一大早，邻居们在楼道里互相拱手：“新年好，{恭喜发财}！”
ctx.en: Early on New Year's morning, the neighbours salute each other in the stairwell: "Happy New Year, wishing you prosperity!"

ctx.s: “{恭喜发财}，红包拿来！”小侄子笑着向我伸出手。
ctx.en: "Happy New Year, now hand over the red envelope!" my little nephew said, holding out his hand with a grin.

ctx.s: 除夕晚上老板在群里发了红包，大家纷纷回复“{恭喜发财}”。
ctx.en: On New Year's Eve the boss sent red envelopes in the group chat, and everyone replied with New Year wishes of prosperity.

ctx.s: 春节期间，饭店门口的服务员见了客人就说“{恭喜发财}”。
ctx.en: During Spring Festival, the staff at the restaurant door greet every guest with a wish for prosperity.

ctx.s: 新春贺卡上，他写了一句“{恭喜发财}，身体健康”。
ctx.en: On the New Year card he wrote: "Wishing you prosperity and good health."

bad.s: 他去年开公司赚了很多钱，真是{恭喜发财}了。
bad.en: (meant: he really got rich running his company last year)
bad.why: It is a greeting said to someone, not a description of a person getting rich.

bad.s: 朋友考上了大学，我对他说：“{恭喜发财}！”
bad.en: (meant: congratulations on getting into university)
bad.why: It wishes wealth, mainly at New Year; congratulating someone on an achievement calls for a plain 'congratulations'.

cards.mean: may whatever you set your heart on come true
cards.lit: what the heart thinks of, the matter is accomplished

use.how: Mostly after 祝你 or 愿你 in greetings and cards: 祝你生日快乐，心想事成！ Sometimes as an attributive: 心想事成的事.

near.diff: 万事如意 wishes that everything in general goes well; 心想事成 wishes that the things you are hoping for come true.

cards.cue: A friend is about to apply for her dream job, and in her card you write that you hope what she is hoping for will happen. What do you wish her?

ctx.s: 快许个愿吧，祝你{心想事成}！
ctx.en: Go on, make a wish, and may it come true!

ctx.s: 他一直想开一家自己的咖啡馆，新年时我祝他{心想事成}。
ctx.en: He has always wanted to open a café of his own, so at New Year I wished that his dream would come true.

ctx.s: 他吹蜡烛前闭眼许愿，朋友们一起喊：“祝你{心想事成}！”
ctx.en: He closed his eyes to make a wish before blowing out the candles, and his friends shouted together: "May it come true!"

ctx.s: 听说你明年要考研究生，祝你{心想事成}，考上理想的学校。
ctx.en: I hear you're sitting the graduate entrance exam next year; I hope it all works out and you get into the school you want.

ctx.s: 同学知道我想当医生，在毕业纪念册上写：“愿你{心想事成}。”
ctx.en: Knowing I want to become a doctor, a classmate wrote in my yearbook: "May your dream come true."

ctx.s: 愿望归愿望，生活里哪有那么多{心想事成}的事呢？
ctx.en: Wishes are one thing, but how often in life do things turn out exactly as you hoped?

bad.s: 我{心想事成}这个周末去爬山。
bad.en: (meant: I'm thinking of going hiking this weekend)
bad.why: It is not a verb for planning or intending; it wishes that someone's hopes come true.

bad.s: 他遇到难题总是{心想事成}，一个问题能想一整天。
bad.en: (meant: he always thinks hard about difficult problems)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with thinking hard; it is about wishes being fulfilled.

cards.mean: giving one's heart and strength to a task
cards.lit: to use up all one's heart and all one's strength

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 她尽心尽力地照顾病人。 Said of devotion to a duty or to helping others; also as a promise: 我一定尽心尽力。

near.diff: 全力以赴 is throwing everything into one challenge or push; 尽心尽力 stresses conscientious, devoted care in a duty or in serving others.

cards.cue: For years a nurse has cared for an elderly patient with total devotion, never cutting a corner. How do her colleagues describe the way she does her job?

ctx.s: 王老师对每个学生都{尽心尽力}。
ctx.en: Mr Wang gives his all to every one of his students.

ctx.s: 这些年她照顾生病的母亲，可以说是{尽心尽力}了。
ctx.en: In all these years of looking after her sick mother, she has truly done everything she could.

ctx.s: “我出差这段时间，我妈就拜托你照顾了。”“放心，我一定{尽心尽力}。”
ctx.en: "While I'm away on business, can I leave my mum in your care?" "Don't worry, I'll do everything I can for her."

ctx.s: 虽然最后没能救回病人，但医生们已经{尽心尽力}了。
ctx.en: Although in the end the patient could not be saved, the doctors had done everything they could.

ctx.s: 老张在这个小区当了十年物业经理，大家都说他办事{尽心尽力}。
ctx.en: Lao Zhang has managed this housing estate for ten years, and everyone says he is utterly conscientious.

ctx.s: 为了帮新同事熟悉工作，他{尽心尽力}，从不嫌麻烦。
ctx.en: He did everything he could to help the new colleague settle in, and never found it a bother.

bad.s: 放假了，我昨天{尽心尽力}地睡了一整天。
bad.en: (meant: I slept the whole day yesterday)
bad.why: It describes devoted effort for a duty or for other people, not doing a leisure activity a lot.

bad.s: 这道菜{尽心尽力}，非常好吃。
bad.en: (meant: this dish was made with great care and is delicious)
bad.why: It describes a person's effort, not a thing; say instead that the cook made it with great care.

cards.mean: without a pause, moving straight on
cards.lit: the horse does not stop its hooves

use.how: Adverbial, usually with 地 before a verb: 他下了飞机就马不停蹄地赶到会场。 Said of people going from one task or place straight on to the next.

near.diff: 争分夺秒 is racing against a deadline, using every minute; 马不停蹄 is going straight on from one task or place to the next without rest.

cards.cue: Straight after landing, the manager goes to a meeting, then to a factory visit, then to a dinner, without even dropping her bags at the hotel. How did she move through the day?

ctx.s: 他下了飞机，{马不停蹄}地赶到了公司。
ctx.en: As soon as he got off the plane, he rushed straight to the office.

ctx.s: 这几天我{马不停蹄}，开完一个会又是另一个会。
ctx.en: These past few days I haven't stopped: one meeting ends and the next begins.

ctx.s: “你刚出差回来，不休息一下吗？”“没时间，明天还得{马不停蹄}地赶去上海。”
ctx.en: "You've only just got back from your trip; won't you rest?" "No time, tomorrow I have to head straight off to Shanghai."

ctx.s: 项目一结束，团队又{马不停蹄}地投入了下一个项目。
ctx.en: The moment the project finished, the team threw themselves straight into the next one.

ctx.s: 记者们{马不停蹄}地从一个现场跑到另一个现场。
ctx.en: The reporters dashed from one scene to the next without a break.

ctx.s: 救援队员三天三夜{马不停蹄}，挨家挨户地搜救。
ctx.en: For three days and nights the rescuers kept going without rest, searching house by house.

bad.s: 他做事总是{马不停蹄}，一点也不认真。
bad.en: (meant: he always does things hastily and carelessly)
bad.why: It means pressing on without rest and carries no criticism of careless, sloppy work.

bad.s: 雨{马不停蹄}地下了一整天。
bad.en: (meant: it rained nonstop all day)
bad.why: It is said of people pressing on from one task or place to the next, not of rain or weather that simply continues.

cards.mean: one of the very best
cards.lit: to be counted first or second

use.how: Attributive with 的 or predicate, often with 在……里: 他的厨艺在我们这儿是数一数二的。 Says someone or something is among the best of a group or place.

near.diff: 名列前茅 is ranking near the top of a list, typically exam or contest results; 数一数二 says someone or something is among the very best of a field or place.

cards.cue: Asked about a local chef, people say that in the whole city maybe one other cook could match him. Where does he stand?

ctx.s: 这家饭馆在我们城市是{数一数二}的。
ctx.en: This restaurant is one of the very best in our city.

ctx.s: 他的篮球水平在全校{数一数二}。
ctx.en: At basketball he is one of the top players in the whole school.

ctx.s: “这家公司怎么样？”“在行业里算得上{数一数二}的大企业。”
ctx.en: "What's this company like?" "It's one of the leading firms in the industry."

ctx.s: 说到做菜，我妈在亲戚里可是{数一数二}的。
ctx.en: When it comes to cooking, my mum is about the best among all our relatives.

ctx.s: 这座图书馆的藏书量在全国也是{数一数二}的。
ctx.en: This library's collection is one of the largest in the whole country.

ctx.s: 他从一个普通工人，做到了公司里{数一数二}的技术专家。
ctx.en: He started as an ordinary worker and became one of the company's top technical experts.

bad.s: 我{数一数二}地把钱点了一遍。
bad.en: (meant: I counted the money one note at a time)
bad.why: It does not mean counting; it says something ranks among the best.

bad.s: 他{数一数二}了这次比赛。
bad.en: (meant: he took first or second place in the contest)
bad.why: It is not a verb and cannot take an object; it describes a person or thing as ranking among the best.

cards.mean: may you succeed straight away (a wish)
cards.lit: success as soon as the horse arrives

use.how: Said as a wish before a contest, exam or venture: 祝你马到成功！ In formal send-offs: 预祝……马到成功。

near.diff: 一帆风顺 wishes a smooth journey or a smooth life; 马到成功 wishes quick success in a particular task someone is about to take on.

cards.cue: Your friend is setting off this afternoon to pitch a deal to a big client. As they leave, what do you wish them?

ctx.s: 明天就要比赛了，祝你{马到成功}！
ctx.en: The competition is tomorrow; I hope you win it!

ctx.s: “我下午去面试。”“加油，祝你{马到成功}！”
ctx.en: "I've got an interview this afternoon." "Go for it, I hope you nail it!"

ctx.s: 考试前一天，妈妈给她发消息：“别紧张，祝你{马到成功}。”
ctx.en: The day before the exam her mother messaged her: "Don't be nervous, I know you'll pass with flying colours."

ctx.s: 出发前，同事们为谈判团队送行，预祝他们{马到成功}。
ctx.en: Before they set off, colleagues saw the negotiating team out and wished them quick success.

ctx.s: 他带队去参加全国大赛，校长握着他的手说：“祝你们{马到成功}！”
ctx.en: As he led the team off to the national contest, the headmaster shook his hand and said: "Go and win!"

ctx.s: 这次创业，朋友们都祝他{马到成功}，可他自己心里一点底也没有。
ctx.en: Friends all wished him instant success with his new business, but he himself had no idea how it would go.

bad.s: 爷爷今天退休了，我们祝他{马到成功}！
bad.en: (meant: we wished grandpa well in his retirement)
bad.why: It wishes quick success in a task about to begin; retirement is not a challenge to win.

bad.s: 他骑马骑得很好，每次都{马到成功}。
bad.en: (meant: he rides very well and always gets there)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with real horses; it is a wish for success in a venture.

cards.mean: many small amounts add up to a lot
cards.lit: pile up little and it becomes much

use.how: Usually a clause on its own after a small regular action: 每天存一点，积少成多。 Used to encourage saving or steady practice, or to warn that small things add up.

near.diff: 日积月累 stresses a long stretch of time; 积少成多 stresses that small amounts add up to a large one.

cards.cue: Your friend says setting aside a few coins a day is pointless. You reply that those coins will eventually make a decent sum. What principle are you citing?

ctx.s: 每天存十块钱，{积少成多}，一年下来也不少。
ctx.en: Save ten yuan a day; it adds up, and by the end of the year it's quite a lot.

ctx.s: 一天背五个单词好像不多，但{积少成多}，一年就是一千八百多个。
ctx.en: Five words a day doesn't seem like much, but it adds up: in a year that's over eighteen hundred.

ctx.s: 别小看这些零钱，{积少成多}，够买一台电脑了。
ctx.en: Don't look down on this small change; it has added up to enough for a computer.

ctx.s: 奶奶把用过的塑料瓶攒起来卖，她说：“{积少成多}，能补贴点家用。”
ctx.en: Grandma saves used plastic bottles to sell. "Little by little it adds up," she says, "it helps with the household money."

ctx.s: 网上每人捐一块钱，{积少成多}，很快就筹够了手术费。
ctx.en: Online everyone gave one yuan, and together it soon covered the cost of the operation.

ctx.s: 小毛病如果不改，{积少成多}，最后会变成大问题。
ctx.en: If you don't fix small faults, they pile up and in the end become a big problem.

bad.s: 他买彩票一下子就{积少成多}，中了五百万。
bad.en: (meant: he suddenly got rich by winning five million in the lottery)
bad.why: It describes small amounts building up gradually, not a sudden windfall.

bad.s: 我想{积少成多}一笔钱去旅行。
bad.en: (meant: I want to save up a sum of money to travel)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; it comments on small amounts adding up, not on the act of saving.

cards.mean: to learn by rote
cards.lit: to memorise rigidly and recite by force

use.how: Predicate or attributive, mostly critical: 学语言不能只靠死记硬背。 Said of memorising study material without understanding it.

cards.cue: A student can recite the whole textbook word for word but cannot answer a single question that asks him to explain it. How has he been studying?

ctx.s: 学数学不能{死记硬背}，要理解公式。
ctx.en: You can't learn maths by rote; you have to understand the formulas.

ctx.s: 考试前一晚，他把答案{死记硬背}了下来，第二天全忘了。
ctx.en: The night before the exam he crammed the answers by heart, and the next day he had forgotten them all.

ctx.s: “这些历史年代怎么记？”“别{死记硬背}，把事件串成故事就好记了。”
ctx.en: "How do I remember all these historical dates?" "Don't just drill them; link the events into a story and they'll stick."

ctx.s: 这种{死记硬背}的教学方法，早就该改一改了。
ctx.en: This rote-learning style of teaching should have been changed long ago.

ctx.s: 她小时候{死记硬背}过很多古诗，现在才慢慢懂得其中的意思。
ctx.en: As a child she learned lots of classical poems by rote, and only now is she slowly understanding them.

ctx.s: 面试官一听就知道，他的回答是{死记硬背}出来的。
ctx.en: The interviewer could tell at once that his answers had been memorised parrot-fashion.

bad.s: 他学习非常认真，每天都{死记硬背}，老师很表扬他。
bad.en: (meant: he studies very hard every day and the teacher praises him for it)
bad.why: It criticises memorising without understanding; it is not praise for diligence.

bad.s: 这本书的内容很{死记硬背}。
bad.en: (meant: this book's content is hard to memorise)
bad.why: It describes a way of learning, not a quality of the material being learned.

cards.mean: to look around in all directions
cards.lit: to look east and gaze west

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 他站在门口东张西望。 Describes someone glancing this way and that, out of curiosity, while searching, or when they should be paying attention.

near.diff: 鬼鬼祟祟 says someone is acting furtively, hiding their purpose; 东张西望 only says they keep looking around.

cards.cue: At a crowded station exit, a woman keeps turning her head this way and that, trying to spot the friend who is meant to pick her up. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 第一次进城，他好奇地{东张西望}。
ctx.en: On his first trip to the city, he looked all around him in curiosity.

ctx.s: 上课的时候别{东张西望}，认真听讲！
ctx.en: Don't keep looking around in class; listen properly!

ctx.s: 她站在车站出口{东张西望}，好像在等什么人。
ctx.en: She stood at the station exit looking this way and that, as if waiting for someone.

ctx.s: “你在找什么？”“我的钥匙不知道掉哪儿了。”他一边说一边{东张西望}。
ctx.en: "What are you looking for?" "I've dropped my keys somewhere," he said, glancing all around.

ctx.s: 小狗走丢以后，站在街口{东张西望}，不知道该往哪儿走。
ctx.en: After getting lost, the puppy stood at the corner looking every which way, not knowing where to go.

ctx.s: 考场上{东张西望}，很容易被当成作弊。
ctx.en: Looking around during an exam can easily get you taken for a cheat.

bad.s: 他{东张西望}了很久，最后决定去北京工作。
bad.en: (meant: he thought it over for a long time and decided to work in Beijing)
bad.why: It is physically looking around, not weighing a decision in one's mind.

bad.s: 他{东张西望}地盯着电脑屏幕工作了一下午。
bad.en: (meant: he stared at his screen working all afternoon)
bad.why: It means glancing restlessly in all directions, the opposite of keeping one's eyes fixed on one thing.

cards.mean: to turn something over and over in one's mind
cards.lit: to ponder on the left and think on the right

use.how: Predicate, usually followed by the outcome: 我左思右想，还是决定不去了。 Describes thinking a problem over from every side.

near.diff: 犹豫不决 is being stuck, unable to decide; 左思右想 is the act of thinking it over, which often ends in a decision or an idea.

cards.cue: For two nights you go over every reason for and against moving to another city for a job, and in the end you say yes. What were you doing those two nights?

ctx.s: 我{左思右想}，还是决定不去了。
ctx.en: I thought it over and over, and decided not to go after all.

ctx.s: 他{左思右想}，觉得这件事还是先不告诉父母为好。
ctx.en: After turning it over and over, he felt it was better not to tell his parents just yet.

ctx.s: 晚上躺在床上，她{左思右想}，怎么也睡不着。
ctx.en: Lying in bed at night, she kept turning things over in her mind and couldn't get to sleep.

ctx.s: “你怎么才回消息？”“我{左思右想}，不知道该怎么回答你。”
ctx.en: "Why did it take you so long to reply?" "I kept going back and forth over it; I didn't know how to answer you."

ctx.s: 给女朋友挑生日礼物，他{左思右想}了好几天，最后选了一条围巾。
ctx.en: He agonised for days over a birthday present for his girlfriend and finally chose a scarf.

ctx.s: 经理{左思右想}，终于明白了问题出在哪里。
ctx.en: After thinking it through from every angle, the manager finally understood where the problem lay.

bad.s: 过马路的时候要{左思右想}，看看有没有车。
bad.en: (meant: look left and right for cars when crossing the road)
bad.why: It is about thinking, not physically looking left and right for traffic.

bad.s: 他是一个很{左思右想}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he is a very thoughtful person)
bad.why: It describes mulling over one particular matter, not a personality trait, and cannot be modified by 'very'.

cards.mean: hard-won
cards.lit: its coming was not easy

story.text: The phrase is usually traced to a line in the household maxims of the late-Ming, early-Qing scholar Zhu Yongchun: for every bowl of porridge and every meal, remember that it did not come easily; for every half thread of silk, keep in mind how hard material things are to produce.
story.source: 朱用纯《治家格言》（《朱子家训》）：一粥一饭，当思来处不易

use.how: Predicate or attributive with 的: 这份成绩来之不易 / 来之不易的机会. Said of a result, chance or possession already gained, usually implying it should be valued.

near.diff: 千辛万苦 describes the hardships themselves; 来之不易 describes the result they produced and implies it must be cherished.

cards.cue: After years of saving, a couple finally buys a small flat and tells their son to take good care of it. How do they describe the flat?

ctx.s: 这份工作{来之不易}，你要好好珍惜。
ctx.en: This job wasn't easy to get; you should value it.

ctx.s: 妈妈常说，每一粒米都{来之不易}，不要浪费。
ctx.en: Mum always says every grain of rice comes at a cost, so don't waste it.

ctx.s: 这场胜利{来之不易}，全队整整练了一年。
ctx.en: This victory was hard-won; the whole team trained for a full year.

ctx.s: 他把这笔{来之不易}的奖学金全部用来买书了。
ctx.en: He spent the whole of that hard-earned scholarship on books.

ctx.s: “你知道这次机会是多么{来之不易}吗？”
ctx.en: "Do you know how hard this chance was to come by?"

ctx.s: 两家公司谈了半年才签下合同，双方都明白这次合作{来之不易}。
ctx.en: The two companies negotiated for six months before signing; both sides know this partnership was hard-won.

bad.s: 这道数学题{来之不易}，我做了一个小时也没做出来。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is hard)
bad.why: It describes something already obtained through effort, not a task that is hard to do; just say the problem is hard.

bad.s: 他今天{来之不易}，路上堵了两个小时。
bad.en: (meant: it was hard for him to get here today)
bad.why: It is not about a person physically arriving; it is said of results, chances or possessions won with effort.

cards.mean: day after day
cards.lit: day repeats day

use.how: Adverbial (日复一日地练习) or attributive (日复一日的生活). Stresses the same thing repeated over a long stretch, often monotonous; pairs with 年复一年.

near.diff: 久而久之 introduces the result that a long time brings; 日复一日 stresses the sameness of each repeated day.

cards.cue: A night watchman describes walking the same corridors and checking the same doors every night for twenty years. How does he describe his routine?

ctx.s: 他{日复一日}地练习写字，从来没停过。
ctx.en: He practised his handwriting day after day and never stopped.

ctx.s: 这种{日复一日}的生活让他觉得很无聊。
ctx.en: This same-every-day life bores him.

ctx.s: 老人{日复一日}地守着这家小店，一守就是三十年。
ctx.en: Day after day the old man kept watch over his little shop, for thirty years.

ctx.s: “你不觉得{日复一日}做同样的事很累吗？”
ctx.en: "Don't you find it tiring doing the same thing day after day?"

ctx.s: 时间就在这样{日复一日}的等待中过去了。
ctx.en: Time slipped away in this waiting, day after day.

ctx.s: 环卫工人{日复一日}、年复一年地清扫着这条街。
ctx.en: Day after day, year after year, the street cleaners sweep this street.

bad.s: 我{日复一日}去了一次超市。
bad.en: (meant: I went to the supermarket once today)
bad.why: It describes something repeated over a long time; it cannot describe a single event or mean 'today'.

bad.s: 明天开始，我们{日复一日}见面吧！
bad.en: (meant: from tomorrow, let's meet every day)
bad.why: It narrates long, often tedious repetition; it is not a neutral 'every day' for making plans or suggestions.

cards.mean: over time, gradually
cards.lit: long, and long again

use.how: Clause-initial connective, usually followed by a comma: 久而久之，… Introduces the outcome that a habit or situation produces after a long time.

near.diff: 日复一日 dwells on the repetition itself; 久而久之 links that repetition to what it eventually leads to.

cards.cue: You chat with a neighbour over the fence every evening, and a year later you have become close friends. How do you link the habit to the result?

ctx.s: 他每天读一点中文报纸，{久而久之}，阅读速度快了很多。
ctx.en: He read a little of a Chinese newspaper every day, and over time his reading got much faster.

ctx.s: 她总是不吃早饭，{久而久之}，胃就出了问题。
ctx.en: She kept skipping breakfast, and eventually her stomach started giving her trouble.

ctx.s: 两个人天天一起上下班，{久而久之}就成了好朋友。
ctx.en: The two of them commuted together every day and, over time, became good friends.

ctx.s: 谎话说多了，{久而久之}，连他自己都信了。
ctx.en: He told the lie so often that in time even he believed it.

ctx.s: “别小看这些坏习惯，{久而久之}会影响健康的。”
ctx.en: "Don't underestimate these bad habits; over time they'll affect your health."

ctx.s: 公司里没人敢提意见，{久而久之}，问题越积越多。
ctx.en: No one at the company dared to speak up, and over time the problems piled up.

bad.s: 我等了他{久而久之}，他还没来。
bad.en: (meant: I waited for him a long time)
bad.why: It is not a duration phrase placed after a verb; it is a connective that introduces a gradual result.

bad.s: {久而久之}以前，这里是一片农田。
bad.en: (meant: long ago this was farmland)
bad.why: It does not mean 'long ago'. It links a long process to its outcome.

cards.mean: let's not put it off; better get going right away (urging action)
cards.lit: the matter should not be delayed

use.how: A clause on its own, followed by what to do now: 事不宜迟，我们马上出发。 Said by someone urging immediate action on a particular matter.

near.diff: 刻不容缓 describes a situation as extremely urgent (这件事刻不容缓); 事不宜迟 is the speaker's call to start right now.

cards.cue: Concert tickets go on sale in ten minutes and your friend is still chatting. You stand up and say: no more dawdling, let's go and queue.

ctx.s: {事不宜迟}，我们现在就出发吧。
ctx.en: No time to lose; let's set off now.

ctx.s: 票快卖完了，{事不宜迟}，赶紧下单！
ctx.en: The tickets are nearly sold out. Don't wait, order now!

ctx.s: 天快下雨了，{事不宜迟}，咱们得赶紧把衣服收进来。
ctx.en: It's about to rain; we'd better get the washing in right away.

ctx.s: 医生看完片子说：“{事不宜迟}，明天就安排手术。”
ctx.en: After looking at the scans the doctor said: "We shouldn't delay. We'll schedule the operation for tomorrow."

ctx.s: 既然大家都同意了，{事不宜迟}，我们今天下午就开始准备。
ctx.en: Since everyone agrees, let's not put it off; we start preparing this afternoon.

ctx.s: 他心想：{事不宜迟}，于是放下电话就去了银行。
ctx.en: He thought: no point waiting. He went to the bank as soon as he hung up.

bad.s: 这家餐厅上菜太慢了，真是{事不宜迟}。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant is far too slow)
bad.why: It urges acting now; it is not a complaint that something is slow or late.

bad.s: 他做事总是{事不宜迟}，从不拖拉。
bad.en: (meant: he always acts promptly)
bad.why: It is not a description of someone's habits; it is said about one matter that calls for action now.

cards.mean: unable to hold back one's feelings
cards.lit: feelings one cannot restrain in oneself

use.how: Adverbial before a verb, often with 地: 情不自禁地笑了起来. Describes an involuntary reaction driven by emotion: laughing, crying, singing, cheering.

near.diff: 不由自主 covers any action one can't control, even physical ones (腿不由自主地发抖); 情不自禁 is always driven by emotion.

cards.cue: At your daughter's first school concert you are on your feet clapping and cheering before you have even decided to. How did you react?

ctx.s: 听到这个好消息，她{情不自禁}地笑了。
ctx.en: Hearing the good news, she couldn't help smiling.

ctx.s: 音乐一响，孩子们{情不自禁}地跟着跳了起来。
ctx.en: As soon as the music started, the children couldn't help dancing along.

ctx.s: 看到老照片，奶奶{情不自禁}流下了眼泪。
ctx.en: Looking at the old photos, Grandma couldn't hold back her tears.

ctx.s: “对不起，刚才看比赛太激动了，我{情不自禁}就喊出声来了。”
ctx.en: "Sorry, I got so excited watching the match that I shouted out without meaning to."

ctx.s: 站在山顶看日出的那一刻，我们都{情不自禁}地欢呼起来。
ctx.en: The moment we watched the sunrise from the summit, we all burst into cheers.

ctx.s: 听到自己的名字，她激动得{情不自禁}地抱住了身边的教练。
ctx.en: Hearing her name called, she was so overcome that she threw her arms around her coach.

bad.s: 冬天太冷，我{情不自禁}地发抖。
bad.en: (meant: it was so cold I shivered)
bad.why: Shivering from cold is physical, not emotional; the idiom needs a feeling as the cause.

bad.s: 他是个很{情不自禁}的人，经常发脾气。
bad.en: (meant: he is a man who can't control his temper)
bad.why: It is not an adjective for someone's character; it describes one moment's involuntary reaction and goes before a verb.

cards.mean: timid as a mouse
cards.lit: one's gall is as small as a mouse (the gallbladder is the seat of courage)

use.how: Predicate describing a person's character: 他胆小如鼠. Mocking or contemptuous; not for a reasonable fear in one situation.

near.diff: 胆战心惊 is a moment of intense fear; 胆小如鼠 labels a lasting cowardly character.

cards.cue: A man boasts that nothing scares him, then runs off at the sight of a small puppy and won't walk down a dark stairwell. How do you mock him?

ctx.s: 别看他个子高，其实{胆小如鼠}。
ctx.en: He may be tall, but he's actually a real coward.

ctx.s: 他{胆小如鼠}，连晚上一个人回家都不敢。
ctx.en: He's such a scaredy-cat he won't even walk home alone at night.

ctx.s: “一只小虫子就把你吓跑了，真是{胆小如鼠}！”
ctx.en: "A tiny bug sent you running. What a scaredy-cat!"

ctx.s: 我小时候{胆小如鼠}，一打雷就躲进被子里。
ctx.en: As a kid I was a total scaredy-cat; at the first clap of thunder I'd hide under the covers.

ctx.s: 他嘴上说什么都不怕，一遇到事却{胆小如鼠}，躲得比谁都快。
ctx.en: He says he fears nothing, but when trouble comes he's a coward and hides faster than anyone.

ctx.s: 故事里的那个国王{胆小如鼠}，一听说要打仗就躲进了宫里。
ctx.en: The king in the story was a coward; at the first word of war he hid in his palace.

bad.s: 他开车{胆小如鼠}，所以从来没出过事故。
bad.en: (meant: he drives cautiously, so he's never had an accident)
bad.why: It is contemptuous, calling someone a coward; it is not praise for caution.

bad.s: 第一次上台演讲，我有点{胆小如鼠}。
bad.en: (meant: giving my first speech, I was a bit nervous)
bad.why: It labels a cowardly character and can't be softened into 'a bit' to describe one-off stage nerves.

cards.mean: needlessly suspicious, imagining things
cards.lit: suspecting gods, suspecting ghosts

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 别疑神疑鬼的 / 整天疑神疑鬼. Criticises someone who suspects people or things without real grounds.

near.diff: 草木皆兵 is panic after a fright that sees enemies everywhere; 疑神疑鬼 is groundless suspicion and worry in everyday life.

cards.cue: Your flatmate is sure someone read her diary because her pen was moved, and now checks the lock five times every night. What do you tell her to stop doing?

ctx.s: 别{疑神疑鬼}的，门是你自己锁好的。
ctx.en: Stop imagining things; you locked the door yourself.

ctx.s: 他最近总是{疑神疑鬼}，觉得同事在背后说他坏话。
ctx.en: Lately he's been paranoid, convinced his colleagues talk about him behind his back.

ctx.s: “手机响一下你就{疑神疑鬼}，到底在担心什么？”
ctx.en: "Every time the phone buzzes you get suspicious. What are you actually worried about?"

ctx.s: 一个人住久了，她晚上听到一点声音就{疑神疑鬼}。
ctx.en: After living alone so long, the slightest sound at night sets her imagining things.

ctx.s: 老板{疑神疑鬼}地把每份报销单都查了三遍。
ctx.en: The boss, suspicious of everyone, checked every expense claim three times.

ctx.s: 丈夫晚回家半小时，她就开始{疑神疑鬼}，一个接一个地打电话。
ctx.en: When her husband was half an hour late she started imagining the worst and made call after call.

bad.s: 警察{疑神疑鬼}地调查了现场，终于找到了小偷。
bad.en: (meant: the police searched the scene carefully and caught the thief)
bad.why: It criticises groundless suspicion; it cannot describe careful, justified investigation.

bad.s: 这座老房子{疑神疑鬼}，大家都说里面有鬼。
bad.en: (meant: this old house is spooky)
bad.why: It describes a person's suspicious state of mind, not a place that seems haunted.

cards.mean: genuinely and sincerely
cards.lit: a true heart and a real intention

use.how: Adverbial with 地 (真心实意地帮助), predicate, or noun (我们的真心实意). Said of a person's sincerity towards others.

near.diff: 全心全意 is giving all one's effort and devotion; 真心实意 is meaning it, not faking it.

cards.cue: Your neighbour has helped you move house three times and never once expected anything in return. How do you describe his help?

ctx.s: 他是{真心实意}想帮你，不是为了钱。
ctx.en: He genuinely wants to help you; it's not about money.

ctx.s: 我{真心实意}地向你道歉，请你原谅我。
ctx.en: I sincerely apologise to you; please forgive me.

ctx.s: 交朋友要{真心实意}，不能只想着自己。
ctx.en: To make friends you have to be sincere, not just think of yourself.

ctx.s: “你这话是{真心实意}的，还是客气客气？”
ctx.en: "Do you really mean that, or are you just being polite?"

ctx.s: 老师对学生的关心是{真心实意}的，从来不做表面文章。
ctx.en: The teacher's care for the students is genuine; it's never just for show.

ctx.s: 客户最后签了合同，因为他们感受到了我们的{真心实意}。
ctx.en: The client finally signed because they could feel our sincerity.

bad.s: 这件衣服的质量很{真心实意}。
bad.en: (meant: this garment is of genuine quality)
bad.why: It describes a person's sincerity, not the authenticity or quality of goods.

bad.s: 他{真心实意}地骗了我。
bad.en: (meant: he really did deceive me)
bad.why: Sincerity contradicts deceit; it is not an intensifier meaning 'really'.

cards.mean: putting on an act
cards.lit: to put on a pattern and make a show

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 装模作样地看书 / 别装模作样了. Criticises pretending: a show without the real feeling or activity behind it.

near.diff: 装腔作势 is putting on airs to impress or intimidate; 装模作样 is any pretence, such as faking busyness or feelings.

cards.cue: A student playing games on his phone hears the teacher's footsteps, quickly opens a textbook and frowns at it. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 老师一进来，他就{装模作样}地看起书来。
ctx.en: As soon as the teacher came in, he made a show of reading.

ctx.s: 别{装模作样}了，我知道你根本没睡着。
ctx.en: Stop pretending; I know you're not asleep at all.

ctx.s: 他根本不懂画，却{装模作样}地在画前站了半天。
ctx.en: He knows nothing about painting, yet he stood in front of it for ages putting on an act.

ctx.s: “你又不是真想帮忙，何必{装模作样}？”
ctx.en: "You don't really want to help, so why the act?"

ctx.s: 她{装模作样}地叹了口气，其实心里高兴得很。
ctx.en: She gave a theatrical sigh, though inside she was delighted.

ctx.s: 弟弟偷吃了蛋糕，还{装模作样}地问妈妈蛋糕去哪儿了。
ctx.en: My little brother ate the cake, then innocently asked Mum where it had gone.

bad.s: 演员在舞台上{装模作样}，演得特别好。
bad.en: (meant: the actor performed brilliantly on stage)
bad.why: It is derogatory, for faking in real life; it is not praise for acting a role.

bad.s: 为了参加婚礼，她{装模作样}地化了妆。
bad.en: (meant: she did her make-up nicely for the wedding)
bad.why: It is not about dressing up; it means pretending to a feeling or activity one does not really have.

cards.mean: to think oneself clever and act on it
cards.lit: to make oneself out to be clever

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 别自作聪明 / 他自作聪明地改了计划. Criticises acting on one's own clever idea without asking, usually with a bad result.

near.diff: 弄巧成拙 names the outcome, a clever trick that backfires; 自作聪明 criticises the attitude of acting on one's own supposed cleverness.
画蛇添足 is spoiling something by adding the unnecessary; 自作聪明 is any self-confident 'clever' move made without asking, often a change or shortcut.

cards.cue: Without asking anyone, a colleague 'improves' the file format the client requested, and now the client's software can't open it. What did he do?

ctx.s: 别{自作聪明}，按说明书做就行。
ctx.en: Don't try to be clever; just follow the instructions.

ctx.s: 他{自作聪明}地改了密码，结果自己也忘了。
ctx.en: He thought he was being clever changing the password, and then forgot it himself.

ctx.s: “谁让你{自作聪明}的？客户要的就是原来的设计。”
ctx.en: "Who told you to get clever? The client wanted the original design."

ctx.s: 我{自作聪明}抄了近路，结果迷了路，比平时晚到了一个小时。
ctx.en: I thought I'd be smart and take a shortcut, got lost, and arrived an hour later than usual.

ctx.s: 实习生{自作聪明}，删掉了报告里他觉得没用的部分。
ctx.en: The intern decided he knew best and deleted the parts of the report he thought were useless.

ctx.s: 故事里的狐狸总爱{自作聪明}，最后掉进了自己挖的坑。
ctx.en: The fox in the story was too clever for its own good and ended up falling into the pit it had dug.

bad.s: 她{自作聪明}，考试总是得第一名。
bad.en: (meant: she is clever and always comes first)
bad.why: It mocks misplaced cleverness; it is never praise for real intelligence.

bad.s: 这个问题太难，我得{自作聪明}地想一想。
bad.en: (meant: this is hard, I need to think it through on my own)
bad.why: It does not mean thinking for oneself; it criticises an ill-judged action already taken or about to be.

cards.mean: to imagine someone fancies you
cards.lit: to make up a lot of feeling all by oneself

use.how: Predicate, often in 别自作多情了 or 是我自作多情. Mocks someone, or oneself, for reading affection or special attention into what was not meant that way.

near.diff: 一厢情愿 is any one-sided wish or plan the other side never agreed to; 自作多情 is wrongly believing someone has feelings for you.

cards.cue: You thought the new colleague's smile and the coffee he brought meant he liked you, then learn he brings coffee for everyone.

ctx.s: 她只是对每个人都很客气，你别{自作多情}了。
ctx.en: She's just polite to everyone; don't kid yourself that she likes you.

ctx.s: 我还以为那束花是送给我的，原来是我{自作多情}。
ctx.en: I thought the flowers were for me; turns out I was flattering myself.

ctx.s: “他是不是喜欢我？”“人家只是借你的笔记，别{自作多情}。”
ctx.en: "Does he like me?" "He just borrowed your notes. Don't get ideas."

ctx.s: 他那条朋友圈根本不是写给你的，是你{自作多情}了。
ctx.en: That post of his wasn't written for you at all; you're reading too much into it.

ctx.s: 那天她冲我笑了一下，我就{自作多情}了好几个星期。
ctx.en: She smiled at me once that day, and I spent weeks imagining she was into me.

ctx.s: 说实话，我怕他对我好只是出于礼貌，是我{自作多情}，所以一直没敢表白。
ctx.en: Honestly, I was afraid he was only being kind out of politeness and I was imagining things, so I never dared to confess.

bad.s: 他对女朋友非常{自作多情}，每天都送礼物。
bad.en: (meant: he is very affectionate to his girlfriend)
bad.why: It does not mean affectionate; it means imagining feelings in someone else that are not there.

bad.s: 我们俩{自作多情}，下个月就结婚了。
bad.en: (meant: we are deeply in love and marrying next month)
bad.why: It mocks one-sided, imagined feelings, so it cannot describe a couple's mutual love.

cards.mean: chatting and laughing together
cards.lit: there is talking and there is laughing

use.how: Adverbial with 地 (有说有笑地走着) or predicate. Describes two or more people in relaxed, friendly conversation.
