near.diff: 谈笑风生 is bookish and praises someone talking with wit and ease; 有说有笑 is everyday and just says people are chatting cheerfully.

cards.cue: On the bus home after a school trip, the students chat and laugh the whole way. How were they travelling?

ctx.s: 下课后，同学们{有说有笑}地走出教室。
ctx.en: After class, the students walked out of the classroom chatting and laughing.

ctx.s: 一家人围着桌子吃饭，{有说有笑}，特别热闹。
ctx.en: The whole family sat round the table eating, talking and laughing; it was very lively.

ctx.s: 刚才你们俩还{有说有笑}的，怎么突然吵起来了？
ctx.en: A moment ago you two were chatting and laughing; how come you're suddenly arguing?

ctx.s: 他们一路上{有说有笑}，一点儿也不觉得累。
ctx.en: They talked and laughed all the way and didn't feel tired at all.

ctx.s: 看到她和新同事{有说有笑}，我就放心了。
ctx.en: Seeing her chatting and laughing with her new colleagues, I stopped worrying.

ctx.s: 以前他总是一个人待着，现在也能跟大家{有说有笑}了。
ctx.en: He used to keep to himself, but now he chats and jokes with everyone.

bad.s: 这个笑话很{有说有笑}，大家都笑了。
bad.en: (meant: the joke was very funny)
bad.why: It describes people chatting and laughing together, not how funny a joke or a thing is.

bad.s: 考试的时候，教室里{有说有笑}，非常安静。
bad.en: (meant: during the exam the room was very quiet)
bad.why: It means people are talking and laughing, the opposite of a silent exam room.

cards.mean: full of praise, unable to stop praising
cards.lit: praise never leaves the mouth

use.how: Predicate whose subject is the people praising: 大家对这道菜赞不绝口, 让人赞不绝口. Not used with 很 or 非常.

near.diff: 交口称赞 stresses that many people praise with one voice; 赞不绝口 stresses that the praise keeps coming.

cards.cue: Every guest at dinner keeps telling the host how wonderful the fish is, again and again, all evening.

ctx.s: 客人们吃了妈妈包的饺子，个个{赞不绝口}。
ctx.en: The guests tried Mum's dumplings and every one of them couldn't stop praising them.

ctx.s: 老师对他的作文{赞不绝口}，还在班上念了一遍。
ctx.en: The teacher was full of praise for his essay and even read it out to the class.

ctx.s: 去过那家民宿的朋友都{赞不绝口}，我们也订了一间。
ctx.en: Friends who've stayed at that guesthouse rave about it, so we booked a room too.

ctx.s: “那部电影怎么样？”“我爸看完{赞不绝口}，说是今年最好看的。”
ctx.en: "How's that film?" "My dad couldn't stop praising it; he says it's the best this year."

ctx.s: 新同事做的方案让经理{赞不绝口}。
ctx.en: The new colleague's proposal had the manager singing its praises.

ctx.s: 这位老师傅的手艺，连行家都{赞不绝口}。
ctx.en: Even experts can't stop praising this old master's craftsmanship.

bad.s: 这道菜非常{赞不绝口}。
bad.en: (meant: this dish is excellent)
bad.why: It describes the people doing the praising, not the thing praised, and it cannot take 'very' before it.

bad.s: 他的报告错误太多，经理看了{赞不绝口}。
bad.en: (meant: the manager kept complaining about it)
bad.why: It means non-stop praise, so it cannot describe non-stop criticism of a bad report.

cards.mean: thrilling, stirring
cards.lit: stirring people's hearts

use.how: Mostly an attribute (激动人心的时刻, 激动人心的消息) or predicate. Said of events, moments, news or speeches, never of one's own feeling.

near.diff: 惊心动魄 is thrilling because of danger or tension that grips you; 激动人心 is thrilling because it is exciting and uplifting.
振奋人心 stresses boosting morale and confidence; 激动人心 stresses excitement in the moment.

cards.cue: The countdown hits zero, the rocket lifts off, and the whole crowd jumps to its feet cheering. What kind of moment is it?

ctx.s: 宣布我们队夺冠的那一刻，是全场最{激动人心}的时刻。
ctx.en: The announcement that our team had won the title was the most thrilling moment of the whole event.

ctx.s: 好了，下面就是{激动人心}的抽奖环节！
ctx.en: Right, now for the exciting part: the prize draw!

ctx.s: 第一次亲眼看到火箭发射，真是{激动人心}。
ctx.en: Seeing a rocket launch with my own eyes for the first time was truly thrilling.

ctx.s: 毕业典礼上，校长发表了一篇{激动人心}的演讲。
ctx.en: At the graduation ceremony, the principal gave a stirring speech.

ctx.s: 站上领奖台、听到国歌响起，难道不是很{激动人心}吗？
ctx.en: Standing on the podium and hearing the anthem play: isn't that thrilling?

ctx.s: 孩子们盼了一年的春游终于到了，这对他们来说是{激动人心}的一天。
ctx.en: The spring outing the children had looked forward to all year finally came; for them it was a thrilling day.

bad.s: 听到这个好消息，我非常{激动人心}。
bad.en: (meant: I was very excited to hear the good news)
bad.why: It describes what stirs people, not the speaker's own feeling; for that, plain 'excited' (jidong) is used.

bad.s: 医生说他的病加重了，真是一个{激动人心}的消息。
bad.en: (meant: this is shocking, upsetting news)
bad.why: It is positive and uplifting; it cannot describe bad or frightening news.

cards.mean: bullying the weak and fearing the strong
cards.lit: bully the soft, fear the hard

use.how: Predicate or attribute (欺软怕硬的人). Condemns someone who pushes the weak around but gives in to anyone strong.

near.diff: 仗势欺人 is bullying others by leaning on one's power or connections; 欺软怕硬 stresses the double standard: harsh to the weak, meek to the strong.

cards.cue: A man shouts at the waiter and the cleaner but turns polite and meek the moment the manager appears.

ctx.s: 那只大狗{欺软怕硬}，只敢冲小狗叫。
ctx.en: That big dog is a bully and a coward; it only dares to bark at small dogs.

ctx.s: “为什么他只对你发脾气？”“因为他{欺软怕硬}啊。”
ctx.en: "Why does he only lose his temper with you?" "Because he picks on the weak and backs down to the strong."

ctx.s: 你别怕他，这种人{欺软怕硬}，你一强硬他就退了。
ctx.en: Don't be afraid of him; his type bullies the weak, and the moment you stand firm he backs off.

ctx.s: 他对新人大呼小叫，见了经理却一声不吭，真是{欺软怕硬}。
ctx.en: He yells at the new staff but doesn't say a word in front of the manager; a classic bully.

ctx.s: 小时候班上有个{欺软怕硬}的男生，专挑个子小的同学欺负。
ctx.en: When I was little there was a boy in my class who picked on the weak and only ever bullied the small kids.

ctx.s: 有的商家{欺软怕硬}，老实人投诉没人理，会闹的马上退款。
ctx.en: Some shops bully the meek: quiet customers' complaints get ignored, while those who kick up a fuss get refunds at once.

bad.s: 他{欺软怕硬}，所以从来不跟人吵架。
bad.en: (meant: he is timid and avoids conflict)
bad.why: It is not mere timidity; it means bullying the weak while giving in to the strong.

bad.s: 这位警察{欺软怕硬}，总是保护弱者。
bad.en: (meant: he stands up to the strong to protect the weak)
bad.why: That is the opposite: the idiom condemns someone who bullies the weak, not one who protects them.

cards.mean: snide and sarcastic in manner
cards.lit: yin and yang, a strange air: an odd, ambiguous manner

use.how: Adverbial (阴阳怪气地说), predicate or complement (说话阴阳怪气的). Describes a veiled, insinuating tone that says one thing and means a jab.

near.diff: 冷嘲热讽 is open mockery and ridicule; 阴阳怪气 is an indirect, insinuating tone where the jab is hidden.

cards.cue: Hearing you got the promotion, a coworker smirks: 'Oh, congratulations, boss, we're all so lucky to have you.' How is he talking?

ctx.s: 有话直说，别{阴阳怪气}的。
ctx.en: If you've got something to say, say it straight; stop being snide.

ctx.s: 她最近说话总是{阴阳怪气}的，是不是对我有意见？
ctx.en: She's been so snide with me lately; does she have a problem with me?

ctx.s: 他一听我升职了，就{阴阳怪气}地说：“哟，以后得叫你领导了。”
ctx.en: As soon as he heard about my promotion, he sneered: "Oh, I suppose I'll have to call you boss now."

ctx.s: 我只是晚到了五分钟，你用不着这么{阴阳怪气}吧？
ctx.en: I was only five minutes late; there's no need to be so sarcastic, is there?

ctx.s: 网上有些评论{阴阳怪气}，看了让人很不舒服。
ctx.en: Some online comments are so snide they make you feel uncomfortable reading them.

ctx.s: 她嘴上说“你真厉害”，可那{阴阳怪气}的语气谁都听得出来。
ctx.en: She said "Aren't you clever", but everyone could hear the sarcasm in her voice.

bad.s: 他讲笑话很{阴阳怪气}，大家都笑得很开心。
bad.en: (meant: he tells jokes in a quirky, funny way)
bad.why: It criticises a snide, insinuating tone; it is not praise for quirky humour.

bad.s: 他气坏了，{阴阳怪气}地大骂了我一顿。
bad.en: (meant: he was furious and shouted at me)
bad.why: It describes veiled, indirect sarcasm, not open, angry shouting.

cards.mean: in total uproar (a household in chaos)
cards.lit: the chickens fly up and the dogs leap about

use.how: Predicate or complement after 得 (闹得鸡飞狗跳, 忙得鸡飞狗跳). Said of a home or group thrown into noisy commotion, often wryly.

near.diff: 鸡犬不宁 stresses that someone's harassment gives everyone no peace; 鸡飞狗跳 paints the noisy scene of everyone rushing about.
乱七八糟 is a messy state of things; 鸡飞狗跳 is a commotion of people in motion.

cards.cue: The alarm didn't go off, the kids can't find their shoes, the dog is barking and everyone is running around shouting.

ctx.s: 两个孩子一闹，家里就{鸡飞狗跳}的。
ctx.en: Once the two kids start acting up, the house is in total uproar.

ctx.s: 早上全家都起晚了，忙得{鸡飞狗跳}。
ctx.en: The whole family overslept this morning, and it was utter chaos.

ctx.s: “你家猫又干什么了？”“它打翻了鱼缸，家里一下子{鸡飞狗跳}。”
ctx.en: "What has your cat done now?" "It knocked over the fish tank and the whole house went into uproar."

ctx.s: 装修那个月，我们家天天{鸡飞狗跳}。
ctx.en: The month we were renovating, our home was in chaos every day.

ctx.s: 过年时亲戚们进进出出，屋里{鸡飞狗跳}。
ctx.en: At New Year, relatives were coming and going, and the house was in uproar.

ctx.s: 新经理一来就改了所有规定，整个部门被搞得{鸡飞狗跳}。
ctx.en: The new manager changed every rule the moment he arrived, and the whole department was thrown into chaos.

bad.s: 他的书桌上{鸡飞狗跳}，到处都是纸。
bad.en: (meant: his desk is a mess, with papers everywhere)
bad.why: It describes a noisy commotion of people rushing about, not a still mess of objects; for a messy desk use luan qi ba zao.

bad.s: 音乐会结束时，观众{鸡飞狗跳}，热烈鼓掌。
bad.en: (meant: the audience applauded enthusiastically)
bad.why: It means chaos and disorder, not enthusiasm or warm applause.

cards.mean: petty little things (squabbles, chores)
cards.lit: chicken feathers and garlic skins: worthless scraps

use.how: Mostly an attribute: 鸡毛蒜皮的小事, 鸡毛蒜皮的矛盾. Dismisses everyday matters as too trivial to matter.

near.diff: 小题大做 is the act of making a big fuss over a small matter; 鸡毛蒜皮 names the small matter itself.

cards.cue: A couple argues for an hour over who forgot to buy toilet paper. What kind of matter are they fighting about?

ctx.s: 为了这点{鸡毛蒜皮}的小事，你们俩至于吵架吗？
ctx.en: Is it really worth you two fighting over such a petty little thing?

ctx.s: 他每天回家都跟我说办公室里那些{鸡毛蒜皮}的事。
ctx.en: Every day he comes home and tells me about all the petty goings-on at the office.

ctx.s: 邻居之间难免有些{鸡毛蒜皮}的矛盾，互相让一让就好了。
ctx.en: Neighbours are bound to have petty squabbles; just give a little on both sides.

ctx.s: 社区工作很琐碎，处理的大多是{鸡毛蒜皮}的事情。
ctx.en: Community work is fiddly; most of what you deal with is trivial stuff.

ctx.s: 别拿这些{鸡毛蒜皮}的事去烦老板，你自己处理就行。
ctx.en: Don't bother the boss with these trivial things; just handle them yourself.

ctx.s: 伤感情的往往不是大事，而是一件件{鸡毛蒜皮}的小事。
ctx.en: What hurts a relationship is often not the big things but one petty little thing after another.

bad.s: 这次地震造成了很多{鸡毛蒜皮}的损失。
bad.en: (meant: the earthquake caused many small losses)
bad.why: It dismisses petty everyday matters; it cannot describe real damage, let alone from a disaster.

bad.s: 她做事很{鸡毛蒜皮}，每个细节都检查。
bad.en: (meant: she is meticulous and checks every detail)
bad.why: It describes trivial matters, not a careful, meticulous person.

cards.mean: absolutely silent, not a sound
cards.lit: not even a crow or a sparrow makes a sound

use.how: Predicate of a place or crowd: 教室里鸦雀无声, often with 顿时 or 一下子. Describes a group of people who are, or suddenly fall, completely silent.

near.diff: 夜深人静 is the quiet of late night when everyone is asleep; 鸦雀无声 is a roomful of people making no sound.

cards.cue: The teacher slams a book on the desk, and the noisy class of forty instantly stops talking. Not a sound.

ctx.s: 老师一走进来，教室里马上{鸦雀无声}。
ctx.en: The moment the teacher walked in, the classroom went dead quiet.

ctx.s: 刚才还吵吵闹闹的，怎么一下子{鸦雀无声}了？
ctx.en: It was so noisy a second ago; why has everyone suddenly gone silent?

ctx.s: 考场里{鸦雀无声}，只听见笔在纸上写字的声音。
ctx.en: The exam hall was utterly silent except for the scratching of pens on paper.

ctx.s: 电影放到最后一幕，整个电影院{鸦雀无声}。
ctx.en: When the film reached its final scene, the whole cinema was completely silent.

ctx.s: 他说完那句话，会议室里顿时{鸦雀无声}，谁也不敢接话。
ctx.en: When he finished saying that, the meeting room fell silent and nobody dared respond.

ctx.s: 校长问是谁打碎了窗户，台下{鸦雀无声}。
ctx.en: The principal asked who had broken the window, and the assembly was utterly silent.

bad.s: 我的手机一整天{鸦雀无声}，一个电话也没有。
bad.en: (meant: my phone was silent all day, no calls)
bad.why: It describes a place or crowd of people being silent, not a phone with no calls.

bad.s: 他{鸦雀无声}地看着我，什么都没说。
bad.en: (meant: he looked at me without a word)
bad.why: It is said of a place full of people, not of one person keeping quiet; for that say yi sheng bu keng.

cards.mean: the slow must start early (often said modestly)
cards.lit: the clumsy bird takes off first

use.how: A clause on its own, often 笨鸟先飞嘛 or 我是笨鸟先飞. Usually said modestly of oneself to explain starting early or working extra.

near.diff: 勤能补拙 is a general maxim that hard work makes up for lack of talent; 笨鸟先飞 is about starting earlier than others.

cards.cue: Knowing you're slower than your classmates, you begin revising a month before anyone else. How do you modestly explain it?

ctx.s: “你怎么这么早就开始复习了？”“{笨鸟先飞}嘛，我基础差。”
ctx.en: "Why have you started revising so early?" "The slow bird has to set off first; my basics are weak."

ctx.s: 我学得慢，只好{笨鸟先飞}，每天早到一个小时练习。
ctx.en: I'm a slow learner, so I have to make up for it by coming in an hour early to practise.

ctx.s: 我知道自己不如别人聪明，所以{笨鸟先飞}，暑假就开始预习了。
ctx.en: I know I'm not as bright as the others, so I got a head start and began preparing in the summer holidays.

ctx.s: 他总说自己是{笨鸟先飞}，其实他是我们组最能干的。
ctx.en: He always says he just starts early to make up for being slow, but he's actually the most capable in our group.

ctx.s: 刚进公司那年，她{笨鸟先飞}，每天最早一个到办公室。
ctx.en: Her first year at the company, she made up for inexperience by being first into the office every day.

ctx.s: 学外语没有捷径，{笨鸟先飞}，早点开始总没错。
ctx.en: There are no shortcuts in learning a language; if you're slow, start early, and you can't go wrong.

bad.s: 他总是拖到最后一天才开始写作业，真是{笨鸟先飞}。
bad.en: (meant: he always leaves his homework to the last minute)
bad.why: It means starting early to make up for being slow; it cannot describe putting things off until the last minute.

bad.s: 他最聪明，所以{笨鸟先飞}，第一个交了卷。
bad.en: (meant: he is the smartest, so he finished first)
bad.why: It means starting early to make up for being slow, not finishing first because of talent.

cards.mean: birds singing and flowers blooming
cards.lit: the language of birds and the fragrance of flowers

use.how: Predicate or attributive describing a place, usually in spring: 公园里鸟语花香 / 一个鸟语花香的早晨. Said of gardens, parks and countryside.

near.diff: 春暖花开 marks the season when it turns warm and things bloom; 鸟语花香 paints a particular place full of birdsong and scent.

cards.cue: You step into a garden on an April morning: songbirds in every tree and the scent of blossom in the air. How do you describe the place?

ctx.s: 春天的公园里{鸟语花香}，很多人来散步。
ctx.en: In spring the park is full of birdsong and flowers, and lots of people come for a walk.

ctx.s: 这个小区种了很多树，早上推开窗就是一片{鸟语花香}。
ctx.en: This estate has planted lots of trees; open the window in the morning and it's all birdsong and blossom.

ctx.s: “你老家怎么样？”“院子里种满了花，树上整天有鸟叫，真是{鸟语花香}。”
ctx.en: "What's your hometown like?" "The yard is full of flowers and birds sing in the trees all day; it's all birdsong and blossom."

ctx.s: 她在作文里写道：清晨的校园{鸟语花香}，同学们在大声读书。
ctx.en: She wrote in her essay: in the early morning the campus is full of birdsong and flowers, and students are reading aloud.

ctx.s: 退休后他在院子里种花养鸟，家里一年到头{鸟语花香}。
ctx.en: After retiring he planted flowers and kept birds in his yard, so all year round his home is full of birdsong and blossom.

ctx.s: 这家民宿的院子里{鸟语花香}，早上是被鸟叫醒的。
ctx.en: The courtyard of this guesthouse is full of birdsong and flowers; in the morning you wake up to the birds.

bad.s: 这道菜{鸟语花香}，大家都喜欢吃。
bad.en: (meant: this dish smells wonderful)
bad.why: It describes a natural scene with birds and flowers, not the smell or taste of food.

bad.s: 他说话{鸟语花香}，大家都爱听。
bad.en: (meant: he speaks sweetly and pleasantly)
bad.why: It is not about pleasant speech; niǎo yǔ is birdsong, and the phrase describes a place, never a person's way of talking.

cards.mean: the warmth and blossom of spring
cards.lit: spring turns warm and the flowers open

use.how: Often a time expression for when winter is over: 等到春暖花开的时候 / 春暖花开的季节; also a predicate: 北京春暖花开了.

near.diff: 鸟语花香 describes how a place looks and sounds; 春暖花开 names the time of year when it gets warm and things bloom.

cards.cue: Your friend wants to visit now, in January. You suggest waiting until the cold is over and the trees are in blossom.

ctx.s: 等到{春暖花开}的时候，我们一起去爬山吧。
ctx.en: When spring comes and the flowers are out, let's go hiking together.

ctx.s: 三月底，北京终于{春暖花开}了。
ctx.en: By the end of March, Beijing has finally warmed up and come into bloom.

ctx.s: “什么时候去南京最好？”“{春暖花开}的四月，到处都是樱花。”
ctx.en: "When is the best time to go to Nanjing?" "April, when it's warm and blooming; there are cherry blossoms everywhere."

ctx.s: 冬天太冷，这家农场要到{春暖花开}才重新开放。
ctx.en: Winter is too cold; this farm won't reopen until spring warms up and things bloom.

ctx.s: 经过一个漫长的冬天，人们都盼着{春暖花开}。
ctx.en: After a long winter, everyone is longing for the warmth and flowers of spring.

ctx.s: 老人说，熬过这个冬天，到了{春暖花开}，身体就会好起来。
ctx.en: The old man said that once he got through this winter, when spring came, his health would pick up.

bad.s: 十月的北京{春暖花开}，最适合旅游。
bad.en: (meant: Beijing in October has lovely weather)
bad.why: It refers only to spring. For pleasant autumn weather the idiom is qiū gāo qì shuǎng.

bad.s: 他升职以后，心情{春暖花开}。
bad.en: (meant: after his promotion he was in a great mood)
bad.why: It describes the season, not a person's mood. For great joy say xīn huā nù fàng, or simply that he is very happy.

cards.mean: crisp, clear autumn weather
cards.lit: in autumn the sky is high and the air is crisp

use.how: Predicate or attributive about autumn weather only: 十月秋高气爽 / 秋高气爽的日子. Often used when recommending outings.

near.diff: 风和日丽 is a calm sunny day in any mild season; 秋高气爽 is specifically the clear, cool, dry feel of autumn.

cards.cue: It's late September: the summer humidity has gone, the sky looks high and blue, and the air feels cool and clean.

ctx.s: 十月的北京{秋高气爽}，是旅游的好季节。
ctx.en: In October Beijing has clear, crisp autumn weather; it's a great season to visit.

ctx.s: 国庆节前后{秋高气爽}，很多人去郊外爬山。
ctx.en: Around National Day in early October the autumn air is clear and crisp, and lots of people go hiking outside the city.

ctx.s: “这几天天气怎么样？”“{秋高气爽}，不冷不热，特别舒服。”
ctx.en: "How's the weather these days?" "Clear and crisp, not cold, not hot; really comfortable."

ctx.s: 运动会选在九月底举行，正赶上{秋高气爽}。
ctx.en: The sports day was held at the end of September, just in time for the clear autumn weather.

ctx.s: 夏天闷热了好几个月，现在终于{秋高气爽}了。
ctx.en: After months of muggy summer, it's finally cool and clear autumn weather.

ctx.s: 夏天的潮气终于散了，趁着{秋高气爽}，把被子拿出去晒晒吧。
ctx.en: The summer damp has finally gone; let's take the quilts out to air while the autumn weather is dry and clear.

bad.s: 四月{秋高气爽}，花都开了。
bad.en: (meant: April has lovely weather and the flowers are out)
bad.why: It is only said of autumn. For warm, blooming spring weather use chūn nuǎn huā kāi.

bad.s: 他这个人{秋高气爽}，从来不生气。
bad.en: (meant: he's cheerful and easygoing)
bad.why: It describes weather, not personality; shuǎng here is crisp air. For an easygoing person say kāi lǎng or shuǎng kuai.

cards.mean: a frozen world of ice and snow
cards.lit: ice in the sky, snow on the ground

use.how: Describes a deeply frozen landscape or winter, often 在冰天雪地里 or as a predicate: 东北的冬天冰天雪地. Often stresses hardship.

cards.cue: Your friend in the far north sends a photo in January: frozen rivers, snow piled high everywhere, thirty below outside.

ctx.s: 东北的冬天{冰天雪地}，外面经常零下二十多度。
ctx.en: Winters in the Northeast are a world of ice and snow; it's often more than twenty below outside.

ctx.s: 孩子们在{冰天雪地}里堆雪人，玩得很开心。
ctx.en: The children were building snowmen out in the ice and snow, having a great time.

ctx.s: “你在哈尔滨冷不冷？”“外面{冰天雪地}，可屋里有暖气，一点儿也不冷。”
ctx.en: "Are you cold in Harbin?" "Outside it's all ice and snow, but there's heating indoors, so I'm not cold at all."

ctx.s: 快递员在{冰天雪地}中送货，真不容易。
ctx.en: Couriers delivering parcels through the ice and snow have a really hard time.

ctx.s: 登山队被困在{冰天雪地}的山顶上，等了两天才获救。
ctx.en: The climbing team was trapped on the frozen, snowbound summit and waited two days to be rescued.

ctx.s: 他从海南来，第一次见到这样{冰天雪地}的景象，兴奋得大叫。
ctx.en: He's from Hainan, and seeing a frozen, snow-covered landscape like this for the first time, he shouted with excitement.

bad.s: 今天有点凉，外面{冰天雪地}，多穿件外套吧。
bad.en: (meant: it's a bit chilly today)
bad.why: It means everything is frozen and covered in snow; far too strong for merely cool weather.

bad.s: 她对我{冰天雪地}，一句话也不说。
bad.en: (meant: she was cold toward me)
bad.why: It is not used for a cold attitude toward someone; for that say lěng bīng bīng or lěng dàn.

cards.mean: sunny with a gentle breeze
cards.lit: the wind is gentle and the sun is beautiful

use.how: Predicate or attributive about the weather on a given day: 那天风和日丽 / 一个风和日丽的下午. Often sets the scene for an outing or event.

near.diff: 秋高气爽 is the crisp, dry feel of autumn; 风和日丽 is any calm, sunny, mild day, most often in spring.

cards.cue: The sun is out, there's only a light breeze, not a cloud in sight: perfect for the picnic you planned for today.

ctx.s: 春天到了，今天又{风和日丽}，我们去公园放风筝吧。
ctx.en: Spring is here and today is sunny with a gentle breeze; let's go and fly kites in the park.

ctx.s: 婚礼那天{风和日丽}，所有照片都拍得很好看。
ctx.en: The wedding day was sunny and calm, and all the photos came out beautifully.

ctx.s: “明天天气怎么样？”“预报说{风和日丽}，适合出门。”
ctx.en: "What's the weather tomorrow?" "The forecast says sunny and mild, good for going out."

ctx.s: 一个{风和日丽}的下午，他们在湖上划船。
ctx.en: One sunny, breezy afternoon, they went rowing on the lake.

ctx.s: 刚才还{风和日丽}的海面，突然刮起了大风。
ctx.en: The sea, calm and sunny a moment ago, was suddenly hit by a strong wind.

ctx.s: 老人们喜欢趁{风和日丽}的时候出来晒太阳。
ctx.en: The old folks like to come out and sit in the sun when the weather is mild and sunny.

bad.s: 外面{风和日丽}，下着小雨。
bad.en: (meant: the weather is mild, with light rain)
bad.why: It means sunny and calm; it cannot describe a rainy day.

bad.s: 他们俩的关系一直{风和日丽}。
bad.en: (meant: their relationship has always been smooth)
bad.why: It describes weather only; for a harmonious relationship say hé mù, or simply that they get on well.

cards.mean: come rain or shine
cards.lit: neither wind nor rain can stop it

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (风雨无阻地) about a routine or commitment that goes on whatever the weather: 他每天跑步，风雨无阻. Also used on notices.

cards.cue: For twenty years the old man has walked his dog at six every morning, through storms and snow, never missing a day.

ctx.s: 爷爷每天早上去公园锻炼，{风雨无阻}。
ctx.en: Grandpa goes to the park to exercise every morning, rain or shine.

ctx.s: 这位快递员十年来{风雨无阻}，从没耽误过一次送货。
ctx.en: For ten years this courier has worked in all weathers and never once delayed a delivery.

ctx.s: “下这么大的雨，你还去跑步？”“说好了{风雨无阻}，当然去。”
ctx.en: "You're still going running in rain like this?" "We agreed rain or shine, so of course I'm going."

ctx.s: 她{风雨无阻}地接送孩子上学，从来没迟到过。
ctx.en: She takes her child to and from school in all weathers and has never once been late.

ctx.s: 这个早市每天清晨开门，{风雨无阻}。
ctx.en: This morning market opens at dawn every day, whatever the weather.

ctx.s: 活动通知上写着：比赛照常进行，{风雨无阻}。
ctx.en: The event notice said: the race will go ahead as planned, rain or shine.

bad.s: 今天{风雨无阻}，我们去爬山吧。
bad.en: (meant: the weather is fine today)
bad.why: It does not describe the weather; it says someone keeps going in spite of bad weather.

bad.s: 他做事{风雨无阻}，谁的话都不听。
bad.en: (meant: he's stubborn and won't listen)
bad.why: It praises dependable persistence through bad weather, not stubbornness toward people.

cards.mean: green hills and clear waters
cards.lit: the hills are green and the waters are lovely

use.how: Predicate or attributive praising the natural scenery of a region: 这里山清水秀 / 山清水秀的小镇.

near.diff: 鸟语花香 is the sound and scent of a garden in spring; 山清水秀 is the landscape of hills and rivers, in any season.

cards.cue: You're describing a village in the south: green hills rise all around it and a clear river winds past the houses.

ctx.s: 桂林{山清水秀}，每年吸引很多游客。
ctx.en: Guilin has beautiful green hills and clear rivers, and draws lots of tourists every year.

ctx.s: 她出生在南方一个{山清水秀}的小村子。
ctx.en: She was born in a small village in the south surrounded by green hills and clear water.

ctx.s: “退休以后想住哪儿？”“找个{山清水秀}的地方，种种菜，钓钓鱼。”
ctx.en: "Where do you want to live after you retire?" "Somewhere with green hills and clear rivers, where I can grow vegetables and go fishing."

ctx.s: 这里以前到处是工厂，现在治理好了，又变得{山清水秀}。
ctx.en: There used to be factories everywhere here; now it's been cleaned up and the hills and rivers are lovely again.

ctx.s: 照片上的小镇{山清水秀}，像一幅画。
ctx.en: The town in the photo, with its green hills and clear water, looks like a painting.

ctx.s: 心情不好的时候，去{山清水秀}的地方走走，会好很多。
ctx.en: When you're feeling down, a walk somewhere with green hills and clear water makes you feel much better.

bad.s: 这个城市高楼很多，真是{山清水秀}。
bad.en: (meant: this city looks impressive)
bad.why: It praises natural hills and rivers, not a cityscape of tall buildings.

bad.s: 她长得{山清水秀}，很多人追她。
bad.en: (meant: she is pretty)
bad.why: It describes landscape only; for a person's delicate good looks say méi qīng mù xiù or qīng xiù.

cards.mean: packed so tight nothing can get through
cards.lit: not even water could seep through

use.how: Usually a complement after 挤得, 堵得, 围得 (围了个水泄不通), about crowds, traffic or a cordon blocking a place.

near.diff: 滴水不漏 praises a plan or speech with no flaw; 水泄不通 describes a place physically jammed by people, cars or a cordon.

cards.cue: Thousands of fans surround the hotel entrance so tightly that nobody can get in or out.

ctx.s: 演唱会门口挤得{水泄不通}。
ctx.en: The entrance to the concert was packed solid.

ctx.s: 下班高峰，这条路堵得{水泄不通}。
ctx.en: At rush hour this road is completely jammed.

ctx.s: “你怎么迟到了？”“商场在打折，电梯口被围得{水泄不通}。”
ctx.en: "Why are you late?" "The mall's having a sale, and the lifts were completely mobbed."

ctx.s: 明星一出机场，就被粉丝围了个{水泄不通}。
ctx.en: The moment the star walked out of the airport, fans packed in around him so tight no one could move.

ctx.s: 春节前的火车站{水泄不通}，买票要排很久。
ctx.en: Before Spring Festival the railway station is jam-packed, and you queue for ages to buy a ticket.

ctx.s: 警察把事故现场围得{水泄不通}，谁也进不去。
ctx.en: The police sealed off the accident scene completely; nobody could get in.

bad.s: 这个杯子{水泄不通}，一滴水都不漏。
bad.en: (meant: this cup is watertight)
bad.why: It is about crowds, traffic or a cordon blocking a place, not about objects that don't leak.

bad.s: 他的计划{水泄不通}，没有一点漏洞。
bad.en: (meant: his plan is airtight)
bad.why: For a flawless plan or argument use dī shuǐ bù lòu or tiān yī wú fèng; this idiom means a place is physically packed.

cards.mean: to make a tense or angry situation even worse
cards.lit: to pour oil onto a fire

use.how: Predicate, or after 是, 等于, 无异于: 你这么说是火上浇油. Criticises words or actions that inflame someone's anger or a conflict.

near.diff: 雪上加霜 is one misfortune piled on another; 火上浇油 is making anger or a conflict flare up further.

cards.cue: Your manager is already furious about the delay, and a colleague picks that moment to point out three more mistakes.

ctx.s: 他已经很生气了，你别再{火上浇油}了。
ctx.en: He's already really angry; don't make it worse.

ctx.s: 妈妈正在骂弟弟，姐姐在旁边说风凉话，简直是{火上浇油}。
ctx.en: Mum was scolding my little brother, and my sister stood there making snide remarks, which only made things worse.

ctx.s: 两家公司本来就有矛盾，这篇报道更是{火上浇油}。
ctx.en: The two companies were already at odds, and this report only inflamed things further.

ctx.s: “我要不要现在去跟老板解释？”“现在去只会{火上浇油}，等他冷静了再说。”
ctx.en: "Should I go and explain to the boss now?" "Going now will only make him angrier; wait until he's calmed down."

ctx.s: 球迷本来就不满，裁判的错判无异于{火上浇油}。
ctx.en: The fans were already unhappy, and the referee's bad call was like pouring oil on the fire.

ctx.s: 吵架的时候翻旧账，等于{火上浇油}。
ctx.en: Dragging up old grievances in the middle of a fight just adds fuel to the fire.

bad.s: 他刚丢了工作，又生了病，真是{火上浇油}。
bad.en: (meant: one misfortune on top of another)
bad.why: That is xuě shàng jiā shuāng. This idiom is about making anger or a conflict flare up, not bad luck piling up.

bad.s: 大家干得正起劲，老板又发了奖金，真是{火上浇油}。
bad.en: (meant: the bonus made a good thing even better)
bad.why: It is always negative. For adding something good to what is already good, use jǐn shàng tiān huā.

cards.mean: fair and reasonable
cards.lit: in keeping with feeling and in keeping with reason

use.how: Predicate or attributive judging a request, explanation, decision or arrangement: 这个要求合情合理 / 合情合理的安排.

near.diff: 理所当然 says something naturally follows and needs no argument; 合情合理 judges it fair, both humanly and logically.

cards.cue: A worker asks for overtime pay after staying late all week. Everyone agrees the request is fair, both legally and humanly.

ctx.s: 他的要求{合情合理}，我们应该答应。
ctx.en: His request is fair and reasonable; we should agree to it.

ctx.s: 加班就给加班费，这是{合情合理}的事。
ctx.en: If you work overtime, you get overtime pay; that's only fair.

ctx.s: “我请三天假，你觉得过分吗？”“家里有急事，请假{合情合理}。”
ctx.en: "Do you think asking for three days off is too much?" "You've got a family emergency; it's perfectly reasonable."

ctx.s: 法官的判决{合情合理}，双方都接受了。
ctx.en: The judge's ruling was fair and reasonable, and both sides accepted it.

ctx.s: 这个解释听起来{合情合理}，可我总觉得哪里不对。
ctx.en: The explanation sounds perfectly reasonable, but I still feel something's off.

ctx.s: 房东涨了一点房租，考虑到物价，也算{合情合理}。
ctx.en: The landlord raised the rent a little, which, given prices, is fair enough.

bad.s: 他是个{合情合理}的人，从不乱发脾气。
bad.en: (meant: he is a reasonable, understanding person)
bad.why: It judges a request, explanation or decision, not a person's character; for a sensible, understanding person say tōng qíng dá lǐ.

bad.s: 这道数学题的答案{合情合理}。
bad.en: (meant: the answer to this maths problem is correct)
bad.why: It is about fairness in human affairs, not correctness; a maths answer is simply right or wrong.

cards.mean: openly, above board
cards.lit: bright and clear, upright and great: done in full daylight with nothing to hide

use.how: Mostly adverbial (光明正大地提出来) or a predicate (做事光明正大). Said of how something is done: in the open, by the rules, with nothing hidden.

near.diff: 光明磊落 praises a person's open, honest character; 光明正大 usually describes doing a particular thing openly rather than in secret.

cards.cue: People hint that you won the contract through a backroom deal. You insist everything was done in the open and anyone may check.

ctx.s: 我们是按规矩办事，{光明正大}，不怕别人查。
ctx.en: We did it by the rules, all in the open; we're not afraid of anyone checking.

ctx.s: 你想请假就{光明正大}地说，别装病。
ctx.en: If you want a day off, just say so openly; don't pretend to be ill.

ctx.s: 有意见可以在会上{光明正大}地提出来，何必在背后议论？
ctx.en: If you disagree, raise it openly in the meeting. Why gossip behind people's backs?

ctx.s: “这笔钱是我凭本事赚来的，来得{光明正大}！”
ctx.en: "I earned this money by my own ability; I came by it fair and square!"

ctx.s: 他喜欢她，就{光明正大}地追求，从不偷偷摸摸。
ctx.en: He liked her, so he courted her openly, never sneaking around.

ctx.s: 这次招标全程公开，评选过程{光明正大}，落选的公司也没话说。
ctx.en: The tender was public from start to finish and the selection was above board, so even the losing firms had nothing to say.

bad.s: 这个房间窗户很大，非常{光明正大}。
bad.en: (meant: the room is very bright)
bad.why: It is about honest, open conduct, not about light. A bright room is míngliàng.

bad.s: 他拿了冠军，大家都觉得非常{光明正大}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone thought it was glorious)
bad.why: It does not mean glorious or honourable (that is guāngróng); it only says something was done openly and fairly.

cards.mean: sneaky, furtive
cards.lit: like ghosts and haunting spirits, creeping about where no one should see

use.how: Adverbial (鬼鬼祟祟地看), predicate (他鬼鬼祟祟的) or attributive (鬼鬼祟祟的人). Describes someone's shifty, suspicious manner.

near.diff: 偷偷摸摸 stresses doing something secretly; 鬼鬼祟祟 stresses that the person looks shifty and suspicious while doing it.
光明正大 is its opposite: acting openly with nothing to hide.

cards.cue: A stranger keeps peering over your neighbour's fence, ducking whenever someone looks his way. How does he look?

ctx.s: 门口有个人{鬼鬼祟祟}的，一直往院子里看。
ctx.en: There's someone acting suspiciously at the gate, staring into the yard the whole time.

ctx.s: 你{鬼鬼祟祟}地躲在门后干什么？
ctx.en: What are you doing skulking behind the door?

ctx.s: 保安发现一个男人在停车场{鬼鬼祟祟}地拉车门，就上前询问。
ctx.en: The guard saw a man furtively trying car doors in the car park and went over to question him.

ctx.s: “他俩在角落里{鬼鬼祟祟}地说什么呢？”“可能在给你准备惊喜吧。”
ctx.en: "What are those two whispering about so shiftily in the corner?" "Maybe they're planning a surprise for you."

ctx.s: 雨夜里，一个{鬼鬼祟祟}的身影溜进了旅馆的后门。
ctx.en: On a rainy night, a furtive figure slipped in through the hotel's back door.

ctx.s: 有话就当面说，别总是{鬼鬼祟祟}的，让人心里不舒服。
ctx.en: If you've got something to say, say it to my face. Always sneaking around makes people uneasy.

bad.s: 侦探{鬼鬼祟祟}地破了案，大家都很佩服他。
bad.en: (meant: the detective solved the case discreetly and cleverly)
bad.why: It is a criticism of shifty, suspicious behaviour and cannot be used as praise for discretion.

bad.s: 这座老房子很{鬼鬼祟祟}，晚上没人敢进去。
bad.en: (meant: the old house is spooky)
bad.why: Despite the ghost in it, it describes how a person behaves, not an eerie or haunted place.

cards.mean: bright and quick-witted (of a child)
cards.lit: clever and nimble-minded

use.how: Predicate or attributive describing a child or young person (这孩子聪明伶俐；聪明伶俐的小姑娘). Not used of grown adults' learning, nor as an adverb.

cards.cue: Your friend's five-year-old learns a card game in one go and chats politely with every guest. How do you compliment the child?

ctx.s: 这孩子{聪明伶俐}，一教就会。
ctx.en: This child is so bright: show him once and he's got it.

ctx.s: 邻居家的小女儿{聪明伶俐}，见了谁都甜甜地打招呼。
ctx.en: The neighbours' little daughter is bright and quick, and greets everyone sweetly.

ctx.s: “你家儿子真是{聪明伶俐}啊！”“哪里哪里，就是嘴快。”
ctx.en: "Your son is so bright!" "Oh, not really, he's just a chatterbox."

ctx.s: 奶奶逢人就夸她那个{聪明伶俐}的小孙子。
ctx.en: Grandma boasts to everyone she meets about her clever little grandson.

ctx.s: 店里新来的小学徒{聪明伶俐}，师傅很喜欢他。
ctx.en: The young new apprentice at the shop is sharp and quick, and the master is very fond of him.

ctx.s: 故事里的小狐狸{聪明伶俐}，几次都骗过了猎人。
ctx.en: The little fox in the story is clever and quick-witted, and fools the hunter again and again.

bad.s: 这位老教授{聪明伶俐}，学问很深。
bad.en: (meant: the old professor is brilliant and learned)
bad.why: It praises a child's or young person's quickness and charm; said of an elderly scholar it sounds patronising.

bad.s: 他{聪明伶俐}地解决了这个技术问题。
bad.en: (meant: he solved the technical problem cleverly)
bad.why: It describes what a person is like, not how an action is done, so it is not used as an adverb before a verb.

cards.mean: clumsy
cards.lit: clumsy hands and clumsy feet

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (笨手笨脚地包饺子). Mild criticism of physical clumsiness, often said of oneself or of a beginner.

near.diff: 手忙脚乱 is being flustered because there is too much to do at once; 笨手笨脚 is lacking skill or coordination even when there is no rush.

cards.cue: Helping in a friend's kitchen, you drop an egg, knock over the salt and nick your finger peeling a potato. You apologise for being what?

ctx.s: 我{笨手笨脚}的，又把杯子打碎了。
ctx.en: I'm so clumsy, I've broken another cup.

ctx.s: 第一次包饺子，他{笨手笨脚}地捏了半天也没捏好。
ctx.en: Making dumplings for the first time, he fumbled with them for ages and still couldn't seal them.

ctx.s: “让我来吧，你{笨手笨脚}的，别把孩子弄醒了。”
ctx.en: "Let me do it; you're all thumbs, you'll wake the baby."

ctx.s: 新来的服务员有点{笨手笨脚}，客人不多也老是打翻杯子。
ctx.en: The new waiter is a bit clumsy: even when there are few customers he keeps knocking over glasses.

ctx.s: 别看他平时{笨手笨脚}，修起自行车来可灵巧了。
ctx.en: He may seem clumsy most of the time, but he's really deft when it comes to fixing bikes.

ctx.s: 小熊{笨手笨脚}地爬上树，想去够蜂蜜。
ctx.en: The little bear clambered clumsily up the tree, trying to reach the honey.

bad.s: 他{笨手笨脚}，数学总是考不及格。
bad.en: (meant: he's slow-witted and always fails maths)
bad.why: It is about clumsy hands and movements, not about intelligence or being a slow learner.

bad.s: 这把椅子太{笨手笨脚}了，搬起来很费劲。
bad.en: (meant: the chair is bulky and hard to move)
bad.why: Only people and animals have clumsy hands and feet; a bulky, heavy object is bènzhòng.

cards.mean: versatile, gifted in many arts
cards.lit: many talents, many arts

story.text: When King Wu of Zhou fell gravely ill, his brother the Duke of Zhou prayed to their ancestors and offered to die in the king's place. He argued that he himself was gifted with many talents and many arts and could serve the spirits well, while the king was less suited to it but was needed to rule the people.

use.how: Predicate or attributive about a person (她多才多艺；多才多艺的人). Praises skill across several fields such as music, art, sport or crafts.

near.diff: 才华横溢 is brimming over with talent, often in one field such as writing; 多才多艺 stresses the range of different skills.

cards.cue: Your new colleague plays the guitar at the party, shows you her oil paintings and turns out to have coached the school football team.

ctx.s: 她{多才多艺}，会弹钢琴，还会画画。
ctx.en: She's very versatile: she plays the piano and paints as well.

ctx.s: 新来的同事{多才多艺}，年会上又唱又跳。
ctx.en: Our new colleague is multi-talented: at the annual party he sang and danced.

ctx.s: “你还会做木工？真是{多才多艺}！”
ctx.en: "You do woodwork too? You really can do everything!"

ctx.s: 学校希望把学生培养成{多才多艺}的人，而不只是会考试。
ctx.en: The school wants to raise all-round, versatile students, not just good exam-takers.

ctx.s: 这位作家{多才多艺}，写小说之余还拍过两部电影。
ctx.en: This writer is remarkably versatile; besides novels, she has also made two films.

ctx.s: 别看他只是个司机，其实{多才多艺}，书法写得特别好。
ctx.en: He may only be a driver, but he's actually very gifted in many ways; his calligraphy is superb.

bad.s: 他{多才多艺}，一辈子只研究物理一门学问。
bad.en: (meant: he was extremely talented, devoting his life to physics)
bad.why: It means talented in many different areas, so it contradicts devotion to a single field.

bad.s: 这家餐厅{多才多艺}，川菜粤菜都有。
bad.en: (meant: the restaurant has a varied menu)
bad.why: It praises a person's talents, not the range of dishes or goods a business offers.

cards.mean: leaving early and coming home late
cards.lit: go out early, come back late

use.how: Predicate (他每天早出晚归). Describes someone's daily pattern of being away from home all day, for work, study or travel.

near.diff: 起早贪黑 stresses hard toil from dawn into the night; 早出晚归 only says the person leaves early and gets home late.

cards.cue: Your neighbour is gone before you wake and back after you're asleep; in a month you've hardly seen him.

ctx.s: 爸爸上班的地方很远，每天{早出晚归}，我很少能跟他一起吃饭。
ctx.en: Dad works a long way off and leaves early and comes home late every day, so I rarely get to eat with him.

ctx.s: 他最近{早出晚归}的，邻居快一个月没见到他了。
ctx.en: He's been out from early till late lately; the neighbours haven't seen him for almost a month.

ctx.s: 旅游那几天我们{早出晚归}，把城里的景点全逛遍了。
ctx.en: On that trip we went out early and came back late every day, and saw every sight in the city.

ctx.s: “你这阵子怎么{早出晚归}？”“公司搬到郊区了，路上要两个小时。”
ctx.en: "Why are you leaving so early and getting back so late these days?" "The office moved to the suburbs; it's a two-hour commute."

ctx.s: 为了不吵醒室友，他{早出晚归}时总是轻手轻脚的。
ctx.en: So as not to wake his roommate, he always moves quietly when he goes out early and comes back late.

ctx.s: 搬到新城市后，她{早出晚归}，三个月后才发现楼下有家面馆。
ctx.en: After moving to the new city she was out from morning till night, and only found the noodle shop downstairs three months later.

bad.s: 我习惯{早出晚归}，每天晚上九点就睡觉。
bad.en: (meant: I keep early hours and go to bed at nine)
bad.why: It means being out of the house from early till late, not going to bed early (that is zǎo shuì zǎo qǐ).

bad.s: 这家超市{早出晚归}，买东西很方便。
bad.en: (meant: the supermarket opens early and closes late)
bad.why: It describes a person leaving home and coming back, not a shop's long opening hours.

cards.mean: working long hours from dawn till dark
cards.lit: rise early and be greedy for the dark, working on after nightfall

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (起早贪黑地干活). Said, often with sympathy or respect, of people who toil long hours to make a living or reach a goal.

near.diff: 早出晚归 only describes leaving early and returning late; 起早贪黑 stresses the hard work filling those hours.
废寝忘食 is being so absorbed that one forgets meals and sleep; 起早贪黑 is long hours of hard labour, often out of necessity.

cards.cue: Your parents ran a small noodle stall, up before dawn to make dough and closing after dark, to pay for your schooling.

ctx.s: 他们夫妻俩{起早贪黑}地开小饭馆，供两个孩子上大学。
ctx.en: The couple worked dawn to dusk running a little restaurant to put their two children through university.

ctx.s: 为了多挣点钱，她{起早贪黑}，白天送快递，晚上去饭馆洗碗。
ctx.en: To earn a bit more, she works from dawn till dark: delivering parcels by day and washing dishes in a restaurant at night.

ctx.s: “我{起早贪黑}地干，一个月才挣这么点儿？”
ctx.en: "I slave away from morning to night, and this is all I earn in a month?"

ctx.s: 父母{起早贪黑}把我们养大，现在该我们照顾他们了。
ctx.en: Our parents worked themselves to the bone raising us; now it's our turn to look after them.

ctx.s: 菜市场的摊主大多{起早贪黑}，凌晨就去批发市场进货。
ctx.en: Most market stallholders work long hours, going to the wholesale market before dawn to buy stock.

ctx.s: 别光知道{起早贪黑}地加班，身体累垮了可不值得。
ctx.en: Don't just work overtime from dawn to dark; it isn't worth wrecking your health.

bad.s: 我们这次度假{起早贪黑}，玩得特别开心。
bad.en: (meant: on holiday we were out sightseeing from morning to night)
bad.why: It means toiling at hard work, so it clashes with a fun holiday; for a busy sightseeing day use zǎo chū wǎn guī.

bad.s: 我每天{起早贪黑}，所以精神特别好。
bad.en: (meant: I keep early hours, so I feel great)
bad.why: It means working from dawn until after dark, which is exhausting, not a healthy early-to-bed routine.

cards.mean: to make excuse after excuse
cards.lit: push it away three times, block it four times

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (别推三阻四；他推三阻四地不肯去). Criticises someone who keeps finding pretexts to dodge a request or duty.

cards.cue: You ask your flatmate to help move a sofa. First he has a call, then a sore back, then he suddenly has to go out.

ctx.s: 让他帮个小忙，他却{推三阻四}的。
ctx.en: I asked him for a small favour and he kept making excuses.

ctx.s: 你要是不想去就直说，别{推三阻四}。
ctx.en: If you don't want to go, just say so; stop making excuses.

ctx.s: 每次轮到他打扫卫生，他总是{推三阻四}，不是头疼就是有事。
ctx.en: Whenever it's his turn to clean, he finds one excuse after another: a headache, or something else to do.

ctx.s: “借你的车用一下，你{推三阻四}干什么？又不是不还。”
ctx.en: "I only want to borrow your car. Why all the excuses? I'll bring it back."

ctx.s: 房东答应修热水器，可一个多月了还在{推三阻四}。
ctx.en: The landlord promised to fix the water heater, but over a month later he's still stalling with excuses.

ctx.s: 记者想采访负责人，对方{推三阻四}，始终不肯露面。
ctx.en: The reporter wanted to interview the person in charge, but they kept putting him off and never appeared.

bad.s: 他出于礼貌{推三阻四}，最后才收下了礼物。
bad.en: (meant: out of politeness he declined the gift several times before accepting)
bad.why: It criticises dodging a duty with excuses; politely refusing a gift several times is zàisān tuīcí.

bad.s: 门卡住了，他{推三阻四}才把门推开。
bad.en: (meant: he pushed the stuck door several times before it opened)
bad.why: The pushing here is figurative, pushing a task away; it is never about physically pushing something.

cards.mean: strong and fit
cards.lit: body strong, strength robust

use.how: Predicate or attributive (他身强力壮；身强力壮的小伙子). Describes a person's physical strength, usually a young or middle-aged adult.

near.diff: 年富力强 is being in the prime of life with energy and experience, said of careers; 身强力壮 is only about bodily strength.

cards.cue: The removal men cancelled. You need someone who can carry a fridge up four flights of stairs, and your burly cousin comes to mind.

ctx.s: 他{身强力壮}，一个人就把冰箱搬上了楼。
ctx.en: He's big and strong: he carried the fridge upstairs on his own.

ctx.s: 你们几个{身强力壮}的小伙子，过来帮忙抬一下桌子。
ctx.en: You strong young lads, come and help lift this table.

ctx.s: 爷爷年轻时{身强力壮}，一口气能挑两担水。
ctx.en: When Grandpa was young he was so strong he could carry two loads of water on a pole without a rest.

ctx.s: “你{身强力壮}的，怎么连这点活儿都嫌累？”
ctx.en: "A strong fellow like you, and this little job is too tiring?"

ctx.s: 救援队挑了几名{身强力壮}的队员进山搜救。
ctx.en: The rescue team picked several of its strongest members to search the mountains.

ctx.s: 就算{身强力壮}，经常熬夜身体也会出问题。
ctx.en: Even if you're strong and fit, staying up late all the time will damage your health.

bad.s: 她有{身强力壮}的意志，从来不放弃。
bad.en: (meant: she has a strong will and never gives up)
bad.why: It is only about the physical strength of the body; a strong will is yìzhì jiānqiáng.

bad.s: 这座桥修得{身强力壮}，再大的车也能过。
bad.en: (meant: the bridge is sturdy)
bad.why: It describes people's bodies, not objects; a sturdy bridge is jiāngù or jiēshi.

cards.mean: out of breath, panting
cards.lit: breath heaving, puffing and blowing (xū xū imitates the sound of panting)

use.how: Adverbial (气喘吁吁地跑来) or predicate, often after 累得 (累得气喘吁吁). Describes heavy breathing after running, climbing or carrying.

near.diff: 筋疲力尽 is being utterly exhausted in general; 气喘吁吁 is the visible, audible panting right after exertion.

cards.cue: The lift is broken. Your friend arrives at your sixth-floor flat, chest heaving, unable to say hello for a moment.

ctx.s: 他一路跑上五楼，到了门口还在{气喘吁吁}。
ctx.en: He ran all the way up to the fifth floor and was still panting at the door.

ctx.s: 快递员{气喘吁吁}地把箱子搬到了门口。
ctx.en: Puffing and panting, the courier carried the box to the door.

ctx.s: “你怎么{气喘吁吁}的？后面有人追你吗？”
ctx.en: "Why are you so out of breath? Is someone chasing you?"

ctx.s: 才爬了几层台阶，我就{气喘吁吁}，看来真该锻炼了。
ctx.en: I'd only climbed a few flights of steps and I was already puffing; I really need to get some exercise.

ctx.s: 他{气喘吁吁}地赶到车站，火车刚刚开走。
ctx.en: He reached the station, panting, just as the train pulled out.

ctx.s: 小女孩{气喘吁吁}地跑进教室，大声说：“老师，下雪了！”
ctx.en: The little girl ran into the classroom out of breath and cried, "Teacher, it's snowing!"

bad.s: 他听了这话{气喘吁吁}，大骂起来。
bad.en: (meant: hearing that, he was furious and started shouting)
bad.why: The qì here is breath, not anger; it describes panting after exertion, not fury.

bad.s: 想了一整天方案，我心里{气喘吁吁}的。
bad.en: (meant: after a day of planning I'm mentally drained)
bad.why: It describes physical panting only and cannot be used for mental tiredness.

cards.mean: all the ups and downs of life
cards.lit: sour, sweet, bitter and spicy: the four strong flavours

use.how: A noun, usually after 人生的 or 生活中的, or as the object of 尝遍, 经历: 尝遍了人生的酸甜苦辣。

near.diff: 悲欢离合 is the joy and grief of meeting and parting with people; 酸甜苦辣 is every kind of experience, good and hard.

cards.cue: An old man looks back on eighty years: poverty, success, illness, a happy marriage, hard times. He says he has tasted it all.

ctx.s: 生活中的{酸甜苦辣}，只有自己最清楚。
ctx.en: Only you yourself really know the ups and downs of your own life.

ctx.s: 爷爷活了八十多岁，尝遍了人生的{酸甜苦辣}。
ctx.en: Grandpa has lived past eighty and has tasted every flavour of life.

ctx.s: 创业这几年，什么{酸甜苦辣}我都经历过了。
ctx.en: In these years of running my own business I've been through every high and low.

ctx.s: 这本书写出了一个小饭馆老板开店二十年的{酸甜苦辣}。
ctx.en: The book captures all the highs and lows of a small restaurant owner's twenty years in business.

ctx.s: “留学一年感觉怎么样？”“{酸甜苦辣}都有，但我不后悔。”
ctx.en: "How was your year abroad?" "A bit of everything, good and bad, but I don't regret it."

ctx.s: 同学聚会上，大家聊起毕业后各自的{酸甜苦辣}，聊到深夜。
ctx.en: At the reunion everyone talked about their ups and downs since graduation until late at night.

bad.s: 今天我中了奖，真是{酸甜苦辣}！
bad.en: (meant: I won a prize today, how wonderful!)
bad.why: It sums up a mix of good and bad experiences over time, not one happy event.

bad.s: 他{酸甜苦辣}地讲完了自己的经历。
bad.en: (meant: he told his story with mixed feelings)
bad.why: It is a noun for life's experiences, not an adverb describing how someone speaks.

cards.mean: the daily necessities of household life
cards.lit: firewood, rice, oil and salt: what a household buys every day

use.how: A noun for the practical, unromantic side of keeping a home, often 柴米油盐的琐事 or 过日子离不开柴米油盐。

cards.cue: After the honeymoon, a young couple's talk turns to rent, groceries and who pays the electricity bill.

ctx.s: 结婚以后，每天想的都是{柴米油盐}。
ctx.en: After getting married, all you think about every day is the household basics.

ctx.s: 过日子哪能离得开{柴米油盐}？
ctx.en: How can you run a household without thinking about everyday necessities?

ctx.s: 她年轻时爱写诗，现在整天忙着{柴米油盐}的琐事。
ctx.en: She loved writing poetry when she was young; now she's busy all day with household chores and shopping.

ctx.s: 父母一辈子为{柴米油盐}操劳，从来没出过远门。
ctx.en: My parents spent their whole lives toiling over daily necessities and never travelled far.

ctx.s: “你们俩吵什么？”“还不是{柴米油盐}那点事。”
ctx.en: "What are you two arguing about?" "Oh, just the usual household stuff."

ctx.s: 爱情再浪漫，最后也要面对{柴米油盐}。
ctx.en: However romantic love is, in the end it has to face the realities of daily life.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜放了很多{柴米油盐}，太咸了。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant's food has too much seasoning)
bad.why: It stands for the everyday business of running a home, not for the actual seasoning in a dish.

bad.s: 公司今年的{柴米油盐}增加了很多。
bad.en: (meant: the company's operating costs rose a lot)
bad.why: It belongs to family and household life, not to a company's budget or expenses.

cards.mean: to rack one's brains
cards.lit: to wring out the last of one's brain juice

use.how: A verb phrase, often followed by 也 or a purpose: 绞尽脑汁想办法。It takes no object of its own.

cards.cue: You have to think of a birthday present for someone who already has everything, and you sit for an hour getting nowhere.

ctx.s: 我{绞尽脑汁}，也想不出该送她什么礼物。
ctx.en: I racked my brains but couldn't think what present to give her.

ctx.s: 为了写好这篇作文，他{绞尽脑汁}想了一个晚上。
ctx.en: To write this essay well he racked his brains all evening.

ctx.s: 这道题我{绞尽脑汁}都没做出来，你会吗？
ctx.en: I racked my brains over this problem and still couldn't solve it. Can you?

ctx.s: 广告公司{绞尽脑汁}，终于想出了一句好口号。
ctx.en: The ad agency racked its brains and finally came up with a good slogan.

ctx.s: “孩子不爱吃蔬菜怎么办？”“我也{绞尽脑汁}了，什么办法都试过。”
ctx.en: "What do you do when your kid won't eat vegetables?" "I've racked my brains too, I've tried everything."

ctx.s: 为了给新店起个好名字，老板{绞尽脑汁}。
ctx.en: The owner racked his brains to find a good name for the new shop.

bad.s: 他{绞尽脑汁}地搬了一下午箱子。
bad.en: (meant: he worked very hard moving boxes all afternoon)
bad.why: It is hard mental effort to think of something, not physical labour.

bad.s: 我{绞尽脑汁}这个问题好几天了。
bad.en: (meant: I've been racking my brains over this problem for days)
bad.why: It takes no direct object; the problem must be linked by a preposition or by a following verb such as 'think'.

cards.mean: a sudden flash of inspiration
cards.lit: the clever mind suddenly stirs

use.how: Usually opens a clause in narration, followed by the idea it produced: 他灵机一动，想出了一个办法。

near.diff: 心血来潮 is a sudden whim to do something; 灵机一动 is a sudden clever idea that solves a problem.

cards.cue: Locked out with no key, a girl suddenly remembers the window above the back door is never shut, and that is how she gets in.

ctx.s: 他{灵机一动}，想出了一个好办法。
ctx.en: Suddenly it came to him, and he thought of a good solution.

ctx.s: 雨伞忘带了，我{灵机一动}，把文件夹顶在头上跑回了家。
ctx.en: I'd forgotten my umbrella, so on a sudden inspiration I held my folder over my head and ran home.

ctx.s: 饭店里没有生日蛋糕，服务员{灵机一动}，在面条上插了一根蜡烛。
ctx.en: The restaurant had no birthday cake, so the waiter had a bright idea and stuck a candle in a bowl of noodles.

ctx.s: 听说这个产品是设计师{灵机一动}想出来的？
ctx.en: I hear the designer came up with this product in a flash of inspiration?

ctx.s: 眼看比赛要输了，教练{灵机一动}，换上了一名新队员。
ctx.en: With the game about to be lost, the coach had a sudden idea and sent on a new player.

ctx.s: “你怎么想到这样修的？”“当时{灵机一动}，就试了试。”
ctx.en: "How did you think of fixing it like that?" "It just came to me at the time, so I gave it a try."

bad.s: 他{灵机一动}，花了三个月才想出这个方案。
bad.en: (meant: after careful thought he worked out this plan)
bad.why: It is a sudden idea in a moment, which contradicts months of slow thinking.

bad.s: 他是一个很{灵机一动}的人，反应特别快。
bad.en: (meant: he is a very quick-witted person)
bad.why: It names one sudden idea at one moment, not a personal trait; it cannot take 'very' or describe a person.

cards.mean: grinning cheekily, not taking it seriously
cards.lit: playful skin and a laughing face

use.how: Describes someone grinning and joking when they should be serious, often after 别 or as an adverbial with 地: 别嬉皮笑脸的！

near.diff: 油嘴滑舌 is about glib, flippant talk; 嬉皮笑脸 is about the cheeky grinning face and attitude.

cards.cue: A teacher is scolding a boy for breaking a window, and the boy just keeps grinning at her as if it were a joke.

ctx.s: 别{嬉皮笑脸}的，我在跟你说正经事！
ctx.en: Wipe that grin off your face, I'm talking to you about something serious!

ctx.s: 老师批评他，他还{嬉皮笑脸}地顶嘴。
ctx.en: When the teacher told him off, he still grinned cheekily and talked back.

ctx.s: 你闯了这么大的祸，怎么还{嬉皮笑脸}？
ctx.en: You've caused all this trouble, and you're still grinning about it?

ctx.s: 他一进门就{嬉皮笑脸}地向妈妈要零花钱。
ctx.en: As soon as he came in he started wheedling his mum for pocket money with a cheeky grin.

ctx.s: 拍证件照要严肃一点，别{嬉皮笑脸}的。
ctx.en: You have to look serious for an ID photo, so stop grinning.

ctx.s: 爸爸气得脸都红了，弟弟却还是一副{嬉皮笑脸}的样子。
ctx.en: Dad was red in the face with anger, but my little brother still had that cheeky grin on.

bad.s: 宝宝看到妈妈，{嬉皮笑脸}的，真可爱。
bad.en: (meant: the baby smiled happily when it saw its mother)
bad.why: It criticises cheekiness when one should be serious; it cannot describe a baby's innocent, happy smile.

bad.s: 她有一张{嬉皮笑脸}，大家都很喜欢她。
bad.en: (meant: she has a sweet smiling face that everyone likes)
bad.why: It is not praise and not a noun for a pretty face; it describes a cheeky, unserious attitude.

cards.mean: glib and flippant
cards.lit: an oily mouth and a slippery tongue

use.how: Describes a person or their talk as glib, joking and insincere, as a predicate or after 别: 这个人油嘴滑舌的。

near.diff: 花言巧语 is sweet talk meant to deceive; 油嘴滑舌 is glib, cheeky banter that just cannot be trusted or taken seriously.

cards.cue: A salesman answers every serious question with a quip and a wink, and you feel you can't believe a word he says.

ctx.s: 这个人{油嘴滑舌}的，说话一点也不靠谱。
ctx.en: That guy is all glib talk; nothing he says is reliable.

ctx.s: 少跟我{油嘴滑舌}，好好说话，你到底去哪儿了？
ctx.en: Cut the smart talk and speak properly: where did you actually go?

ctx.s: 她不喜欢{油嘴滑舌}的男生，更喜欢踏实的人。
ctx.en: She doesn't like smooth-talking boys; she prefers someone steady and down-to-earth.

ctx.s: 电话里我问他正经问题，他却{油嘴滑舌}，满嘴俏皮话。
ctx.en: On the phone I asked him a serious question, and he just gave me glib quips.

ctx.s: 做销售要会说话，但不能{油嘴滑舌}，否则客户不信任你。
ctx.en: In sales you need to talk well, but you can't be glib, or customers won't trust you.

ctx.s: 别看他平时说话{油嘴滑舌}，关键时刻还挺可靠。
ctx.en: He may talk all glib banter day to day, but when it counts he's quite dependable.

bad.s: 他{油嘴滑舌}，口才很好，在辩论赛上拿了第一。
bad.en: (meant: he is very eloquent and won the debate)
bad.why: It criticises flippant, insincere talk; it is never praise for real eloquence in a debate.

bad.s: 这道菜太油了，吃完我{油嘴滑舌}的。
bad.en: (meant: the dish was so greasy my mouth felt oily)
bad.why: It is only used figuratively about a way of talking, never about food or a greasy mouth.

cards.mean: full of festive cheer
cards.lit: an air of joy spreading far and wide

use.how: Describes people's faces or a whole place full of joy over a happy occasion, as a predicate or with 地 and 的: 家家户户喜气洋洋。

near.diff: 兴高采烈 is lively excitement about doing something; 喜气洋洋 is the happy glow of a celebration or good news, often of a whole place.

cards.cue: On New Year's Eve the whole village is hung with red lanterns and every family is laughing and setting off firecrackers.

ctx.s: 春节到了，家家户户{喜气洋洋}。
ctx.en: Spring Festival has arrived and every household is full of festive cheer.

ctx.s: 婚礼现场布置得{喜气洋洋}的，到处都是红色。
ctx.en: The wedding venue was decorated in festive style, with red everywhere.

ctx.s: 女儿考上了大学，家里一下子{喜气洋洋}的。
ctx.en: Our daughter got into university, and suddenly the whole house was full of joy.

ctx.s: 丰收以后，村子里到处{喜气洋洋}。
ctx.en: After the bumper harvest, the whole village was full of festive cheer.

ctx.s: 今天办公室里怎么{喜气洋洋}的？有什么喜事吗？
ctx.en: Why is the office so full of cheer today? Is there something to celebrate?

ctx.s: 球队夺冠的消息传来，整个城市{喜气洋洋}。
ctx.en: When the news of the team's championship came, the whole city was in a festive mood.

bad.s: 他每天下班回家，{喜气洋洋}地躺在沙发上看电视。
bad.en: (meant: every day after work he relaxes contentedly on the sofa)
bad.why: It describes the joy of a happy occasion or good news, not ordinary daily relaxation.

bad.s: 大家都很{喜气洋洋}这个好消息。
bad.en: (meant: everyone is delighted about the good news)
bad.why: It takes no object and is not modified by 'very'; the cause goes in a separate clause before it.

cards.mean: sighing and moaning
cards.lit: making sounds of 'ai' and heaving sighs

use.how: A verb phrase for audible sighing out of worry or gloom, often criticised: 别整天唉声叹气的。Takes no object.

near.diff: 垂头丧气 is a dejected look, head hanging; 唉声叹气 is the audible sighing and complaining.

cards.cue: Your flatmate keeps letting out long, heavy sighs at his desk, over and over, and you finally ask what's wrong.

ctx.s: 别整天{唉声叹气}的，事情总会解决的。
ctx.en: Stop sighing all day long; it'll get sorted out eventually.

ctx.s: 他一边看工资单，一边{唉声叹气}。
ctx.en: He kept sighing as he looked at his payslip.

ctx.s: 你从早上起就{唉声叹气}，到底出什么事了？
ctx.en: You've been sighing since this morning. What on earth has happened?

ctx.s: {唉声叹气}解决不了问题，不如想想办法。
ctx.en: Sighing won't solve anything; better to think of a way out.

ctx.s: 奶奶听说菜价又涨了，忍不住{唉声叹气}起来。
ctx.en: When Grandma heard vegetable prices had gone up again, she couldn't help sighing and grumbling.

ctx.s: 考试成绩出来以后，教室里一片{唉声叹气}。
ctx.en: When the exam results came out, the classroom was filled with sighs.

bad.s: 听到这个好消息，他高兴得{唉声叹气}。
bad.en: (meant: he was so happy he gave a sigh of relief)
bad.why: It expresses worry or gloom, never happiness; a sigh of relief is a different expression.

bad.s: 他一直在{唉声叹气}自己的工作。
bad.en: (meant: he keeps moaning about his job)
bad.why: It takes no object; the cause must come before it, after a preposition or in a separate clause.

cards.mean: unexpected, contrary to expectations
cards.lit: going beyond what was expected

use.how: As a predicate (结果出乎意料), an attributive with 的, an adverbial with 地 (出乎意料地好), or opening 出乎意料的是。

cards.cue: Everyone was sure the favourite would win the final easily, but an unknown newcomer beat him in straight sets.

ctx.s: 比赛的结果{出乎意料}。
ctx.en: The result of the match was unexpected.

ctx.s: 这家小店的菜{出乎意料}地好吃。
ctx.en: The food at this little place was surprisingly good.

ctx.s: {出乎意料}的是，平时最安静的她第一个举了手。
ctx.en: Unexpectedly, she, usually the quietest, was the first to raise her hand.

ctx.s: 新手机的销量{出乎意料}，连公司自己都没想到。
ctx.en: Sales of the new phone were beyond expectations; even the company hadn't seen it coming.

ctx.s: “面试顺利吗？”“{出乎意料}地顺利，他们当场就录用了我。”
ctx.en: "Did the interview go well?" "Surprisingly well, they hired me on the spot."

ctx.s: 我以为他会生气，没想到他的反应这么平静，真是{出乎意料}。
ctx.en: I thought he'd be angry, but he reacted so calmly. It was a real surprise.

bad.s: 天气预报说今天下雨，果然{出乎意料}地下雨了。
bad.en: (meant: as forecast, it rained)
bad.why: It means against expectations, but 'as expected' in the same sentence says the opposite.

bad.s: 这个结果{出乎意料}了我。
bad.en: (meant: this result surprised me)
bad.why: It takes no object; to name the person surprised, 'my' goes inside it, between its two halves.

cards.mean: just in case
cards.lit: to guard against the one chance in ten thousand

use.how: Usually after a clause stating a precaution, or after 为了: 多带点钱，以防万一。It does not take a clause of its own.

near.diff: 有备无患 states the principle that preparation removes worry; 以防万一 explains one specific small precaution.
未雨绸缪 is planning well ahead for future trouble, more formal; 以防万一 is an everyday small precaution.

cards.cue: The sky is clear, but before leaving you still slip a small umbrella into your bag. Why bother?

ctx.s: 今天可能下雨，带把伞吧，{以防万一}。
ctx.en: It might rain today; take an umbrella, just in case.

ctx.s: 我又把文件备份了一份，{以防万一}。
ctx.en: I made another backup of the file, just in case.

ctx.s: 为了{以防万一}，出国前最好买一份旅游保险。
ctx.en: To be on the safe side, it's best to buy travel insurance before going abroad.

ctx.s: “路这么近，还用开导航吗？”“开着吧，{以防万一}。”
ctx.en: "It's so close, do we really need the satnav?" "Keep it on, just in case."

ctx.s: 医生让他在家里备点药，{以防万一}。
ctx.en: The doctor told him to keep some medicine at home, just in case.

ctx.s: 虽然准备得很充分，他还是多打印了几份讲稿，{以防万一}。
ctx.en: Although he was well prepared, he still printed a few extra copies of his speech, just in case.

bad.s: {以防万一}他不来，我们怎么办？
bad.en: (meant: what if he doesn't come, what do we do?)
bad.why: It names a precaution taken just in case; to ask 'what if', the plain word for 'in case' is used alone, not this idiom.

bad.s: 他昨天摔倒了，{以防万一}。
bad.en: (meant: he fell over yesterday, unfortunately)
bad.why: It explains a precaution taken before something might happen, not an accident that already did.

cards.mean: greatly disappointed
cards.lit: to greatly lose what one had hoped for

use.how: Predicate, often after 让人 / 令人: 结果令人大失所望。 Said when something falls far short of what one expected. Already intensified, so no 很 before it.

near.diff: 心灰意冷 is losing heart and the will to go on; 大失所望 is only the letdown when a result is far below expectations.

cards.cue: You queued two hours for a famous restaurant and the food turned out bland and overpriced. How did it leave you?

ctx.s: 这家餐厅名气很大，可菜的味道让我们{大失所望}。
ctx.en: This restaurant is very famous, but the food left us thoroughly disappointed.

ctx.s: 球迷们本来很期待这场比赛，结果主队踢得这么差，大家都{大失所望}。
ctx.en: The fans had been looking forward to the match, but the home team played so badly that everyone was bitterly disappointed.

ctx.s: “新手机怎么样？”“别提了，电池太不耐用，真让人{大失所望}。”
ctx.en: "How's the new phone?" "Don't ask. The battery dies so fast, it's a real letdown."

ctx.s: 他满怀希望地去面试，却{大失所望}地回来了。
ctx.en: He went to the interview full of hope and came back sorely disappointed.

ctx.s: 这部续集剧情拖沓，令不少原著粉丝{大失所望}。
ctx.en: The sequel's plot drags, which badly disappointed many fans of the original book.

ctx.s: 公司公布的业绩远低于预期，投资者{大失所望}，股价随即下跌。
ctx.en: The company's results came in far below expectations; investors were deeply disappointed and the share price fell at once.

bad.s: 爷爷去世了，全家人都{大失所望}。
bad.en: (meant: the whole family was grief-stricken when Grandpa died)
bad.why: It describes a letdown when expectations are not met, not grief over a death or loss.

bad.s: 他对这次考试的结果很{大失所望}。
bad.en: (meant: he was very disappointed with his exam result)
bad.why: The idiom already contains 'greatly', so it cannot take a degree adverb such as 'very' before it.

cards.mean: with many people pitching in at once
cards.lit: seven hands and eight feet: many hands and feet all moving at once

use.how: Adverbial, usually with 地 before a verb: 大家七手八脚地把他扶起来。 Describes a group all helping at the same time, often a bit hurriedly.

near.diff: 手忙脚乱 is one person (or group) flustered and disorganised; 七手八脚 is many people pitching in together.

cards.cue: An old man slips on the pavement and several passers-by rush over at once to lift him up. How do they help him?

ctx.s: 他摔倒了，大家{七手八脚}地把他扶了起来。
ctx.en: He fell over, and everyone rushed in together to help him up.

ctx.s: 搬家那天，朋友们{七手八脚}，一个小时就把东西都搬上了车。
ctx.en: On moving day my friends all pitched in, and within an hour everything was loaded onto the van.

ctx.s: 客人快到了，全家人{七手八脚}地摆桌子、端菜。
ctx.en: The guests were almost here, and the whole family bustled about together setting the table and bringing out dishes.

ctx.s: 车陷进了泥里，路过的村民{七手八脚}地帮忙往外推。
ctx.en: The car got stuck in the mud, and villagers passing by all crowded round to help push it out.

ctx.s: “别急，大家一起来！”同学们{七手八脚}地把倒下的展板重新立了起来。
ctx.en: "Don't panic, everyone together!" The classmates all grabbed hold and set the fallen display board upright again.

ctx.s: 火刚冒烟，邻居们就{七手八脚}地提水来灭，总算没酿成大祸。
ctx.en: As soon as smoke appeared, the neighbours all ran over with buckets of water, and a disaster was narrowly avoided.

bad.s: 他一个人在厨房里{七手八脚}地做饭。
bad.en: (meant: alone in the kitchen, he was cooking in a fluster)
bad.why: It needs many people working at once; one person alone in a flap cannot be described this way.

bad.s: 她做事{七手八脚}，又快又细致。
bad.en: (meant: she is dexterous, quick and careful)
bad.why: It does not praise skill; it pictures a crowd of people all pitching in, often a little chaotically.

cards.mean: rich and varied
cards.lit: abundant and many-coloured

use.how: Attributive or predicate for life, activities, content or culture: 丰富多彩的课外活动、生活丰富多彩。 Warmly positive; very common in writing.

near.diff: 五彩缤纷 describes many bright colours you can see; 丰富多彩 describes the variety of life, activities or content.

cards.cue: A brochure wants to praise a school's after-class programme: calligraphy, basketball, choir, robotics and more. What word does it use for the programme?

ctx.s: 学校的课外活动{丰富多彩}，有书法、篮球和合唱。
ctx.en: The school's extracurricular activities are rich and varied: calligraphy, basketball and choir.

ctx.s: 退休以后，奶奶的生活反而更加{丰富多彩}了。
ctx.en: Since retiring, Grandma's life has actually become fuller and more varied.

ctx.s: 这座城市每年夏天都会举办{丰富多彩}的音乐节和夜市。
ctx.en: Every summer the city holds all kinds of lively music festivals and night markets.

ctx.s: “你们春节一般怎么过？”“挺{丰富多彩}的，逛庙会、看灯会、走亲戚。”
ctx.en: "How do you usually spend Spring Festival?" "There's lots going on: temple fairs, lantern shows, visiting relatives."

ctx.s: 这本杂志内容{丰富多彩}，从科技到美食都有涉及。
ctx.en: The magazine's content is wide-ranging, covering everything from technology to food.

ctx.s: 博物馆通过{丰富多彩}的展品，向游客展示了这个民族的历史与文化。
ctx.en: Through a rich variety of exhibits, the museum presents the history and culture of this people to visitors.

bad.s: 她的裙子是红色的，非常{丰富多彩}。
bad.en: (meant: her red dress is very colourful)
bad.why: A single-coloured object is not varied; the idiom praises the variety of life, activities or content.

bad.s: 他很{丰富多彩}地介绍了学校。
bad.en: (meant: he gave a lively introduction to the school)
bad.why: It describes things like life or programmes, not the manner of doing something; it is not used as an adverb.

cards.mean: single-mindedly devoted to one task
cards.lit: with a focused heart and a committed will

story.text: Mencius tells of Yi Qiu, the finest go player in the land, who taught two pupils. One gave his whole heart and will to the lesson and listened only to Yi Qiu. The other listened too, but his mind was on a swan that might be about to fly over, and on drawing his bow to shoot it. He learned far less, and Mencius says it was not because he was less clever.

use.how: Usually adverbial with 地: 专心致志地学习、研究、工作。 Also a predicate. Praises sustained, undivided attention to one piece of work.

near.diff: 全神贯注 is total attention in the moment (watching, listening); 专心致志 stresses devoting oneself to a task, often over time.

cards.cue: A scientist turns down every other post and spends years doing nothing but her one research project. How does she work?

ctx.s: 做事要{专心致志}，不能三心二意。
ctx.en: Whatever you do, give it your whole mind; don't keep changing your focus.

ctx.s: 他{专心致志}地研究了十年，终于写成了这本书。
ctx.en: He devoted ten years single-mindedly to his research and finally finished the book.

ctx.s: 这几年她{专心致志}地搞科研，连周末都很少休息。
ctx.en: For the past few years she has devoted herself wholly to research, rarely taking even a weekend off.

ctx.s: “你能不能放下手机？做作业要{专心致志}！”妈妈说。
ctx.en: "Can you put your phone down? Homework needs your full attention!" said Mum.

ctx.s: 要想学好一门乐器，就得{专心致志}，不能今天学这个明天学那个。
ctx.en: To learn an instrument well you have to commit to it, not try one thing today and another tomorrow.

ctx.s: 他辞去了其他职务，好{专心致志}地写完这部小说。
ctx.en: He gave up his other posts so that he could devote himself entirely to finishing the novel.

bad.s: 他{专心致志}地一边看电视一边写作业。
bad.en: (meant: he did his homework while watching TV)
bad.why: It means undivided attention to one task, so doing two things at once contradicts it.

bad.s: 他对女朋友非常{专心致志}。
bad.en: (meant: he is very faithful to his girlfriend)
bad.why: It is about concentrating on work or study, not faithfulness in a relationship.

cards.mean: to treat everyone equally, without favour
cards.lit: to look on all alike and show the same kindness to all

story.text: The phrase goes back to the Tang writer Han Yu. In his essay On Man he wrote that the sage looks on all alike and extends the same benevolence to all, caring for those close at hand while also raising up those far away.

use.how: Predicate, often 对……一视同仁. Said of a teacher, parent, shop, official or law that treats everyone the same, with no favourites.

near.diff: 大公无私 is selflessly putting the public good above one's own interest; 一视同仁 is treating everyone the same.

cards.cue: A teacher gives the same attention and the same marks standard to the top student and the class troublemaker alike. How does she treat them?

ctx.s: 王老师对每个学生都{一视同仁}，从不偏心。
ctx.en: Ms Wang treats every student the same and never plays favourites.

ctx.s: 不管是老顾客还是新顾客，我们店都{一视同仁}。
ctx.en: Regular customer or new one, our shop treats everyone alike.

ctx.s: 法律面前人人平等，执法必须{一视同仁}。
ctx.en: Everyone is equal before the law, so it must be enforced the same way for all.

ctx.s: “凭什么他迟到不扣钱？”“放心，公司的规定对谁都{一视同仁}。”
ctx.en: "Why doesn't he get docked for being late?" "Don't worry, the company's rules apply to everyone equally."

ctx.s: 这家医院对本地病人和外地病人{一视同仁}，挂号排队都一样。
ctx.en: This hospital treats local and out-of-town patients alike; everyone registers and queues the same way.

ctx.s: 父母应该对几个孩子{一视同仁}，否则容易引起兄弟姐妹之间的矛盾。
ctx.en: Parents should treat all their children equally, or it can easily cause friction between siblings.

bad.s: 这两件衣服颜色{一视同仁}，我分不清。
bad.en: (meant: the two shirts are the same colour, I can't tell them apart)
bad.why: It is about treating people without favour, not about things looking identical.

bad.s: 经理对自己的亲戚特别{一视同仁}，总给他们升职。
bad.en: (meant: the manager favours his relatives and keeps promoting them)
bad.why: It means the opposite of favouritism, and it cannot take a degree adverb like 'especially'.

cards.mean: done in one smooth go, without a break
cards.lit: finished in a single breath

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 这篇文章一气呵成。 Praises writing, a performance or a piece of work done in one uninterrupted, flowing effort.

near.diff: 一蹴而就 is achieving something in one easy step, mostly in negatives (不可能一蹴而就); 一气呵成 praises work done in one unbroken flow.

cards.cue: A writer sits down at midnight and writes a whole short story straight through by dawn, never stopping. How was the story written?

ctx.s: 这篇作文他{一气呵成}，中间一次都没停笔。
ctx.en: He wrote the whole essay in one go, without putting his pen down once.

ctx.s: 她的演奏{一气呵成}，台下掌声雷动。
ctx.en: Her performance flowed from start to finish without a break, and the audience burst into thunderous applause.

ctx.s: 这部电影节奏紧凑，故事讲得{一气呵成}。
ctx.en: The film is tightly paced and tells its story in one seamless sweep.

ctx.s: 灵感来了，他熬了一个通宵，把整首歌{一气呵成}地写完了。
ctx.en: Inspiration struck, and he stayed up all night writing the whole song in one go.

ctx.s: “这幅字写得真流畅！”“是啊，看得出是{一气呵成}的。”
ctx.en: "This calligraphy flows beautifully!" "Yes, you can tell it was written in a single unbroken go."

ctx.s: 装修工人从拆旧到铺地板{一气呵成}，三天就完工了。
ctx.en: The builders went straight from stripping out the old fittings to laying the floor without a pause, and finished in three days.

bad.s: 学好汉语不可能{一气呵成}，要慢慢来。
bad.en: (meant: you can't master Chinese overnight; take it slowly)
bad.why: It praises a piece of work done in one flowing go; it cannot mean that a long-term goal is reached in one step.

bad.s: 这个项目我们断断续续做了三年，终于{一气呵成}。
bad.en: (meant: after three years of stop-start work, we finally finished)
bad.why: It means done without a break, which contradicts three years of stop-start work.

cards.mean: to solve something once and for all
cards.lit: toil once, rest forever

story.text: In the Eastern Han, after the general Dou Xian defeated the Xiongnu, the historian Ban Gu wrote an inscription carved on Mount Yanran to mark the victory. It says that this was a case of toiling once to rest for long, of spending for a short while to gain lasting peace.

use.how: Adverbial (一劳永逸地解决) or attributive (一劳永逸的办法); very often negated: 没有一劳永逸的办法。 Said of a fix that settles a problem for good.

near.diff: 一蹴而就 is about reaching a goal quickly in one step; 一劳永逸 is about one effort whose result lasts and needs no repeating.

cards.cue: Instead of patching the leaking pipe every month, you replace the whole section so it never needs fixing again. What kind of fix is that?

ctx.s: 换根好一点的水管，就能{一劳永逸}，不用每个月都修了。
ctx.en: Put in a better pipe and the problem's solved for good; no more repairs every month.

ctx.s: 学习语言没有{一劳永逸}的办法，必须天天练习。
ctx.en: There's no once-and-for-all shortcut to learning a language; you have to practise every day.

ctx.s: 他把账单都设成自动还款，{一劳永逸}，再也不怕忘记了。
ctx.en: He set all his bills to pay automatically, which settled it for good; now he never worries about forgetting.

ctx.s: “我们干脆把旧系统全换掉吧？”“换了也不是{一劳永逸}，以后还得维护。”
ctx.en: "Why don't we just replace the whole old system?" "Even then it won't be solved forever; it'll still need maintenance."

ctx.s: 健康不是{一劳永逸}的事，锻炼一阵子就停是没用的。
ctx.en: Health isn't something you sort out once and for all; exercising for a while and then stopping is no use.

ctx.s: 政府希望通过这次改革{一劳永逸}地解决农村用水难的问题。
ctx.en: The government hopes this reform will solve the problem of rural water shortages once and for all.

bad.s: 他很{一劳永逸}，什么活都不想干。
bad.en: (meant: he is lazy and doesn't want to do any work)
bad.why: It does not describe a lazy person; it describes a solution that settles a matter for good.

bad.s: 他每天{一劳永逸}地工作到深夜。
bad.en: (meant: he works tirelessly until late every night)
bad.why: It means one effort with a lasting result, so it cannot describe toiling again every day.

cards.mean: to plummet suddenly (grades, sales, reputation)
cards.lit: to drop a thousand zhang (thousands of metres) in one fall

story.text: Han Yu wrote a poem on hearing the monk Ying play the qin. He describes the music climbing upward note by note, so high that not another inch can be gained, and then suddenly losing its hold and plunging more than a thousand zhang. The image of the music's fall later came to mean any sudden steep decline.

use.how: Predicate after a subject such as 成绩、生意、销量、地位、人气: 生意一落千丈。 Describes a sudden, steep fall in level or standing.

near.diff: 一败涂地 is a complete, crushing defeat; 一落千丈 is a sharp fall in level, such as grades, sales or status.

cards.cue: A popular bakery is caught using expired ingredients, and within a month hardly anyone buys from it. What happened to its business?

ctx.s: 他迷上游戏以后，成绩{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: After he got hooked on video games, his grades took a nosedive.

ctx.s: 那家店被曝光用过期食材，生意{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: Once it came out that the shop used expired ingredients, its business collapsed.

ctx.s: 这位明星因为一句不当言论，人气{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: Because of one inappropriate remark, the star's popularity plummeted.

ctx.s: 自从新的竞争对手进入市场，这个品牌的销量就{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: Ever since a new competitor entered the market, the brand's sales have plunged.

ctx.s: 受伤之后，他的状态{一落千丈}，再也没能回到国家队。
ctx.en: After the injury his form fell away sharply, and he never made it back to the national team.

ctx.s: 随着工厂纷纷倒闭，这座曾经的工业重镇地位{一落千丈}。
ctx.en: As its factories closed one after another, this former industrial hub fell sharply in standing.

bad.s: 他从楼梯上{一落千丈}，摔伤了腿。
bad.en: (meant: he fell down the stairs and hurt his leg)
bad.why: It is figurative, for a sharp fall in level or standing, not a physical fall.

bad.s: 经过努力，他的成绩{一落千丈}，老师很高兴。
bad.en: (meant: through hard work his grades shot up and the teacher was pleased)
bad.why: It means a steep drop, never a rise, so it cannot describe grades improving.

cards.mean: to amaze everyone with a sudden first success
cards.lit: with one cry, it astonishes everyone

story.text: King Wei of Qi spent his days drinking and left the state to drift. Chunyu Kun, who liked riddles, asked him about a great bird in the palace that for three years had neither flown nor sung. The king answered that this bird, once it flew, would soar to the sky, and once it sang, would astonish everyone. He then took the government in hand.

use.how: Predicate: 他在比赛中一鸣惊人。 Said of someone unknown or quiet who suddenly does something remarkable, often a first work or first big contest.

near.diff: 一举成名 just means becoming famous at a stroke; 一鸣惊人 stresses that someone overlooked suddenly astonishes everyone.

cards.cue: A shy student nobody noticed enters the speech contest for the first time and wins first prize, stunning the whole school. What did he do?

ctx.s: 这个平时不爱说话的同学，在演讲比赛中{一鸣惊人}，拿了第一名。
ctx.en: This usually quiet student stunned everyone in the speech contest and took first place.

ctx.s: 她的第一部小说就{一鸣惊人}，卖了上百万册。
ctx.en: Her very first novel was a sensation, selling over a million copies.

ctx.s: 这支没人看好的小球队竟然打败了冠军，真是{一鸣惊人}。
ctx.en: This little team that nobody rated actually beat the champions; what a stunning breakthrough.

ctx.s: “你准备了这么久，有把握吗？”“不试试怎么知道？说不定能{一鸣惊人}呢。”
ctx.en: "You've prepared so long; are you confident?" "How will I know if I don't try? Maybe I'll surprise everyone."

ctx.s: 他默默练了三年，决心在全国比赛上{一鸣惊人}。
ctx.en: He trained quietly for three years, determined to astonish everyone at the national championship.

ctx.s: 这家初创公司推出的第一款产品就{一鸣惊人}，迅速占领了市场。
ctx.en: The start-up's very first product made a huge splash and quickly captured the market.

bad.s: 他突然大叫，{一鸣惊人}，吓了我一跳。
bad.en: (meant: he suddenly shouted and startled me)
bad.why: It is figurative, for a sudden remarkable success, not a loud noise that startles someone.

bad.s: 他是多年的老冠军，这次又{一鸣惊人}地赢了。
bad.en: (meant: the long-time champion won again this time)
bad.why: It implies a sudden success after obscurity, which does not fit an established champion winning again.

cards.mean: a helping hand (to lend someone)
cards.lit: the strength of one arm

use.how: Noun phrase, the object of 助 (also 出 or 尽): 助你一臂之力、为……出一臂之力。 Offering or asking for a specific piece of help; a little formal and polite.

near.diff: 助人为乐 describes someone who enjoys helping others as a trait; 一臂之力 is the help given in one particular case.

cards.cue: Your friend is short of people to run a charity event, and you politely offer to help out. What do you offer them?

ctx.s: 你要是搬家缺人手，我可以助你{一臂之力}。
ctx.en: If you're short of hands for the move, I can give you a hand.

ctx.s: “这次活动缺一个翻译，你能不能助我们{一臂之力}？”
ctx.en: "We're short of an interpreter for this event. Could you lend us a hand?"

ctx.s: 多亏老同学助了我{一臂之力}，我才渡过了难关。
ctx.en: It was only thanks to an old classmate's help that I got through that difficult time.

ctx.s: 洪水过后，各地志愿者纷纷赶来，助灾区{一臂之力}。
ctx.en: After the flood, volunteers poured in from all over to help the stricken area.

ctx.s: 如贵公司有需要，我方愿助{一臂之力}。
ctx.en: Should your company need it, we would be glad to lend our assistance.

ctx.s: 这项新技术为医生早期发现疾病助了{一臂之力}。
ctx.en: This new technology has given doctors a helping hand in detecting disease early.

bad.s: 他{一臂之力}地帮我搬了箱子。
bad.en: (meant: he helped me carry the boxes)
bad.why: It is a noun phrase used as the object of a verb meaning 'help', not an adverb before a verb.

bad.s: 我只有{一臂之力}，搬不动这么重的箱子。
bad.en: (meant: I'm not strong enough to lift such a heavy box)
bad.why: It means help given to someone, not a measure of one's own physical strength.

cards.mean: achieved in a single step (usually: it cannot be)
cards.lit: done with a single step, or a single kick

use.how: Almost always negated, about big goals that take time: 不是一蹴而就的, 不可能一蹴而就, 绝非一蹴而就.

near.diff: 一劳永逸 is one effort that settles a problem for good; 一蹴而就 is reaching a goal at once, and usually says you can't.

cards.cue: A friend is upset that after a month of piano lessons she still plays badly. Remind her that real skill doesn't come in one leap.

ctx.s: 学语言不是{一蹴而就}的事，要每天坚持。
