ctx.en: Learning a language isn't something you finish in one go; you have to keep at it every day.

ctx.s: 减肥哪能{一蹴而就}？你才练了三天。
ctx.en: How could losing weight happen overnight? You've only exercised for three days.

ctx.s: 市长在会上说：“改革需要时间，不可能{一蹴而就}。”
ctx.en: The mayor told the meeting: "Reform takes time; it can't be done in one stroke."

ctx.s: 你以为写小说能{一蹴而就}吗？他这本书改了整整五年。
ctx.en: Do you think a novel gets written in one go? He spent five whole years revising this one.

ctx.s: 城市的污染问题由来已久，治理也绝非{一蹴而就}。
ctx.en: The city's pollution has built up over a long time, and cleaning it up won't happen in a single step.

ctx.s: 很多年轻人创业时幻想{一蹴而就}，却低估了其中的困难。
ctx.en: Many young founders dream of instant success and underestimate how hard it is.

bad.s: 他{一蹴而就}地踢进了一个球。
bad.en: (meant: he scored with a single kick)
bad.why: It is not about kicking a ball; it is about reaching a large goal at once, and is mostly used to say this can't happen.

bad.s: 祝你考试{一蹴而就}！
bad.en: (meant: good luck passing on the first try)
bad.why: It is not a wish or a blessing; it is used, usually negated, to warn that something takes time.

cards.mean: to press on stubbornly against all advice
cards.lit: one intention, going alone

story.text: Sima Qian describes Zhao Yu, a strict official under Emperor Wu of Han. When high ministers came to visit him, he never returned their calls; he cut himself off from friends and guests so that no one could ask him for favours, and simply 'stood alone and pursued his single purpose'. The phrase was then about refusing influence; today it means stubbornly ignoring everyone's advice.

use.how: Predicate, often after 不顾劝阻 or 却: 他却一意孤行. Criticises someone who acts on a decision everyone advised against.

near.diff: 固执己见 is clinging to an opinion in a discussion; 一意孤行 is going ahead and acting on it despite warnings.

cards.cue: Everyone on the team warned the manager the plan would fail, but he pushed it through anyway and it collapsed. Describe what he did.

ctx.s: 大家都劝他别辞职，可他{一意孤行}。
ctx.en: Everyone told him not to quit, but he went ahead regardless.

ctx.s: 你要是再{一意孤行}，出了事可别怪我们没提醒你。
ctx.en: If you keep ignoring everyone, don't blame us when something goes wrong; we warned you.

ctx.s: 董事会反对扩张，总经理却{一意孤行}，公司最后亏了大钱。
ctx.en: The board opposed expanding, but the CEO insisted on his own way, and the company lost a fortune.

ctx.s: 他明知道有风险，为什么还要{一意孤行}？
ctx.en: He knew the risks, so why did he insist on going his own way?

ctx.s: 医生让他住院观察，他却{一意孤行}，第二天就去爬雪山了。
ctx.en: The doctor told him to stay in hospital, but he ignored it and went off climbing a snowy mountain the next day.

ctx.s: 历史上不少君主{一意孤行}，最终导致国家衰败。
ctx.en: Many rulers in history disregarded all counsel and in the end brought their states to ruin.

bad.s: 她{一意孤行}地学习，终于考上了大学。
bad.en: (meant: she studied single-mindedly and got into university)
bad.why: It criticises ignoring advice; it is not praise for dedication. For dedication, say she studied wholeheartedly instead.

bad.s: 他一个人{一意孤行}去旅行了。
bad.en: (meant: he went travelling on his own)
bad.why: The character for 'alone' here does not mean travelling solo; the idiom means acting against everyone's advice.

cards.mean: full of twists and setbacks along the way
cards.lit: one sweeping stroke, three turns of the brush

story.text: The phrase began as calligraphy advice. In a note attributed to Wang Xizhi on Lady Wei's treatise on the brush, he says that each long sweeping stroke should turn the brush three times, so the line moves instead of running flat. It was later said of writing with twists in its structure, and then of any course of events full of setbacks.
story.source: 王羲之《题卫夫人〈笔阵图〉后》

use.how: Predicate or before 的, about a process, story or relationship: 事情一波三折; 一波三折的谈判. Usually looks back on a bumpy course.

near.diff: 一帆风顺 is the opposite: everything goes smoothly from start to finish.

cards.cue: Your flight was cancelled, the next one delayed, then your bag was lost, but you finally got there. Sum up the trip.

ctx.s: 这次搬家{一波三折}，总算搬完了。
ctx.en: This move had one hitch after another, but it's finally done.

ctx.s: 他们的恋爱{一波三折}，最后还是结了婚。
ctx.en: Their romance had plenty of ups and downs, but they got married in the end.

ctx.s: “签证办得怎么样？”“别提了，{一波三折}，到现在还没下来。”
ctx.en: "How's the visa going?" "Don't ask. Problem after problem, and it still hasn't come through."

ctx.s: 这部电影情节{一波三折}，观众一直猜不到结局。
ctx.en: The film's plot keeps twisting, and the audience can't guess the ending.

ctx.s: 经过{一波三折}的谈判，双方终于签了合同。
ctx.en: After negotiations full of twists and turns, the two sides finally signed.

ctx.s: 这个项目从立项到完成，过程可谓{一波三折}。
ctx.en: From approval to completion, this project ran into setback after setback.

bad.s: 今天海上{一波三折}，船晃得厉害。
bad.en: (meant: the sea was rough today)
bad.why: It is not about real waves; it describes a process or story full of twists and setbacks.

bad.s: 这件事很顺利，{一波三折}就办好了。
bad.en: (meant: it went smoothly and was done quickly)
bad.why: It means the opposite of smooth: many setbacks along the way.

cards.mean: to press on while the first burst of energy lasts
cards.lit: the first drum roll rouses the fighting spirit

story.text: When Qi attacked Lu at Changshao, Cao Gui rode with the Duke of Lu and stopped him from sounding the attack when Qi first drummed. Only after Qi had drummed three times did he let Lu drum, and Lu won. He explained: battle is a matter of courage; the first drum rouses it, the second drains it, by the third it is gone. Theirs was spent while Lu's was full.

use.how: Adverbial before the verb, often urging: 一鼓作气把活干完; 一鼓作气爬到山顶. About pushing through a task while the energy lasts.

near.diff: 一气呵成 says a piece of work was done smoothly without a break; 一鼓作气 is about seizing momentum to push through a challenge.
再接再厉 is encouragement to keep improving after a success; 一鼓作气 is about not stopping now, before the energy fades.

cards.cue: Your team has just carried the heaviest furniture upstairs and everyone is still fired up. Urge them to finish the move now, before they tire.

ctx.s: 我们{一鼓作气}爬到了山顶。
ctx.en: We kept our momentum and climbed all the way to the top.

ctx.s: 别停下来，趁大家还有劲，{一鼓作气}把活干完！
ctx.en: Don't stop; while everyone still has the energy, let's push on and finish the job!

ctx.s: 上半场领先后，球队{一鼓作气}，又连进三球。
ctx.en: Ahead at half-time, the team kept up the pressure and scored three more in a row.

ctx.s: 已经过了科目一，为什么不{一鼓作气}把驾照考下来？
ctx.en: You've passed the first driving test, so why not keep going and get your licence now?

ctx.s: 考完第一门后，她没有休息，{一鼓作气}复习下一门。
ctx.en: After the first exam she didn't take a break but went straight on to revising for the next.

ctx.s: 战士们{一鼓作气}，攻下了山头。
ctx.en: The soldiers charged on in one surge and took the hilltop.

bad.s: 他学钢琴已经{一鼓作气}十年了。
bad.en: (meant: he has persevered with piano for ten years)
bad.why: It is about the first burst of energy, not long persistence. Years of steady effort call for a word of perseverance instead.

bad.s: 他敲鼓敲得很{一鼓作气}。
bad.en: (meant: he plays the drums energetically)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with real drumming, and it is not an adjective that can follow 'very'.

cards.mean: a tiny fraction of a huge whole
cards.lit: one hair out of nine oxen

story.text: Sima Qian was castrated as punishment after he spoke up for a defeated general before Emperor Wu. In a letter to his friend Ren An he explained why he had not chosen death: if he had simply been executed, it would have been like nine oxen losing a single hair, no different from the death of an ant. So he bore the disgrace in order to finish his history.

use.how: Predicate or object, usually after 只是, 不过是: 这点钱对他来说只是九牛一毛. Always measured against a large total.

near.diff: 微不足道 is trivial in itself; 九牛一毛 is small compared with a huge whole it belongs to.

cards.cue: A billionaire gives a hundred thousand dollars to charity and the press praises him. Point out how little that is next to his fortune.

ctx.s: 这点钱对他来说只是{九牛一毛}。
ctx.en: That kind of money is nothing to him; he wouldn't even notice it.

ctx.s: 公司捐了一百万，跟它的利润比起来不过是{九牛一毛}。
ctx.en: The company gave a million, but next to its profits that's a drop in the ocean.

ctx.s: 我读过的书，和图书馆的藏书相比简直是{九牛一毛}。
ctx.en: The books I've read are a tiny fraction of what the library holds.

ctx.s: 全国浪费的粮食那么多，我们省下的虽是{九牛一毛}，但也值得做。
ctx.en: So much food is wasted nationwide; what we save is a tiny fraction, but it's still worth doing.

ctx.s: 这次涨的几块钱，跟富人的财产比只是{九牛一毛}，对穷人却是很大的负担。
ctx.en: Next to a rich person's wealth, this rise of a few yuan is a tiny fraction, but for the poor it is a heavy burden.

ctx.s: 王总一年收入几千万，请大家吃顿饭，{九牛一毛}而已。
ctx.en: Mr Wang earns tens of millions a year; treating everyone to dinner costs him next to nothing.

bad.s: 他很小气，连{九牛一毛}都不肯给。
bad.en: (meant: he's so stingy he won't give a cent)
bad.why: Confused with the idiom for a miser who won't pluck one hair. This one compares a small part with a huge whole; it does not mean 'even a little'.

bad.s: 这件事{九牛一毛}，你不用管。
bad.en: (meant: it's a trivial matter, don't bother)
bad.why: It needs a huge whole to compare against. For something unimportant in itself, call it trivial instead.

cards.mean: flooded with mixed feelings at once
cards.lit: a hundred feelings meet together

story.text: As the Western Jin collapsed into war, the young scholar Wei Jie fled south. About to cross the Yangtze, worn out and grieving, he looked at the vast water and said that seeing this boundless expanse, a hundred feelings gathered in him at once; anyone who had feelings at all, how could he put them aside? The book records his words with a slightly different second character.

use.how: Predicate for a person, often with 心中 or before 地: 他百感交集. Said at a big moment: a reunion, a farewell, a return.

near.diff: 悲喜交加 is specifically sorrow and joy together; 百感交集 is many feelings at once, too many to name.

cards.cue: Back at the school you left decades ago, you feel joy, regret, nostalgia and sadness all at once. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 看到老家的房子，他{百感交集}。
ctx.en: Seeing his old family home, he was overcome with emotion.

ctx.s: 毕业典礼上，她{百感交集}，说不出话来。
ctx.en: At the graduation ceremony, so many feelings rushed in that she couldn't speak.

ctx.s: 二十年后再见到老师，我心里{百感交集}。
ctx.en: Seeing my teacher again after twenty years, I felt a flood of mixed emotions.

ctx.s: 接过冠军奖杯的那一刻，你是不是{百感交集}？
ctx.en: The moment you took the trophy, did all kinds of feelings hit you at once?

ctx.s: 读着女儿出国前留下的信，母亲{百感交集}。
ctx.en: Reading the letter her daughter left before going abroad, the mother was torn by many emotions.

ctx.s: 离开工作了三十年的工厂那天，老张{百感交集}地回头看了一眼。
ctx.en: The day he left the factory where he'd worked for thirty years, Lao Zhang looked back once, full of mixed emotions.

bad.s: 今天我买了新衣服，心里{百感交集}。
bad.en: (meant: I bought new clothes and I'm really happy)
bad.why: It means many mixed feelings at a moving moment, not simple happiness. Simply say you are happy.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜{百感交集}，什么口味都有。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant has every kind of flavour)
bad.why: It describes a person's emotions, never a variety of things.

cards.mean: endlessly varied, taking countless forms
cards.lit: a thousand changes, ten thousand transformations

use.how: Predicate or before 的, about weather, clouds, situations, techniques: 天气千变万化; 千变万化的图案. Not a verb with an object.

near.diff: 瞬息万变 stresses speed: a situation or market changing from moment to moment; 千变万化 stresses the countless forms something takes.
五花八门 is many different kinds side by side; 千变万化 is one thing that keeps changing form.

cards.cue: Watching clouds drift over a mountain, you see them become one shape after another, never the same twice. Describe them.

ctx.s: 天上的云{千变万化}，一会儿像马，一会儿像狗。
ctx.en: The clouds keep changing shape: one moment a horse, the next a dog.

ctx.s: 孙悟空会七十二变，{千变万化}，妖怪根本认不出他。
ctx.en: The Monkey King has seventy-two transformations and can take any form; the demons never recognise him.

ctx.s: 万花筒里的图案{千变万化}，孩子们看得入迷。
ctx.en: The patterns in the kaleidoscope never stop changing, and the children are spellbound.

ctx.s: 中国菜的做法{千变万化}，同一块豆腐能做出几十道菜。
ctx.en: Chinese cooking has endless variations; the same tofu can become dozens of dishes.

ctx.s: “这些都是同一个字？”“对，在书法家笔下，一个字也能写出{千变万化}的样子。”
ctx.en: "Are these all the same character?" "Yes. In a calligrapher's hand, even one character can take countless forms."

ctx.s: 你知道吗？围棋的下法{千变万化}，几乎没有两盘完全一样的棋。
ctx.en: Did you know? Go can be played in endlessly varied ways; almost no two games are ever the same.

bad.s: 他{千变万化}了自己的计划。
bad.en: (meant: he changed his plan many times)
bad.why: It is not a verb and cannot take an object; it describes something that takes ever-changing forms.

bad.s: 他是个{千变万化}的人，答应的事经常变卦。
bad.en: (meant: he's fickle and often goes back on his word)
bad.why: It neutrally describes varied forms, not an unreliable person. Fickleness needs a different word.

cards.mean: at the critical moment, hanging by a thread
cards.lit: a thousand jun (an old weight) hanging from a single hair

use.how: Mostly in 千钧一发之际 or 千钧一发的时刻, about a split second of real danger, often just before a rescue or escape.

near.diff: 迫在眉睫 is a task or threat that is urgently close; 千钧一发 is the split second of extreme danger itself.

cards.cue: A child runs into the road; the driver slams the brakes and the car stops inches away. Describe that instant.

ctx.s: 就在这{千钧一发}的时刻，消防员冲了进去。
ctx.en: At that critical instant, the firefighters rushed in.

ctx.s: {千钧一发}之际，司机猛踩刹车，车停在了孩子面前。
ctx.en: At the last possible moment the driver slammed on the brakes, and the car stopped right in front of the child.

ctx.s: 火车越来越近，小狗还卡在铁轨上，情况{千钧一发}。
ctx.en: The train was getting closer and the puppy was still stuck on the tracks; everything hung by a thread.

ctx.s: 你还记得那次{千钧一发}的经历吗？我们差点掉下悬崖。
ctx.en: Do you remember that close call? We nearly went over the cliff.

ctx.s: 比赛只剩最后几秒，守门员在{千钧一发}之际扑出了点球。
ctx.en: With seconds left in the match, the goalkeeper saved the penalty at the decisive moment.

ctx.s: 回想起那{千钧一发}的一刻，他现在还觉得后怕。
ctx.en: Thinking back to that moment when everything hung by a thread, he still feels shaken.

bad.s: 这个月的房租要交了，真是{千钧一发}。
bad.en: (meant: rent is due, it's urgent)
bad.why: It is for a split second of real danger, not an ordinary deadline. Just say it is urgent.

bad.s: 他力气很大，有{千钧一发}之力。
bad.en: (meant: he has enormous strength)
bad.why: Confused with the phrase for the strength of a thousand jun. This idiom describes a moment of danger, not strength.

cards.mean: so lifelike it seems alive (a painting, a carving)
cards.lit: vivid, as if alive

use.how: Predicate or complement, praising a depiction: a painting, sculpture, craft or written character: 画得栩栩如生. Never about a real living thing.

near.diff: 惟妙惟肖 praises an imitation for being exactly like the original, including impersonations; 栩栩如生 says a depiction seems alive.

cards.cue: At a museum you see an old ink painting of shrimps so real you half expect them to swim off the paper. Praise it.

ctx.s: 他捏的泥人{栩栩如生}。
ctx.en: The clay figures he makes look alive.

ctx.s: 这幅画上的马{栩栩如生}，好像要跑出来一样。
ctx.en: The horse in this painting is so lifelike it looks ready to gallop out of the frame.

ctx.s: 你看这尊木雕，是不是{栩栩如生}？
ctx.en: Look at this wood carving; doesn't it seem alive?

ctx.s: 博物馆里的兵马俑个个{栩栩如生}。
ctx.en: Every one of the terracotta warriors in the museum looks lifelike.

ctx.s: 这些糖做的小动物{栩栩如生}，孩子们都舍不得吃。
ctx.en: The little sugar animals are so lifelike the children can't bear to eat them.

ctx.s: 这部小说里的乡村老师形象{栩栩如生}，好像就生活在我们身边。
ctx.en: The village teacher in this novel is so vividly drawn he seems to live among us.

bad.s: 我奶奶九十岁了，还{栩栩如生}。
bad.en: (meant: my grandma is ninety and still full of life)
bad.why: It praises a depiction that looks alive, not a real person's vitality. Say she is still full of energy instead.

bad.s: 这首歌{栩栩如生}，我很喜欢。
bad.en: (meant: this song is lively, I love it)
bad.why: It is for visual or written depictions that seem alive; a song can be lively, but not lifelike.

cards.mean: busy streets full of traffic
cards.lit: carriages like flowing water, horses like a dragon

story.text: When Emperor Zhang of the Eastern Han wanted to give titles to the brothers of Empress Dowager Ma, she refused. She said that passing the Zhuolong Gate she had seen the people calling on her family, their carriages like flowing water and their horses like a swimming dragon. Her family was already grand enough, she said, and she refused to add honours.

use.how: Predicate or before 的, describing a street or city scene: 街上车水马龙; 车水马龙的大街. Traffic that is busy but moving.

near.diff: 人山人海 is huge crowds of people; 车水马龙 is a lively stream of vehicles on the streets.
水泄不通 is packed so tight nothing moves; 车水马龙 is busy traffic that keeps flowing.

cards.cue: From your hotel window downtown you watch cars and buses streaming along the avenue all evening. Describe the street.

ctx.s: 市中心的大街上{车水马龙}，非常热闹。
ctx.en: The streets downtown are busy with traffic and full of life.

ctx.s: 这里以前是一片农田，现在已经{车水马龙}了。
ctx.en: This used to be farmland; now it's busy with traffic.

ctx.s: 站在天桥上，看着下面{车水马龙}的街道，他觉得自己很渺小。
ctx.en: Standing on the footbridge, watching the stream of traffic below, he felt very small.

ctx.s: 一到晚上，酒店门口就{车水马龙}，客人来来往往。
ctx.en: Every evening, cars pull up one after another at the hotel entrance as guests come and go.

ctx.s: 离开{车水马龙}的城市，回到安静的山村，她终于睡了个好觉。
ctx.en: Leaving the busy city behind for a quiet mountain village, she finally got a good night's sleep.

ctx.s: 你住的地方{车水马龙}的，晚上不吵吗？
ctx.en: There's so much traffic where you live; isn't it noisy at night?

bad.s: 地铁里{车水马龙}，挤得我透不过气。
bad.en: (meant: the subway was so crowded I could hardly breathe)
bad.why: It describes vehicles flowing along streets, not people packed inside. For packed crowds, use the idiom about mountains and seas of people.

bad.s: 昨天高速公路上发生了{车水马龙}的事故。
bad.en: (meant: there was a multi-car crash on the motorway)
bad.why: It paints a lively, busy street scene, not a crash or disaster.

cards.mean: uniquely blessed by nature or circumstance
cards.lit: to receive from heaven, alone, in rich measure

use.how: Predicate or attribute about lasting natural advantages of a place or a person's gifts: 这里的条件得天独厚；得天独厚的地理位置。

near.diff: 天时地利 is favourable timing and place for one undertaking; 得天独厚 is a lasting natural advantage someone or somewhere has.

cards.cue: A town has mild weather, rich soil and clean mountain water, so its tea is the best in the region. How do you describe its conditions?

ctx.s: 这个小镇气候温和、水源充足，种茶的条件{得天独厚}。
ctx.en: This town has a mild climate and plenty of water; its conditions for growing tea are exceptional.

ctx.s: 她有一副{得天独厚}的好嗓子，一开口就让人记住了。
ctx.en: She has a naturally gifted voice; people remember her the moment she starts singing.

ctx.s: 这座城市靠海又有深水港，发展航运可以说是{得天独厚}。
ctx.en: The city is on the coast and has a deep-water port; for shipping it is uniquely well placed.

ctx.s: “你们这儿风景这么好，游客一定很多吧？”“是啊，我们这里{得天独厚}，一年四季都有人来。”
ctx.en: "The scenery here is so lovely, you must get lots of tourists?" "Yes, we're blessed by nature here; people come all year round."

ctx.s: 别总羡慕别人{得天独厚}，没有好条件也能靠努力弥补。
ctx.en: Stop envying people who were born with every advantage; hard work can make up for what you lack.

ctx.s: 凭借{得天独厚}的地理位置，这里自古就是商旅往来的要道。
ctx.en: Thanks to its uniquely favourable location, this place has been a major trade route since ancient times.

bad.s: 他昨天买彩票中了大奖，真是{得天独厚}。
bad.en: (meant: he was really lucky to win the lottery yesterday)
bad.why: It describes lasting natural advantages of a place or a person's gifts, not a single lucky event.

bad.s: 他{得天独厚}了一个好嗓子。
bad.en: (meant: he was blessed with a good voice)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; make the voice the subject, or use the idiom as an attribute before 'voice'.

cards.mean: so carried away by success that one forgets oneself
cards.lit: so pleased with oneself that one forgets one's own body

story.text: Ruan Ji, one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove, loved wine and played the zither well. The Book of Jin says that when he was enjoying himself he would forget his own body entirely. The phrase first described that carefree absorption; later it came to mean losing self-control out of pride after a success.

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (得意忘形地) about someone who shows off or gets careless after a success; often in warnings: 别得意忘形。

near.diff: 忘乎所以 can come from any excitement; 得意忘形 comes specifically from success and self-satisfaction.

cards.cue: Your friend just got promoted and is already bragging and ordering old colleagues around. What warning do you give?

ctx.s: 他考了第一名就{得意忘形}，在班上到处炫耀。
ctx.en: As soon as he came top of the class he got carried away and showed off to everyone.

ctx.s: 刚升职别{得意忘形}，大家都在看着你呢。
ctx.en: You've only just been promoted, don't let it go to your head; everyone is watching you.

ctx.s: 比赛领先了几分，球员们有点{得意忘形}，结果被对手反超了。
ctx.en: A few points ahead, the players got cocky, and the other team overtook them.

ctx.s: “我中奖了！”“恭喜，不过别{得意忘形}，先想想钱该怎么用。”
ctx.en: "I won the prize!" "Congratulations, but don't get carried away; think first about how to use the money."

ctx.s: 人在顺境中最容易{得意忘形}，这时候更要保持清醒。
ctx.en: People lose their heads most easily when things are going well; that's when you most need to stay clear-headed.

ctx.s: 他刚签下一笔大单，一时{得意忘形}，在酒桌上把公司的计划全说了出去。
ctx.en: Having just landed a big deal, he got carried away and blurted out the company's whole plan over drinks.

bad.s: 看到孩子平安回家，妈妈{得意忘形}地哭了。
bad.en: (meant: seeing her child home safe, the mother wept with joy)
bad.why: It criticises conceit after a success; relief and tears of joy have nothing to do with it.

bad.s: 老师表扬了我，我感到很{得意忘形}。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher praised me and I felt very proud and happy)
bad.why: It is a judgement on someone's behaviour, not a pleasant feeling one reports, so it cannot follow 'I feel very'.

cards.mean: to muddle along, doing only what gets one by
cards.lit: if one can get by, just get by for now

story.text: On Mount Wutai lived a bird called the hanhao chong. In midsummer its feathers were bright and it sang, 'Even the phoenix is not as fine as me.' By the depth of winter its feathers had fallen out, it looked like a bare chick, and all it sang was, 'Get by if I can, just get by.'
story.source: 元·陶宗仪《南村辍耕录·寒号虫》

use.how: Predicate or attribute (得过且过的心态) about a person's attitude to work or life: no aims, no effort beyond getting through the day.

near.diff: 敷衍了事 is doing one task carelessly to be done with it; 得过且过 is a general attitude of living without aims.

cards.cue: Your cousin has no plans, does the minimum at work and says he'll think about the future later. How do you describe the way he lives?

ctx.s: 他对工作没什么追求，每天{得过且过}。
ctx.en: He has no ambitions at work; he just muddles through each day.

ctx.s: 年轻人不能{得过且过}，总得为将来打算打算。
ctx.en: Young people can't just drift along; they have to plan for the future.

ctx.s: 这家工厂的管理人员{得过且过}，设备坏了也没人愿意修。
ctx.en: The managers at this factory just get by; when equipment breaks, nobody wants to fix it.

ctx.s: 你难道就打算这样{得过且过}下去吗？
ctx.en: Are you really planning to keep drifting along like this?

ctx.s: 失业以后，他整天{得过且过}，连简历都懒得改。
ctx.en: After losing his job he just let the days drift by and couldn't even be bothered to update his CV.

ctx.s: 抱着{得过且过}的心态，是做不好任何事情的。
ctx.en: With a just-get-by attitude, you won't do anything well.

bad.s: 这次考试我{得过且过}，终于通过了。
bad.en: (meant: I scraped through this exam)
bad.why: The 'get by' here is not passing an exam; the idiom criticises an aimless attitude to life, not a narrow pass.

bad.s: 爷爷生活很节俭，日子{得过且过}，从不浪费。
bad.en: (meant: grandpa lives frugally and never wastes anything)
bad.why: It means lacking effort or aims, not being thrifty; it would insult the grandfather.

cards.mean: the way the general trend is heading
cards.lit: where the great momentum is heading

use.how: Usually after 是, or as the object of 面对 or 顺应, about broad social, economic or historical trends: 这是大势所趋。

near.diff: 势在必行 says something must be done now; 大势所趋 says the general trend is heading that way.

cards.cue: A bookshop owner asks whether selling online is a passing fad. You say the whole industry is moving there and resisting is pointless. What do you call it?

ctx.s: 用手机付款已经是{大势所趋}，很多小店也不收现金了。
ctx.en: Paying by phone is now the way things are going; many small shops no longer take cash.

ctx.s: 新能源汽车取代燃油车，是{大势所趋}。
ctx.en: New-energy cars replacing petrol cars is the direction things are clearly heading.

ctx.s: “我们公司还要不要做线上业务？”“必须做，这是{大势所趋}。”
ctx.en: "Should our company still go into online business?" "We have to; that's where everything is heading."

ctx.s: 面对{大势所趋}，传统书店只能想办法转型。
ctx.en: Faced with the general trend, traditional bookshops can only try to reinvent themselves.

ctx.s: 人口向大城市集中，既是{大势所趋}，也带来了不少问题。
ctx.en: People concentrating in big cities is an unstoppable trend, but it also brings many problems.

ctx.s: 难道你看不出远程办公是{大势所趋}吗？
ctx.en: Can't you see that remote work is where things are heading?

bad.s: 看天色，今天下午{大势所趋}会下雨。
bad.en: (meant: from the look of the sky it will probably rain this afternoon)
bad.why: It is about broad social or historical trends, not a forecast of a single event like the weather.

bad.s: 我{大势所趋}地换了一份新工作。
bad.en: (meant: I followed the trend and changed jobs)
bad.why: It is not an adverb describing a person's action; it names a broad trend and usually follows 'is'.

cards.mean: to step forward boldly to face a challenge
cards.lit: to straighten one's body and step out

use.how: Predicate about someone who steps forward when others hang back, to face danger or trouble on others' behalf: 关键时刻，他挺身而出。

near.diff: 见义勇为 is praise for bravely helping a stranger, often against a criminal; 挺身而出 stresses stepping forward in any crisis when others hold back.

cards.cue: A man collapses on a crowded train and everyone freezes, until one woman pushes through and starts first aid. What did she do?

ctx.s: 看到同事被老板冤枉，他马上{挺身而出}替她说话。
ctx.en: When he saw his colleague wrongly blamed by the boss, he stepped up at once and spoke for her.

ctx.s: 公司遇到危机时，是她{挺身而出}，带大家渡过了难关。
ctx.en: When the company was in crisis, it was she who stepped up and led everyone through it.

ctx.s: 地铁上有人突然晕倒，一位护士{挺身而出}，给他做了急救。
ctx.en: Someone fainted on the subway, and a nurse stepped forward and gave him first aid.

ctx.s: “这件事就没人敢管吗？”“总得有人{挺身而出}吧。”
ctx.en: "Doesn't anyone dare deal with this?" "Somebody has to step up."

ctx.s: 关键时刻能{挺身而出}的人，才值得大家信任。
ctx.en: Only people who step forward when it really matters deserve everyone's trust.

ctx.s: 那年洪水来袭，村里的年轻人纷纷{挺身而出}，日夜守在堤坝上。
ctx.en: The year the flood came, the village's young people stepped forward one after another and guarded the dykes day and night.

bad.s: 老师走进教室时，全班同学{挺身而出}向他问好。
bad.en: (meant: when the teacher came in, the whole class stood up to greet him)
bad.why: It means bravely stepping forward to face danger or trouble, not physically standing up from one's seat.

bad.s: 小王总喜欢{挺身而出}，抢着回答老师的每个问题。
bad.en: (meant: Xiao Wang is always eager to answer every question)
bad.why: It is about facing danger or difficulty for others, not eagerness to speak up in class.

cards.mean: the whole room bursts out laughing
cards.lit: the whole hall roars with great laughter

use.how: Predicate whose subject is a group in one room (全班、观众、大家), or object of 引起/引得: 引得全场哄堂大笑。

near.diff: 捧腹大笑 is one or more people laughing very hard; 哄堂大笑 is a whole room bursting into laughter at once.

cards.cue: In the middle of a quiet lecture a puppy trots onto the stage, and every student in the hall laughs at the same moment. What happens?

ctx.s: 他的一句玩笑，引得全班{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: One joke from him and the whole class burst out laughing.

ctx.s: 主持人不小心念错了名字，台下观众{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: The host misread a name by accident and the whole audience roared with laughter.

ctx.s: 小明把“老师”写成了“老鼠”，同学们看了{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: Xiao Ming wrote 'mouse' instead of 'teacher', and the whole class burst out laughing when they saw it.

ctx.s: 婚礼上，新郎紧张得把誓词念反了，宾客们{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: At the wedding the groom was so nervous he read his vows backwards, and the guests all burst out laughing.

ctx.s: 你知道他在年会上说了什么，竟然让全场{哄堂大笑}吗？
ctx.en: Do you know what he said at the annual party that made the whole room crack up?

ctx.s: 一只小狗突然跑上讲台，教室里响起一阵{哄堂大笑}。
ctx.en: A puppy suddenly ran up onto the platform and the classroom erupted in laughter.

bad.s: 他一个人在房间里看喜剧，{哄堂大笑}。
bad.en: (meant: alone in his room watching a comedy, he laughed out loud)
bad.why: It needs a whole roomful of people laughing together; one person laughing alone cannot be described this way.

bad.s: 我们在公园里{哄堂大笑}地玩了一下午。
bad.en: (meant: we played and laughed happily in the park all afternoon)
bad.why: It is one sudden burst of laughter from a room of people, not a long stretch of fun, and it is not an adverb.

cards.mean: nervously apprehensive about what is coming
cards.lit: heart up, heart down: not at ease

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (忐忑不安地) about one's own nervous state while waiting for an uncertain outcome: 等结果时我心里忐忑不安。

near.diff: 毛骨悚然 is the creepy horror at an eerie sight or story; 忐忑不安 is nervous worry about how something will turn out.
提心吊胆 is lasting fear that something bad or dangerous will happen; 忐忑不安 is restless unease over how an uncertain matter will turn out.

cards.cue: You've handed in your resignation letter and now spend the whole night wondering how your boss will react. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 听说老板要找我谈话，我心里{忐忑不安}，不知道是好事还是坏事。
ctx.en: Hearing the boss wanted a word with me, I felt uneasy, not knowing whether it was good news or bad.

ctx.s: 第一次见女朋友的父母，他心里{忐忑不安}。
ctx.en: Meeting his girlfriend's parents for the first time, he felt very nervous inside.

ctx.s: 她{忐忑不安}地推开了面试官办公室的门。
ctx.en: Full of nerves, she pushed open the door of the interviewer's office.

ctx.s: “医生，检查结果怎么样？”妈妈{忐忑不安}地问。
ctx.en: "Doctor, how are the test results?" Mum asked anxiously.

ctx.s: 交了辞职信以后，他整晚{忐忑不安}，不知道老板会怎么回应。
ctx.en: After handing in his resignation he was uneasy all night, not knowing how his boss would respond.

ctx.s: 带着{忐忑不安}的心情，他拨通了那个多年没联系的号码。
ctx.en: With his heart in his mouth, he dialled the number he hadn't called in years.

bad.s: 这部恐怖片太可怕了，我看得{忐忑不安}。
bad.en: (meant: the horror film was so scary I was terrified)
bad.why: It is nervous worry about an uncertain outcome, not horror at something creepy on screen.

bad.s: 他的消息{忐忑不安}了我一整天。
bad.en: (meant: his news made me anxious all day)
bad.why: It describes the subject's own state and cannot take an object; it needs 'made me' in front of it.

cards.mean: creepy enough to make one's hair stand on end
cards.lit: hair and bones stand up in fright

use.how: Predicate, often in 令人毛骨悚然 or 听得毛骨悚然, about eerie sights, sounds, stories or gruesome details.

near.diff: 不寒而栗 is more formal and often about the thought of danger or cruelty; 毛骨悚然 is the physical creep at an eerie sight, sound or story.

cards.cue: Alone at home after midnight, you hear slow footsteps in the empty flat upstairs. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 半夜听到楼上传来哭声，我不禁{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: Hearing crying from upstairs in the middle of the night made my hair stand on end.

ctx.s: 这个鬼故事讲得太真了，听得大家{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: The ghost story was told so vividly that it gave everyone the creeps.

ctx.s: 那条小路又黑又静，走在上面让人{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: That little path is dark and silent; walking along it sends shivers down your spine.

ctx.s: “你看过那部恐怖片吗？”“看过，有几个镜头现在想起来还{毛骨悚然}。”
ctx.en: "Have you seen that horror film?" "Yes, a few of the scenes still give me the creeps when I think of them."

ctx.s: 警方公布的案情细节令人{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: The details of the case released by the police are chilling.

ctx.s: 他回头一看，镜子里竟多了一张脸，顿时{毛骨悚然}。
ctx.en: He looked back and saw an extra face in the mirror, and his hair stood on end.

bad.s: 明天就要面试了，我紧张得{毛骨悚然}。
bad.en: (meant: I have an interview tomorrow and I'm extremely nervous)
bad.why: It is horror at something eerie or gruesome, not nerves before an upcoming event.

bad.s: 今天太冷了，我冻得{毛骨悚然}。
bad.en: (meant: it's so cold I've got goosebumps)
bad.why: It describes fear at something creepy, not a physical reaction to cold.

cards.mean: heart-stopping, breathtakingly thrilling
cards.lit: startling the heart and shaking the soul

story.text: In his Grading of Poets, the critic Zhong Rong praised the anonymous 'Old Poems' of the Han: their words were gentle and beautiful, their meaning sad and far-reaching; they startled the heart and shook the soul, and were worth almost a thousand gold pieces a word. The phrase first praised deeply moving writing; today it describes thrilling or dangerous events.

use.how: Predicate or attribute about events, scenes, matches or experiences full of tension and danger: 比赛打得惊心动魄；惊心动魄的一夜。

near.diff: 扣人心弦 is gripping suspense in a story or match; 惊心动魄 adds danger and shock, as in a near-disaster.

cards.cue: The final went to the last second, with the lead changing hands again and again and the crowd on its feet. How was the match?

ctx.s: 这场决赛打得{惊心动魄}，直到最后一秒才分出胜负。
ctx.en: The final was a nail-biter; it wasn't decided until the last second.

ctx.s: 电影里的追车场面拍得{惊心动魄}。
ctx.en: The car-chase scenes in the film are heart-stopping.

ctx.s: “昨晚的比赛你看了吗？”“看了，太{惊心动魄}了，我的心都快跳出来了。”
ctx.en: "Did you watch last night's match?" "Yes, it was so thrilling my heart nearly jumped out of my chest."

ctx.s: 飞机遇到强气流的那几分钟，真是{惊心动魄}。
ctx.en: Those few minutes when the plane hit severe turbulence were truly terrifying.

ctx.s: 回忆起那次雪山遇险，他说那是一生中最{惊心动魄}的一夜。
ctx.en: Recalling his ordeal on the snowy mountain, he said it was the most harrowing night of his life.

ctx.s: 这本小说描写了一场{惊心动魄}的海上救援。
ctx.en: The novel describes a breathtaking rescue at sea.

bad.s: 听说考试推迟了，我{惊心动魄}。
bad.en: (meant: I was shocked to hear the exam had been postponed)
bad.why: It describes thrilling or dangerous events and scenes, not a person's surprise at a piece of news.

bad.s: 这个公园的风景{惊心动魄}，很适合散步。
bad.en: (meant: the park's scenery is breathtakingly beautiful and great for walks)
bad.why: English 'breathtaking' misleads: it means tension and danger, not beauty; so a calm park cannot be described this way.

cards.mean: refreshingly new to see or hear
cards.lit: ears and eyes made new all at once

use.how: Mostly in 令人/让人耳目一新 or 耳目一新的感觉, about the fresh impression a design, work, style or change makes on its audience.

near.diff: 焕然一新 says the thing itself now looks brand new; 耳目一新 says the viewer or listener gets a fresh, new impression.

cards.cue: A band turns a tired old folk song into a jazz piece, and the audience feels they are hearing it for the first time. What effect does it have?

ctx.s: 餐厅重新装修后，让人{耳目一新}。
ctx.en: After the restaurant was redecorated, it felt completely fresh.

ctx.s: 这位新导演的作品给人一种{耳目一新}的感觉。
ctx.en: This new director's work feels refreshingly original.

ctx.s: “这次的设计方案怎么样？”“很有创意，看了让人{耳目一新}。”
ctx.en: "What do you think of the design proposal?" "Very creative; it's a breath of fresh air."

ctx.s: 新校长推出的几项改革，令老师们{耳目一新}。
ctx.en: The reforms introduced by the new head struck the teachers as refreshingly new.

ctx.s: 乐队把老歌改编成了爵士风格，听起来{耳目一新}。
ctx.en: The band rearranged the old song in a jazz style, and it sounds completely fresh.

ctx.s: 换了新的排版以后，这本杂志是不是让你{耳目一新}？
ctx.en: Since the magazine changed its layout, doesn't it feel refreshingly new to you?

bad.s: 我昨天买了一部{耳目一新}的手机。
bad.en: (meant: I bought a brand-new phone yesterday)
bad.why: It describes the fresh impression something makes on people, not that an object is newly bought.

bad.s: 他{耳目一新}地看着窗外的风景。
bad.en: (meant: he looked at the view with fresh eyes)
bad.why: It is not an adverb for how someone looks; it is the effect something has on its audience.

cards.mean: heard so often one knows it by heart
cards.lit: the ear knows it so well that one can tell it in detail

story.text: Ouyang Xiu lost his father when he was a small child, and his mother told him what kind of man his father had been. In the memorial he later wrote for his parents, he records her saying that his father used certain words so often when teaching the younger members of the family that her ears had grown used to them, and so she could repeat them in detail.

use.how: Predicate or attribute: 这个故事大家都耳熟能详 / 耳熟能详的歌. Said of stories, songs, sayings or names heard again and again.

near.diff: 家喻户晓 says something is known in every household; 耳熟能详 says a person has heard it so often they could retell it.

cards.cue: Your grandfather has told the same three war stories at every family dinner for years, and you could now tell them yourself.

ctx.s: 这首儿歌大家都{耳熟能详}。
ctx.en: Everyone knows this children's song by heart.

ctx.s: 《西游记》里的故事，中国孩子几乎都{耳熟能详}。
ctx.en: Nearly every Chinese child knows the stories of Journey to the West inside out.

ctx.s: 这句广告词天天在电视上播，连老人都{耳熟能详}了。
ctx.en: That advertising slogan is on TV every day; even the elderly can recite it now.

ctx.s: “你听过这句名言吗？”“当然，从小听到大，早就{耳熟能详}了。”
ctx.en: "Have you heard this famous saying?" "Of course; I've heard it all my life and know it by heart."

ctx.s: 他讲的都是些{耳熟能详}的道理，可真正做到的人并不多。
ctx.en: What he talks about are principles we've all heard countless times, yet few people actually live by them.

ctx.s: 奶奶常讲家乡的往事，我早已{耳熟能详}，连细节都说得出来。
ctx.en: Grandma often talks about the old days back home; I've heard it so often I can give you every detail.

bad.s: 我对他的长相{耳熟能详}。
bad.en: (meant: I know his face very well)
bad.why: The idiom is about things heard over and over, such as stories or songs, not about faces or things one has seen.

bad.s: 我{耳熟能详}这首歌。
bad.en: (meant: I know this song by heart)
bad.why: It does not take a direct object; put the thing first: 'this song, I know it by heart', or use 'dui ... er shu neng xiang'.

cards.mean: harried and swamped with problems
cards.lit: a scorched head and a burnt forehead

story.text: A guest saw that a house had a straight chimney with firewood piled beside it and told the owner to build a bent chimney and move the wood, or there would be a fire. The owner ignored him. Soon the house caught fire and the neighbours put it out. To thank them the owner gave a feast, seating those with scorched heads and burnt foreheads in the places of honour, but he never invited the man who had warned him.

use.how: Usually after 得 or as a result: 忙得焦头烂额, 被……搞得焦头烂额. Describes someone worn down by a pile of troubles or urgent tasks.

near.diff: 手忙脚乱 is flustered fumbling in one hectic moment; 焦头烂额 is being battered by many troubles over days or weeks.

cards.cue: This month your landlord sold the flat, your car broke down and your boss moved the deadline forward. How do you describe your state?

ctx.s: 这几天又是搬家又是加班，我忙得{焦头烂额}。
ctx.en: These past few days I've been moving house and working overtime, and I'm completely swamped.

ctx.s: 孩子生病，工作又出了问题，她被弄得{焦头烂额}。
ctx.en: Her child is ill and there's trouble at work too; she's completely frazzled.

ctx.s: 年底各种报表一起来，财务部的人个个{焦头烂额}。
ctx.en: At year's end all the reports land at once, and everyone in finance is at their wits' end.

ctx.s: “你怎么瘦了这么多？”“公司的事搞得我{焦头烂额}，哪有时间吃饭。”
ctx.en: "Why have you lost so much weight?" "Things at the company have me so swamped I have no time to eat."

ctx.s: 新产品一上市就接到大量投诉，经理正{焦头烂额}地处理。
ctx.en: The new product drew a flood of complaints as soon as it launched, and the manager is scrambling to deal with them.

ctx.s: 与其等问题堆起来弄得{焦头烂额}，不如现在就早做准备。
ctx.en: Rather than wait until the problems pile up and overwhelm you, it's better to prepare now.

bad.s: 他工作{焦头烂额}，真是个好员工。
bad.en: (meant: he works very hard; he's a great employee)
bad.why: It describes being overwhelmed and harried by trouble, not diligence, so it is not praise for hard work.

bad.s: 他做饭的时候不小心{焦头烂额}了。
bad.en: (meant: he burned himself while cooking)
bad.why: In modern use it is only figurative, about being swamped by problems; it is never used for real burns.

cards.mean: without a single idea of how to deal with it
cards.lit: hands as if tied, and not one plan

use.how: Predicate, often 对……束手无策 or 一时束手无策. Said of someone facing a problem who wants to act but cannot think of any way.

near.diff: 无能为力 says something is beyond one's power, often when declining to help; 束手无策 says one has no idea at all what to do.

cards.cue: Your car dies on a dark country road, you know nothing about engines, and your phone has no signal.

ctx.s: 电脑突然死机了，我完全{束手无策}。
ctx.en: My computer suddenly froze and I had no idea what to do.

ctx.s: 面对这种罕见的病，年轻医生一时{束手无策}，只好去请教老专家。
ctx.en: Faced with such a rare disease, the young doctor had no idea what to do and had to go and ask a senior specialist.

ctx.s: 孩子哭个不停，新手爸爸{束手无策}地站在一旁。
ctx.en: The baby wouldn't stop crying, and the new father stood beside it, helpless and clueless.

ctx.s: “水管漏水了，怎么办？”“我也{束手无策}，赶快叫师傅吧。”
ctx.en: "The pipe's leaking, what do we do?" "I haven't a clue either; call a plumber, quick."

ctx.s: 洪水来得太快，村民们一时{束手无策}。
ctx.en: The flood came so fast that for a moment the villagers didn't know what to do.

ctx.s: 遇到困难不能{束手无策}，先冷静下来想想办法。
ctx.en: When you hit trouble you can't just stand there helpless; calm down first and think of a way.

bad.s: 他不想帮忙，就{束手无策}地站在旁边看。
bad.en: (meant: he didn't want to help, so he just stood by and watched)
bad.why: It means wanting to act but having no way to; standing by on purpose is a different idea, expressed by 'xiu shou pang guan'.

bad.s: 我实在{束手无策}他。
bad.en: (meant: I can't do anything about him)
bad.why: It takes no object; the pattern is 'dui ta shu shou wu ce', 'about him I am at a loss'.

cards.mean: at ease, feeling fully justified
cards.lit: the heart at peace, because reason is on one's side

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 心安理得地收下. Said of feeling no guilt; often critical, about someone untroubled by what should trouble them.

near.diff: 问心无愧 declares that one has done nothing wrong; 心安理得 is the easy, guilt-free feeling, often said ironically of someone who should feel bad.

cards.cue: Your flatmate eats your food every day without asking and doesn't feel the slightest bit bad about it.

ctx.s: 这钱是我自己辛苦挣的，花得{心安理得}。
ctx.en: I earned this money through my own hard work, so I spend it with a clear conscience.

ctx.s: 他把同事的功劳算在自己头上，还一副{心安理得}的样子。
ctx.en: He took credit for his colleague's work and looks perfectly at ease about it.

ctx.s: 她每天让父母做饭洗衣，自己{心安理得}地玩手机。
ctx.en: Every day she lets her parents cook and do the laundry while she plays on her phone without a second thought.

ctx.s: 这么贵重的礼物，我怎么能{心安理得}地收下？
ctx.en: How could I accept such an expensive gift with an easy conscience?

ctx.s: 把借的钱全部还清以后，他才{心安理得}地过了个年。
ctx.en: Only after paying back all the money he'd borrowed could he enjoy the New Year with his mind at ease.

ctx.s: 有些人占了公家的便宜，不但不脸红，反而{心安理得}。
ctx.en: Some people help themselves to public property and, far from blushing, feel entirely entitled.

bad.s: 考试结束了，我终于{心安理得}了。
bad.en: (meant: the exam is over and I'm finally relieved)
bad.why: It is about feeling morally justified, not about relief after stress; for relief say 'song le yi kou qi'.

bad.s: 这个房间很安静，让人{心安理得}。
bad.en: (meant: this room is quiet and makes you feel calm)
bad.why: It concerns one's conscience about what one has done, not calm caused by a peaceful place.

cards.mean: an unspoken mutual understanding
cards.lit: hearts shine on each other, but nothing is declared

use.how: Adverbial with 地 or attribute with 的: 心照不宣地笑了, 心照不宣的秘密. Said of two or more people who all know something but none says it.

near.diff: 心领神会 is grasping someone's hint at once; 心照不宣 stresses that everyone knows and all keep quiet about it.

cards.cue: The boss says 'let's revisit this later', and everyone at the table knows it means no; they just nod, and nobody says it aloud.

ctx.s: 花瓶是谁打碎的，兄妹俩{心照不宣}，谁也不说破。
ctx.en: Brother and sister both knew who had broken the vase, but neither said a word about it.

ctx.s: 他们俩在谈恋爱，这是办公室里{心照不宣}的秘密。
ctx.en: That the two of them are dating is the office's open secret that nobody mentions.

ctx.s: 老板说“再考虑考虑”，大家都{心照不宣}：这事没戏了。
ctx.en: The boss said "let's think about it more", and everyone silently understood: it's dead.

ctx.s: “这件事要不要跟他说清楚？”“不用了，彼此{心照不宣}就好。”
ctx.en: "Should we spell it out to him?" "No need; it's better if we both just understand without saying."

ctx.s: 比赛快结束时，两支球队{心照不宣}地放慢了节奏。
ctx.en: Near the end of the match, both teams slowed the pace by tacit agreement.

ctx.s: 他们从不提那次吵架，像是有个{心照不宣}的约定。
ctx.en: They never mention that quarrel, as if they had an unspoken pact.

bad.s: 我{心照不宣}地把真相告诉了他。
bad.en: (meant: I quietly told him the truth)
bad.why: It means the matter is understood without being said, so it cannot describe actually telling someone.

bad.s: 他{心照不宣}，可我什么都不知道。
bad.en: (meant: he kept it to himself, and I knew nothing)
bad.why: The understanding must be shared by both sides; for one person keeping a secret say 'bao mi' or 'bu ken shuo'.

cards.mean: frantic with worry
cards.lit: the heart anxious as if it were on fire

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地. Said of someone burning with worry when something bad may be happening or time is running out.

near.diff: 坐立不安 shows restlessness and can be mild nerves; 心急如焚 is burning, urgent worry, as when someone may be in danger.

cards.cue: Your child hasn't come home from school, it's getting dark, and nobody answers the phone.

ctx.s: 孩子发高烧不退，妈妈{心急如焚}。
ctx.en: The child's high fever won't come down, and the mother is frantic.

ctx.s: 女儿到半夜还没回家，电话也打不通，我{心急如焚}。
ctx.en: My daughter still wasn't home at midnight and her phone was unreachable; I was beside myself with worry.

ctx.s: 父亲病重，他却被困在机场，{心急如焚}。
ctx.en: His father was gravely ill, yet he was stuck at the airport, frantic.

ctx.s: “医生，我丈夫怎么样了？”她{心急如焚}地问。
ctx.en: "Doctor, how is my husband?" she asked desperately.

ctx.s: 眼看截止时间就要到了，文件还没传上去，小王{心急如焚}。
ctx.en: The deadline was nearly upon him and the file still hadn't uploaded; Xiao Wang was frantic.

ctx.s: 得知家乡发生地震，在外地工作的人们{心急如焚}，纷纷打电话回家。
ctx.en: Hearing of the earthquake back home, people working elsewhere were desperate with worry and rushed to phone their families.

bad.s: 他是个{心急如焚}的人，做什么都很快。
bad.en: (meant: he's an impatient person who does everything fast)
bad.why: It is a passing state of intense worry, not a personality trait; an impatient person is 'ji xing zi'.

bad.s: 今天天气太热了，我{心急如焚}。
bad.en: (meant: it's so hot today, I'm burning up)
bad.why: The fire is only an image for worry; it says nothing about feeling physically hot.

cards.mean: relaxed and refreshed (by open scenery)
cards.lit: the heart opened wide, the spirit delighted

story.text: Fan Zhongyan wrote an essay for the rebuilt Yueyang Tower overlooking Dongting Lake. He describes climbing the tower on a clear spring day, with calm water, sunlight and endless views, and says that a person standing there feels the heart open wide and the spirit at ease, forgetting both honour and disgrace.

use.how: Predicate, often in 让人/令人心旷神怡. Said of the calm, refreshed feeling given by wide views, fresh air or beautiful surroundings.

near.diff: 心满意足 is the satisfaction of getting what one wanted; 心旷神怡 is the open, refreshed feeling a place or view gives.

cards.cue: After weeks in a cramped office, you reach a mountain top and see sea and sky stretching out in front of you in a cool breeze.

ctx.s: 站在山顶往下看，真让人{心旷神怡}。
ctx.en: Looking down from the mountain top is truly refreshing to the soul.

ctx.s: 海风迎面吹来，我感到{心旷神怡}。
ctx.en: The sea breeze blew in my face and I felt wonderfully refreshed.

ctx.s: 雨后的公园空气清新，散步的人都觉得{心旷神怡}。
ctx.en: After the rain the park air is fresh, and everyone out walking feels relaxed and uplifted.

ctx.s: “草原上的风景怎么样？”“蓝天白云，一望无际，叫人{心旷神怡}！”
ctx.en: "What's the scenery like on the grasslands?" "Blue sky, white clouds, as far as the eye can see; it lifts your spirits!"

ctx.s: 推开窗，湖光山色尽收眼底，他顿时{心旷神怡}，疲劳全消。
ctx.en: He opened the window to the whole view of lake and hills, and at once felt refreshed, his tiredness gone.

ctx.s: 这篇游记把江南写得很美，读来令人{心旷神怡}。
ctx.en: This travel essay paints the south so beautifully that reading it is refreshing in itself.

bad.s: 听到考试通过的消息，我{心旷神怡}。
bad.en: (meant: hearing I'd passed the exam, I was overjoyed)
bad.why: It is the calm, open feeling given by scenery or surroundings, not excitement at good news.

bad.s: 我们{心旷神怡}了这里的风景。
bad.en: (meant: we enjoyed the scenery here)
bad.why: It takes no object; say the scenery 'rang ren xin kuang shen yi', makes people feel refreshed.

cards.mean: engraved on one's heart, never forgotten
cards.lit: carved into the bone, engraved on the heart

use.how: Mostly attribute: 刻骨铭心的爱情 / 教训 / 经历; also predicate. Said of deep love, pain, gratitude or lessons that mark one for life.

near.diff: 记忆犹新 says a memory is still vivid; 刻骨铭心 says an experience left a deep emotional mark that will last a lifetime.

cards.cue: Fifty years on, your grandmother still cannot speak of the night she said goodbye to her first love without tears.

ctx.s: 那是一段{刻骨铭心}的爱情。
ctx.en: It was a love she would never forget.

ctx.s: 第一次创业失败，给了他一个{刻骨铭心}的教训。
ctx.en: His first failed business taught him a lesson he'll carry for life.

ctx.s: 战争的经历对爷爷来说{刻骨铭心}，他一辈子都忘不了。
ctx.en: For Grandpa the war was seared into him; he never forgot it his whole life.

ctx.s: “你还记得高考那天吗？”“当然，那种紧张的感觉真是{刻骨铭心}。”
ctx.en: "Do you remember the day of the college entrance exam?" "Of course; that tension is still burned into me."

ctx.s: 在异国他乡生病的那个冬天，是我一生中最{刻骨铭心}的日子。
ctx.en: That winter I fell ill far from home in a foreign country was the most unforgettable time of my life.

ctx.s: 老师在我最困难时给我的帮助，我至今{刻骨铭心}。
ctx.en: The help my teacher gave me when I was at my lowest is still engraved on my heart.

bad.s: 昨天的午饭很好吃，真是{刻骨铭心}。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday's lunch was delicious and memorable)
bad.why: It is far too heavy for an ordinary pleasant thing; it is reserved for experiences of deep love, pain or gratitude.

bad.s: 我把这些单词背得{刻骨铭心}。
bad.en: (meant: I've memorised these words thoroughly)
bad.why: It is about emotional experiences that mark a person, not rote memorising; say 'bei de hen shu'.

cards.mean: to brood over a grievance
cards.lit: something troubling held in one's breast and never let go

use.how: Predicate, often 对……耿耿于怀 or 一直耿耿于怀. Said of a slight, an injustice or a defeat that someone cannot let go of.

near.diff: 念念不忘 is keeping something constantly in mind, often fondly; 耿耿于怀 is only for a grievance or setback that still rankles.

cards.cue: Three years ago a friend forgot your birthday party, and you still bring it up with a sour face.

ctx.s: 别再为那点小事{耿耿于怀}了。
ctx.en: Stop dwelling on such a small thing.

ctx.s: 他至今还对那次被冤枉{耿耿于怀}。
ctx.en: He still can't get over being wrongly accused that time.

ctx.s: 比赛只输了一分，队员们好几天都{耿耿于怀}。
ctx.en: They lost by a single point, and the players were still brooding over it days later.

ctx.s: “你还在生我的气吗？”“说实话，你那天的话我一直{耿耿于怀}。”
ctx.en: "Are you still angry with me?" "Honestly, what you said that day still rankles."

ctx.s: 没被提拔这件事，她一直{耿耿于怀}，工作也没了热情。
ctx.en: She has never got over being passed for promotion, and has lost all enthusiasm for her work.

ctx.s: 生活中不如意的事很多，总是{耿耿于怀}只会让自己更累。
ctx.en: Life is full of disappointments; nursing every one of them only wears you out.

bad.s: 我一直对奶奶做的饺子{耿耿于怀}。
bad.en: (meant: I've never forgotten Grandma's dumplings)
bad.why: It is only for grievances and setbacks that still rankle, never for fond memories; use 'nian nian bu wang' instead.

bad.s: 他一直{耿耿于怀}我。
bad.en: (meant: he holds a grudge against me)
bad.why: It takes no direct object; the pattern is 'ta dui wo geng geng yu huai'.

cards.mean: unable to stop thinking about something
cards.lit: thinking of it thought after thought, never forgetting

use.how: Predicate, often 对……念念不忘, or attribute: 念念不忘的人. Said of a person, place, taste or goal one keeps returning to in one's mind.

near.diff: 耿耿于怀 is brooding over a grievance; 念念不忘 is keeping something in mind, usually something one misses or longs for.

cards.cue: Years after a trip to Chengdu, you still talk about one little noodle shop there and keep saying you must go back.

ctx.s: 他对那家小店的牛肉面{念念不忘}。
ctx.en: He still can't stop thinking about the beef noodles at that little shop.

ctx.s: 回国好多年了，她还{念念不忘}在法国留学的日子。
ctx.en: She's been back home for years, yet she still thinks fondly of her student days in France.

ctx.s: 爷爷最{念念不忘}的，是老家门前那棵大槐树。
ctx.en: What Grandpa misses most is the big locust tree in front of his old home.

ctx.s: “你怎么又提起她了？”“没办法，我就是对她{念念不忘}。”
ctx.en: "Why are you bringing her up again?" "I can't help it; I just can't get her out of my mind."

ctx.s: 这位老科学家到了晚年，仍{念念不忘}那项没完成的研究。
ctx.en: Even in old age, the scientist never stopped thinking about his unfinished research.

ctx.s: 一次旅行让人{念念不忘}，往往不是因为风景，而是因为同行的人。
ctx.en: What makes a trip unforgettable is often not the scenery but the people you went with.

bad.s: 我每天出门都{念念不忘}带钥匙。
bad.en: (meant: I always remember to take my keys when I go out)
bad.why: It means dwelling on something one longs for or cannot let go of, not remembering to do a routine task; just say 'ji de'.

bad.s: 他是个{念念不忘}的人，什么都记得。
bad.en: (meant: he has a great memory and remembers everything)
bad.why: It describes being preoccupied with one particular thing, not a good memory in general; say 'ji xing hao'.

cards.mean: goes without saying
cards.lit: understood without being said

use.how: A predicate after a topic like 重要性, 意义, 好处 or 用意: 其中的道理不言而喻。 Says that a meaning or value needs no explaining.

near.diff: 显而易见 says a fact or conclusion is easy to see from the evidence; 不言而喻 says a meaning, value or feeling needs no words.

cards.cue: An article says that clean water matters to everyone's health, and adds that nobody needs to be told why. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 健康的重要性{不言而喻}。
ctx.en: The importance of health goes without saying.

ctx.s: 父母对孩子的爱是{不言而喻}的。
ctx.en: Parents' love for their children goes without saying.

ctx.s: 这次合作对两家公司的意义{不言而喻}，双方都非常重视。
ctx.en: What this partnership means to both companies goes without saying; both sides take it very seriously.

ctx.s: 老板没有明说，但他的意思{不言而喻}：再出错就得走人。
ctx.en: The boss didn't spell it out, but his meaning was clear without words: one more mistake and you're out.

ctx.s: 两人相视一笑，彼此的默契{不言而喻}。
ctx.en: The two of them exchanged a smile; the understanding between them needed no words.

ctx.s: 这条围巾是她亲手织的，其中的心意{不言而喻}。
ctx.en: She knitted this scarf herself; the feeling behind it needs no words.

bad.s: 他{不言而喻}地离开了房间。
bad.en: (meant: he left the room without a word)
bad.why: It is said of a meaning that needs no explaining, not of a person staying silent; for leaving without a word say yì shēng bù kēng.

bad.s: 我对这件事{不言而喻}，所以没发表意见。
bad.en: (meant: I had nothing to say about it, so I kept quiet)
bad.why: Its subject is the point or value that is self-evident, never the person who keeps quiet.

cards.mean: plainly obvious (of a conclusion)
cards.lit: clear and easy to see

use.how: A predicate or attributive about a fact, difference or conclusion (结论显而易见), or at the head of a sentence: 显而易见，他没准备。

near.diff: 不言而喻 stresses that something need not be said; 显而易见 stresses that anyone looking at the evidence can see it.

cards.cue: The sales chart shows one product's line shooting up and the other's flat. Anyone looking can tell which one wins. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 这个错误{显而易见}，你怎么没发现？
ctx.en: This mistake is plain to see; how did you miss it?

ctx.s: {显而易见}，他没有认真准备这次面试。
ctx.en: Obviously, he didn't prepare properly for this interview.

ctx.s: 数据摆在这里，结论{显而易见}：新方案效果更好。
ctx.en: The data is right here and the conclusion is obvious: the new plan works better.

ctx.s: 两种手机的差别{显而易见}，一个比另一个轻得多。
ctx.en: The difference between the two phones is obvious: one is much lighter than the other.

ctx.s: 医生看了片子说，骨折{显而易见}，需要马上手术。
ctx.en: The doctor looked at the X-ray and said the fracture was plain to see and needed surgery right away.

ctx.s: 城市扩张带来的交通问题已经{显而易见}了。
ctx.en: The traffic problems caused by the city's expansion are now obvious to everyone.

bad.s: 她长得{显而易见}，大家都注意到她了。
bad.en: (meant: she is striking to look at, everyone noticed her)
bad.why: It says a fact or conclusion is obvious, not that a person stands out; for a striking person use yǐn rén zhù mù.

bad.s: 他{显而易见}地告诉我真相。
bad.en: (meant: he told me the truth clearly)
bad.why: It describes facts being obvious, not a clear way of speaking; say he told me míngmíng báibái (plainly).

cards.mean: (formal) beyond dispute, leaving no room to question it
cards.lit: there is no need to cast any doubt on it

use.how: A predicate about a fact, claim or quality (他的能力毋庸置疑), or at the head of a sentence. Used to assert something firmly in speeches, reports and essays.

near.diff: 显而易见 says a thing is easy to see; 毋庸置疑 asserts that it cannot be doubted, and sounds more formal and authoritative.

cards.cue: A spokesperson insists that the company's commitment to safety is so firm that nobody can question it. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 他的专业能力{毋庸置疑}。
ctx.en: His professional ability is beyond question.

ctx.s: 这份报告的数据来源可靠，结论{毋庸置疑}。
ctx.en: The report's data comes from reliable sources; its conclusions are beyond dispute.

ctx.s: {毋庸置疑}，科技正在改变我们的生活方式。
ctx.en: There is no doubt that technology is changing the way we live.

ctx.s: 发言人表示，公司对产品质量的承诺是{毋庸置疑}的。
ctx.en: The spokesperson said the company's commitment to product quality is beyond question.

ctx.s: 尽管他有不少缺点，但他对球队的贡献{毋庸置疑}。
ctx.en: Despite his many flaws, his contribution to the team is beyond dispute.

ctx.s: 记者问判断会不会出错，专家回答：证据确凿，{毋庸置疑}。
ctx.en: A reporter asked whether the judgement could be wrong; the expert replied: the evidence is conclusive, there is no room for doubt.

bad.s: 妈妈，我{毋庸置疑}想吃冰淇淋！
bad.en: (meant: Mum, I really want ice cream!)
bad.why: It is a formal assertion about facts or claims, not a way to stress a personal wish in casual talk; just say tèbié xiǎng.

bad.s: 我对他的话{毋庸置疑}。
bad.en: (meant: I don't doubt what he says at all)
bad.why: It describes the claim itself, not a person's attitude; to say you fully believe someone use shēn xìn bù yí.

cards.mean: not open to serious criticism, understandable
cards.lit: nothing that may be heavily faulted

use.how: A predicate about a motive or action, often followed by a reservation: 追求利润本无可厚非，但要守法。 A mild defence, not praise.

near.diff: 情有可原 excuses a wrong already done because of the circumstances; 无可厚非 says the action or motive itself is not really wrong.

cards.cue: Your friend wants a better-paid job. You think that's a perfectly fair wish, but you add that she shouldn't lie on her CV. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 想多赚点钱，这{无可厚非}。
ctx.en: Wanting to earn a bit more money is perfectly understandable.

ctx.s: 年轻人追求时尚本来{无可厚非}，但不能超出自己的能力。
ctx.en: There's nothing wrong with young people following fashion, but they shouldn't spend beyond their means.

ctx.s: 他第一次上台，紧张一点{无可厚非}，但总该把台词背熟吧。
ctx.en: It was his first time on stage, so being a bit nervous is understandable, but he should at least have learned his lines.

ctx.s: 商家为了吸引顾客打折促销，本身{无可厚非}。
ctx.en: Shops offering discounts to attract customers is not something to criticise in itself.

ctx.s: 问：她拒绝加班有错吗？答：合同里没写，她拒绝也{无可厚非}。
ctx.en: Q: Was she wrong to refuse overtime? A: It isn't in her contract, so you can hardly blame her.

ctx.s: 评论员写道，球队换帅的决定{无可厚非}，问题出在时机上。
ctx.en: The commentator wrote that the decision to change coaches was defensible; the problem was the timing.

bad.s: 他的画画得{无可厚非}，真是天才！
bad.en: (meant: his painting is flawless, he's a genius!)
bad.why: It only says something is not blameworthy, a mild defence; for faultless work use wú kě tiāo tì.

bad.s: 我们要{无可厚非}地批评他。
bad.en: (meant: we must criticise him severely)
bad.why: It does not mean severely; it is a predicate judging an action excusable, the opposite of harsh criticism.

cards.mean: unmoved, showing no reaction
cards.lit: nothing stirs within the heart

use.how: A predicate about a person facing pleas, suffering or emotion: 他却无动于衷。 Usually reproaches coldness or stubborn indifference.

near.diff: 漠不关心 is a general lack of concern; 无动于衷 is failing to react to a specific appeal, sight or event that should move one.

cards.cue: A child is crying in front of her father and pleading with him, and he just keeps reading his newspaper. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 孩子哭了半天，他却{无动于衷}。
ctx.en: The child cried for ages, but he remained completely unmoved.

ctx.s: 看到这么感人的电影，你怎么能{无动于衷}？
ctx.en: How can you watch such a moving film and feel nothing?

ctx.s: 不管我怎么劝，他都{无动于衷}，坚持要辞职。
ctx.en: No matter how I tried to talk him round, he wouldn't budge and insisted on quitting.

ctx.s: 面对员工的抱怨，管理层始终{无动于衷}。
ctx.en: Faced with the staff's complaints, management showed no reaction at all.

ctx.s: 老人摔倒了，旁边几个人却{无动于衷}，这让大家很气愤。
ctx.en: An old man fell, yet the people next to him did nothing, which made everyone angry.

ctx.s: 她把信读了两遍，仍然{无动于衷}，随手放进了抽屉。
ctx.en: She read the letter twice, still unmoved, and tossed it into the drawer.

bad.s: 这台机器坏了，按什么按钮都{无动于衷}。
bad.en: (meant: the machine is broken, it doesn't respond to any button)
bad.why: It describes a person's heart not being moved, not a machine that fails to respond; say méiyǒu fǎnyìng.

bad.s: 他遇到危险时{无动于衷}，真勇敢！
bad.en: (meant: he stayed calm in danger, how brave!)
bad.why: It reproaches coldness and is never praise for calm courage; for that use miàn bù gǎi sè.

cards.mean: caring for someone in every little detail
cards.lit: no detail so small that it is not reached

use.how: Modifies care for people: 无微不至地照顾, 无微不至的关怀, 照顾得无微不至. Warm praise of devoted attention.

near.diff: 一丝不苟 is meticulousness in doing a task; 无微不至 is attentive, loving care for a person.

cards.cue: While you were ill, your grandmother cooked your favourite soup, checked your temperature at night and even warmed your slippers. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 妈妈对我的照顾{无微不至}。
ctx.en: My mother looks after me in every little way.

ctx.s: 住院期间，护士们{无微不至}地照顾他。
ctx.en: While he was in hospital, the nurses cared for him attentively in every detail.

ctx.s: 他对女朋友关心得{无微不至}，连她怕冷都记着。
ctx.en: He looks after his girlfriend so attentively that he even remembers she feels the cold.

ctx.s: 这家酒店的服务真是{无微不至}，连雨伞都提前准备好了。
ctx.en: This hotel's service is so attentive that they even had umbrellas ready in advance.

ctx.s: 你别看他平时话不多，对老人的照顾可是{无微不至}。
ctx.en: He may not say much, but the way he looks after the old folks is attentive in every detail.

ctx.s: 感谢信里写道：感谢老师三年来{无微不至}的关怀。
ctx.en: The thank-you letter read: thank you, teacher, for three years of caring for us in every way.

bad.s: 他打扫房间{无微不至}，连角落都擦干净了。
bad.en: (meant: he cleaned the room thoroughly, even the corners)
bad.why: It is about caring for people, not thoroughness in a chore; for careful cleaning use yì sī bù gǒu.

bad.s: 老板对员工的监视{无微不至}，大家都很不满。
bad.en: (meant: the boss watches staff in every detail, and everyone resents it)
bad.why: It is warm praise for loving care and cannot describe surveillance or control.

cards.mean: of no use, not helping at all
cards.lit: of no help to the matter

use.how: A predicate about an action or measure that fails to help: 后悔也无济于事。 It takes no object; say 对……无济于事.

near.diff: 杯水车薪 says the help is far too small for the need; 无济于事 says it does no good at all, for any reason.

cards.cue: You missed the last train home. Standing on the platform shouting at the empty tracks will change nothing. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 现在后悔也{无济于事}了。
ctx.en: Regretting it now won't do any good.

ctx.s: 光着急是{无济于事}的，得想办法。
ctx.en: Just worrying gets us nowhere; we need to find a solution.

ctx.s: 他吃了好几种药，可都{无济于事}。
ctx.en: He took several kinds of medicine, but none of them helped.

ctx.s: 问：要不要再给他打个电话？答：他已经决定了，打了也{无济于事}。
ctx.en: Q: Should I call him again? A: He's made up his mind; calling won't help.

ctx.s: 她又是道歉又是解释，却{无济于事}，客户还是取消了订单。
ctx.en: She apologised and explained, but it was no use; the client still cancelled the order.

ctx.s: 报道指出，临时修补{无济于事}，大桥必须彻底重建。
ctx.en: The report pointed out that temporary repairs are useless; the bridge must be completely rebuilt.

bad.s: 这个人{无济于事}，什么都不会。
bad.en: (meant: this person is useless, he can't do anything)
bad.why: It is said of an action or measure that fails to help, not of a useless person; just say méiyòng.

bad.s: 这些药{无济于事}我的病。
bad.en: (meant: this medicine didn't help my illness)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; put the matter before it with duì, as in: for my illness, the medicine was of no use.

cards.mean: to fabricate something out of nothing
cards.lit: to produce something out of nothing

story.text: The phrase echoes the Daodejing, which says that all things are born of being, and being is born of non-being. It is also the name of the seventh of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, a collection of military ruses: create the appearance of something that is not there in order to deceive the enemy. In everyday speech only the sense of making things up survives.

use.how: A predicate or attributive about rumours, accusations and reports: 纯属无中生有, 无中生有的传言. Accuses someone of inventing claims.

near.diff: 捕风捉影 builds a claim on flimsy hints; 无中生有 invents it with no basis whatsoever.

cards.cue: A newspaper reports that you quarrelled with your boss at a meeting, but you were on holiday that whole week and nothing of the kind happened. Which idiom fits?

ctx.s: 我根本没说过这种话，你别{无中生有}！
ctx.en: I never said anything like that; don't make things up!

ctx.s: 这篇报道完全是{无中生有}，记者根本没去现场。
ctx.en: This report is pure fabrication; the reporter never even went to the scene.

ctx.s: 有人在网上{无中生有}，说这家餐厅用过期食品。
ctx.en: Someone online invented a story that this restaurant uses expired food.

ctx.s: 问：他说你拿了公司的钱，是真的吗？答：纯属{无中生有}！
ctx.en: Q: He says you took company money; is it true? A: It's a complete fabrication!

ctx.s: 律师警告说，{无中生有}地损害他人名誉要承担法律责任。
ctx.en: The lawyer warned that damaging someone's reputation with fabricated claims carries legal liability.

ctx.s: 老同事们都了解她，那些{无中生有}的传言很快就没人信了。
ctx.en: Her old colleagues knew her well, and soon nobody believed those made-up rumours.

bad.s: 这个地方{无中生有}，什么都没有。
bad.en: (meant: this place is empty, there's nothing here)
bad.why: It does not mean empty; it means inventing claims or stories that have no basis.

bad.s: 我做了个梦，梦里的事都是{无中生有}的。
bad.en: (meant: the things in my dream weren't real)
bad.why: It accuses someone of deliberately inventing claims; a dream is simply unreal, so say it was not true.

cards.mean: so ashamed one wishes the ground would swallow one
cards.lit: no ground in which to hide oneself

use.how: A predicate or complement of feeling: 羞得无地自容, 让我无地自容. Describes intense shame or embarrassment, usually one's own.

near.diff: 面红耳赤 describes a red face from shame, anger or effort; 无地自容 is the inner feeling of wanting to disappear from shame.

cards.cue: Your teacher reads your plagiarised essay aloud next to the original, in front of the whole class. How do you feel?

ctx.s: 被老师当众批评，他羞得{无地自容}。
ctx.en: Criticised by the teacher in front of everyone, he wished the ground would swallow him up.

ctx.s: 想起当年说过的那些傻话，我就{无地自容}。
ctx.en: When I think of the silly things I said back then, I want to sink into the floor.

ctx.s: 她发现自己错怪了朋友，惭愧得{无地自容}。
ctx.en: When she realised she had wrongly blamed her friend, she was overwhelmed with shame.

ctx.s: 问：上台忘词是什么感觉？答：台下几百人看着，我简直{无地自容}。
ctx.en: Q: What's it like to forget your lines on stage? A: Hundreds of people watching; I just wanted to disappear.

ctx.s: 谎言被揭穿的那一刻，他{无地自容}，低着头一句话也说不出来。
ctx.en: The moment his lie was exposed, he was mortified; he hung his head and couldn't say a word.

ctx.s: 父亲的一番话让我{无地自容}：原来他早就知道我逃课了。
ctx.en: What my father said left me mortified: he had known all along that I was skipping class.

bad.s: 房子太小了，我们一家人{无地自容}。
bad.en: (meant: the flat is so small our family has no room)
bad.why: It is about shame, not a lack of physical space; for a flat too small to live in say zhù bú xià.

bad.s: 他做了坏事还{无地自容}，一点也不害羞。
bad.en: (meant: he did wrong and was shameless about it)
bad.why: It means overwhelming shame, the opposite of shamelessness; for shameless use tián bù zhī chǐ.

cards.mean: by fair means or foul
cards.lit: not choosing one's means

use.how: After a purpose clause (为了……不择手段) or as an adverbial: 不择手段地打压对手. Always condemns using unscrupulous means to reach a goal.

near.diff: 千方百计 is trying every possible way and can be neutral or praise; 不择手段 condemns using unethical means.

cards.cue: To win the promotion, a manager spread lies about his rival and stole her ideas. Which idiom describes how he went about it?

ctx.s: 为了赚钱，他{不择手段}。
ctx.en: He'll do anything, fair or foul, to make money.

ctx.s: 有些商家{不择手段}地欺骗顾客。
ctx.en: Some businesses will use any trick to cheat their customers.

ctx.s: 为了当上经理，她{不择手段}，连好朋友都出卖了。
ctx.en: To become manager she stopped at nothing, even betraying her best friend.

ctx.s: 为了赢一场比赛就{不择手段}，值得吗？
ctx.en: Is it worth stooping to anything just to win one match?

ctx.s: 我们想成功，但绝不能{不择手段}。
ctx.en: We want to succeed, but never by unscrupulous means.

ctx.s: 电影里的反派是个{不择手段}的人，什么坏事都干得出来。
ctx.en: The villain in the film is utterly unscrupulous, capable of any wicked deed.

bad.s: 他学习{不择手段}，什么方法都试过，终于考上了大学。
bad.en: (meant: he tried every study method and finally got into university)
bad.why: It always condemns immoral means; for trying every way to succeed use qiān fāng bǎi jì.

bad.s: 她买衣服{不择手段}，随便拿一件就走。
bad.en: (meant: she isn't picky when buying clothes, she grabs anything)
bad.why: It is not about being unfussy in choosing things; it means using any unscrupulous means to reach a goal.

cards.mean: without a moment's thought, answering on the spot
cards.lit: not borrowing (needing) any thinking or searching

use.how: Adverbial before a verb of answering, saying or writing: 他不假思索地回答。 Can praise quick fluency or hint at rashness, depending on context.

near.diff: 毫不犹豫 is acting without hesitation, from resolve; 不假思索 is responding without stopping to think at all.
脱口而出 is words slipping out, often ones you regret; 不假思索 is the speed of the reply, not the slip.

cards.cue: The teacher asks a hard question and one student fires back the answer instantly, without pausing to think. How did she answer?

ctx.s: 老师一提问，她就{不假思索}地说出了答案。
ctx.en: As soon as the teacher asked, she gave the answer without a moment's thought.

ctx.s: 问他最喜欢哪座城市，他{不假思索}地说：“当然是成都！”
ctx.en: Asked which city he likes best, he answered on the spot: "Chengdu, of course!"

ctx.s: 这些字他练了上千遍，现在能{不假思索}地写出来。
ctx.en: He has practised these characters a thousand times; now he can write them without thinking.

ctx.s: 面试官问你为什么想来，你最好别{不假思索}地随口回答。
ctx.en: When the interviewer asks why you want to join, better not to answer offhand without thinking.

ctx.s: 借钱这么大的事，你应该好好想想，怎么能{不假思索}就答应了？
ctx.en: Lending money is a big deal; you should have thought it over. How could you agree without a moment's thought?

ctx.s: 记者话音刚落，部长便{不假思索}地给出了明确答复。
ctx.en: The reporter had barely finished when the minister gave a clear reply on the spot.

bad.s: 这个问题太难了，我{不假思索}了很久。
bad.en: (meant: I thought about it for a long time)
bad.why: It means answering with no thought at all, so it cannot describe long thinking.

bad.s: 我昨天{不假思索}他的生日，真不好意思。
bad.en: (meant: I forgot about his birthday)
bad.why: It is not 'forget' and takes no object; it describes how quickly someone answers or acts.

cards.mean: neither servile nor arrogant; dignified
cards.lit: neither low (humble) nor high (overbearing)

use.how: Describes a person's manner toward someone, often someone more powerful: 他的态度不卑不亢。 Also adverbial: 不卑不亢地回答。

near.diff: 落落大方 is natural, unselfconscious ease in company; 不卑不亢 is keeping one's dignity before power or pressure.

cards.cue: Facing the company's powerful chairman, a young engineer neither flatters him nor talks down, but calmly states her view. How was her manner?

ctx.s: 他见了老板也{不卑不亢}，大家都很佩服他。
ctx.en: Even in front of the boss he is neither servile nor arrogant, and everyone admires him.

ctx.s: 面对客户的刁难，她{不卑不亢}地解释了公司的规定。
ctx.en: Faced with the client's awkward demands, she explained company policy with calm dignity.

ctx.s: 爸爸常对我说：“做人要{不卑不亢}，别看不起人，也别怕人。”
ctx.en: Dad often tells me: "Be dignified: don't look down on anyone, and don't be afraid of anyone."

ctx.s: 这位外交官在谈判中{不卑不亢}，赢得了对方的尊重。
ctx.en: The diplomat was neither servile nor overbearing in the talks and earned the other side's respect.

ctx.s: 你觉得他回答记者时的态度算不算{不卑不亢}？
ctx.en: Do you think his manner when answering the reporters counts as dignified?

ctx.s: 那个新来的实习生说话{不卑不亢}，经理对他印象很好。
ctx.en: The new intern speaks with quiet dignity, and the manager was very impressed.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜味道{不卑不亢}，还不错。
bad.en: (meant: the food is moderate, not too strong)
bad.why: It describes how a person carries themselves toward others, not taste or degree.

bad.s: 他对老师{不卑不亢}，太没礼貌了。
bad.en: (meant: he was rude to the teacher)
bad.why: It is praise for dignified manners; it cannot be used to criticise rudeness.

cards.mean: to one's heart's content; like mad (busy, having fun)
cards.lit: is it not a joy?

story.text: The phrase comes from the opening lines of the Analects, where Confucius says: to learn and practise it in due time, is that not a pleasure? When friends come from afar, is that not a joy? In the original it is a rhetorical question about joy. Later speakers reused it as a complement of degree meaning 'to an extreme degree', so today people are busy or play 'like mad'.

use.how: Mostly a complement after 得 describing a lively activity taken to the extreme: 忙得不亦乐乎, 玩得不亦乐乎, 吵得不亦乐乎.

near.diff: 乐此不疲 is enjoying something so much one never tires of it, over time; 不亦乐乎 is how intense one moment of activity is.

cards.cue: Before the Spring Festival the whole family rushes about cleaning, shopping and cooking from morning till night. How busy are they?

ctx.s: 孩子们在雪地里玩得{不亦乐乎}。
ctx.en: The kids were having a whale of a time in the snow.

ctx.s: 快过年了，妈妈每天忙得{不亦乐乎}。
ctx.en: With New Year coming, Mum is run off her feet every day.

ctx.s: 他俩为了一道数学题吵得{不亦乐乎}，谁也不让谁。
ctx.en: The two of them argued like mad over a maths problem, neither giving way.

ctx.s: 你看，爷爷在公园里跟老朋友下棋，下得{不亦乐乎}。
ctx.en: Look, Grandpa is playing chess with his old friends in the park, enjoying himself no end.

ctx.s: 搬家那天，我们几个人从早到晚忙得{不亦乐乎}。
ctx.en: On moving day a few of us were frantically busy from morning to night.

ctx.s: 聚会上大家又唱又跳，闹得{不亦乐乎}，直到半夜才散。
ctx.en: At the party everyone sang and danced and made merry like mad until midnight.

bad.s: 这部电影{不亦乐乎}，你一定要去看。
bad.en: (meant: this film is great fun)
bad.why: It does not describe a thing as fun; it follows a verb plus de to say how intensely people are doing something.

bad.s: 葬礼上，大家悲伤得{不亦乐乎}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone was deeply sad at the funeral)
bad.why: It suits lively, bustling activity and carries a light tone; it cannot express grief.

cards.mean: to gain something without working for it
cards.lit: not labouring and yet reaping

use.how: Predicate or in 想不劳而获 / 不劳而获的人; criticises living off others' work or wanting reward without effort.

near.diff: 坐享其成 is enjoying a result that others worked for; 不劳而获 is the wider wish or habit of getting anything without effort.

cards.cue: A young man keeps buying lottery tickets and chasing easy-money schemes, hoping to get rich without ever doing a day's work. What does he want?

ctx.s: 世界上没有{不劳而获}的好事。
ctx.en: There is no such thing as a free lunch in this world.

ctx.s: 他整天想着{不劳而获}，从来不肯好好工作。
ctx.en: He spends all day dreaming of getting something for nothing and never works properly.

ctx.s: 别相信那种“躺着赚钱”的广告，想{不劳而获}只会上当。
ctx.en: Don't trust those 'earn money lying down' ads; wanting something for nothing only gets you cheated.

ctx.s: 他总想找一份不用干活、工资又高的工作，这不是想{不劳而获}吗？
ctx.en: He keeps looking for a job with high pay and no work; isn't that just wanting something for nothing?

ctx.s: 父母从小就告诉我，{不劳而获}的钱拿着心里不踏实。
ctx.en: My parents taught me as a child that money you didn't work for never sits easy.

ctx.s: 他从小就有{不劳而获}的思想，长大后吃了不少苦头。
ctx.en: He grew up expecting something for nothing, and paid for it dearly as an adult.

bad.s: 这台新洗衣机让我们{不劳而获}地洗衣服。
bad.en: (meant: we can do the laundry effortlessly)
bad.why: It is a moral criticism of taking reward without work, not a way to say a task is easy.

bad.s: 他每天加班到深夜，终于{不劳而获}地升了职。
bad.en: (meant: he worked late every night and finally earned a promotion)
bad.why: It means gaining without working, so it contradicts the hard work described; it is also a criticism, never praise.

cards.mean: to have the same idea independently
cards.lit: not consulting, yet matching

use.how: Predicate, usually with 跟/与…不谋而合 or 我们的想法不谋而合; said of ideas, plans or views that coincide without prior discussion.

near.diff: 异口同声 is saying the same words at the same moment; 不谋而合 is ideas or plans matching without any prior discussion.
一拍即合 is agreeing instantly once someone proposes; 不谋而合 is reaching the same idea separately before talking.

cards.cue: You and a friend, without talking about it, each bought the same book as a present for your teacher. How did your choices relate?

ctx.s: 我们俩的想法{不谋而合}，都想去云南旅行。
ctx.en: We both had the same idea without talking: we each wanted to travel to Yunnan.

ctx.s: 没想到你的方案跟我的{不谋而合}！
ctx.en: I never expected your plan to match mine so exactly!

ctx.s: 两位科学家在不同的国家研究，结论却{不谋而合}。
ctx.en: The two scientists worked in different countries, yet independently reached the same conclusion.

ctx.s: “你也打算辞职创业？”“是啊，看来咱们{不谋而合}。”
ctx.en: "You're planning to quit and start a business too?" "Yes, looks like we had the same idea."

ctx.s: 他提出的建议与经理心里的打算{不谋而合}，当场就被采纳了。
ctx.en: His suggestion happened to match exactly what the manager had in mind and was adopted on the spot.

ctx.s: 这位作家的观点，和古人的看法竟然{不谋而合}。
ctx.en: This writer's view turns out to coincide with that of the ancients.

bad.s: 我们开了三次会，最后终于{不谋而合}了。
bad.en: (meant: after three meetings we finally agreed)
bad.why: It means matching without consulting; an agreement reached through discussion is not a coincidence of ideas.

bad.s: 我{不谋而合}他的看法。
bad.en: (meant: my view is the same as his)
bad.why: It takes no object; say that my view and his matched, with the views as the subject.

cards.mean: too dreadful to contemplate (consequences)
cards.lit: cannot bear to imagine

use.how: Predicate of 后果 or a clause: (否则)后果不堪设想。 Said of what would happen if something went wrong; often after 如果/要是/否则.

near.diff: 不可思议 is amazing or hard to believe, good or bad; 不堪设想 is only a dreadful outcome that might happen.

cards.cue: A driver nodded off at the wheel and woke just before hitting a lorry. What would the consequences have been if he hadn't woken up?

ctx.s: 幸亏发现得早，不然后果{不堪设想}。
ctx.en: Luckily it was spotted early; otherwise the consequences would have been too dreadful to think about.

ctx.s: 开车时千万别看手机，出了事后果{不堪设想}。
ctx.en: Never look at your phone while driving; if something happens the consequences are unthinkable.

ctx.s: 要是那天孩子没被拉住，真是{不堪设想}啊！
ctx.en: If the child hadn't been grabbed that day, it doesn't bear thinking about!

ctx.s: 如果大坝出现裂缝而无人发现，下游的情况将{不堪设想}。
ctx.en: If the dam cracked and no one noticed, the situation downstream would be too terrible to imagine.

ctx.s: 医生说，再晚送来一个小时，结果就{不堪设想}了。
ctx.en: The doctor said that had he been brought in an hour later, the outcome would not bear thinking about.

ctx.s: 泄露客户资料的后果{不堪设想}，你想过没有？
ctx.en: The consequences of leaking client data would be dreadful; have you thought about that?

bad.s: 这个计划成功的话，收益{不堪设想}。
bad.en: (meant: the profit would be beyond imagining)
bad.why: It only describes terrible outcomes, never good ones; huge gains need a different expression.

bad.s: 他小时候的生活很苦，{不堪设想}。
bad.en: (meant: his childhood was unimaginably hard)
bad.why: It is about a dreadful outcome that could happen, not hardship already lived through.

cards.mean: to disagree, quietly unconvinced
cards.lit: not taking it to be so (not thinking it right)

use.how: Predicate or adverbial, often 对…不以为然 or 不以为然地摇摇头; shows disagreement with a view, often unspoken or mildly dismissive.

near.diff: 不以为意 is not taking something seriously or not minding it; 不以为然 is thinking a view is wrong.

cards.cue: Your colleague says remote work makes people lazy. You don't agree, and you just give a small shake of the head. How do you feel about his claim?

ctx.s: 他说这部电影很好看，我却{不以为然}。
ctx.en: He said the film was great, but I wasn't convinced.

ctx.s: 听了我的建议，奶奶{不以为然}地摇了摇头。
