ctx.en: Hearing my suggestion, Grandma shook her head, unconvinced.

ctx.s: 很多人认为学历最重要，对此我一直{不以为然}。
ctx.en: Many people think qualifications matter most; I have never agreed with that.

ctx.s: “你好像对他的说法{不以为然}？”“嗯，我觉得他说得太绝对了。”
ctx.en: "You don't seem to agree with what he said?" "No, I think he's too absolute."

ctx.s: 专家的预测公布后，不少网友表示{不以为然}。
ctx.en: After the expert's forecast was published, many netizens said they didn't buy it.

ctx.s: 父亲对我选的专业有些{不以为然}，但没有反对。
ctx.en: My father was a little sceptical of the major I chose, but he didn't object.

bad.s: 他发烧了，却{不以为然}，照常去上班。
bad.en: (meant: he had a fever but didn't take it seriously)
bad.why: Not taking something seriously is a different idiom; this one means disagreeing with a view.

bad.s: 我对你的意见{不以为然}，完全同意。
bad.en: (meant: I fully agree with your opinion)
bad.why: It expresses disagreement, so it contradicts saying that you fully agree.

cards.mean: to leave without saying goodbye
cards.lit: not taking leave, yet departing

use.how: Predicate of a person who leaves a place or people without a farewell: 他不辞而别了。 Often carries surprise, hurt or blame.

near.diff: 扬长而去 is striding off defiantly in front of others; 不辞而别 is leaving quietly without telling anyone.

cards.cue: A housemate packed up during the night and moved out without a word to anyone. What did he do?

ctx.s: 他昨晚{不辞而别}，连张纸条都没留。
ctx.en: He left last night without saying goodbye, not even leaving a note.

ctx.s: 对不起，那天走得太急，{不辞而别}，请你原谅。
ctx.en: I'm sorry I left in such a hurry that day without saying goodbye; please forgive me.

ctx.s: 为什么你要{不辞而别}？大家都在找你！
ctx.en: Why did you leave without a word? Everyone's been looking for you!

ctx.s: 那位保姆干了半年，突然{不辞而别}，家里乱成一团。
ctx.en: The nanny worked for six months, then suddenly left without notice, and the household was thrown into chaos.

ctx.s: 聚会还没结束，他就悄悄{不辞而别}了。
ctx.en: Before the party was over he had quietly slipped away without saying goodbye.

ctx.s: 小说里，男主角{不辞而别}，只在桌上留下一封信。
ctx.en: In the novel the hero leaves without a farewell, leaving only a letter on the table.

bad.s: 他跟大家一一握手告别后，{不辞而别}了。
bad.en: (meant: he said goodbye to everyone and left)
bad.why: It means leaving without a farewell, so it contradicts saying goodbye first.

bad.s: 他上个月{不辞而别}了这家公司。
bad.en: (meant: last month he left this company without saying goodbye)
bad.why: It takes no object; the place left must come before it with a preposition (from this company), not after it.

cards.mean: indispensable
cards.lit: cannot be lacking even slightly

use.how: Predicate or attributive with 的, said of a thing or person that something cannot do without: 水是生命不可或缺的。 The subject is the needed thing.

near.diff: Almost the same meaning; 必不可少 is a little plainer and more common in speech, 不可或缺 more written.

cards.cue: In a report on the team, you want to say that one quiet engineer is someone the project simply could not run without.

ctx.s: 手机已经成了生活中{不可或缺}的东西。
ctx.en: The mobile phone has become something we can't do without in daily life.

ctx.s: 在这个团队里，她是{不可或缺}的一员。
ctx.en: On this team she is an indispensable member.

ctx.s: 阳光和水分对植物的生长来说都{不可或缺}。
ctx.en: Sunlight and water are both indispensable to a plant's growth.

ctx.s: 你觉得在一段友谊中，什么是{不可或缺}的？
ctx.en: What do you think is indispensable in a friendship?

ctx.s: 诚信是企业长期发展{不可或缺}的基础。
ctx.en: Integrity is an indispensable foundation for a company's long-term growth.

ctx.s: 对南方人来说，米饭是每顿饭里{不可或缺}的主食。
ctx.en: For southerners, rice is the staple that no meal can be without.

bad.s: 他{不可或缺}这本词典。
bad.en: (meant: he can't do without this dictionary)
bad.why: It takes no object; the needed thing is the subject: the dictionary is indispensable to him.

bad.s: 他每天都{不可或缺}地迟到。
bad.en: (meant: he is late every day without fail)
bad.why: It means something is indispensable, not that something happens without fail.

cards.mean: sparing no effort (to promote or support)
cards.lit: not leaving any strength unused

use.how: Adverbial with 地 before verbs like 支持, 帮助, 推广, 宣传: 不遗余力地支持. Said of sustained effort for a cause, a person or a plan.

near.diff: 全力以赴 is throwing everything into one's own task or contest; 不遗余力 is sustained effort to support or promote something.

cards.cue: For twenty years an old teacher has used every spare hour and all his savings to help poor village children go to school. How has he helped them?

ctx.s: 这些年，父母一直{不遗余力}地支持我的梦想。
ctx.en: All these years my parents have spared no effort in supporting my dream.

ctx.s: 老校长{不遗余力}地帮助山区孩子上学。
ctx.en: The old headmaster spared no effort helping children from the mountains go to school.

ctx.s: 他退休后仍{不遗余力}地推广传统书法。
ctx.en: Even after retiring he works tirelessly to promote traditional calligraphy.

ctx.s: 政府表示将{不遗余力}地保护这片湿地。
ctx.en: The government says it will spare no effort to protect this wetland.

ctx.s: 为了让新产品打开市场，公司在宣传上{不遗余力}。
ctx.en: To open up the market for the new product, the company has spared no effort on promotion.

ctx.s: 你真的相信他会{不遗余力}地帮你吗？
ctx.en: Do you really believe he'll do everything he can to help you?

bad.s: 这个箱子太重了，我搬得{不遗余力}。
bad.en: (meant: I carried it with all my strength)
bad.why: It is not a complement of degree and does not describe one physical exertion; it is sustained effort for a cause.

bad.s: 这次考试很简单，我{不遗余力}就通过了。
bad.en: (meant: the exam was easy and I passed effortlessly)
bad.why: It means putting every ounce of effort into something, the opposite of doing it effortlessly.

cards.mean: to neglect one's proper job or studies
cards.lit: not attending to one's proper occupation

use.how: Predicate or after 是/被批评: 他整天打游戏，不务正业。 Said of a person, or a company, putting effort into things other than its real job; also used jokingly of one's own hobbies.

cards.cue: A student skips class for months to stream video games all day, and his father complains about him to the neighbours.

ctx.s: 他整天打游戏，也不去上课，妈妈说他{不务正业}。
ctx.en: He plays games all day and doesn't go to class; his mother says he's neglecting what he should be doing.

ctx.s: 他上班时间总在网上卖东西，老板觉得他有点{不务正业}。
ctx.en: He's always selling things online during working hours, and his boss thinks he's neglecting his real job.

ctx.s: 这家银行不好好做金融，跑去投资房地产，被批评{不务正业}。
ctx.en: Instead of sticking to banking, this bank went into property and was criticised for straying from its core business.

ctx.s: “你一个医生，怎么写起小说来了？”“业余爱好而已，算不上{不务正业}。”
ctx.en: "You're a doctor, how come you've started writing novels?" "It's just a hobby; it's not like I'm neglecting my job."

ctx.s: 年轻时他被村里人看作{不务正业}的人，后来却成了有名的歌手。
ctx.en: When he was young the villagers saw him as a good-for-nothing who neglected real work, but he later became a famous singer.

ctx.s: 别总说孩子学画画是{不务正业}，兴趣也很重要。
ctx.en: Stop saying that a child learning to paint is neglecting their studies; interests matter too.

bad.s: 他失业了，现在{不务正业}。
bad.en: (meant: he lost his job and is unemployed now)
bad.why: It criticises someone who has a proper job or studies and neglects them; it does not mean being out of work.

bad.s: 他今天发烧了，所以{不务正业}，请假在家休息。
bad.en: (meant: he's sick, so he took the day off)
bad.why: Taking sick leave is not neglect; the idiom judges a habit of spending effort on the wrong things.

cards.mean: refusing to be outdone
cards.lit: not willing to show weakness

use.how: Predicate, often after 也: 对手进了一球，我们也不甘示弱。 Describes answering a rival's move with an equal or stronger one.

near.diff: 争先恐后 is a crowd all rushing to be first; 不甘示弱 is one side responding to another's challenge so as not to fall behind.

cards.cue: The other team has just scored, and within minutes your team hits back and levels the game. How do you describe your team's response?

ctx.s: 哥哥跑了第一，弟弟也{不甘示弱}，拼命追了上去。
ctx.en: The older brother took the lead, and the younger one, not to be outdone, ran all out to catch him.

ctx.s: 对方进了一个球，我们队{不甘示弱}，很快就扳平了比分。
ctx.en: The other side scored, but our team refused to be outdone and soon equalised.

ctx.s: 一家店降价以后，对面那家也{不甘示弱}，打出了更低的价格。
ctx.en: After one shop cut its prices, the shop across the road wasn't going to be outdone and offered even lower ones.

ctx.s: 她说我不会做饭，我当然{不甘示弱}，第二天就做了一桌菜。
ctx.en: She said I couldn't cook, so of course I wasn't going to take that lying down: the next day I made a whole spread.

ctx.s: 面对大公司的压力，这家小公司{不甘示弱}，推出了自己的新产品。
ctx.en: Under pressure from the big firms, this small company refused to be outdone and launched its own new product.

ctx.s: “你看隔壁班的合唱多好！”“我们班也{不甘示弱}，你等着看吧。”
ctx.en: "Look how good the class next door is at singing!" "Our class won't be outdone either, just you wait."

bad.s: 考试没考好，他{不甘示弱}，在房间里哭了一整天。
bad.en: (meant: he couldn't accept the bad result and cried all day)
bad.why: It means rising to a challenge by competing back; crying in disappointment is the opposite of not showing weakness.

bad.s: 他是个很{不甘示弱}的人，从来不愿意帮助别人。
bad.en: (meant: he's a stubborn person who never helps anyone)
bad.why: It means rising to a rival's challenge so as not to fall behind; it says nothing about being stubborn or unwilling to help others.

cards.mean: impossible to reason with
cards.lit: cannot be made to understand by reason

use.how: Predicate, often with 简直 or 太…了: 他简直不可理喻。 A sharp judgement of a person, or their behaviour, that will not listen to reason.

near.diff: 无理取闹 is making a scene without cause; 不可理喻 says that trying to reason with the person is hopeless.

cards.cue: However calmly you explain the facts, your neighbour refuses to listen and keeps insisting he is right. What do you call him?

ctx.s: 我跟他解释了半天，他就是不听，真是{不可理喻}。
ctx.en: I spent ages explaining it to him and he just wouldn't listen; there's no reasoning with him.

ctx.s: 那个顾客自己弄坏了东西，店员怎么解释他都不听，简直{不可理喻}。
ctx.en: That customer broke the thing himself, and whatever the shop assistant explained, he wouldn't listen. There's just no reasoning with him.

ctx.s: “你怎么又跟她吵起来了？”“她太{不可理喻}了，什么道理都听不进去。”
ctx.en: "Why are you arguing with her again?" "She's impossible to reason with; she won't hear a word of sense."

ctx.s: 因为一片树叶落到他家院子里就报警，这种行为实在{不可理喻}。
ctx.en: Calling the police because one leaf fell into his yard: that kind of behaviour is beyond all reason.

ctx.s: 小说里的老父亲固执得{不可理喻}，谁劝都没用。
ctx.en: The old father in the novel is unreasonably stubborn; no one can talk him round.

ctx.s: 你们都觉得他{不可理喻}，可有没有人认真听过他的理由？
ctx.en: You all think he's impossible to reason with, but has anyone actually listened to his reasons?

bad.s: 这道数学题太难了，我觉得{不可理喻}。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is incomprehensible)
bad.why: It is about a person who won't listen to reason, not a thing that is hard to understand.

bad.s: 奶奶耳朵听不清，跟她说话真{不可理喻}。
bad.en: (meant: grandma is hard of hearing, so talking to her is hard)
bad.why: It accuses someone of stubborn unreasonableness; using it of someone who simply can't hear is wrong and rude.

cards.mean: to chatter on annoyingly
cards.lit: chattering and chattering without stopping

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 他喋喋不休地抱怨。 Said of someone talking on and on, to the annoyance of the listener.

near.diff: 七嘴八舌 is many people talking at once; 喋喋不休 is someone going on and on without stopping.

cards.cue: On a long train ride, your seatmate talks about his ex-wife for three hours without a pause, though you stopped listening long ago.

ctx.s: 他一上车就{喋喋不休}地讲他的旅行，大家都听烦了。
ctx.en: As soon as he got in the car he went on and on about his trip, and everyone got sick of it.

ctx.s: 会上他{喋喋不休}地说了一个小时，别人根本插不上话。
ctx.en: At the meeting he droned on for an hour and nobody else could get a word in.

ctx.s: “你能不能别再{喋喋不休}了？我已经知道错了。”
ctx.en: "Can you please stop going on about it? I already know I was wrong."

ctx.s: 那个推销员在门口{喋喋不休}，我怎么拒绝都没用。
ctx.en: The salesman kept talking at the door, and nothing I said to refuse him did any good.

ctx.s: 为了一点小事，她在电话里{喋喋不休}地说了半天。
ctx.en: Over a trivial matter, she went on and on over the phone for ages.

ctx.s: 与其{喋喋不休}地抱怨，不如想想怎么解决问题。
ctx.en: Rather than complaining endlessly, you'd do better to think about how to solve the problem.

bad.s: 他平时很少说话，今天开会也只是{喋喋不休}地说了两句。
bad.en: (meant: he only said a couple of sentences at the meeting)
bad.why: It means talking on and on without stopping; a couple of sentences contradicts it.

bad.s: 妈妈每天都{喋喋不休}我，让我早点睡觉。
bad.en: (meant: mum nags me every day to go to bed early)
bad.why: It is intransitive and cannot take the person being talked at as its object; the listener has to be introduced with the preposition dui, meaning to, before it.

cards.mean: to shoot one's mouth off without basis
cards.lit: to let one's mouth run wherever it pleases

use.how: Predicate, often in 别/不能信口开河: 没有证据就别信口开河。 Criticises claims or promises made casually, without facts or thought.

near.diff: 胡说八道 is blunt, colloquial 'utter nonsense'; 信口开河 stresses claims or promises made carelessly, without basis or thought of consequences.

cards.cue: Without checking a single fact, a TV guest confidently promises that house prices will halve next year.

ctx.s: 没调查清楚就别{信口开河}，会害了别人的。
ctx.en: Don't go making claims before you've looked into it; you could hurt someone.

ctx.s: 他说三天就能完成，完全是{信口开河}，根本做不到。
ctx.en: He said it could be done in three days, but he was just talking; it's impossible.

ctx.s: 作为专家，在电视上可不能{信口开河}。
ctx.en: As an expert, you can't just say whatever comes into your head on television.

ctx.s: “我保证下个月就把钱全还你。”“你上次也这么说，别再{信口开河}了。”
ctx.en: "I promise I'll pay you back in full next month." "You said that last time too; stop making promises you can't keep."

ctx.s: 这位网红为了流量{信口开河}，受到很多网友批评。
ctx.en: This influencer made wild claims to get clicks and was criticised by many people online.

ctx.s: 他一喝酒就{信口开河}，答应了一大堆根本办不到的事。
ctx.en: Whenever he drinks, he talks big and promises all kinds of things he can't possibly do.

bad.s: 她口才很好，开会时总是{信口开河}，大家都很佩服。
bad.en: (meant: she is eloquent and everyone admires her)
bad.why: It criticises talk without basis; it is never praise for eloquence.

bad.s: 周末我们在公园里{信口开河}地聊了聊天气。
bad.en: (meant: we chatted casually about the weather)
bad.why: It is about irresponsible claims or promises, not relaxed small talk.

cards.mean: the implied meaning, what is left unsaid
cards.lit: the meaning outside the words

use.how: A noun phrase: subject (言外之意是…) or object (听出他的言外之意). Names what a speaker means but does not say.

cards.cue: Your host glances at the clock and remarks that it's getting late. What is she really telling you without saying it?

ctx.s: 她说“时间不早了”，{言外之意}就是希望客人回家。
ctx.en: She said "It's getting late", which really meant she wanted the guests to go home.

ctx.s: 你没听出他的{言外之意}吗？他是不想借钱给你。
ctx.en: Didn't you catch what he was implying? He doesn't want to lend you money.

ctx.s: 老板说“你最近好像挺闲的”，{言外之意}是嫌你干得不够多。
ctx.en: The boss said "You seem to have a lot of free time lately", meaning that he thinks you're not doing enough.

ctx.s: “我做的菜怎么样？”“挺有创意的。”“你的{言外之意}是不好吃吧？”
ctx.en: "How's my cooking?" "Very creative." "What you mean is it doesn't taste good, right?"

ctx.s: 好的诗常常有{言外之意}，要慢慢体会。
ctx.en: Good poems often say more than their words do, and you have to take time to feel it.

ctx.s: 学外语最难的不是词汇，而是听懂别人的{言外之意}。
ctx.en: The hardest part of learning a foreign language isn't vocabulary; it's understanding what people imply.

bad.s: 这个词的{言外之意}是“苹果”，你查查字典就知道了。
bad.en: (meant: the dictionary meaning of this word is 'apple')
bad.why: It is the unspoken implication in a situation, the opposite of a word's literal dictionary meaning.

bad.s: 他没有直说，而是{言外之意}地拒绝了我。
bad.en: (meant: he turned me down indirectly)
bad.why: It is a noun, 'the implied meaning', not an adverb describing how someone acts.

cards.mean: to go back on one's word
cards.lit: what goes out from you comes back to you

story.text: The small state of Zou fought a skirmish with Lu, and thirty-three of its officers were killed while the common people stood by and did nothing to save them. Duke Mu of Zou asked Mencius what to do. Mencius answered that in years of famine the people had starved while the duke's granaries were full, and no official had told him. He quoted Zengzi: 'Beware, beware! What goes out from you comes back to you.' The people had simply paid the officials back. Later the phrase came to mean saying one thing and then doing the opposite.

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 你怎么能出尔反尔？ 出尔反尔的做法. Criticises someone who promises or agrees to something and then goes back on it.

cards.cue: The landlord signed a contract keeping the rent the same, then a week later demanded more. How do you describe what he did?

ctx.s: 你昨天答应帮我，今天又说不行，怎么能{出尔反尔}呢？
ctx.en: Yesterday you promised to help me and today you say you can't. How can you go back on your word like that?

ctx.s: 房东签了合同又要涨房租，这种{出尔反尔}的做法让人很生气。
ctx.en: The landlord signed the contract and then wanted to raise the rent; that kind of going back on a deal is infuriating.

ctx.s: 父母说话要算数，如果{出尔反尔}，孩子就不会再信你了。
ctx.en: Parents must keep their word; if you keep going back on it, your children will stop believing you.

ctx.s: “上次你也说不再迟到了。”“这次我保证，绝不{出尔反尔}。”
ctx.en: "Last time you also said you wouldn't be late again." "This time I promise, I won't go back on my word."

ctx.s: 那家公司在谈判中多次{出尔反尔}，最后没人愿意和它合作。
ctx.en: That company went back on what it had agreed several times during the talks, and in the end nobody would work with it.

ctx.s: 他向来说话算话，从来没有{出尔反尔}过。
ctx.en: He has always kept his word; he has never once gone back on it.

bad.s: 他早上从北京出发，晚上又{出尔反尔}回到了北京。
bad.en: (meant: he left Beijing in the morning and came back in the evening)
bad.why: It is about breaking one's word, not physically going somewhere and coming back.

bad.s: 我仔细想了想，发现原来的看法错了，就{出尔反尔}改正了。
bad.en: (meant: after thinking it over I corrected my mistaken view)
bad.why: It is harsh criticism of breaking promises to others; honestly correcting one's own opinion is not that.

cards.mean: opinions differ widely
cards.lit: many voices, all tangled together

use.how: Predicate, often after a topic: 关于原因，众说纷纭。 Says that many people give different answers to one question and none is settled.

near.diff: 议论纷纷 is everyone talking about something; 众说纷纭 stresses that their answers differ and there is no agreement.

cards.cue: Historians still disagree about who built an ancient bridge; each one gives a different answer and none can prove it.

ctx.s: 关于这次停电的原因，大家{众说纷纭}。
ctx.en: There are all sorts of theories about what caused the power cut.

ctx.s: 喝咖啡到底对身体好不好，专家们{众说纷纭}。
ctx.en: Experts disagree widely on whether coffee is actually good for you.

ctx.s: 对于这部电影的结局，网友{众说纷纭}，有人喜欢，有人失望。
ctx.en: People online have very different views on the film's ending: some love it, some are disappointed.

ctx.s: “他为什么突然辞职？”“公司里{众说纷纭}，有人说是跳槽，有人说是生病。”
ctx.en: "Why did he suddenly quit?" "Everyone at the company has a different story: some say he's changing jobs, some say he's ill."

ctx.s: 这座古塔是谁建的，至今{众说纷纭}，没有定论。
ctx.en: Who built this ancient pagoda is still disputed, with no settled answer.

ctx.s: 在{众说纷纭}的时候，我们更需要冷静地看事实。
ctx.en: When opinions are all over the place, we need all the more to look calmly at the facts.

bad.s: 下课了，教室里{众说纷纭}，非常吵。
bad.en: (meant: after class the room was full of noisy chatter)
bad.why: It means differing opinions on one question, not a room full of noisy chatter.

bad.s: 大家都同意这个计划，真是{众说纷纭}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone spoke up in support of the plan)
bad.why: It means opinions diverge; when everyone agrees it is the opposite situation.

cards.mean: to talk about with relish
cards.lit: to talk about something with delight, savouring it

use.how: Predicate with an object or with 对/被: 球迷至今津津乐道这场比赛。 Said of a story or event people love retelling; can be ironic about boasting.

near.diff: 津津有味 is eating, reading or watching with relish; 津津乐道 is talking about something with relish.
念念不忘 is being unable to stop thinking about something; 津津乐道 is happily and repeatedly talking about it.

cards.cue: At every family dinner your uncle retells, with obvious delight, the day he shook hands with a famous footballer.

ctx.s: 爷爷总是{津津乐道}他年轻时当兵的故事。
ctx.en: Grandpa always loves telling stories about his time in the army when he was young.

ctx.s: 那场比赛最后一秒的进球，球迷们到现在还{津津乐道}。
ctx.en: Fans still talk with relish about that last-second goal.

ctx.s: 那家小店的牛肉面，是老顾客们最{津津乐道}的。
ctx.en: That little shop's beef noodles are what its regulars most love to talk about.

ctx.s: 这位作家和猫的趣事，一直被读者{津津乐道}。
ctx.en: Readers never tire of talking about the funny stories about this writer and the cat.

ctx.s: 他对自己的成功{津津乐道}，却从不提别人的帮助。
ctx.en: He loves to hold forth about his own success but never mentions the help he got.

ctx.s: “你又在讲你钓到大鱼的事？”“这么难得的事，当然值得{津津乐道}。”
ctx.en: "Are you telling the story of your big fish again?" "Something that rare deserves to be talked about!"

bad.s: 他饿坏了，{津津乐道}地吃完了一大碗面。
bad.en: (meant: he hungrily ate a big bowl of noodles with relish)
bad.why: It is about talking with relish; it cannot describe eating with relish.

bad.s: 大家都在{津津乐道}那场可怕的车祸，很多人都哭了。
bad.en: (meant: everyone was talking about the terrible crash)
bad.why: It implies delight and enjoyment; a tragedy is talked about with grief, so the idiom is badly out of place.

cards.mean: to speak one's mind freely
cards.lit: to say freely all one wishes to say

use.how: Predicate, often after 可以/能/请: 今天大家可以畅所欲言。 Describes an open setting where people can say everything they think.

near.diff: 直言不讳 is speaking bluntly without softening, even at risk of offence; 畅所欲言 is about a free atmosphere where everyone can say all they think.

cards.cue: Opening a brainstorming session, the manager tells the team that no idea is too silly and nothing said will be held against anyone.

ctx.s: 今天是自由讨论，大家可以{畅所欲言}。
ctx.en: Today is an open discussion, so everyone feel free to say whatever you think.

ctx.s: 在这个小组里，每个人都能{畅所欲言}，没有人会笑你。
ctx.en: In this group everyone can speak their mind; nobody will laugh at you.

ctx.s: “我说的话会不会让领导不高兴？”“放心，今天就是请你来{畅所欲言}的。”
ctx.en: "Won't what I say upset the management?" "Don't worry, you've been invited precisely to speak freely."

ctx.s: 校长希望学生们在座谈会上{畅所欲言}，提出真实的意见。
ctx.en: The principal hopes the students will speak freely at the forum and give their honest opinions.

ctx.s: 老朋友们一边喝茶一边{畅所欲言}，一直聊到深夜。
ctx.en: The old friends drank tea and talked openly about everything until late at night.

ctx.s: 如果员工不敢{畅所欲言}，公司就很难发现问题。
ctx.en: If employees don't dare to speak their minds, it's hard for the company to spot its problems.

bad.s: 他喝多了，{畅所欲言}地把服务员骂了一顿。
bad.en: (meant: he got drunk and freely cursed the waiter)
bad.why: It is positive, about freely sharing views in an open setting, not venting abuse at someone.

bad.s: 小王一开会就{畅所欲言}，别人都插不上话，大家很烦。
bad.en: (meant: Xiao Wang talks so much at meetings that it annoys everyone)
bad.why: It is positive and about everyone being free to speak; it cannot describe someone annoyingly hogging the floor.

cards.mean: to speak bluntly, without mincing words
cards.lit: to speak straight out, avoiding no taboo subject

use.how: Adverbial (直言不讳地指出) or predicate. Said of someone who openly states criticism or an unwelcome truth.

near.diff: 心直口快 is a personality that blurts out whatever it thinks; 直言不讳 is openly stating an unwelcome truth on a given occasion.

cards.cue: Everyone at the meeting praised the plan, but one engineer stood up and said plainly that it would fail. How did she speak?

ctx.s: 朋友{直言不讳}地告诉我，这件衣服不适合我。
ctx.en: My friend told me straight out that this outfit doesn't suit me.

ctx.s: 会上，她{直言不讳}地指出了方案里的三个问题。
ctx.en: At the meeting she bluntly pointed out three problems in the plan.

ctx.s: 你觉得我的论文怎么样？请{直言不讳}，不用客气。
ctx.en: What do you think of my thesis? Please be blunt, don't be polite.

ctx.s: 这位评论家一向{直言不讳}，很多导演都怕他。
ctx.en: This critic has always been outspoken, and many directors are afraid of him.

ctx.s: 面对记者的提问，部长{直言不讳}地承认了工作中的失误。
ctx.en: Faced with the reporters' questions, the minister frankly admitted the mistakes that had been made.

ctx.s: 他在信中{直言不讳}，把公司管理上的问题一条条列了出来。
ctx.en: In his letter he held nothing back, listing the company's management problems one by one.

bad.s: 他{直言不讳}地走进了办公室。
bad.en: (meant: he walked straight into the office)
bad.why: The 'straight' here is about speech, not direction; the idiom only describes how someone speaks.

bad.s: 他不想让别人知道这件事，所以{直言不讳}。
bad.en: (meant: he didn't want anyone to know, so he kept quiet)
bad.why: The idiom means speaking openly and holding nothing back, the opposite of keeping quiet.

cards.mean: to advise someone earnestly and patiently
cards.lit: a toiling mouth and a grandmother's heart: urging again and again with an old woman's kindly care

use.how: Adverbial before 劝/说/叮嘱 (苦口婆心地劝他) or predicate. Stresses patient, repeated urging meant to make someone change.

near.diff: 语重心长 describes the weight and sincerity of what is said in one talk; 苦口婆心 stresses urging patiently, again and again.

cards.cue: For a whole month a mother kept patiently reasoning with her son, day after day, to get him to stop gaming all night. How did she advise him?

ctx.s: 妈妈{苦口婆心}地劝他少玩游戏，他就是不听。
ctx.en: His mother kept patiently urging him to play fewer games, but he just wouldn't listen.

ctx.s: 老师{苦口婆心}说了半天，他终于答应回学校上课了。
ctx.en: After the teacher had reasoned with him at length, he finally agreed to come back to class.

ctx.s: 我{苦口婆心}劝了你多少次，你怎么还是不戴头盔？
ctx.en: How many times have I begged you, and you still don't wear a helmet?

ctx.s: 医生{苦口婆心}地劝了好几回，老人才答应戒酒。
ctx.en: Only after the doctor had patiently urged him several times did the old man agree to give up drinking.

ctx.s: 不管社区工作人员怎么{苦口婆心}地劝，那家人还是不肯搬走。
ctx.en: No matter how patiently the community workers pleaded, that family still refused to move out.

ctx.s: 经过朋友们一次又一次{苦口婆心}的劝说，他总算把烟戒了。
ctx.en: After his friends had patiently reasoned with him time and again, he finally quit smoking.

bad.s: 这个药{苦口婆心}，但是效果很好。
bad.en: (meant: this medicine tastes bitter but works well)
bad.why: The 'mouth' part means painstaking, earnest words, not a bitter taste; the idiom describes a person giving advice, never medicine or food.

bad.s: 他{苦口婆心}地骂了我一顿，让我马上滚出去。
bad.en: (meant: he gave me a harsh telling-off and told me to get out)
bad.why: It implies patient, caring persuasion; an angry scolding that drives someone away is the opposite.

cards.mean: sincere and weighty (words of advice)
cards.lit: the words are heavy and the heart is long: weighty words from a deeply caring heart

use.how: Adverbial before 说/叮嘱 (语重心长地说) or attributive (语重心长的话). Usually an elder or superior speaking earnestly to someone younger.

near.diff: 苦口婆心 stresses patient, repeated persuasion; 语重心长 stresses how weighty and heartfelt the words are, even if said only once.

cards.cue: Before his grandson left for university, the old man took him aside and said a few solemn, heartfelt words about how to live. How did he speak?

ctx.s: 爷爷{语重心长}地对我说：“做人要诚实。”
ctx.en: Grandpa said to me earnestly, "You must be an honest person."

ctx.s: 毕业那天，校长{语重心长}地叮嘱我们不要忘记初心。
ctx.en: On graduation day the principal earnestly urged us never to forget why we started.

ctx.s: 父亲那番{语重心长}的话，我到现在还记得。
ctx.en: I still remember those heartfelt words of advice from my father.

ctx.s: 老教授拍拍他的肩膀，{语重心长}地说：“年轻人，别着急。”
ctx.en: The old professor patted his shoulder and said earnestly, "Young man, don't be in a hurry."

ctx.s: 这封信写得{语重心长}，字里行间都是对学生的关心。
ctx.en: The letter was written with deep sincerity; every line showed care for the students.

ctx.s: 他本以为会挨批评，没想到经理只是{语重心长}地提醒他注意身体。
ctx.en: He expected a telling-off, but the manager just earnestly reminded him to look after his health.

bad.s: 他{语重心长}地讲了个笑话，大家都笑了。
bad.en: (meant: he told a joke and everyone laughed)
bad.why: It describes solemn, earnest advice; it cannot describe telling a joke.

bad.s: 这个箱子太{语重心长}了，我搬不动。
bad.en: (meant: this box is too heavy for me to carry)
bad.why: The 'heavy' refers to the weight of words, not physical weight; the idiom only describes speech.

cards.mean: mere hearsay
cards.lit: heard on the road, passed on along the way

story.text: Confucius said that to hear something on the road and repeat it further along the way is to throw away virtue: passing on what you have picked up by chance, without checking it, is a moral failing and not just a careless habit.

use.how: Predicate, attributive (道听途说的消息) or after 是/靠. Dismisses information as unverified, second-hand talk.

near.diff: 捕风捉影 is making claims or accusations on no basis at all; 道听途说 is information picked up second-hand and repeated unchecked.

cards.cue: Your neighbour says the factory is closing because someone at the market told her so. How would you describe her news?

ctx.s: 这些都是{道听途说}，你别当真。
ctx.en: That's all just hearsay, don't take it seriously.

ctx.s: 写新闻不能靠{道听途说}，一定要找到可靠的来源。
ctx.en: You can't write news based on hearsay; you must find a reliable source.

ctx.s: 你说他要辞职了？是真的，还是{道听途说}的？
ctx.en: You say he's resigning? Is that true, or just something you heard?

ctx.s: 网上很多{道听途说}的健康知识，其实没有科学根据。
ctx.en: A lot of second-hand health tips online have no scientific basis.

ctx.s: 他把{道听途说}的消息讲得跟亲眼看见一样。
ctx.en: He tells news he only heard about as if he had seen it with his own eyes.

ctx.s: 法官提醒证人，只陈述亲眼所见，不要说{道听途说}的内容。
ctx.en: The judge reminded the witness to state only what he saw himself, not things he had heard from others.

bad.s: 我昨天在路上{道听途说}，遇到了一个老同学。
bad.en: (meant: on the road yesterday I ran into an old classmate)
bad.why: The road is only an image; the idiom means unverified hearsay, not anything that happened on a road.

bad.s: 这是校长亲口宣布的{道听途说}，大家放心吧。
bad.en: (meant: this is news the principal announced in person, so relax)
bad.why: Something announced first-hand by the source is the opposite of hearsay, and the idiom is dismissive.

cards.mean: to quote out of context
cards.lit: to cut off one stanza and take a meaning from it

story.text: In the Zuo Zhuan, Lupu Gui of Qi married a woman of his own clan, which custom forbade. Asked why, he replied that when people recite the Book of Songs they cut out a single stanza and take from it only the meaning they want; he too had simply taken what he wanted. The idiom grew from his phrase about cutting off a stanza, and came to mean lifting words out of their context.

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (断章取义地引用). Criticises quoting a fragment so that it seems to say what the whole does not.

near.diff: 以偏概全 judges the whole from one part; 断章取义 distorts what someone said or wrote by lifting out a fragment.

cards.cue: A newspaper printed only half of the minister's sentence, so it looked as if she had said the opposite of what she meant. What did the paper do?

ctx.s: 你只截取了我说的半句话，这是{断章取义}。
ctx.en: You've lifted just half of what I said; that's quoting me out of context.

ctx.s: 我的原话不是这个意思，请不要{断章取义}。
ctx.en: That's not what my original words meant; please don't quote me out of context.

ctx.s: 这段视频被人剪掉了前后内容，{断章取义}地传到了网上。
ctx.en: Someone cut what came before and after in this clip and posted it online out of context.

ctx.s: 读古书最怕{断章取义}，要把上下文一起看。
ctx.en: The worst thing when reading classical texts is to take lines out of context; you have to read what surrounds them.

ctx.s: 那家媒体{断章取义}，把专家的提醒写成了警告。
ctx.en: That outlet quoted the expert out of context, turning a reminder into a warning.

ctx.s: 他引用老师的话时{断章取义}，故意漏掉了后半句。
ctx.en: When he quoted the teacher he twisted her words, deliberately leaving out the second half of the sentence.

bad.s: 这篇文章太长了，我{断章取义}，只讲第一部分。
bad.en: (meant: the article is long, so I'll pick out just the first part to discuss)
bad.why: It is always a criticism of distorting meaning, never a neutral way of saying you are taking an excerpt.

bad.s: 老师让我们把课文{断章取义}，分成四段。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher had us divide the text into four sections)
bad.why: It has nothing to do with dividing a text into parts; it means misrepresenting words by quoting a fragment.

cards.mean: vivid and lifelike (description)
cards.lit: to paint the sounds and paint the colours

use.how: Adverbial (绘声绘色地讲) or complement after 得 (讲得绘声绘色). Said of vivid storytelling, description or imitation.

near.diff: 栩栩如生 says a picture, carving or character looks alive; 绘声绘色 says someone tells or describes something vividly.

cards.cue: Grandpa tells how he met a bear in the woods, imitating its roar and every movement, and the children hang on every word. How does he tell it?

ctx.s: 爷爷讲故事讲得{绘声绘色}，孩子们都听入迷了。
ctx.en: Grandpa tells stories so vividly that the children are spellbound.

ctx.s: 她{绘声绘色}地描述了旅行中遇到的趣事。
ctx.en: She gave a lively account of the funny things that happened on her trip.

ctx.s: 他在电话里把事故经过讲得{绘声绘色}，我听得心惊肉跳。
ctx.en: On the phone he described the accident so vividly that my heart was in my mouth.

ctx.s: 你说得这么{绘声绘色}，好像你当时就在现场似的。
ctx.en: You describe it so vividly, as if you had been there yourself.

ctx.s: 导游{绘声绘色}地讲起这座古城的传说，游客们都停下了脚步。
ctx.en: The guide began telling the legends of the old town so vividly that the tourists all stopped to listen.

ctx.s: 他{绘声绘色}地模仿老师上课的样子，全班哈哈大笑。
ctx.en: He did a lifelike impression of the teacher in class, and the whole class roared with laughter.

bad.s: 这幅画颜色很{绘声绘色}，挂在客厅很好看。
bad.en: (meant: this painting's colours are bright and it looks good in the living room)
bad.why: Despite 'painting colours' in its image, it describes vivid telling or describing, not the colours of a real painting.

bad.s: 他的嗓音很{绘声绘色}，很适合唱歌。
bad.en: (meant: he has a lovely voice, well suited to singing)
bad.why: It describes how vivid an account is, not the quality of someone's voice.

cards.mean: to argue unreasonably, twisting words
cards.lit: to force words and seize the argument

use.how: Predicate (你这是强词夺理) or adverbial. Criticises someone who is in the wrong but argues anyway with twisted reasoning.

near.diff: 胡搅蛮缠 is pestering and making a scene with no reasoning at all; 强词夺理 puts on a show of argument to defend a weak position.

cards.cue: Caught running a red light, a driver insists the light was only just red and the camera angle was unfair. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 明明是你错了，还{强词夺理}！
ctx.en: You're obviously in the wrong, and you're still arguing!

ctx.s: 他迟到了一个小时，却{强词夺理}，说是我们来得太早。
ctx.en: He was an hour late, yet he twisted things round and said we had come too early.

ctx.s: 你别{强词夺理}了，证据都在这儿。
ctx.en: Stop twisting the facts, the evidence is right here.

ctx.s: 孩子打碎了花瓶，还{强词夺理}地说是花瓶自己掉下去的。
ctx.en: The child broke the vase and still insisted it had fallen off by itself.

ctx.s: 面对质问，那位发言人只能{强词夺理}，越说越没人信。
ctx.en: Under questioning the spokesman could only argue lamely, and the more he said, the less anyone believed him.

ctx.s: 辩论要讲道理，靠{强词夺理}是赢不了评委的。
ctx.en: A debate is about reasoning; you won't win the judges over by twisting words.

bad.s: 他的论证{强词夺理}，证据充分，大家都被说服了。
bad.en: (meant: his argument was strong and well supported, and everyone was convinced)
bad.why: It is not praise for a 'strong' argument; the idiom accuses someone of arguing when they are in the wrong.

bad.s: 我们{强词夺理}地讨论了一下午，终于有了结论。
bad.en: (meant: we debated hard all afternoon and finally reached a conclusion)
bad.why: It is not a word for lively discussion; it accuses one person of twisting words to defend being wrong.

cards.mean: the latecomer overtakes those ahead
cards.lit: those who come later end up on top

story.text: Ji An, a blunt minister of Emperor Wu of Han, saw men who had once ranked below him promoted over his head. He told the emperor: Your Majesty uses officials the way one stacks firewood, and the pieces that come later end up on top. In its origin it was a complaint; today it usually praises a latecomer that overtakes those who started earlier.

use.how: Predicate, said of a person, team, company or country that started late or fell behind and then pulled ahead: 他们后来居上，拿了冠军。

near.diff: 青出于蓝 is a student surpassing their own teacher; 后来居上 is any latecomer overtaking those who started earlier.

cards.cue: A small startup launched years after the big firms, yet within three years it has more users than any of them. What happened?

ctx.s: 他上学期成绩一般，这学期{后来居上}，考了全班第一。
ctx.en: His grades were average last term, but this term he overtook everyone and came top of the class.

ctx.s: 比赛最后一圈，那位年轻选手{后来居上}，超过了所有人。
ctx.en: On the last lap the young runner came from behind and passed everyone.

ctx.s: 这家公司起步最晚，却{后来居上}，成了行业里的龙头。
ctx.en: This company started the latest, yet it overtook the rest and became the industry leader.

ctx.s: 别看我们现在落后，只要努力，完全可以{后来居上}。
ctx.en: We may be behind now, but if we work hard we can certainly overtake them.

ctx.s: 电动车市场竞争激烈，几个新品牌已经有{后来居上}之势。
ctx.en: The electric car market is fiercely competitive, and several new brands are already on course to overtake the old ones.

ctx.s: 他是最后一个加入团队的，没想到{后来居上}，第一个升了职。
ctx.en: He was the last to join the team, but surprisingly he got ahead of everyone and was the first promoted.

bad.s: 他每天都{后来居上}，总是最后一个到办公室。
bad.en: (meant: he's always the last to arrive at the office)
bad.why: It means overtaking those ahead, not simply arriving late.

bad.s: 我们队从头到尾一直领先，最后也是{后来居上}。
bad.en: (meant: our team led from start to finish and won)
bad.why: A team that led all along did not come from behind; the idiom needs a latecomer passing the leaders.

cards.mean: first impressions take hold and colour later judgment
cards.lit: what enters first becomes the master

use.how: Predicate, adverbial or attributive (先入为主的印象/观念). Said of an early impression or idea that biases later judgment, usually as a warning.

near.diff: 偏听偏信 is trusting only one side's account; 先入为主 is letting whatever you heard or thought first decide the matter.

cards.cue: You read one bad review before seeing a film, and you dislike it even though the film itself is fine. What is shaping your opinion?

ctx.s: 第一次见面印象不好，我就{先入为主}地认为他不好相处。
ctx.en: Our first meeting went badly, so I assumed from then on that he was hard to get along with.

ctx.s: 看病的时候，医生不能{先入为主}，要把检查做完再下结论。
ctx.en: When treating a patient, a doctor mustn't go on first impressions, but should finish the tests before deciding.

ctx.s: 人们常有一种{先入为主}的观念，觉得贵的东西一定好。
ctx.en: People often have a preconceived idea that expensive things must be good.

ctx.s: 你是不是{先入为主}了？先听听他怎么解释吧。
ctx.en: Aren't you prejudging this? Hear his explanation first.

ctx.s: 审案时，法官必须避免{先入为主}，只看证据。
ctx.en: In hearing a case, a judge must avoid preconceptions and look only at the evidence.

ctx.s: 因为先看了电视剧，我{先入为主}，总觉得原著的主角就该是那个演员的样子。
ctx.en: Because I saw the TV series first, it's stuck with me: I always picture the novel's hero as that actor.

bad.s: 他每天都{先入为主}，第一个走进教室。
bad.en: (meant: every day he's the first to walk into the classroom)
bad.why: 'Entering first' is not about arriving somewhere; the idiom is about first impressions biasing judgment.

bad.s: 排队的时候要{先入为主}，后来的人等一等。
bad.en: (meant: in a queue it's first come, first served)
bad.why: First come, first served is a different phrase; this idiom describes a bias in judgment, not the order of a queue.

cards.mean: to depend on each other to survive
cards.lit: to lean on each other as one's very life

story.text: Li Mi, summoned to serve the Jin court, wrote to the emperor asking to be excused. Orphaned as a small child, he had been raised by his grandmother, now old and ill: without her he would not have lived to manhood, and without him she could not live out her years. Grandmother and grandson, he wrote, lived for each other. The idiom is traced to this line of the letter, though the wording there is slightly different.

use.how: Predicate, typically 两人相依为命 or 和…相依为命. Said of people, or a person and an animal, who have only each other, usually in hardship.

near.diff: 同甘共苦 is sharing good times and bad as partners; 相依为命 says each has only the other to live for.

cards.cue: After the war took the rest of the family, an old woman and her little grandson were left with only each other. How did they live?

ctx.s: 父母去世后，姐弟俩{相依为命}。
ctx.en: After their parents died, the sister and brother had only each other.

ctx.s: 老人和他的狗{相依为命}，已经十几年了。
ctx.en: The old man and his dog have had only each other for more than ten years.

ctx.s: 那些年家里很穷，我和妈妈{相依为命}，日子过得很苦。
ctx.en: We were very poor in those years; my mother and I depended on each other, and life was hard.

ctx.s: 小说讲的是一对在战乱中{相依为命}的祖孙。
ctx.en: The novel is about a grandparent and grandchild who cling to each other through the chaos of war.

ctx.s: 你们母女{相依为命}这么多年，她舍不得你出国也很正常。
ctx.en: You and your mother have relied only on each other for so many years; it's natural she can't bear to let you go abroad.

ctx.s: 地震后，这两位失去家人的老人互相照顾，{相依为命}。
ctx.en: After the earthquake, the two old people who had lost their families looked after each other and lived for each other.

bad.s: 我和同事{相依为命}，一起完成了这个项目。
bad.en: (meant: my colleague and I worked closely together to finish the project)
bad.why: It means having only each other to survive hardship; it is far too heavy for ordinary teamwork.

bad.s: 这两家公司{相依为命}，签了合作合同。
bad.en: (meant: the two companies depend on each other and signed a cooperation agreement)
bad.why: It describes people, or a person and an animal, whose lives hang on each other, not business partners.

cards.mean: sharing the same ideals and goals
cards.lit: aims the same, paths in agreement

use.how: Mostly attributive before 的: 志同道合的朋友/伙伴. Said of people bound by shared aims, values or interests, not of a couple's romantic attraction.

near.diff: 情投意合 is mutual affection and getting on well, often of a couple; 志同道合 is sharing the same aims and pursuing them together.

cards.cue: You join a hiking club and meet people who also want to protect the mountains, so you start a volunteer group together. What kind of people have you found?

ctx.s: 在大学里，他遇到了一群{志同道合}的朋友。
ctx.en: At university he met a group of friends who shared his ideals.

ctx.s: 我们几个{志同道合}的人一起创办了这家环保公司。
ctx.en: A few of us with the same goals founded this environmental company together.

ctx.s: “你为什么加入这个读书会？”“想认识一些{志同道合}的人。”
ctx.en: "Why did you join this book club?" "I wanted to meet some like-minded people."

ctx.s: 两位科学家{志同道合}，合作研究了二十多年。
ctx.en: The two scientists shared the same aims and worked together on research for over twenty years.

ctx.s: 这个网站让喜欢古典音乐的人找到了{志同道合}的伙伴。
ctx.en: This website lets classical music lovers find kindred spirits.

ctx.s: 创业初期最重要的，是找到{志同道合}、能长期坚持的合伙人。
ctx.en: What matters most when starting a business is finding partners who share your goals and will stay the course.

bad.s: 他在网上{志同道合}了几个新朋友。
bad.en: (meant: online he made a few like-minded new friends)
bad.why: It describes people who share aims; it is not a verb meaning 'to befriend' and cannot take an object.

bad.s: 他俩{志同道合}，认识一个月就结婚了。
bad.en: (meant: they fell for each other and married after a month)
bad.why: It describes a shared purpose, not the romantic attraction of a couple who click.

cards.mean: to repay kindness with harm
cards.lit: to repay a kindness as if it were an injury

use.how: A predicate, often after 却 or 竟然: 他却恩将仇报. Condemns someone who harms the very person who helped them.

near.diff: 忘恩负义 is forgetting or betraying a kindness; 恩将仇报 goes further and actively harms the benefactor.

cards.cue: You lent a friend money when he was broke, and now he spreads lies about you so he can take your job. What has he done?

ctx.s: 我好心借钱给他，他却{恩将仇报}，反过来骗了我一大笔。
ctx.en: I kindly lent him money, and he repaid me with harm by cheating me out of a large sum.

ctx.s: 农夫救了冻僵的蛇，蛇醒来却咬了他，这是一个{恩将仇报}的故事。
ctx.en: The farmer saved a frozen snake, and when it woke it bit him: a story of kindness repaid with harm.

ctx.s: “当初是他收留了你，你怎么能{恩将仇报}，去举报他？”
ctx.en: "He took you in back then; how can you repay him by reporting him?"

ctx.s: 老师资助他上完大学，他后来却在背后诬告老师，真是{恩将仇报}。
ctx.en: His teacher paid for his university, yet later he falsely accused that teacher behind his back. What ingratitude.

ctx.s: 公司在他最困难时录用了他，他却把客户资料卖给对手，这种{恩将仇报}的行为让人寒心。
ctx.en: The company hired him at his lowest point, and he sold its client data to a rival; that kind of betrayal is chilling.

ctx.s: 小说里的这个人物{恩将仇报}，害死了曾经救过他的恩人。
ctx.en: This character in the novel repays kindness with harm and causes the death of the man who once saved him.

bad.s: 他打过我，所以我{恩将仇报}，也打了他。
bad.en: (meant: he hit me, so I hit him back)
bad.why: It requires a kindness being repaid with harm; paying back harm with harm is a different idiom.

bad.s: 朋友送了我礼物，我{恩将仇报}，请他吃了顿饭。
bad.en: (meant: a friend gave me a gift, so I returned the favour with a meal)
bad.why: It means repaying kindness with harm; here a favour is being kindly returned.

cards.mean: courtesy calls for courtesy in return
cards.lit: propriety values going and coming

story.text: The phrase comes from the Book of Rites, which says that propriety values reciprocity: to give and receive nothing in return is not proper, and to receive and give nothing in return is not proper either.

use.how: Often a comment on its own or after 这叫/讲究: 这叫礼尚往来. Said about returning gifts, visits or favours; also used jokingly for paying back a jab.

near.diff: 投桃报李 is repaying one specific kindness gratefully; 礼尚往来 is the general custom of give and take, and can be used ironically.

cards.cue: Last week your neighbour brought you homemade dumplings, so today you bring them a box of pastries. What custom are you following?

ctx.s: 你上次请我吃饭，这次我请你，这叫{礼尚往来}。
ctx.en: You treated me to dinner last time, so this time it's on me. That's give and take.

ctx.s: 邻居送来饺子，我们也回送了一盒点心，{礼尚往来}嘛。
ctx.en: The neighbours brought dumplings, so we sent back a box of pastries; one good turn deserves another.

ctx.s: 中国人讲究{礼尚往来}，收了别人的礼物，一般要找机会回礼。
ctx.en: Chinese people set store by reciprocity: if you receive a gift, you usually find a chance to give one back.

ctx.s: “你怎么又给我带茶叶了？”“你上次送我的书我很喜欢，{礼尚往来}。”
ctx.en: "You've brought me tea again?" "I loved the book you gave me last time. Fair's fair."

ctx.s: 两家公司每年互相派人参观学习，{礼尚往来}，关系越来越好。
ctx.en: Every year the two companies send staff to visit and learn from each other, and with this give and take their relationship keeps improving.

ctx.s: 他在会上挖苦了我一句，下次开会我也{礼尚往来}，回敬了他一句。
ctx.en: He took a dig at me in the meeting, so at the next one I returned the courtesy with a dig of my own.

bad.s: 他每年都送我生日礼物，我却从来不回礼，真是{礼尚往来}。
bad.en: (meant: he gives me presents but I never give any back)
bad.why: It means returning courtesy; never giving anything back is exactly the opposite of it.

bad.s: 老板，请您{礼尚往来}地批准我的假期。
bad.en: (meant: boss, please kindly approve my leave)
bad.why: It describes an exchange between two sides, not politeness in a request; it cannot mean 'kindly'.

cards.mean: eyes brimming with tears of emotion
cards.lit: hot tears filling the eye sockets

use.how: A predicate, often after 感动得/激动得: 感动得热泪盈眶. Tears welling up from being deeply moved, proud or overjoyed, not from pain.

near.diff: 泪流满面 is a face streaming with tears from any cause; 热泪盈眶 is tears welling in the eyes, usually from being moved.

cards.cue: At your graduation your grandmother watches you walk across the stage, and her eyes fill with tears of pride. How does she look?

ctx.s: 看到女儿走上领奖台，妈妈{热泪盈眶}。
ctx.en: Seeing her daughter step onto the podium, the mother's eyes filled with tears.

ctx.s: 这部电影的结尾让很多观众{热泪盈眶}。
ctx.en: The ending of this film brought tears to many viewers' eyes.

ctx.s: “你怎么哭了？”“没什么，听到这首歌，突然就{热泪盈眶}了。”
ctx.en: "Why are you crying?" "It's nothing, I heard this song and my eyes just suddenly welled up."

ctx.s: 时隔多年回到故乡，老人站在老房子前{热泪盈眶}，却强忍着没让眼泪掉下来。
ctx.en: Back in his hometown after many years, the old man stood in front of his old house, eyes brimming, but held the tears back.

ctx.s: 收到全班同学写的感谢信，即将退休的老师感动得{热泪盈眶}。
ctx.en: Receiving a thank-you letter from the whole class, the teacher about to retire was moved to tears.

ctx.s: 终场哨声响起，坚持了四年的队员们{热泪盈眶}，紧紧抱在一起。
ctx.en: When the final whistle blew, the players who had stuck it out for four years hugged each other, tears welling in their eyes.

bad.s: 他摔断了腿，疼得{热泪盈眶}。
bad.en: (meant: he broke his leg and the pain made him cry)
bad.why: It is tears of being moved or proud, never tears caused by physical pain.

bad.s: 孩子丢了玩具，在地上{热泪盈眶}地大哭大闹。
bad.en: (meant: the child lost a toy and threw a crying tantrum on the floor)
bad.why: It describes quiet tears welling up from deep emotion, not loud crying in a tantrum.

cards.mean: to kick someone when they are down
cards.lit: when someone falls into a well, to drop stones on them

story.text: In his epitaph for his friend Liu Zongyuan, the Tang writer Han Yu criticised false friends: in good times they swear lifelong loyalty, but when a friend falls into a pit they do not reach down to pull him out; instead they push him further in and throw stones down on him.

use.how: A predicate, often 对某人落井下石 or 别落井下石. Condemns attacking or harming someone who is already in trouble.

near.diff: 趁火打劫 is grabbing gain from someone's crisis; 落井下石 is adding to the harm of someone already down.

cards.cue: A colleague has just been demoted after a mistake, and another colleague goes to the boss to list all his old errors too. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 他已经很难过了，你别再{落井下石}了。
ctx.en: He's upset enough already; don't kick him while he's down.

ctx.s: 真正的朋友会在你困难时帮你，而不是{落井下石}。
ctx.en: A true friend helps you when you're struggling instead of piling on.

ctx.s: “他被辞退了，我们要不要也去告他一状？”“人家已经这样了，何必{落井下石}？”
ctx.en: "He's been fired. Should we file a complaint against him too?" "He's already in this state; why kick him when he's down?"

ctx.s: 公司出事以后，以前的合作伙伴纷纷{落井下石}，到处说他的坏话。
ctx.en: After his company got into trouble, his former partners one after another turned on him, badmouthing him everywhere.

ctx.s: 那位演员道歉以后，网上还有人{落井下石}，翻出他的旧事继续攻击。
ctx.en: After the actor apologised, people online still piled on, digging up his past to keep attacking him.

ctx.s: 这位球员受伤离场，对方球迷却在看台上起哄，这种{落井下石}的做法让人不齿。
ctx.en: The player was carried off injured, yet the opposing fans jeered from the stands; kicking someone when they're down like that is contemptible.

bad.s: 朋友生病住院，我{落井下石}，每天去医院照顾他。
bad.en: (meant: when my friend was in hospital I helped by visiting every day)
bad.why: It means harming someone in trouble; helping them in their trouble is the exact opposite.

bad.s: 我们公司{落井下石}，终于把产品卖到了国外。
bad.en: (meant: our company finally broke into foreign markets)
bad.why: It condemns attacking someone who has fallen; it has nothing to do with success or progress.

cards.mean: to profit from someone else's crisis
cards.lit: to loot a house while it is on fire

story.text: It is the fifth of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, the traditional collection of tricks of war: when the enemy is struck by disaster or thrown into disorder, take that moment to attack and seize what you want.

use.how: A predicate or attributive: 这是趁火打劫, 趁火打劫的行为. Condemns using a disaster or someone's emergency to grab money or advantage.

near.diff: 落井下石 is harming someone already in trouble; 趁火打劫 is taking advantage of the trouble to gain something for oneself.

cards.cue: During a flood, a shop next to the shelter triples the price of bottled water. What is it doing?

ctx.s: 台风来了，有的商店却把矿泉水涨价三倍，这不是{趁火打劫}吗？
ctx.en: With a typhoon coming, some shops tripled the price of bottled water. Isn't that exploiting the disaster?

ctx.s: “车坏在高速上，拖车要价两千。”“这明摆着是{趁火打劫}。”
ctx.en: "My car broke down on the motorway and the tow truck wants two thousand." "That's blatantly taking advantage of you."

ctx.s: 他家着急卖房子还债，买家拼命压价，简直是{趁火打劫}。
ctx.en: His family had to sell the house fast to pay debts, and the buyer kept forcing the price down. That's profiting from their crisis.

ctx.s: 疫情期间高价倒卖口罩，这种{趁火打劫}的行为必须严查。
ctx.en: Reselling masks at inflated prices during the epidemic is profiteering from a crisis and must be strictly investigated.

ctx.s: 公司陷入危机时，竞争对手{趁火打劫}，高薪挖走了他们的核心技术人员。
ctx.en: While the company was in crisis, a rival took advantage and poached its key engineers with high salaries.

ctx.s: 地震后，几个小偷{趁火打劫}，溜进没人看守的商店偷东西。
ctx.en: After the earthquake, a few thieves took advantage of the chaos and slipped into unguarded shops to steal.

bad.s: 消防员{趁火打劫}，冲进大楼救出了三个孩子。
bad.en: (meant: the firefighter rushed into the fire and rescued three children)
bad.why: It condemns profiting from a crisis; the fire image does not make it fit a rescue.

bad.s: 他考试没考好，同学们却{趁火打劫}，一直嘲笑他。
bad.en: (meant: he failed the exam and classmates kept mocking him)
bad.why: It needs someone grabbing a gain from the crisis; mocking a person who is down gains nothing.

cards.mean: scheming against one another
cards.lit: centres hooked together, corners vying with each other

story.text: The Tang poet Du Mu, describing the vast Epang Palace of the Qin, wrote that its buildings each followed the lie of the land, their centres hooking together and their roof corners contending like rivals. The phrase was first about architecture and later came to mean people plotting against each other.

use.how: A predicate or noun, often 互相勾心斗角 or 厌倦了勾心斗角. Said of people in one group, like colleagues or relatives, secretly plotting against each other.

near.diff: 明争暗斗 is rivalry both open and hidden; 勾心斗角 stresses the calculated, behind-the-scenes scheming.

cards.cue: In an office, colleagues smile at each other but secretly plot to undermine one another for promotion. What is going on there?

ctx.s: 我不喜欢那家公司，同事之间总是{勾心斗角}。
ctx.en: I don't like that company; the colleagues are always scheming against each other.

ctx.s: 这部宫廷剧讲的是后宫妃子们{勾心斗角}的故事。
ctx.en: This palace drama is about the concubines of the imperial harem plotting against one another.

ctx.s: “你为什么辞职？”“我只想好好做事，不想每天跟人{勾心斗角}。”
ctx.en: "Why did you quit?" "I just want to do my job properly, not scheme against people every day."

ctx.s: 老人去世以后，几个子女为了遗产{勾心斗角}，亲情越来越淡。
ctx.en: After the old man died, his children schemed against each other over the inheritance, and the family bond faded.

ctx.s: 小团队人少事多，大家没时间{勾心斗角}，反而合作得很愉快。
ctx.en: In a small team with lots to do, nobody has time for intrigue, so people actually work together happily.

ctx.s: 他在这个圈子里待了几十年，早就厌倦了那些{勾心斗角}。
ctx.en: He's been in this circle for decades and has long since grown tired of all the intrigue.

bad.s: 两个队在决赛中{勾心斗角}，踢得非常精彩。
bad.en: (meant: the two teams battled hard in a thrilling final)
bad.why: It condemns secret scheming among insiders, not open, fair competition that one praises.

bad.s: 为了解出这道数学题，他{勾心斗角}了一个晚上。
bad.en: (meant: he racked his brains all evening over this maths problem)
bad.why: It means plotting against other people, not thinking hard about a problem on one's own.

cards.mean: to meet point with point in sharp opposition
cards.lit: needle point facing needle point

use.how: A predicate or adverbial: 双方针锋相对, 观点针锋相对, 针锋相对地反驳. Two sides directly opposing each other in argument, views or tactics.

near.diff: 以牙还牙 is paying back harm with the same harm; 针锋相对 is sharp, point-for-point opposition, usually in argument.

cards.cue: In a meeting, every time one manager makes a point, the other immediately rebuts it point by point and neither gives ground. How are they arguing?

ctx.s: 会上两个部门的经理{针锋相对}，谁也不让谁。
ctx.en: At the meeting the two department managers went head to head, neither giving an inch.

ctx.s: 辩论赛上，正方和反方{针锋相对}，场面十分激烈。
ctx.en: In the debate the two sides clashed point for point, and it got very heated.

ctx.s: 对于房价问题，两位专家的观点{针锋相对}。
ctx.en: On the question of house prices, the two experts' views are diametrically opposed.

ctx.s: 采访中，记者的问题很尖锐，他的回答也{针锋相对}，毫不退让。
ctx.en: In the interview the journalist's questions were sharp, and his answers met them head on without backing down.

ctx.s: “他说我们的方案太贵，你怎么回应的？”“我{针锋相对}地列出了他们方案的隐藏成本。”
ctx.en: "He said our plan was too expensive; how did you respond?" "I countered directly by listing the hidden costs of their plan."

ctx.s: 对方加强了防守，我们也{针锋相对}，换上了两名进攻球员。
ctx.en: They tightened their defence, so we countered directly by bringing on two attacking players.

bad.s: 两个老朋友见面后{针锋相对}，聊得非常开心。
bad.en: (meant: the two old friends met face to face and had a lovely chat)
bad.why: It means sharp opposition, not sitting face to face for a friendly talk.

bad.s: 我和女朋友{针锋相对}，一起看了一场电影。
bad.en: (meant: my girlfriend and I sat together and watched a film)
bad.why: It describes two sides clashing in argument; it cannot mean being together or side by side.

cards.mean: to lead by example
cards.lit: to make oneself the standard

use.how: A predicate, often with 要/先/带头: 父母要以身作则. Said of parents, teachers or leaders who do first what they ask of those under them.

near.diff: 身体力行 is personally practising what one advocates; 以身作则 is doing it so as to set the standard for others.

cards.cue: A coach who wants the players on time always arrives first and leaves last, so the team follows. What is the coach doing?

ctx.s: 想让孩子少玩手机，父母先要{以身作则}。
ctx.en: If you want your kids on their phones less, you as parents have to set the example first.

ctx.s: 一个好领导不光会讲道理，更要{以身作则}。
ctx.en: A good leader doesn't just talk; above all they lead by example.

ctx.s: 队长在训练中{以身作则}，每次都跑在最前面。
ctx.en: The captain leads by example in training, always running at the front.

ctx.s: “你自己都不遵守规定，凭什么要求我们？”“好，从今天起我{以身作则}。”
ctx.en: "You don't follow the rules yourself, so what right do you have to demand it of us?" "Fine, from today I'll set the example."

ctx.s: 经理要求大家节约用纸，他自己先{以身作则}，所有文件都双面打印。
ctx.en: The manager asked everyone to save paper and set the example himself by printing every document double-sided.

ctx.s: 校长每天第一个到学校，{以身作则}，老师们也不好意思迟到了。
ctx.en: The principal is the first to arrive at school every day, setting an example, so the teachers are too embarrassed to be late.

bad.s: 他总是迟到，经常{以身作则}。
bad.en: (meant: he is always late and sets a bad example)
bad.why: It is praise for setting a good example; it cannot describe setting a bad one.

bad.s: 今天我{以身作则}，自己做了一顿晚饭吃。
bad.en: (meant: today I did it myself and cooked my own dinner)
bad.why: It means setting an example for others to follow; cooking for yourself has no one being led.

cards.mean: selfless and impartial
cards.lit: wholly for the public, with nothing for oneself

use.how: A predicate or attributive praising someone who puts fairness and the common good above personal interest: 他办事大公无私. Often negated ironically: 他可不是大公无私.

near.diff: 铁面无私 is stern impartiality that bends for no one; 大公无私 stresses putting the common good above one's own interest.

cards.cue: The village head shares out relief money after a flood, gives the most to the poorest families and takes nothing for his own household. What is he like?

ctx.s: 他处理问题{大公无私}，大家都很信任他。
ctx.en: He handles matters selflessly and fairly, so everyone trusts him.

ctx.s: “让他管这笔钱，你放心吗？”“放心，他这个人{大公无私}，一分钱也不会往自己口袋里装。”
ctx.en: "Are you comfortable with him managing this money?" "Yes, he puts the common good first; he won't pocket a single cent."

ctx.s: 评比时，班长把奖励给了表现更好的同学，没有给自己的好朋友，真是{大公无私}。
ctx.en: In the class awards, the monitor gave the prize to the classmate who did better, not to her best friend. Truly impartial.

ctx.s: 这位老会计{大公无私}，单位分房时主动把名额让给了更困难的同事。
ctx.en: The old accountant is selfless: when the work unit allocated flats, he gave up his place to a colleague in greater need.

ctx.s: 村里分配补助时，村长{大公无私}，先照顾最困难的人家，自己家一分不要。
ctx.en: When the village shared out aid, the village head acted selflessly, looking after the neediest families first and taking nothing for his own.

ctx.s: 别把他想得那么{大公无私}，他推荐的人其实都是他的老同学。
ctx.en: Don't think he's so selfless; the people he recommends are actually all his old classmates.

bad.s: 他{大公无私}地把所有零食都给了女朋友。
bad.en: (meant: he generously gave all his snacks to his girlfriend)
bad.why: It praises putting the common good and fairness above private ties; favouring one's girlfriend is not it.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜很{大公无私}，分量特别足。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant is generous, the portions are big)
bad.why: It describes a person's integrity in public matters, not generosity of food or things.

cards.mean: extravagant and wasteful
cards.lit: to spread things out lavishly and waste them

use.how: Predicate or object of 反对/避免: 婚礼不要铺张浪费。 Criticises showy, excessive spending of money or materials, often on events or public funds.

near.diff: 挥金如土 describes a person throwing money around like dirt; 铺张浪费 criticises the lavish scale and waste of an event, a lifestyle or public spending.

cards.cue: A company holds a year-end banquet with far more dishes than anyone can eat and fireworks no one asked for. How would a critic describe it?

ctx.s: 婚礼简单一点就好，没必要{铺张浪费}。
ctx.en: A simple wedding is fine; there's no need to be extravagant.

ctx.s: 点了一桌子菜，最后剩了一大半，真是{铺张浪费}。
ctx.en: We ordered a whole table of dishes and left more than half; what a waste.

ctx.s: “年会要搞得这么大吗？这不是{铺张浪费}吗？”
ctx.en: "Does the annual party have to be this big? Isn't that just wasteful extravagance?"

ctx.s: 他虽然很有钱，生活却一点也不{铺张浪费}。
ctx.en: Although he is very rich, he lives without any extravagance at all.

ctx.s: 政府部门应当带头反对{铺张浪费}，节约每一分公款。
ctx.en: Government departments should lead the way in opposing extravagance and save every cent of public money.

ctx.s: 这场开幕式花了大量经费，被不少网友批评{铺张浪费}。
ctx.en: The opening ceremony cost a huge sum and many people online criticised it as extravagant and wasteful.

bad.s: 我的手机坏了，只好{铺张浪费}买了一个新的。
bad.en: (meant: my phone broke, so I had to spend money on a new one)
bad.why: Replacing something you need is not extravagance; the idiom criticises showy, excessive spending.

bad.s: 他上课总是{铺张浪费}时间。
bad.en: (meant: he always wastes time in class)
bad.why: The idiom takes no object and is about lavish spending of money or things; for time, use the plain verb làngfèi with its object.

cards.mean: spending more than one earns
cards.lit: what comes in does not cover what goes out

use.how: Predicate about the finances of a person, household or organisation: 公司已经入不敷出。 Describes a situation, not a character.

near.diff: 捉襟见肘 is being stretched thin in any resource, money, staff or time; 入不敷出 says precisely that income is lower than spending.

cards.cue: Every month the family's bills come to more than both salaries together, and their savings keep shrinking. How are their finances?

ctx.s: 他刚工作，工资不高，房租又贵，常常{入不敷出}。
ctx.en: He has just started working; his pay is low and his rent is high, so he often spends more than he earns.

ctx.s: 这家小餐馆开了一年，一直{入不敷出}，只好关门了。
ctx.en: The little restaurant ran at a loss for its whole first year and had to close.

ctx.s: “你每个月都{入不敷出}，还买这么贵的包？”
ctx.en: "You spend more than you earn every month, and you're still buying such an expensive bag?"

ctx.s: 老人看病花了很多钱，家里渐渐{入不敷出}了。
ctx.en: The old man's medical bills were large, and gradually the family's spending outran its income.

ctx.s: 由于游客减少，这个景区已经连续几年{入不敷出}。
ctx.en: Because visitor numbers fell, the scenic area has run a deficit for several years in a row.

ctx.s: 如果不控制开支，学校的经费很快就会{入不敷出}。
ctx.en: If spending is not controlled, the school's budget will soon fall short of its costs.

bad.s: 这次考试我{入不敷出}，分数比上次低。
bad.en: (meant: I did worse in this exam than last time)
bad.why: It is only about money coming in and going out, not about results or performance.

bad.s: 他是个{入不敷出}的人，从来不请客。
bad.en: (meant: he is stingy and never treats anyone)
bad.why: It describes a financial situation, not a stingy character; a stingy person is xiǎoqi.

cards.mean: to lose one's entire fortune
cards.lit: to pour out the household and sweep away the property

use.how: Predicate, or result after 弄得/落得/让: 赌博让他倾家荡产。 Said of a person or family ruined by gambling, bad investment, illness or disaster.

near.diff: 一贫如洗 describes the state of being utterly penniless; 倾家荡产 is the event of losing everything one used to own.

cards.cue: In one year a shopkeeper gambles away his savings, his house and finally the shop itself. What has happened to him?

ctx.s: 他沉迷赌博，最后{倾家荡产}。
ctx.en: He became addicted to gambling and in the end lost everything he owned.

ctx.s: “炒股要小心，别弄得{倾家荡产}。”
ctx.en: "Be careful trading stocks; don't end up losing everything."

ctx.s: 为了给儿子治病，这对夫妻几乎{倾家荡产}。
ctx.en: To pay for their son's treatment, the couple spent almost everything they had.

ctx.s: 一场大火烧光了仓库，老板一夜之间{倾家荡产}。
ctx.en: A fire burned down the warehouse, and the owner was ruined overnight.

ctx.s: 有人借高利贷去投资，结果落得{倾家荡产}的下场。
ctx.en: Some people borrow from loan sharks to invest and end up completely ruined.

ctx.s: 就算{倾家荡产}，我也要把这场官司打下去。
ctx.en: Even if it costs me everything I have, I will fight this lawsuit to the end.

bad.s: 他做生意很成功，{倾家荡产}地赚了很多钱。
bad.en: (meant: his business succeeded and he made a fortune)
bad.why: It means losing one's whole fortune, the opposite of making one.

bad.s: 赌博{倾家荡产}了他的父亲。
bad.en: (meant: gambling ruined his father)
bad.why: It takes no object; make the ruined person the subject, with ràng: gambling made his father lose everything.

cards.mean: genuine goods at a fair price; real and true
cards.lit: the goods are genuine and the price is honest

use.how: Predicate or attributive with 的: 这家店货真价实；货真价实的专家。 First about goods, then about anything that is truly what it claims to be.

near.diff: 名副其实 says a name or reputation matches reality; 货真价实 is more colloquial, starts from goods, and stresses 'real, not fake'.

cards.cue: At a market stall the honey is pure and fairly priced, unlike the fake stuff sold at tourist shops. How does a shopper praise the stall?

ctx.s: 这家小店的东西{货真价实}，回头客特别多。
ctx.en: This little shop sells genuine goods at fair prices, so it has lots of regular customers.

ctx.s: “放心买吧，我们卖的都是{货真价实}的新疆大枣。”
ctx.en: "Buy with confidence; all our dates are the real thing from Xinjiang."

ctx.s: 网上买东西，怎么知道是不是{货真价实}呢？
ctx.en: When you shop online, how can you tell whether the goods are genuine?

ctx.s: 他可不是冒牌的，是{货真价实}的医生。
ctx.en: He's no fake; he is a real, qualified doctor.

ctx.s: 这部电影没有花哨的宣传，却是一部{货真价实}的好作品。
ctx.en: The film had no flashy publicity, but it is a genuinely good piece of work.

ctx.s: 这家老字号开了一百多年，靠的就是{货真价实}。
ctx.en: This old brand has been open for over a century, and it owes that to honest goods at honest prices.

bad.s: 他对朋友{货真价实}，从来不说谎。
bad.en: (meant: he is sincere with his friends and never lies)
bad.why: It says a thing or person is genuinely what it claims to be, not that someone treats others honestly; use zhēnchéng (sincere).

bad.s: 我们要{货真价实}每一位顾客。
bad.en: (meant: we must treat every customer honestly)
bad.why: It is not a verb and cannot take an object; for treating customers honestly, use chéngshí (honest).

cards.mean: to keep at something steadily over time
cards.lit: to hold on to it with constancy

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (持之以恒地), often in advice: 学语言要持之以恒。 About keeping up a regular effort or habit over a long period.

near.diff: 坚持不懈 stresses not slackening in the face of difficulty; 持之以恒 stresses steady, regular effort kept up over a long time.

cards.cue: A coach tells a beginner that twenty minutes of running every day for a year beats one exhausting week of training. What quality is the coach asking for?

ctx.s: 学外语没有捷径，每天学一点，关键是{持之以恒}。
ctx.en: There is no shortcut to learning a foreign language: study a little every day, and the key is to keep it up steadily.

ctx.s: “减肥不能三天两头换方法，少吃多动，{持之以恒}才有效。”
ctx.en: "You can't switch diets every few days; eat less, move more and keep it up steadily, that's what works."

ctx.s: 他每天早上跑步，十年来{持之以恒}，身体一直很好。
ctx.en: He has run every morning without fail for ten years, and he has always been healthy.

ctx.s: 只要每天练一会儿，{持之以恒}，你的钢琴一定会越弹越好。
ctx.en: As long as you practise a little every day and keep it up, your piano playing will keep getting better.

ctx.s: 很多人新年都会定计划，可是能一年到头{持之以恒}的有几个？
ctx.en: Lots of people make New Year plans, but how many keep them up steadily all year round?

ctx.s: 老师在评语里写道：希望你在学习上{持之以恒}，不要三天打鱼两天晒网。
ctx.en: The teacher wrote in the report: I hope you keep up your studies steadily instead of working in fits and starts.

bad.s: 他{持之以恒}了三天，就放弃了。
bad.en: (meant: he kept at it for three days, then gave up)
bad.why: It praises perseverance over a long period; it cannot describe a three-day effort that ends in giving up.

bad.s: 他是一个很{持之以恒}的人，脾气从来不变。
bad.en: (meant: he is a steady person whose temper never changes)
bad.why: It means persevering in an effort, not having a stable personality or mood.

cards.mean: careful and conscientious in one's duties
cards.lit: cautious and fearful, as if in constant danger

story.text: The phrase is very old. In the Book of Songs, in the ode 'Yun Han', a king facing a terrible drought describes himself with these words, trembling with dread 'as if before thunder'. Originally it meant anxious, fearful caution; over time it came to mean the careful, conscientious way a responsible person does their job.

use.how: Predicate, attributive or adverbial (兢兢业业地工作). Praises someone's long, careful and dutiful work, often an ordinary worker's.

near.diff: 勤勤恳恳 stresses diligence and hard work; 兢兢业业 adds carefulness and a strong sense of responsibility, of not wanting to make mistakes.

cards.cue: At a retirement party, colleagues praise a clerk who for thirty years never let a careless error into the accounts. How do they describe her work?

ctx.s: 他几十年如一日，在岗位上{兢兢业业}，从来没出过差错。
ctx.en: For decades, day in and day out, he has done his job conscientiously and never made a mistake.

ctx.s: 王老师在这所学校{兢兢业业}地工作了三十年。
ctx.en: Mr Wang worked conscientiously at this school for thirty years.

ctx.s: “我爸当了一辈子会计，{兢兢业业}，没拿过别人一分钱。”
ctx.en: "My dad was an accountant all his life, careful and dutiful, and never took a cent that wasn't his."

ctx.s: 像她这样{兢兢业业}的人，为什么一直没有升职？
ctx.en: Why has someone as conscientious as her never been promoted?

ctx.s: 正是这些默默无闻、{兢兢业业}的普通员工，撑起了整个公司。
ctx.en: It is these unnoticed, dutiful ordinary employees who hold the whole company up.

ctx.s: 退休那天，老站长说：我只是{兢兢业业}做好了自己的本职工作。
ctx.en: On the day he retired, the old stationmaster said: I simply did my own job carefully and conscientiously.

bad.s: 他玩新游戏{兢兢业业}，一玩就是一整天。
bad.en: (meant: he is very devoted to his new game and plays all day)
bad.why: It praises the careful performance of work or duties, not enthusiasm for a hobby.

bad.s: 他害怕考试，紧张得{兢兢业业}的。
bad.en: (meant: he was so nervous about the exam he was trembling)
bad.why: Although it once meant 'fearful', today it only means conscientious in one's duties, never nervousness.

cards.mean: with skill to spare, handling it effortlessly
cards.lit: the blade moves freely with room to spare

story.text: Cook Ding carved an ox for Lord Wenhui so smoothly that it looked like a dance. He explained that he did not hack at bone but followed the natural gaps between the joints: the gaps have space, and the edge of his knife has no thickness, so the blade moves through them with room to spare. An ordinary cook changes his knife every month; his had lasted nineteen years and was still as sharp as new.

use.how: Predicate, often after 得 or 在……中: 处理得游刃有余。 Credits a person's skill and experience in a demanding job or situation.

near.diff: 得心应手 says one's hands do just what the mind wants; 游刃有余 stresses spare capacity, coping easily even with something complex.
轻而易举 says the task itself is easy; 游刃有余 says a hard task is easy for this skilled person.

cards.cue: A veteran interpreter handles a tense three-way negotiation, switching languages calmly and even smoothing over an awkward joke. How was her performance?

ctx.s: 他用中文做报告，还能随口开几句玩笑，真是{游刃有余}。
ctx.en: He gives the presentation in Chinese and even throws in a few off-the-cuff jokes; he handles it with room to spare.

ctx.s: 面对记者的刁钻问题，发言人回答得{游刃有余}。
ctx.en: Faced with the reporters' tricky questions, the spokesperson answered with complete ease.

ctx.s: “你一个人管三个部门，忙得过来吗？”“放心，我应付得{游刃有余}。”
ctx.en: "You're running three departments by yourself; can you cope?" "Don't worry, I'm handling it with room to spare."

ctx.s: 刚当老师时他手忙脚乱，现在同时管两个班也{游刃有余}了。
ctx.en: When he first started teaching he was all at sea; now he runs two classes at once with ease.

ctx.s: 经过多年的历练，她在复杂的人际关系中也能{游刃有余}。
ctx.en: After years of experience, she moves through even complicated relationships with ease.

ctx.s: 这位老厨师掌勺几十年，一个人做一桌宴席都{游刃有余}。
ctx.en: This old chef has cooked for decades; he can prepare a whole banquet alone without breaking a sweat.

bad.s: 这个箱子很轻，我{游刃有余}地搬起来了。
bad.en: (meant: the box was light and I lifted it easily)
bad.why: It credits skill in complex work or situations, not physical ease with a trivial task; use qīng ér yì jǔ or simply qīngsōng.

bad.s: 他很快就{游刃有余}了这个难题。
bad.en: (meant: he quickly handled this difficult problem with ease)
bad.why: It describes how someone copes and cannot take an object; say chǔlǐ de yóu rèn yǒu yú (handled it with ease).

cards.mean: outstanding, head and shoulders above others
cards.lit: to rise out of one's kind and stand above the crowd

story.text: In Mencius, the disciple Gongsun Chou asks how Confucius compared with others. Mencius quotes You Ruo: the qilin among beasts, the phoenix among birds, Mount Tai among hills and the sage among people all belong to their kind, yet they rise out of their kind and stand above the crowd; and since people first lived, none has been greater than Confucius.

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 他在同学中出类拔萃；出类拔萃的人才。 Describes a lasting quality of excellence compared with one's peers.

near.diff: 脱颖而出 is the moment of emerging ahead in a competition or selection; 出类拔萃 describes a lasting state of being far better than one's peers.

cards.cue: A professor writes a reference for a student who has been far ahead of every classmate, year after year. How does she describe him?

ctx.s: 她从小学习就好，在同学中一直{出类拔萃}。
ctx.en: She has done well at school since she was little and has always stood far above her classmates.

ctx.s: “你们班谁最优秀？”“小李吧，各方面都{出类拔萃}。”
ctx.en: "Who's the best in your class?" "Xiao Li, I'd say; he's outstanding in every way."

ctx.s: 学校希望培养出更多{出类拔萃}的人才。
ctx.en: The school hopes to produce more outstanding talent.

ctx.s: 这家公司的产品设计在整个行业里都算得上{出类拔萃}。
ctx.en: This company's product design counts as outstanding in the whole industry.

ctx.s: 他的球技虽然{出类拔萃}，脾气却很差，教练很头疼。
ctx.en: His football skills are outstanding, but his temper is terrible and the coach is at his wits' end.

ctx.s: 推荐信写道：该生成绩{出类拔萃}，具有很强的研究能力。
ctx.en: The reference letter read: this student's results are outstanding and his research ability is strong.

bad.s: 他在比赛最后一轮{出类拔萃}，拿了冠军。
bad.en: (meant: in the final round he came out on top and won)
bad.why: It describes a lasting superiority, not the moment of coming out on top in one contest; that is tuō yǐng ér chū.

bad.s: 这家饭店的菜{出类拔萃}地好吃。
bad.en: (meant: this restaurant's food is exceptionally tasty)
bad.why: It is not an intensifying adverb before an adjective; say tèbié hǎochī, or make the restaurant itself the subject of the idiom.

cards.mean: to stand out from the crowd
cards.lit: the point of an awl pokes out through the bag

story.text: When Qin besieged Handan, Lord Pingyuan of Zhao needed twenty retainers to go with him to Chu but could find only nineteen. Mao Sui offered himself. The lord said a capable man is like an awl in a bag, whose point shows at once, yet in three years no one had noticed Mao Sui. Mao Sui replied that he was asking to be put in the bag today; had he been put in earlier, the whole awl would have come out, not just its tip.

use.how: Predicate, usually 从/在……中脱颖而出. About a person or product emerging ahead of many rivals in a competition, selection or market.

near.diff: 出类拔萃 describes lasting excellence over one's peers; 脱颖而出 is the act of breaking out ahead of many competitors and getting noticed.

cards.cue: Five hundred people apply for a single design job; an unknown graduate's portfolio catches every judge's eye and she gets it. What did she do?

ctx.s: 她从几百名选手中{脱颖而出}，进入了决赛。
ctx.en: She beat hundreds of contestants to stand out and reach the final.

ctx.s: “面试的人那么多，你是怎么{脱颖而出}的？”
ctx.en: "With so many people interviewing, how did you manage to stand out?"

ctx.s: 这款小众手机凭借超长的续航在市场上{脱颖而出}。
ctx.en: This niche phone stood out in the market thanks to its very long battery life.

ctx.s: 那年的作文比赛里，一个农村孩子的文章意外{脱颖而出}。
ctx.en: In that year's essay competition, a village child's essay unexpectedly came out on top.

ctx.s: 新人演员在这部剧里{脱颖而出}，一下子成了热门人物。
ctx.en: The newcomer stood out in the series and became famous almost overnight.

ctx.s: 想要在激烈的竞争中{脱颖而出}，光靠运气是不够的。
ctx.en: If you want to stand out in fierce competition, luck alone is not enough.

bad.s: 他{脱颖而出}了教室，去操场踢球。
bad.en: (meant: he rushed out of the classroom to play football)
bad.why: Its 'coming out' is not physically leaving a place; it means emerging ahead of rivals, and it takes no place object.

bad.s: 他一直{脱颖而出}，十年来都是班里第一。
bad.en: (meant: he has always been outstanding, top of the class for ten years)
bad.why: It is the moment of emerging from a crowd of rivals, not a lasting state; for that use chū lèi bá cuì.

cards.mean: deliberately unconventional, trying to be different
cards.lit: to put up the new and set up the different

story.text: A New Account of Tales of the World records that the monk Zhi Dun, discussing Zhuangzi's chapter 'Free and Easy Wandering', put forward new ideas beyond the two famous commentaries and different views from all the scholars, insights none of them had reached. In this origin the phrase was praise; today it more often hints that someone is being different just to be different.

use.how: Predicate, or after 为了/故意/一味: 不能只为了标新立异。 About ideas, dress or designs that break with convention, usually implying it is for show.

near.diff: 别出心裁 praises an original, inventive idea; 标新立异 usually suggests being different for its own sake, to attract attention.

cards.cue: A student dyes his hair green and writes his essay in a strange made-up format, not because it helps, but just so he is like no one else. What is he doing?

ctx.s: 他穿得这么奇怪，就是想{标新立异}，吸引别人注意。
ctx.en: He dresses so oddly just to be different and get people's attention.

ctx.s: 设计要考虑实用，不能只为了{标新立异}。
ctx.en: A design has to be practical; it can't just be about being unconventional.

ctx.s: “你这个方案是认真的，还是故意{标新立异}？”
ctx.en: "Is this plan of yours serious, or are you just being different on purpose?"

ctx.s: 有些餐厅一味{标新立异}，菜做得好看却不好吃。
ctx.en: Some restaurants are so bent on being unusual that their dishes look good but taste bad.

ctx.s: 年轻人喜欢{标新立异}，这本身不是坏事，关键要有真本事。
ctx.en: Young people like to be different, which isn't bad in itself; what matters is having real ability.

ctx.s: 评论家认为，这位导演的新片{标新立异}有余，内涵不足。
ctx.en: Critics felt the director's new film had plenty of novelty for its own sake but little substance.

bad.s: 他上个月{标新立异}地搬进了新家。
bad.en: (meant: last month he moved into a new home)
bad.why: The 'new' in it means new ideas or styles; the idiom has nothing to do with new things like a house.

bad.s: 这个城市每年都{标新立异}，变化很大。
bad.en: (meant: the city renews itself every year and changes a lot)
bad.why: It describes someone deliberately pursuing unconventional ideas or style, not a place changing fast; for that say rì xīn yuè yì.

cards.mean: a late bloomer
cards.lit: a great vessel is completed late

story.text: The phrase comes from the Daodejing, in a passage of paradoxes about the Way: the great square has no corners, the great vessel is completed late, the great sound is barely heard, the great image has no shape. Later readers took the great vessel that takes longest to finish as a picture of a person of great ability who succeeds late in life.

use.how: Predicate or after 是/可谓, said of a person whose success came late: 他是大器晚成。 Also used to encourage someone still waiting for success.

near.diff: 后起之秀 is a young newcomer who quickly outshines others; 大器晚成 is someone who succeeds only after many years.

cards.cue: Your friend's father published his first novel at fifty-eight and it became a bestseller. How do you describe him?

ctx.s: 他四十多岁才出第一本书，真是{大器晚成}。
ctx.en: He only published his first book in his forties; a real late bloomer.

ctx.s: 别着急，有的人就是{大器晚成}，你的机会还在后头。
ctx.en: Don't worry, some people just bloom late; your chance is still ahead of you.

ctx.s: 这位画家年轻时默默无闻，六十岁以后才成名，可谓{大器晚成}。
ctx.en: The painter was unknown when young and only became famous after sixty; truly a late bloomer.

ctx.s: “我现在转行还来得及吗？”“当然，说不定你就是{大器晚成}的那种人。”
ctx.en: "Is it too late for me to change careers?" "Of course not; maybe you're the late-blooming type."

ctx.s: 奶奶常说，小时候不起眼的孩子，长大了也可能{大器晚成}。
ctx.en: Grandma always said that a child who seems ordinary may still turn out a late bloomer.
