bad.en: (meant: he selflessly rushed into the fire to save others)
bad.why: It is a criticism of despair and self-neglect, not a praise word for selfless courage.

cards.mean: to rely on one's own efforts
cards.lit: by one's own strength, to start life anew

use.how: Predicate or modifier: 我们要自力更生。 Said of a person, family, company or country that supports itself instead of depending on others' help.

near.diff: 白手起家 is building wealth or a business from nothing; 自力更生 is supporting oneself without outside help, with or without success.

cards.cue: A village that used to live on government aid now grows and sells its own produce and needs no outside help. How do they live?

ctx.s: 他十八岁就离开家，开始{自力更生}。
ctx.en: He left home at eighteen and began supporting himself.

ctx.s: 父母年纪大了，我们得学会{自力更生}。
ctx.en: Our parents are getting old; we have to learn to stand on our own feet.

ctx.s: 这个村子不再依靠救济，靠种茶{自力更生}。
ctx.en: The village no longer depends on handouts; it supports itself by growing tea.

ctx.s: “毕业后还要家里给钱吗？”“不用，我想{自力更生}。”
ctx.en: "Will you still need money from home after graduating?" "No, I want to make it on my own."

ctx.s: 关键技术买不来，只能{自力更生}，自己研发。
ctx.en: Key technology can't be bought; we have to rely on ourselves and develop it.

ctx.s: 残疾以后，他没有依赖别人，而是学了一门手艺，{自力更生}。
ctx.en: After becoming disabled he didn't depend on others; he learned a trade and supported himself.

bad.s: 这道题太难了，我请老师帮我{自力更生}。
bad.en: (meant: I asked the teacher to help me work it out)
bad.why: It means doing without others' help; asking someone for help contradicts it.

bad.s: 这棵树枯了一冬，春天又{自力更生}了。
bad.en: (meant: the tree revived in spring)
bad.why: It is said of people, families or countries supporting themselves, not of a plant coming back to life.

cards.mean: from start to finish
cards.lit: from the beginning to the end

use.how: Adverbial before the verb, often with 都 or 一直: 他自始至终都没说话。 Stresses that something held through a whole event or process without change.

near.diff: 始终如一 praises staying the same over a long time; 自始至终 simply marks the whole span of one event, often with 都.

cards.cue: At a two-hour meeting, one person never said a single word, from the moment it opened until it closed. How long was he silent?

ctx.s: 开会的时候，他{自始至终}没说一句话。
ctx.en: He didn't say a word from the start of the meeting to the end.

ctx.s: 这场比赛{自始至终}都很精彩。
ctx.en: The match was exciting from beginning to end.

ctx.s: “你相信他吗？”“我{自始至终}都相信他。”
ctx.en: "Do you believe him?" "I've believed him all along."

ctx.s: 整个项目她{自始至终}都参与了，最了解情况。
ctx.en: She was involved in the whole project from start to finish, so she knows it best.

ctx.s: 手术进行了六个小时，医生{自始至终}保持着冷静。
ctx.en: The operation lasted six hours, and the surgeon stayed calm throughout.

ctx.s: 这部小说{自始至终}围绕着一个家庭展开。
ctx.en: From first page to last, the novel revolves around one family.

bad.s: 我{自始至终}去过北京三次。
bad.en: (meant: I have been to Beijing three times in total)
bad.why: It marks the whole span of one event, not a total count of repeated trips.

bad.s: 他从早上{自始至终}工作到晚上。
bad.en: (meant: he worked from morning to night)
bad.why: It already means 'from start to end', so adding a separate 'from morning to night' frame is redundant and ungrammatical.

cards.mean: some day in the future
cards.lit: there will be a morning, one day

use.how: At the start of a clause, about an uncertain future day: 有朝一日我要去看看。 Often a hope or ambition, sometimes a warning; not for a fixed date.

near.diff: 总有一天 insists that the day will surely come; 有朝一日 is softer, a day that may come, often hoped for.

cards.cue: A poor student dreams aloud of standing on a big stage as a famous singer, though she has no idea when or how. How does she start her sentence?

ctx.s: {有朝一日}，我一定要去西藏看看。
ctx.en: One day I'm definitely going to visit Tibet.

ctx.s: 他从小就梦想{有朝一日}能当上宇航员。
ctx.en: Since he was little he has dreamed of one day becoming an astronaut.

ctx.s: “你想过回老家吗？”“想过，{有朝一日}会回去的。”
ctx.en: "Have you thought of moving back to your hometown?" "I have; some day I'll go back."

ctx.s: 今天你这样对待别人，{有朝一日}别人也会这样对待你。
ctx.en: If you treat people like this today, some day they'll treat you the same way.

ctx.s: 科学家们希望，{有朝一日}这种病能够被彻底治愈。
ctx.en: Scientists hope this disease can one day be completely cured.

ctx.s: 临别时他说：“{有朝一日}我们还会再见面的。”
ctx.en: As they parted he said, "Some day we'll meet again."

bad.s: 我们{有朝一日}下午三点见面吧。
bad.en: (meant: let's meet at three o'clock one afternoon)
bad.why: It refers to an uncertain future, so it cannot go with a set time or appointment.

bad.s: 我{有朝一日}去过一次上海。
bad.en: (meant: I once went to Shanghai)
bad.why: It looks to the future; it cannot describe a trip that already happened.

cards.mean: pleasing to the eye and mind
cards.lit: delighting the heart and pleasing the eyes

use.how: Predicate or modifier, often 让人赏心悦目 or 赏心悦目的: 风景赏心悦目。 Said of scenery, design, handwriting or a performance that is pleasant to look at.

near.diff: 引人注目 means something stands out and draws attention, good or bad; 赏心悦目 means it is pleasant and soothing to look at.

cards.cue: You open a friend's notebook: neat handwriting, soft colours, tidy margins. Just looking at it puts you in a good mood. How would you praise it?

ctx.s: 湖边的风景真是{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: The scenery by the lake is a real pleasure to look at.

ctx.s: 她的字写得工工整整，让人看了{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: Her handwriting is so neat that it's a joy to look at.

ctx.s: 这家餐厅的菜不但好吃，摆盘也{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: This restaurant's food is not only tasty, the plating is lovely to look at too.

ctx.s: “新网页怎么样？”“颜色很舒服，看着挺{赏心悦目}的。”
ctx.en: "How's the new website?" "The colours are easy on the eye; it's really pleasant to look at."

ctx.s: 春天的公园里，花开满园，令人{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: In spring the park is full of flowers, a delight to the eye.

ctx.s: 两位舞者配合默契，动作优美，{赏心悦目}。
ctx.en: The two dancers moved in perfect harmony, graceful and a delight to watch.

bad.s: 听到这个好消息，他{赏心悦目}，高兴得跳了起来。
bad.en: (meant: hearing the good news, he was overjoyed and jumped for joy)
bad.why: It describes a sight that is pleasant to look at, not a person's own joy at hearing news.

bad.s: 车祸现场非常{赏心悦目}，很多人围着看。
bad.en: (meant: the accident scene drew a crowd of onlookers)
bad.why: It is praise for a pleasant sight; an accident scene may draw attention but is no pleasure to look at.

cards.mean: eye-catching, drawing attention
cards.lit: to draw people's eyes to fix on it

use.how: Predicate or modifier: 一个引人注目的变化。 Said of a person, object, event or result that stands out and gets noticed, for good or ill.

near.diff: 赏心悦目 is about being pleasing to look at; 引人注目 is about standing out and being noticed, even for bad reasons.
引人入胜 is drawing someone deep into a story or scene; 引人注目 is only catching the eye and being noticed.

cards.cue: In a hall full of people in grey suits, one guest walks in wearing a bright yellow coat, and every head turns. How would you describe her?

ctx.s: 她穿了一条红裙子，在人群中特别{引人注目}。
ctx.en: She wore a red dress and really stood out in the crowd.

ctx.s: 这座新建的大楼造型奇特，十分{引人注目}。
ctx.en: The new building has an unusual shape and catches everyone's eye.

ctx.s: “我们低调一点吧，别太{引人注目}。”
ctx.en: "Let's keep a low profile; we don't want to draw attention."

ctx.s: 今年最{引人注目}的变化，是年轻人越来越喜欢国货。
ctx.en: The most striking change this year is that young people increasingly like home-grown brands.

ctx.s: 这位新人在比赛中表现出色，成绩{引人注目}。
ctx.en: The newcomer did brilliantly in the competition, with results that turned heads.

ctx.s: 新闻里那张照片很{引人注目}，转发的人特别多。
ctx.en: That photo in the news drew a lot of attention, and huge numbers of people shared it.

bad.s: 我{引人注目}地听老师讲课。
bad.en: (meant: I listened attentively to the teacher)
bad.why: It describes something that draws others' attention, not a listener paying close attention.

bad.s: 这本小说太{引人注目}了，我一口气读完了。
bad.en: (meant: the novel was so gripping I read it in one go)
bad.why: It is about standing out to be noticed, not about a story absorbing you as you read.

cards.mean: drawing one in, enthralling
cards.lit: to lead people into a wonderful place

story.text: The phrase is traced to an anecdote in A New Account of Tales of the World: a Jin dynasty official known as General Wang is recorded as saying that wine truly leads a person into a wonderful place. The 'wonderful place' later came to mean the absorbing heart of a story, a landscape or a work of art.

use.how: Predicate or modifier: 情节引人入胜。 Said of a story, film, book, talk or scenery that draws you deeper and holds you there.

near.diff: 引人注目 is catching the eye at first sight; 引人入胜 is pulling the reader or viewer in and keeping them absorbed.

cards.cue: You meant to read one chapter before bed, but the plot kept pulling you deeper, and suddenly it was three in the morning. How was the book?

ctx.s: 这部电影的情节{引人入胜}，一点也不无聊。
ctx.en: The film's plot is gripping; not boring at all.

ctx.s: 他讲历史故事讲得{引人入胜}，学生们都听入迷了。
ctx.en: He tells history stories so enthrallingly that the students are spellbound.

ctx.s: “这本书好看吗？”“开头就{引人入胜}，我停不下来。”
ctx.en: "Is the book good?" "It draws you in from the start; I couldn't put it down."

ctx.s: 山路越走越深，景色也越来越{引人入胜}。
ctx.en: The deeper the mountain path went, the more enchanting the scenery became.

ctx.s: 一篇好的开头，应该{引人入胜}，让读者想继续读下去。
ctx.en: A good opening should draw readers in and make them want to keep reading.

ctx.s: 这个纪录片用一个个真实的人物，讲述了一段{引人入胜}的历史。
ctx.en: Through a series of real people, the documentary tells an absorbing piece of history.

bad.s: 她的新发型很{引人入胜}，大家都多看了两眼。
bad.en: (meant: her new hairstyle caught everyone's eye)
bad.why: It is about being drawn deeper into a story or scene; a hairstyle simply catches the eye and has nothing to draw you into.

bad.s: 这个菜的味道{引人入胜}，我吃了两碗饭。
bad.en: (meant: this dish tastes wonderful)
bad.why: It is used for stories, works and scenery that absorb you, not for the taste of food.

cards.mean: to the great satisfaction of all (when wrongdoers are punished)
cards.lit: greatly gladdening people's hearts

use.how: Used as a predicate or before 的 about news that a wrongdoer has been punished or a public wrong set right: 这个判决大快人心。

near.diff: 拍手称快 describes people clapping and cheering; 大快人心 describes the event itself as satisfying to the public.

cards.cue: A gang that cheated hundreds of elderly people out of their savings is finally sentenced, and the whole town feels justice has been done.

ctx.s: 骗子终于被抓了，真是{大快人心}！
ctx.en: The swindler has finally been caught. Everyone is so glad!

ctx.s: 这家黑心工厂被查封的消息，可以说{大快人心}。
ctx.en: The news that the unscrupulous factory has been shut down has delighted everyone.

ctx.s: 法院对酒驾撞人者的重判，是一个{大快人心}的判决。
ctx.en: The heavy sentence for the drunk driver who hit a pedestrian is a verdict that satisfies the public.

ctx.s: “听说那个欺负同学的家伙被开除了？”“对，{大快人心}啊。”
ctx.en: "I heard the guy who bullied his classmates got expelled?" "Yes, and everyone's glad."

ctx.s: 多年逍遥法外的贪官最终落网，市民纷纷说这件事{大快人心}。
ctx.en: The corrupt official who had evaded justice for years was finally caught, and residents said it was a great relief to them all.

ctx.s: 警方这次打掉了一个电信诈骗团伙，{大快人心}，也给其他骗子敲响了警钟。
ctx.en: The police broke up a phone-scam ring, to everyone's satisfaction, and it is a warning to other fraudsters.

bad.s: 今天天气很好，我们去公园玩，{大快人心}。
bad.en: (meant: the weather was nice and we had fun in the park)
bad.why: It is the public's satisfaction at a wrongdoer being punished, not ordinary personal fun or happiness.

bad.s: 他考上了理想的大学，全家人都觉得{大快人心}。
bad.en: (meant: the family was overjoyed at his exam result)
bad.why: Good news about a success is not what it describes; it needs a bad person getting what they deserve.

cards.mean: deeply rooted in people's hearts
cards.lit: to go deep into people's hearts

use.how: Used as a predicate about an idea, value, image or slogan that the public has accepted deeply: 环保理念已经深入人心。

near.diff: 家喻户晓 means everyone knows of it; 深入人心 means people have taken it to heart and believe in it.

cards.cue: Twenty years ago few people sorted their rubbish; now almost everyone believes it matters and does it without being told.

ctx.s: 垃圾分类的观念已经{深入人心}。
ctx.en: The idea of sorting rubbish has taken firm hold among people.

ctx.s: 这部电视剧里的老师形象{深入人心}，很多人因此当了老师。
ctx.en: The teacher in this TV series won people's hearts, and many became teachers because of her.

ctx.s: “安全第一”这句口号人人都会说，可它真的{深入人心}了吗？
ctx.en: Everyone can recite the slogan "safety first", but has it really taken root in people's hearts?

ctx.s: 经过多年宣传，男女平等的思想逐渐{深入人心}。
ctx.en: After years of promotion, the idea of equality between men and women gradually took root in people's minds.

ctx.s: 这个品牌之所以成功，是因为它“质量可靠”的形象早已{深入人心}。
ctx.en: The brand succeeded because its image of reliable quality has long been firmly established in consumers' minds.

ctx.s: 老校长说：“好的规矩，要靠大家认同，才能真正{深入人心}。”
ctx.en: The old principal said, "Good rules only truly take root when everyone believes in them."

bad.s: 他昨天受的伤很重，刀口{深入人心}。
bad.en: (meant: the knife wound was very deep)
bad.why: It is about ideas taking hold in people's minds, never about a physical wound or depth.

bad.s: 这个新闻刚发布五分钟，就已经{深入人心}了。
bad.en: (meant: the news spread everywhere within minutes)
bad.why: It describes deep, lasting acceptance built over time, not news spreading quickly within minutes.

cards.mean: approachable and easy to talk to
cards.lit: plain and easy, close to people

story.text: When the Duke of Zhou's son Boqin was enfeoffed in Lu, he took three years to report on his rule, because he had changed the local customs and rites. Jiang Taigong, enfeoffed in Qi, reported in five months, saying he had simplified the rites and followed local ways. The Duke of Zhou sighed that Lu would one day serve Qi: if government is not simple and easy, the people will not come close; if it is plain, easy and close to the people, they will surely turn to it. In the original the phrase reads "close to the people" rather than "close to others".

use.how: Used as a predicate or attribute praising someone of higher status who is friendly and unpretentious with ordinary people: 校长很平易近人。

near.diff: 和蔼可亲 stresses a kind, gentle manner; 平易近人 stresses that a person of rank does not put on airs.

cards.cue: The company's famous founder eats in the staff canteen, chats with interns and never mentions his title.

ctx.s: 我们的新经理虽然职位高，却很{平易近人}，大家都喜欢找他聊天。
ctx.en: Our new manager is very approachable; everyone likes to go and chat with him.

ctx.s: 没想到这位大明星这么{平易近人}，还主动跟粉丝合影。
ctx.en: I never expected the big star to be so down-to-earth; she even offered to take photos with fans.

ctx.s: 那位老教授学问很大，却一点架子也没有，非常{平易近人}。
ctx.en: The old professor is very learned but has no airs at all; he is very easy to talk to.

ctx.s: “院长会不会很严肃？”“放心吧，他是个{平易近人}的人。”
ctx.en: "Is the dean very stern?" "Don't worry, he's very approachable."

ctx.s: 市长常常走进普通居民家里，这种{平易近人}的作风赢得了大家的信任。
ctx.en: The mayor often visits ordinary residents' homes, and this unpretentious style has won people's trust.

ctx.s: 一位好的领导，既要有能力，也要{平易近人}，让下属敢说真话。
ctx.en: A good leader should be capable and also approachable, so that staff dare to speak honestly.

bad.s: 这道数学题很{平易近人}，大家都会做。
bad.en: (meant: this maths problem is easy)
bad.why: It describes a person's manner toward others, not how easy a task or problem is.

bad.s: 我家小狗很{平易近人}，见谁都摇尾巴。
bad.en: (meant: my puppy is friendly to everyone)
bad.why: It praises a person, usually someone of higher status, for not putting on airs; it is not used for animals.

cards.mean: to bully others by trading on a powerful backer
cards.lit: the fox borrows the tiger's might

story.text: A tiger caught a fox. The fox said: Heaven has made me king of the beasts, so if you eat me you defy Heaven; walk behind me and see whether the animals dare to stay. The tiger followed, and every animal fled at the sight of them. The tiger thought they feared the fox, not knowing they feared the tiger. Jiang Yi told this fable to King Xuan of Chu: the north feared the king's army, not his minister Zhao Xixu.

use.how: Used as a predicate or attribute criticising someone who bosses others around on the strength of a superior or powerful relative: 他不过是狐假虎威。

near.diff: 仗势欺人 is bullying by relying on any power, including one's own; 狐假虎威 stresses that the power belongs to someone else.

cards.cue: The boss's nephew joined last month as a junior clerk, yet he orders everyone around and says, "My uncle will hear about this."

ctx.s: 他仗着舅舅是校长，在班里{狐假虎威}，其实自己什么本事也没有。
ctx.en: Because his uncle is the headmaster, he throws his weight around in class, though he himself has no ability at all.

ctx.s: 别怕她，她只是{狐假虎威}，自己根本做不了主。
ctx.en: Don't be afraid of her; she's just borrowing someone else's authority and can't decide anything herself.

ctx.s: 老板一出差，那个秘书就没法再{狐假虎威}了。
ctx.en: As soon as the boss went away on business, the secretary could no longer use his name to push people around.

ctx.s: “你算什么？不过是借着经理的名头{狐假虎威}罢了！”
ctx.en: "Who do you think you are? You're just using the manager's name to bully us!"

ctx.s: 小说里的管家{狐假虎威}，对下人百般刁难，见了主人却低声下气。
ctx.en: In the novel the steward uses his master's power to torment the servants, yet grovels before the master himself.

ctx.s: 有些人自己没什么权力，却靠着和领导的关系{狐假虎威}，这种风气必须改。
ctx.en: Some people with no power of their own trade on their ties with the leadership to intimidate others; this practice has to change.

bad.s: 他自己当上了总经理，开始{狐假虎威}，对员工大喊大叫。
bad.en: (meant: once he became general manager himself he began bullying staff)
bad.why: The power here is his own; the idiom needs someone borrowing a more powerful backer's authority.

bad.s: 老虎在山上{狐假虎威}，动物们都很害怕。
bad.en: (meant: the tiger on the mountain was fearsome)
bad.why: It is a figurative criticism of a person, not a description of a real tiger being frightening.

cards.mean: courteous and refined
cards.lit: refined and gentle, full of courtesy

use.how: Used as a predicate, attribute or adverbial (彬彬有礼地) about someone's polite, cultivated manners: 他对人彬彬有礼。

near.diff: 落落大方 is being relaxed and natural, not shy; 彬彬有礼 is being polite and well-mannered.

cards.cue: The young man holds the door, greets each guest by name, thanks the waiter and never interrupts anyone.

ctx.s: 这个孩子见了长辈总是{彬彬有礼}。
ctx.en: This child is always polite and well-mannered with his elders.

ctx.s: 酒店的服务员{彬彬有礼}地把我们带到了房间。
ctx.en: The hotel attendant courteously showed us to our room.

ctx.s: 他看起来{彬彬有礼}，说话也很客气，大家对他印象都不错。
ctx.en: He seems courteous and speaks politely, so everyone has a good impression of him.

ctx.s: “你男朋友人怎么样？”“很{彬彬有礼}，见了我爸妈又是问好又是倒茶。”
ctx.en: "What's your boyfriend like?" "Very courteous; when he met my parents he greeted them properly and poured them tea."

ctx.s: 谈判时，对方代表始终{彬彬有礼}，但在关键问题上寸步不让。
ctx.en: During the negotiations the other side's representative was unfailingly polite but would not give an inch on the key issues.

ctx.s: 一个{彬彬有礼}的人，不一定就是真心待你的人。
ctx.en: Someone who is courteous is not necessarily someone who sincerely cares about you.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜{彬彬有礼}，味道很好。
bad.en: (meant: the restaurant's dishes are refined and tasty)
bad.why: It describes a person's manners, not food or things.

bad.s: 他把房间收拾得{彬彬有礼}，干干净净。
bad.en: (meant: he tidied his room neatly)
bad.why: It describes a person's courteous manners toward others, not how neat or orderly a place is.

cards.mean: natural and poised, at ease with others
cards.lit: open and easy, generous in bearing

use.how: Used as a predicate, attribute or adverbial about someone's natural, unselfconscious manner in public or with strangers: 她回答问题落落大方。

near.diff: 彬彬有礼 is being polite and well-mannered; 落落大方 is being relaxed and natural rather than shy or awkward.

cards.cue: A sixteen-year-old student is interviewed on live television and answers calmly and naturally, with no blushing or stammering.

ctx.s: 她第一次上台演讲，却一点也不紧张，{落落大方}。
ctx.en: It was her first time giving a speech on stage, yet she wasn't nervous at all; she was poised and natural.

ctx.s: 面试时要{落落大方}，不要低着头说话。
ctx.en: In an interview you should be natural and at ease; don't talk with your head down.

ctx.s: 这个小女孩见了客人不躲不藏，{落落大方}地打招呼。
ctx.en: The little girl didn't hide from the guests but greeted them naturally and confidently.

ctx.s: “新来的同事怎么样？”“人很开朗，说话{落落大方}的。”
ctx.en: "What's the new colleague like?" "Very outgoing, and she speaks with real ease."

ctx.s: 记者问到尴尬的问题，他{落落大方}地承认了自己的错误。
ctx.en: When the reporter asked an awkward question, he admitted his mistake openly and without embarrassment.

ctx.s: 她穿着简单，举止{落落大方}，给评委留下了很深的印象。
ctx.en: She was simply dressed and carried herself with natural poise, which made a strong impression on the judges.

bad.s: 他请客很{落落大方}，一顿饭花了好几千。
bad.en: (meant: he was generous with money when treating people)
bad.why: The second half alone can mean generous with money, but the idiom only describes a relaxed, natural manner, not spending freely.

bad.s: 这件衣服太{落落大方}了，我穿着又宽又长。
bad.en: (meant: this garment is too big and loose for me)
bad.why: It praises a natural, easy bearing; it does not mean large or loose-fitting.

cards.mean: hiding malice behind a smile
cards.lit: a knife hidden inside a smile

story.text: Li Yifu, a chief minister under Emperor Gaozong of Tang, looked mild and respectful and always smiled when he spoke with people, but he was narrow-minded and vicious, and secretly ruined anyone who crossed him. People of the time said there was a knife in his smile, and because he was soft on the outside and harmful within, they also called him Li the Cat.

use.how: Used as a predicate or attribute criticising someone who is friendly to your face while plotting to harm you: 这个人笑里藏刀。

near.diff: 口蜜腹剑 stresses sweet words with evil intent; 笑里藏刀 stresses a friendly smiling manner hiding it. They are very close.

cards.cue: Your colleague always greets you with a big smile, and you later learn she has been quietly telling the boss you are unreliable.

ctx.s: 别看他整天对你笑眯眯的，他其实是{笑里藏刀}。
ctx.en: Don't be fooled by how he beams at you all day; he's hiding a knife behind that smile.

ctx.s: 我最怕{笑里藏刀}的人，当面一套，背后一套。
ctx.en: What I fear most are people who smile while plotting against you: one thing to your face, another behind your back.

ctx.s: 电视剧里的那个皇后{笑里藏刀}，看得观众直起鸡皮疙瘩。
ctx.en: The empress in that TV drama smiles sweetly while scheming, and she gives the audience goosebumps.

ctx.s: “他今天突然请我吃饭，会不会{笑里藏刀}啊？”
ctx.en: "He suddenly invited me to dinner today. Could there be a knife behind that smile?"

ctx.s: 直到被对手抢走了客户，他才明白对方当初{笑里藏刀}。
ctx.en: Only when his rival stole his clients did he realise the man's friendliness had hidden malice all along.

ctx.s: 那些满脸堆笑却{笑里藏刀}的朋友，比说话难听但真诚的人可怕得多。
ctx.en: Friends who greet you all smiles while scheming against you are far more dangerous than people who speak bluntly but sincerely.

bad.s: 厨师{笑里藏刀}，一边笑一边切菜。
bad.en: (meant: the chef smiled while chopping vegetables)
bad.why: The knife is figurative; it means hidden malice behind friendliness, not literally holding a knife.

bad.s: 他心里很难过，但还是{笑里藏刀}，不让别人担心。
bad.en: (meant: he hid his sadness behind a smile)
bad.why: It is hidden hostility toward others, not putting on a brave smile to hide one's own sadness.

cards.mean: to probe or hint by indirect questions
cards.lit: to knock at the side and strike from the flank

use.how: Used as a predicate or adverbial (旁敲侧击地问) about getting information or making a point indirectly instead of asking or saying it straight out.

near.diff: 拐弯抹角 criticises talking round in circles; 旁敲侧击 is a deliberate tactic of indirect questions or hints to find out or suggest something.

cards.cue: You want to know if your friend has a girlfriend, so instead of asking, you ask who he went to the cinema with and why he has been so cheerful lately.

ctx.s: 妈妈{旁敲侧击}地问我最近是不是谈恋爱了。
ctx.en: Mum dropped hints, asking in a roundabout way whether I'd started seeing someone.

ctx.s: 我想知道他的工资，又不好直接问，只能{旁敲侧击}。
ctx.en: I wanted to know his salary but couldn't ask outright, so I could only probe indirectly.

ctx.s: 老板{旁敲侧击}了好几次，意思是希望我们周末加班。
ctx.en: The boss hinted several times that he wanted us to work over the weekend.

ctx.s: “你别{旁敲侧击}了，想知道我考了多少分就直接问吧。”
ctx.en: "Stop fishing with roundabout questions. If you want to know my score, just ask."

ctx.s: 警察没有直接提案子，而是{旁敲侧击}，从他的回答里找破绽。
ctx.en: The police didn't mention the case directly but probed indirectly, looking for holes in his answers.

ctx.s: 同事们{旁敲侧击}地打听新经理的来历，可谁也没问出什么。
ctx.en: Colleagues made roundabout inquiries about the new manager's background, but nobody found out anything.

bad.s: 他在门外{旁敲侧击}，敲了半天门也没人开。
bad.en: (meant: he knocked on the door for ages)
bad.why: It is figurative, about indirect questions or hints, not physically knocking on something.

bad.s: 他{旁敲侧击}地对我说：“你明天必须交报告。”
bad.en: (meant: he told me directly that the report was due)
bad.why: A blunt, direct order is the opposite of what it means; it describes hints and indirect probing.

cards.mean: to cut corners on labour and materials
cards.lit: to steal on work and reduce materials

use.how: Used as a predicate or attribute criticising builders, makers or workers who skimp on work or materials to save money; also figuratively of any job done with corners cut.

near.diff: 敷衍了事 is doing a task perfunctorily to get it over with; 偷工减料 is deliberately skimping on labour or materials, often for profit.

cards.cue: A new school building cracks within a year, and inspectors find the builder used less steel and cheaper cement than the contract required.

ctx.s: 这座桥才建好两年就出现裂缝，肯定是{偷工减料}了。
ctx.en: The bridge has cracks only two years after it was built; they must have skimped on work and materials.

ctx.s: 装修的时候你得经常去看看，防止工人{偷工减料}。
ctx.en: During the renovation you need to check in often, so the workers don't cut corners.

ctx.s: 这家店的包子越来越小，馅也少了，明显在{偷工减料}。
ctx.en: This shop's buns keep getting smaller with less filling; they're clearly skimping.

ctx.s: “这么便宜的价格，他们会不会{偷工减料}？”
ctx.en: "At such a low price, won't they cut corners?"

ctx.s: 调查发现，开发商为了多赚钱，在楼房的地基上{偷工减料}。
ctx.en: The investigation found that the developer had skimped on the building's foundations to make more money.

ctx.s: 写论文也不能{偷工减料}，该查的资料一份都不能少。
ctx.en: You can't cut corners on a thesis either; you have to consult every source you should.

bad.s: 为了节约用电，我们决定{偷工减料}，晚上早点关灯。
bad.en: (meant: to save electricity we turn the lights off early)
bad.why: It is a criticism of skimping on a job's quality, not a neutral word for saving resources.

bad.s: 他工作效率很高，每天都{偷工减料}，提前完成任务。
bad.en: (meant: he is efficient and finishes early)
bad.why: It is never praise for efficiency; it means lowering quality by cheating on work or materials.

cards.mean: sloppy and long-winded, not clean or quick
cards.lit: dragging mud and trailing water

use.how: Used as a predicate or adverbial, often after 不 or 别, about writing, speech or actions that are drawn-out and indecisive: 做事不要拖泥带水。

near.diff: 干净利落 is its opposite: neat, quick and decisive.

cards.cue: Your colleague's emails ramble for pages before reaching the point, and every decision she makes comes with three rounds of second thoughts.

ctx.s: 他做事从不{拖泥带水}，说干就干。
ctx.en: He never dithers; once he decides to do something, he does it.

ctx.s: 这篇文章写得{拖泥带水}，读了半天也不知道重点在哪儿。
ctx.en: This article is long-winded and muddled; I read it for ages and still couldn't find the point.

ctx.s: 既然已经决定分手，就别再{拖泥带水}了。
ctx.en: Since you've decided to break up, don't drag it out any longer.

ctx.s: “你说话能不能别这么{拖泥带水}？直接告诉我结果。”
ctx.en: "Can you stop rambling? Just tell me the result."

ctx.s: 这场比赛主队的进攻{拖泥带水}，错过了好几次机会。
ctx.en: The home side's attacks were slow and messy, and they wasted several chances.

ctx.s: 新领导处理问题干脆利落，和以前{拖泥带水}的作风完全不同。
ctx.en: The new leader deals with problems crisply, quite unlike the old dithering way of doing things.

bad.s: 下雨天路不好走，我的鞋子{拖泥带水}。
bad.en: (meant: my shoes were muddy and wet)
bad.why: It is figurative, about sloppy, drawn-out work or speech, not actual mud and water on shoes.

bad.s: 他做菜非常{拖泥带水}，又快又好吃。
bad.en: (meant: he cooks quickly and well)
bad.why: It is a criticism of slow, messy work, so it cannot praise speed or skill.

cards.mean: to make a decision promptly on the spot
cards.lit: facing the critical moment, decide at once

use.how: A verb phrase, often after 必须, 要 or 他 as predicate: 关键时刻他当机立断。 Praises a quick, decisive call at a critical moment.

near.diff: 毫不犹豫 describes doing anything without hesitation; 当机立断 is specifically making a decisive call at a critical, urgent moment.

cards.cue: A fire breaks out in the warehouse, and the manager immediately orders everyone out and calls for help without waiting for head office. How do you praise her?

ctx.s: 情况紧急，你必须{当机立断}。
ctx.en: It's an emergency; you have to decide right now.

ctx.s: 会议讨论了半天也没有结果，最后总经理{当机立断}，拍板定了方案。
ctx.en: The meeting went round in circles for ages; in the end the general manager made the call on the spot and settled the plan.

ctx.s: 多亏经理{当机立断}，公司才避免了更大的损失。
ctx.en: Thanks to the manager's quick decision, the company avoided an even bigger loss.

ctx.s: “还等什么？{当机立断}吧，马上把病人送医院！”
ctx.en: "What are you waiting for? Make the call: get the patient to hospital now!"

ctx.s: 面对突如其来的暴雨，船长{当机立断}，下令返航。
ctx.en: Faced with the sudden storm, the captain decided on the spot and ordered the ship back to port.

ctx.s: 做生意有时候需要{当机立断}，犹豫太久就会错过机会。
ctx.en: In business you sometimes have to decide on the spot; hesitate too long and you miss the chance.

bad.s: 我想了三个月，终于{当机立断}买了这辆车。
bad.en: (meant: after three months of thinking I finally decided to buy the car)
bad.why: It means deciding instantly at a critical moment; three months of thought is the opposite.

bad.s: 他是一个{当机立断}。
bad.en: (meant: he is a decisive person)
bad.why: It is a verb phrase describing an action, not a noun for a kind of person; to call someone decisive use a plain adjective instead.

cards.mean: irresolute by nature, always wavering
cards.lit: soft and yielding, rarely deciding

use.how: An adjective for a person's character: 他太优柔寡断了; also 优柔寡断的性格. Criticises someone who habitually cannot make decisions.

near.diff: 犹豫不决 is being unable to decide in one particular case; 优柔寡断 is a lasting weakness of character.

cards.cue: Your friend takes weeks to pick a restaurant, a phone or a job offer, and always ends up missing out. What flaw of character do you point out?

ctx.s: 他什么都好，就是有点{优柔寡断}。
ctx.en: He's great in every way, except he's a bit indecisive.

ctx.s: 你这种{优柔寡断}的性格得改一改，不然总会错过机会。
ctx.en: You need to change that indecisive nature of yours, or you'll keep missing your chances.

ctx.s: 一个{优柔寡断}的人，很难当好领导。
ctx.en: Someone who is irresolute by nature will find it hard to be a good leader.

ctx.s: 她知道自己性格{优柔寡断}，所以很羡慕做事果断的人。
ctx.en: She knows she's indecisive by nature, so she really admires people who act decisively.

ctx.s: “你为什么不早点拒绝他？”“唉，都怪我太{优柔寡断}。”
ctx.en: "Why didn't you turn him down sooner?" "Sigh, it's because I'm far too indecisive."

ctx.s: 小说的主人公{优柔寡断}，一次次错过了心爱的人。
ctx.en: The novel's hero is irresolute and misses the woman he loves time after time.

bad.s: 这位老师说话{优柔寡断}，学生们都很喜欢她。
bad.en: (meant: this teacher speaks gently, and the students love her)
bad.why: The idiom criticises a habit of indecision; it cannot be used to praise someone's soft, gentle way of speaking.

bad.s: 今天的天气{优柔寡断}，一会儿晴一会儿雨。
bad.en: (meant: the weather is changeable today)
bad.why: It describes a person's character in making decisions; weather cannot be indecisive.

cards.mean: firm and decisive (of a reply)
cards.lit: to chop through nails and cut iron

use.how: Usually adverbial with 地 before 说, 回答 or 拒绝: 他斩钉截铁地说。 Describes speech or an attitude that is firm and leaves no room for doubt.

near.diff: 一言为定 seals an agreement between two people; 斩钉截铁 describes the firm, uncompromising way one person says something.

cards.cue: Asked whether he would ever sell his late father's shop, the son answered at once and in a tone that left no doubt: never. How did he answer?

ctx.s: 他{斩钉截铁}地说：“不行！”
ctx.en: He said flatly: "No way!"

ctx.s: 我问她会不会回来，她{斩钉截铁}地回答：“不会。”
ctx.en: I asked if she'd come back, and she answered firmly: "No."

ctx.s: 面对对方的高价收购，老板{斩钉截铁}地拒绝了。
ctx.en: Faced with the other side's high buyout offer, the owner turned it down flat.

ctx.s: 她的语气{斩钉截铁}，谁也不敢再劝她。
ctx.en: Her tone was so firm that no one dared try to talk her round again.

ctx.s: “你确定是他吗？”“我能{斩钉截铁}地告诉你，就是他。”
ctx.en: "Are you sure it was him?" "I can tell you with absolute certainty: it was him."

ctx.s: 记者追问此事，发言人{斩钉截铁}地否认了所有传闻。
ctx.en: When reporters pressed the matter, the spokesperson flatly denied all the rumours.

bad.s: 工人们正在工地上{斩钉截铁}，非常辛苦。
bad.en: (meant: the workers are cutting metal on the building site)
bad.why: It is only a figure for firm speech or attitude, never a literal description of cutting metal.

bad.s: 他犹豫了半天，最后{斩钉截铁}地说：“也许吧。”
bad.en: (meant: after hesitating he finally said, 'maybe')
bad.why: A hesitant 'maybe' is the opposite of a firm reply; the idiom needs a clear, definite statement.

cards.mean: fickle, always changing one's mind
cards.lit: three in the morning, four in the evening

story.text: A man who kept monkeys had to cut their food, so he told them they would get three nuts in the morning and four in the evening. The monkeys were furious. He then offered four in the morning and three in the evening, and they were delighted, though the total was the same. The fable first mocked people fooled by an empty change of words; today the phrase is used for someone who keeps changing their mind or loyalties.
story.source: 《庄子·齐物论》, also in 《列子·黄帝》

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 他做事朝三暮四; 朝三暮四的人. Criticises someone who keeps switching plans, jobs, partners or loyalties.

near.diff: 三心二意 is not putting one's whole mind into what one is doing now; 朝三暮四 is repeatedly switching from one choice or loyalty to another.
出尔反尔 is going back on a specific promise; 朝三暮四 is a general habit of changing one's mind or attachments.

cards.cue: Your cousin has changed his university major three times in two years and now wants to switch again. How do you criticise this habit?

ctx.s: 你不能这样{朝三暮四}，选定了就要坚持。
ctx.en: You can't keep changing your mind like this; once you've chosen, stick with it.

ctx.s: 他今天想学画画，明天想学钢琴，总是{朝三暮四}的。
ctx.en: Today he wants to learn painting, tomorrow piano; he's always flitting from one thing to another.

ctx.s: 她不喜欢{朝三暮四}的男人，只想找个踏实的人。
ctx.en: She doesn't like fickle men; she just wants someone steady and reliable.

ctx.s: 老板最怕员工{朝三暮四}，干几个月就跳槽。
ctx.en: What bosses fear most is fickle staff who job-hop after a few months.

ctx.s: “这次你真的不会再改主意了吧？”“放心，我不是{朝三暮四}的人。”
ctx.en: "You really won't change your mind again this time?" "Don't worry, I'm not the fickle type."

ctx.s: 他在感情上{朝三暮四}，朋友们都不敢把人介绍给他。
ctx.en: He's so fickle in love that his friends don't dare introduce anyone to him.

bad.s: 这个城市的天气{朝三暮四}，早上冷晚上热。
bad.en: (meant: the weather in this city is changeable)
bad.why: It criticises a person's fickle choices or loyalties; changeable weather needs a different expression.

bad.s: 他每天{朝三暮四}地工作，从早忙到晚。
bad.en: (meant: he works from morning to night every day)
bad.why: The numbers and times are not about working hours; it means fickle, not busy all day.

cards.mean: changing from one moment to the next
cards.lit: in the space of a blink and a breath, ten thousand changes

use.how: Predicate or attributive, of situations, markets, weather or battles: 市场瞬息万变; 瞬息万变的局势. Stresses speed and unpredictability of change.

near.diff: 日新月异 is steady progress seen over days and months, and is positive; 瞬息万变 is rapid, unpredictable change from moment to moment.
千变万化 stresses the endless variety of forms; 瞬息万变 stresses how fast things change.

cards.cue: A stock trader explains why she can't leave her screen even for a coffee: prices could swing in either direction any second. How does she describe the market?

ctx.s: 股市{瞬息万变}，谁也说不准明天会怎样。
ctx.en: The stock market changes by the second; nobody can say what tomorrow will bring.

ctx.s: 山里的天气{瞬息万变}，出发前一定要带好雨衣。
ctx.en: Mountain weather changes in an instant, so be sure to bring a raincoat before you set off.

ctx.s: 面对{瞬息万变}的病情，医生必须随时做好抢救准备。
ctx.en: Faced with a patient's condition that can change at any moment, the doctors must be ready to intervene at all times.

ctx.s: 比赛场上局势{瞬息万变}，最后一分钟还可能被翻盘。
ctx.en: On the pitch the situation changes in a flash; a lead can be overturned even in the final minute.

ctx.s: 战场上形势{瞬息万变}，指挥官必须随时调整计划。
ctx.en: On the battlefield things change from moment to moment, and the commander must adjust plans constantly.

ctx.s: 网络舆论{瞬息万变}，昨天的热点今天就没人提了。
ctx.en: Online opinion shifts by the minute; yesterday's hot topic is forgotten today.

bad.s: 十年过去了，家乡的面貌{瞬息万变}，到处都是新楼。
bad.en: (meant: over ten years my hometown has changed greatly)
bad.why: Change spread over years is described with idioms of steady progress; this one is for change happening moment by moment.

bad.s: 他的发型{瞬息万变}，变得很好看。
bad.en: (meant: his hairstyle changed a lot and looks great now)
bad.why: It describes a fast-shifting, unpredictable situation, not a single change in someone's look.

cards.mean: a thorough transformation
cards.lit: to shed the mortal womb and exchange one's bones

story.text: The phrase began as a Daoist term. A person who cultivated the Way successfully was said to shed the body they were born with and exchange ordinary human bones for the bones of an immortal. Later it came to mean any complete change of a person or thing, especially a change for the better.

use.how: Predicate or after 发生了/经历了 ... 的变化: 他像是脱胎换骨了。 Said of a person, team or organisation changed completely, usually for the better.

near.diff: 焕然一新 is about looking brand new on the surface (a room, a street); 脱胎换骨 is a change to the very nature of a person or organisation.
面目全非 is changed beyond recognition, usually for the worse; 脱胎换骨 is a deep change, usually for the better.

cards.cue: A lazy, rude student came back from a year of military service disciplined, polite and hard-working, a completely different person. How do his teachers describe him?

ctx.s: 当了两年兵，他像{脱胎换骨}了一样。
ctx.en: After two years in the army he seems like a completely new person.

ctx.s: 新教练来了以后，这支球队{脱胎换骨}，连赢了好几场。
ctx.en: After the new coach arrived, the team was utterly transformed and won several games in a row.

ctx.s: 经过这次改革，这家老工厂发生了{脱胎换骨}的变化。
ctx.en: After this reform, the old factory went through a complete transformation.

ctx.s: “你最近变化好大啊！”“是啊，生了一场大病，我感觉自己{脱胎换骨}了。”
ctx.en: "You've changed so much lately!" "Yes, after a serious illness I feel like a different person."

ctx.s: 要想{脱胎换骨}，光改几个坏习惯是不够的。
ctx.en: If you want to transform yourself completely, just changing a few bad habits isn't enough.

ctx.s: 这款手机的新版本几乎{脱胎换骨}，跟旧款完全不一样。
ctx.en: The new version of this phone is practically reinvented; it's nothing like the old model.

bad.s: 她剪了短发，{脱胎换骨}了。
bad.en: (meant: she cut her hair short and looks different)
bad.why: A new haircut is a surface change; the idiom means a change to someone's whole character or nature.

bad.s: 他出了车祸，身体{脱胎换骨}，再也不能走路了。
bad.en: (meant: after the accident his body was badly damaged)
bad.why: Despite the word for bone, it has nothing to do with injury; it means a thorough, usually positive transformation.

cards.mean: going from bad to worse
cards.lit: each time, the state of things sinks lower

story.text: Asked where the Way could be found, Zhuangzi named ants, weeds, tiles and even dung. He explained with an image from the market: to judge how fat a pig is, you press lower and lower down its leg, and the lower you press, the clearer it becomes. His wording was 'each time lower, the more evident'. Later writers reversed the words into today's form, meaning that things keep getting worse.

use.how: A predicate after a subject such as 身体, 生意, 成绩, 经济: 他的身体每况愈下。 Describes a gradual, continuing decline.

near.diff: 一落千丈 is a sudden, steep fall; 每况愈下 is a gradual decline that keeps getting worse.

cards.cue: Year after year, the old bookshop sold fewer books, cut staff, then hours, and now struggles to pay rent. How do you describe its business?

ctx.s: 爷爷年纪大了，身体{每况愈下}。
ctx.en: Grandpa is getting old and his health is going from bad to worse.

ctx.s: 自从附近开了大超市，这家小店的生意就{每况愈下}。
ctx.en: Ever since a big supermarket opened nearby, this little shop's business has gone steadily downhill.

ctx.s: 他上了高中以后迷上游戏，成绩{每况愈下}。
ctx.en: After starting high school he got hooked on games, and his grades kept slipping.

ctx.s: “这家餐厅最近怎么样？”“服务{每况愈下}，我都不想去了。”
ctx.en: "How's that restaurant these days?" "The service keeps getting worse; I don't even want to go anymore."

ctx.s: 这位作家后期的作品质量{每况愈下}，读者越来越少。
ctx.en: The quality of the writer's later works declined steadily, and he had fewer and fewer readers.

ctx.s: 由于长期污染，这条河的水质{每况愈下}。
ctx.en: Because of long-term pollution, the river's water quality has been getting steadily worse.

bad.s: 经过治疗，他的病情{每况愈下}，很快就出院了。
bad.en: (meant: after treatment his condition improved and he was soon discharged)
bad.why: It means getting worse and worse, never better.

bad.s: 他从楼梯上{每况愈下}，摔伤了腿。
bad.en: (meant: he fell down the stairs)
bad.why: It is about a situation declining over time, not physically going down or falling.

cards.mean: seen so often it is no longer news
cards.lit: seen again and again, no longer fresh

story.text: The Han official Lu Jia divided his wealth among his five sons and planned to travel, staying with each son in turn. With visits elsewhere, he said, he would come to each of them only two or three times a year, because a guest who comes too often no longer gets fresh food prepared for him, and he did not want to burden them. His wording used a different first character; the present form came later.
story.source: 《史记·郦生陆贾列传》 (as 数见不鲜)

use.how: A predicate after a phenomenon, often with 已经 or 早就: 这种骗局已经屡见不鲜。 Said of things, often problems, that happen so often they no longer surprise anyone.

near.diff: 家常便饭 is colloquial and says something is routine in one's own life (加班是家常便饭); 屡见不鲜 is more written and describes a phenomenon in society.
习以为常 is about a person being used to something; 屡见不鲜 is about the thing being common.

cards.cue: A journalist writes that fake online reviews used to cause outrage, but now they appear so often that nobody is shocked any more. What does she say about them?

ctx.s: 这种电话诈骗现在已经{屡见不鲜}了。
ctx.en: This kind of phone scam is so common now that it's nothing new.

ctx.s: 在大城市，堵车早就{屡见不鲜}，没人会觉得奇怪。
ctx.en: In big cities traffic jams are an everyday sight; nobody finds them strange.

ctx.s: 名人在网上发错消息的事{屡见不鲜}。
ctx.en: Celebrities posting the wrong thing online is nothing new.

ctx.s: “又有人插队了！”“这种事{屡见不鲜}，别生气了。”
ctx.en: "Someone's cut in line again!" "That happens all the time; don't get upset."

ctx.s: 十年前无人驾驶汽车还很新奇，如今在一些城市已经{屡见不鲜}。
ctx.en: Ten years ago driverless cars were a novelty; now in some cities they're a common sight.

ctx.s: 这类新闻{屡见不鲜}，说明问题还没有得到真正解决。
ctx.en: Stories like this come up again and again, which shows the problem has not really been solved.

bad.s: 这道菜{屡见不鲜}，不太新鲜了，别吃了。
bad.en: (meant: this dish isn't fresh any more, don't eat it)
bad.why: The 'fresh' in it means novel, not freshly made; it says a phenomenon is common, not that food has gone off.

bad.s: 我{屡见不鲜}他，所以不想再见他了。
bad.en: (meant: I've seen him so often I don't want to see him again)
bad.why: It cannot take a person as an object; it is a predicate saying that a kind of event is common.

cards.mean: emerging one after another without end
cards.lit: appearing layer upon layer, never exhausted

use.how: A predicate after things that keep appearing: 新产品层出不穷; 问题层出不穷. Stresses that new ones, often of new kinds, keep emerging.

near.diff: 络绎不绝 is people or vehicles arriving in a continuous stream; 层出不穷 is new things, ideas or problems constantly emerging.
接二连三 is events happening in quick succession; 层出不穷 stresses an endless supply of new ones, often over a longer period.

cards.cue: Every few months there is a new app, a new gadget and a new online trend that nobody had heard of before. How do you describe these innovations?

ctx.s: 现在手机的新功能{层出不穷}。
ctx.en: New phone features keep appearing all the time.

ctx.s: 网络上的新词{层出不穷}，老年人常常看不懂。
ctx.en: New internet slang keeps popping up, and older people often can't follow it.

ctx.s: 这家公司创意{层出不穷}，每年都有新产品上市。
ctx.en: This company has an endless stream of ideas and launches new products every year.

ctx.s: 这套系统用了三年，各种新问题还是{层出不穷}。
ctx.en: This system has been in use for three years, and new kinds of problems still keep cropping up.

ctx.s: “诈骗手段怎么这么多？”“是啊，新花样{层出不穷}，防不胜防。”
ctx.en: "Why are there so many scam tricks?" "I know, new ones keep appearing; you can't guard against them all."

ctx.s: 随着科技发展，各种新职业{层出不穷}。
ctx.en: As technology develops, all kinds of new professions keep emerging.

bad.s: 春节期间，商场里的顾客{层出不穷}。
bad.en: (meant: during Spring Festival customers kept streaming into the mall)
bad.why: For customers streaming in, use the idiom for a steady flow of arrivals; this one is for new things or phenomena emerging.

bad.s: 他的钱{层出不穷}，花也花不完。
bad.en: (meant: he has so much money it never runs out)
bad.why: It is about new kinds of things constantly appearing, not about an amount of money that never runs out.

cards.mean: arriving in a steady, unbroken stream
cards.lit: linked one after another, never breaking off

use.how: A predicate after people, visitors or vehicles: 游客络绎不绝; 来参观的人络绎不绝. Describes a continuous flow of arrivals, never things or ideas.

near.diff: 人山人海 is a huge crowd gathered in one place at one time; 络绎不绝 is people coming one group after another without a break.
层出不穷 is new things or problems constantly emerging; 络绎不绝 is a steady stream of people or vehicles arriving.

cards.cue: From opening time to closing time, visitors keep arriving at the new museum, group after group, never a quiet moment. How do you describe them?

ctx.s: 博物馆一开门，游客就{络绎不绝}。
ctx.en: As soon as the museum opened, visitors came in a steady stream.

ctx.s: 新店开张那天，来祝贺的朋友{络绎不绝}。
ctx.en: On the day the new shop opened, friends came to congratulate them one after another all day.

ctx.s: 国庆期间，前往景区的车辆{络绎不绝}。
ctx.en: During the National Day holiday, cars kept streaming towards the scenic spot.

ctx.s: “你们医院每天都这么忙吗？”“是啊，看病的人从早到晚{络绎不绝}。”
ctx.en: "Is your hospital this busy every day?" "Yes, patients keep coming from morning till night."

ctx.s: 这位老画家去世后，前来悼念的人{络绎不绝}。
ctx.en: After the old painter died, people came to pay their respects in an unbroken stream.

ctx.s: 山顶的寺庙香火很旺，上山的人{络绎不绝}。
ctx.en: The temple on the summit is very popular, and people climb the mountain in a continuous stream.

bad.s: 最近公司的问题{络绎不绝}，老板很头疼。
bad.en: (meant: problems at the company keep coming up)
bad.why: It describes people or vehicles arriving in a stream; problems that keep emerging take a different idiom.

bad.s: 他说话{络绎不绝}，一个小时都没停。
bad.en: (meant: he talked non-stop for an hour)
bad.why: It is about a stream of arrivals, not about one person talking without pause; that needs a different idiom.

cards.mean: only a handful (of outstanding ones)
cards.lit: they can be counted by bending one's fingers

use.how: Predicate or attributive about how few there are of a group, often notable ones: 这样的专家屈指可数。屈指可数的几家医院

near.diff: 寥寥无几 stresses disappointing emptiness (hardly anyone came); 屈指可数 says the few can be named one by one, often because they stand out.

cards.cue: You want to say that in the whole country you could name the top violin makers on your two hands.

ctx.s: 这个小镇上的饭馆{屈指可数}，大家都很熟悉。
ctx.en: There are only a handful of restaurants in this little town, and everyone knows them all.

ctx.s: 全国能做这种手术的医生{屈指可数}。
ctx.en: Only a handful of doctors in the whole country can perform this operation.

ctx.s: 他是我们公司{屈指可数}的几位技术骨干之一。
ctx.en: He is one of the few key technical experts in our company.

ctx.s: 那个年代，全村考上大学的人{屈指可数}，他就是其中之一。
ctx.en: In those days only a handful of people in the whole village got into university, and he was one of them.

ctx.s: “这家店开了多少年了？”“本地比它老的店{屈指可数}。”
ctx.en: "How long has this shop been open?" "There are only a handful of shops around here older than it."

ctx.s: 在中国足球史上，能在欧洲顶级联赛站稳脚跟的球员{屈指可数}。
ctx.en: In the history of Chinese football, the players who established themselves in Europe's top leagues are very few.

bad.s: 他{屈指可数}了一下，发现还差三天。
bad.en: (meant: he counted on his fingers and found three days were left)
bad.why: It is a fixed description meaning 'very few', not a verb for counting on one's fingers; say you counted with your fingers instead.

bad.s: 商场里的顾客{屈指可数}，挤得走不动。
bad.en: (meant: the mall was packed with countless shoppers)
bad.why: It means there are very few; it cannot describe a crowd too large to count.

cards.mean: demand exceeds supply
cards.lit: supply cannot meet the demand

use.how: Predicate about goods, tickets, housing, skilled workers in a market: 新款手机供不应求。 Also 出现供不应求的局面.

cards.cue: A bakery's new pastry sells out every morning within an hour, and the shop simply cannot bake enough of it.

ctx.s: 这款新手机一上市就{供不应求}。
ctx.en: As soon as this new phone came out, demand outstripped supply.

ctx.s: 春节前的火车票总是{供不应求}。
ctx.en: Train tickets before the Spring Festival are always in short supply.

ctx.s: “怎么又卖完了？”“这种蛋糕太受欢迎，天天{供不应求}。”
ctx.en: "Sold out again?" "This cake is so popular that we can never make enough."

ctx.s: 由于护士{供不应求}，很多医院不得不提高工资。
ctx.en: Because there are not enough nurses to meet demand, many hospitals have had to raise pay.

ctx.s: 一线城市的学区房长期{供不应求}，价格一路上涨。
ctx.en: In the biggest cities, flats near good schools have long been in short supply, and prices keep rising.

ctx.s: 今年苹果减产，市场上出现了{供不应求}的局面。
ctx.en: The apple harvest was poor this year, so the market saw demand exceed supply.

bad.s: 仓库里堆满了卖不出去的货，真是{供不应求}。
bad.en: (meant: there is far more stock than buyers)
bad.why: It means supply falls short of demand; an unsold surplus is the opposite situation (gōng guò yú qiú).

bad.s: 这家工厂{供不应求}客户的订单。
bad.en: (meant: this factory cannot keep up with its customers' orders)
bad.why: It is a complete predicate and takes no object; say the factory's products are in short supply, or that it cannot meet the orders.

cards.mean: far too little to solve the problem
cards.lit: a cup of water on a cartload of burning firewood

story.text: Mencius argued that humaneness overcomes its opposite as water overcomes fire. But, he said, people who practise humaneness today are like someone throwing one cup of water on a whole cartload of firewood that is burning; when the fire does not go out, they conclude that water cannot beat fire.

use.how: Predicate, often after 只是 or 无异于, about money, aid or effort far smaller than a need: 这点钱对他来说只是杯水车薪。

near.diff: 九牛一毛 says an amount is tiny compared with what someone has; 杯水车薪 says it is tiny compared with what a problem needs.
无济于事 says something does not help at all, for any reason; 杯水车薪 says it helps a little but is far too small.

cards.cue: A family owes huge hospital bills, and a neighbour hands over a small envelope of cash; it is kind, but nowhere near enough.

ctx.s: 他欠了那么多债，这点钱只是{杯水车薪}。
ctx.en: He owes so much that this bit of money is only a drop in the ocean.

ctx.s: 两台水泵对这么大的洪水来说简直是{杯水车薪}。
ctx.en: Against a flood this big, two pumps are hopelessly inadequate.

ctx.s: “每月加两百块工资有用吗？”“房租涨了那么多，{杯水车薪}啊。”
ctx.en: "Does a two-hundred-yuan raise help?" "With rent up that much, it barely scratches the surface."

ctx.s: 政府的补贴虽然及时，但对受灾地区来说仍是{杯水车薪}。
ctx.en: The government subsidy came quickly, but for the disaster area it is still far too little.

ctx.s: 靠几个志愿者清理整条河的垃圾，无异于{杯水车薪}。
ctx.en: Relying on a few volunteers to clear the rubbish from the whole river is a hopeless drop in the bucket.

ctx.s: 面对巨大的资金缺口，这笔捐款只能算{杯水车薪}，问题还得从根本上解决。
ctx.en: Faced with a huge funding gap, this donation is only a drop in the bucket; the problem needs a fundamental solution.

bad.s: 你送的礼物虽然{杯水车薪}，但我很感动。
bad.en: (meant: your gift was small, but it touched me)
bad.why: It describes help hopelessly short of a need, so it belittles a gift; it does not mean 'modest but kind'.

bad.s: 他的房间很小，只有{杯水车薪}。
bad.en: (meant: his room is tiny)
bad.why: It is not a general word for 'small'; it only measures help or resources against a large problem.

cards.mean: a dazzling array of fine things on display
cards.lit: precious jades fill the eyes

use.how: Predicate about goods, books, artworks or dishes on display: 货架上的商品琳琅满目。 Also attributive: 琳琅满目的展品. Not used of people.

near.diff: 应有尽有 says nothing is missing from the range; 琳琅满目 describes the eye-catching sight of many fine things laid out.
五花八门 is any wide, even confusing, variety (methods, excuses); 琳琅满目 is a pleasing display of attractive objects.

cards.cue: You walk into a jewellery and craft fair where every stall glitters with beautiful things laid out to admire.

ctx.s: 超市的货架上{琳琅满目}，什么都有。
ctx.en: The supermarket shelves are crammed with all kinds of goods; they have everything.

ctx.s: 夜市上摆满了{琳琅满目}的小吃和工艺品。
ctx.en: The night market is filled with a dazzling array of snacks and handicrafts.

ctx.s: 走进书店，{琳琅满目}的新书让她不知道先看哪本。
ctx.en: Walking into the bookshop, she faced so many fine new books that she didn't know which to look at first.

ctx.s: “展览怎么样？”“展品{琳琅满目}，一天都看不完。”
ctx.en: "How was the exhibition?" "There was such a wealth of exhibits that you couldn't see it all in a day."

ctx.s: 春节前，商店的橱窗里{琳琅满目}，到处是年货。
ctx.en: Before the Spring Festival, shop windows are full of eye-catching New Year goods.

ctx.s: 博物馆的这个展厅里{琳琅满目}，陈列着历代精美的瓷器。
ctx.en: This museum hall is a feast for the eyes, displaying exquisite porcelain from every dynasty.

bad.s: 广场上的游客{琳琅满目}，非常热闹。
bad.en: (meant: the square was full of tourists)
bad.why: It describes fine objects on display, never people; a crowd needs a different expression.

bad.s: 他的作业里错误{琳琅满目}。
bad.en: (meant: his homework was full of mistakes)
bad.why: It is praise for a beautiful display; it cannot describe a pile of mistakes.

cards.mean: all sorts and kinds (of people)
cards.lit: of every shape and every colour

use.how: Mostly attributive before a plural noun: 形形色色的人、形形色色的问题. Says a group contains many different kinds; not used of one thing.

near.diff: 五花八门 often hints the variety is odd or bewildering (tricks, excuses); 形形色色 neutrally says there are many kinds, especially of people.

cards.cue: A taxi driver says that in twenty years on the road he has carried every kind of passenger you can imagine.

ctx.s: 做出租车司机，每天都会遇到{形形色色}的人。
ctx.en: As a taxi driver, you meet all sorts of people every day.

ctx.s: 火车站里来来往往的都是{形形色色}的旅客。
ctx.en: The people coming and going in the station are travellers of every kind.

ctx.s: “当记者累吗？”“累，但能接触到{形形色色}的人和事。”
ctx.en: "Is being a reporter tiring?" "Yes, but you get to meet all kinds of people and situations."

ctx.s: 城市里生活着{形形色色}的人，每个人都有自己的故事。
ctx.en: All kinds of people live in the city, and each has a story of their own.

ctx.s: 这部小说描写了旧上海{形形色色}的人物。
ctx.en: This novel portrays the many different characters of old Shanghai.

ctx.s: 节目请来了{形形色色}的嘉宾，有农民，有科学家，也有明星。
ctx.en: The show invited all sorts of guests: farmers, scientists and celebrities.

bad.s: 她今天穿了一件{形形色色}的裙子。
bad.en: (meant: she wore a colourful dress)
bad.why: It means many different kinds within a group, not 'colourful'; one bright dress is wǔ yán liù sè.

bad.s: 这里的人非常{形形色色}。
bad.en: (meant: the people here are very diverse)
bad.why: It cannot take a degree adverb like hěn or fēicháng; say there are all sorts of people here instead.

cards.mean: each has its own merits
cards.lit: each has its thousand autumns (its own lasting worth)

use.how: Predicate after two or more people or things being compared: 这两家店各有千秋。 Says each is good in a different way, so no clear winner.

near.diff: 不相上下 says two are about equal on the same measure; 各有千秋 says each is strong in its own, different way.

cards.cue: A friend asks which of two cities is better to live in; one has the food, the other the scenery, and you refuse to pick.

ctx.s: 这两家火锅店{各有千秋}，一家汤底香，一家肉新鲜，我都喜欢。
ctx.en: The two hotpot places each have their own strengths: one has a fragrant broth, the other fresh meat. I like them both.

ctx.s: “你觉得北京好还是上海好？”“{各有千秋}吧，很难比较。”
ctx.en: "Which do you think is better, Beijing or Shanghai?" "Each has its own appeal; it's hard to compare."

ctx.s: 三位歌手风格不同，{各有千秋}，评委很难打分。
ctx.en: The three singers have different styles and each has merits, so the judges found it hard to score them.

ctx.s: 中西医{各有千秋}，不必非要分个高低。
ctx.en: Chinese and Western medicine each have their strengths; there is no need to rank one above the other.

ctx.s: 这几款车在价格和性能上{各有千秋}，就看你更看重什么了。
ctx.en: These cars each have advantages in price or performance; it depends on what matters more to you.

ctx.s: 两位作家的作品{各有千秋}：一位擅长写人物，一位擅长写景。
ctx.en: The two writers each excel in their own way: one at character, the other at landscape.

bad.s: 这部电影{各有千秋}，非常精彩。
bad.en: (meant: this film is excellent)
bad.why: It compares two or more things that are each good; it cannot describe a single film.

bad.s: 这两个方案都很糟糕，真是{各有千秋}。
bad.en: (meant: both plans are equally bad)
bad.why: It is praise: each has real merits. Things that are equally bad are bàn jīn bā liǎng.

cards.mean: to put on a par (usually: cannot be)
cards.lit: to raise two things together and discuss them side by side

use.how: Almost always negated or in a rhetorical question: A和B不能相提并论。 怎么能把A和B相提并论？ Takes no object; the two things go before it.

cards.cue: Someone compares a neighbourhood five-a-side kickabout with the World Cup final, and you object that the two are not in the same league.

ctx.s: 小区的足球赛怎么能和世界杯{相提并论}？
ctx.en: How can a neighbourhood football match be compared with the World Cup?

ctx.s: 我的厨艺和专业厨师根本不能{相提并论}。
ctx.en: My cooking is nowhere near a professional chef's; the two can't be compared.

ctx.s: “你们俩都是老师，差不多吧？”“我刚入职，哪能和他{相提并论}。”
ctx.en: "You're both teachers, so you're about the same, right?" "I've just started; I can't be mentioned in the same breath as him."

ctx.s: 意外失误和故意违规性质不同，不应{相提并论}。
ctx.en: An accidental mistake and a deliberate violation are different in nature and should not be treated as equal.

ctx.s: 有人把这部网剧和经典名著{相提并论}，我觉得太夸张了。
ctx.en: Some people put this web series on a par with the classics, which I think is going too far.

ctx.s: 今天的交通条件和三十年前已不可{相提并论}。
ctx.en: Transport today simply cannot be compared with what it was thirty years ago.

bad.s: 老师把我们两个人的作文{相提并论}了一下，说都写得很好。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher compared our two essays and said both were good)
bad.why: It is not a neutral verb 'to compare'; it is used to deny that two things are on a par.

bad.s: 我们{相提并论}这两个问题吧。
bad.en: (meant: let's discuss these two problems together)
bad.why: It takes no object and does not mean 'discuss together'; the two things must come before it.

cards.mean: complementing and reinforcing each other
cards.lit: each assists the other and each completes the other

use.how: Predicate after two abstract things: 理论和实践是相辅相成的。 Also 相辅相成的关系. Used of factors, qualities or activities, rarely of people doing a task.

near.diff: 息息相关 only says two things are closely tied; 相辅相成 says each actively strengthens the other.

cards.cue: A coach explains that reading builds a child's vocabulary, and a bigger vocabulary in turn makes reading easier and more fun.

ctx.s: 读书和写作是{相辅相成}的。
ctx.en: Reading and writing reinforce each other.

ctx.s: 在学习语言时，听和说{相辅相成}，缺一不可。
ctx.en: In language learning, listening and speaking complement each other; you need both.

ctx.s: “休息不会耽误训练吗？”“不会，休息和训练是{相辅相成}的。”
ctx.en: "Won't resting hold back my training?" "No, rest and training go hand in hand."

ctx.s: 经济发展与环境保护并不矛盾，而是可以{相辅相成}。
ctx.en: Economic growth and environmental protection are not in conflict; they can reinforce each other.

ctx.s: 这家公司的设计和技术{相辅相成}，产品才这么受欢迎。
ctx.en: The company's design and technology strengthen each other, which is why its products are so popular.

ctx.s: 理论指导实践，实践检验理论，两者形成了{相辅相成}的关系。
ctx.en: Theory guides practice and practice tests theory; the two form a mutually reinforcing relationship.

bad.s: 搬家那天，几个朋友{相辅相成}，很快就搬完了。
bad.en: (meant: my friends helped one another and finished the move quickly)
bad.why: It is about two abstract factors strengthening each other, not people pitching in on a job.

bad.s: 他们俩的意见完全相反，真是{相辅相成}。
bad.en: (meant: their views are completely opposite)
bad.why: It means the two support each other, so it cannot describe completely opposite views.

cards.mean: closely bound up with each other
cards.lit: connected breath by breath

use.how: Predicate in the pattern A与B息息相关 or A和B息息相关, about issues that directly affect people's lives or each other: 物价与百姓生活息息相关。

near.diff: 唇亡齿寒 warns that if one falls the other is endangered; 息息相关 just says the two are closely connected.
相辅相成 says two things strengthen each other; 息息相关 only says they are closely connected, in either direction.

cards.cue: A news anchor introduces a report on food prices by stressing how directly they touch every household's daily life.

ctx.s: 天气和农民的收入{息息相关}。
ctx.en: The weather is closely tied to farmers' incomes.

ctx.s: 房价的变化与每个家庭都{息息相关}。
ctx.en: Changes in house prices closely affect every family.

ctx.s: “为什么要关心环境问题？”“因为它和我们的健康{息息相关}啊。”
ctx.en: "Why should we care about the environment?" "Because it's closely bound up with our health."

ctx.s: 一个城市的发展，和交通是否方便{息息相关}。
ctx.en: A city's development is closely linked to how convenient its transport is.

ctx.s: 这次改革涉及的都是与老百姓生活{息息相关}的问题。
ctx.en: This reform deals with issues that directly concern ordinary people's lives.

ctx.s: 睡眠质量与情绪状态{息息相关}，长期失眠容易让人焦虑。
ctx.en: Sleep quality is closely bound up with mood; long-term insomnia easily makes people anxious.

bad.s: 我和小王{息息相关}，每天一起吃午饭。
bad.en: (meant: Xiao Wang and I are close friends)
bad.why: It links issues or factors that affect each other, not two friends who are close.

bad.s: 这两幅画的风格{息息相关}，看起来差不多。
bad.en: (meant: the two paintings look very similar)
bad.why: It means closely connected in effect, not similar in appearance.

cards.mean: following on logically and naturally
cards.lit: follow the line of reason and the writing takes shape

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (顺理成章地) about a result that follows logically from what came before: 他顺理成章地当上了队长。

near.diff: 水到渠成 says success arrives once conditions have ripened over time; 顺理成章 says a step follows logically from what came before.
理所当然 says something is only right or to be expected, often taken for granted; 顺理成章 stresses the logical sequence leading to it.

cards.cue: A deputy manager has run the team well for years, so when the manager retires, the promotion follows quite logically.

ctx.s: 他成绩最好，{顺理成章}地拿到了奖学金。
ctx.en: He had the best grades, so it followed naturally that he got the scholarship.

ctx.s: 既然双方都同意了这个方案，下一步签合同就{顺理成章}了。
ctx.en: Since both sides have agreed to the plan, signing the contract is the logical next step.

ctx.s: 他在中国生活了十年，又会说中文，{顺理成章}地成了公司中国区的负责人。
ctx.en: He had lived in China for ten years and spoke Chinese, so it followed naturally that he became head of the company's China office.

ctx.s: “你怎么就当上班长了？”“原来的班长转学了，我是副班长，接班也就{顺理成章}了。”
ctx.en: "How did you become class monitor?" "The old monitor changed schools and I was the deputy, so taking over followed naturally."

ctx.s: 从这些数据出发，得出这个结论是{顺理成章}的。
ctx.en: Starting from these data, reaching this conclusion follows logically.

ctx.s: 公司在国内站稳脚跟后，{顺理成章}地开始开拓海外市场。
ctx.en: Once the company was firmly established at home, it moved on, as a natural next step, to markets abroad.

bad.s: 昨天他突然中了彩票，真是{顺理成章}。
bad.en: (meant: he won the lottery yesterday, amazing)
bad.why: It describes a result that follows logically from what came before; pure luck follows from nothing.

bad.s: 这次旅行一路{顺理成章}，没遇到任何麻烦。
bad.en: (meant: the trip went smoothly with no trouble)
bad.why: It is about logical consequence, not a smooth, trouble-free journey; that is yí lù shùn lì.

cards.mean: success comes naturally when conditions are ripe
cards.lit: when the water arrives, a channel forms by itself

story.text: Exiled to Huangzhou on a very small income, Su Shi wrote to his friend Qin Guan describing how he got by: he rationed his savings strictly, allowing himself a fixed small sum for each day. As for what he would do when the savings ran out, he said he would not plan it now: when the water comes, the channel forms by itself, so there was no need to worry in advance.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (水到渠成的事): says a result follows easily because the groundwork has already been laid. Describes an outcome, not an action someone performs.

near.diff: 顺理成章 says something follows logically or reasonably; 水到渠成 says a result arrives on its own once enough conditions have built up.

cards.cue: A small bakery spent years perfecting its bread and winning loyal regulars; opening a second shop then happened with almost no strain. How do you describe it?

ctx.s: 只要你坚持练习，到时候自然{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: As long as you keep practising, it will all fall into place when the time comes.

ctx.s: 这支球队磨合了整整两个赛季，今年夺冠可以说是{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: The team spent two whole seasons gelling together, so winning the title this year came about quite naturally.

ctx.s: 先把基础打扎实，好成绩就会{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: Get the basics solid first, and good marks will follow naturally.

ctx.s: “合作什么时候能签下来？”“双方信任建立起来，签约自然{水到渠成}。”
ctx.en: "When will the partnership be signed?" "Once the two sides trust each other, the signing will follow naturally."

ctx.s: 别急着逼他表态，等时机成熟，一切都会{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: Don't push him to commit yet; when the time is right, everything will come together.

ctx.s: 他在这个领域默默积累了十年，去年出版专著可谓{水到渠成}。
ctx.en: He quietly built up ten years of work in the field, so publishing a monograph last year came quite naturally.

bad.s: 他运气真好，几乎没准备就{水到渠成}地拿了冠军。
bad.en: (meant: he was lucky and won without preparing)
bad.why: It describes success that follows from groundwork already laid, not luck without preparation.

bad.s: 我今晚一定要{水到渠成}这份报告。
bad.en: (meant: I must finish this report tonight)
bad.why: It is not a transitive verb for doing a task; it describes a result that comes about naturally.

cards.mean: to prepare in advance before trouble comes
cards.lit: before the rain comes, bind the nest tight

story.text: In an ancient poem a bird speaks: an owl has already carried off its young, and now, before the sky turns dark with rain, it gathers mulberry roots and binds up the openings of its nest so that it will hold. The image of securing the home before the rain became the idiom for preparing ahead of trouble.

use.how: Intransitive predicate, often after 要, 必须, 提前 or 这叫: 我们要未雨绸缪。 Praises or urges preparation made before a problem arrives.

near.diff: 亡羊补牢 is repairing things after a loss has happened; 未雨绸缪 is preparing before anything has gone wrong.

cards.cue: Business is booming, yet the owner sets aside an emergency fund and trains backup staff in case hard times come. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 趁年轻多存点钱，就是在{未雨绸缪}。
ctx.en: Saving a bit more while you're young is a way of preparing for the future.

ctx.s: 公司趁业务好的时候{未雨绸缪}，提前培训后备人员。
ctx.en: While business is good, the company is preparing ahead by training backup staff early.

ctx.s: 台风季节快到了，市里已经开始{未雨绸缪}，清理排水管道。
ctx.en: Typhoon season is near, and the city has already started preparing by clearing the drains.

ctx.s: “现在生意这么好，为什么还要准备应急资金？”“就得趁现在{未雨绸缪}，不能等出了问题再想办法。”
ctx.en: "Business is so good right now, why set up an emergency fund?" "Now is exactly when to plan ahead; we can't wait until something goes wrong."

ctx.s: 面对人口老龄化，社会必须{未雨绸缪}，尽早完善养老体系。
ctx.en: Facing an ageing population, society must prepare ahead and improve the pension system early.

ctx.s: 她做事向来{未雨绸缪}，重要文件总要备份好几份。
ctx.en: She always plans ahead; she keeps several backups of every important file.

bad.s: 房子被淹了以后，我们才{未雨绸缪}，买了抽水机。
bad.en: (meant: after the flood we finally bought a pump)
bad.why: It means preparing before trouble arrives; buying the pump only after the flood is fixing things too late.

bad.s: 我们要{未雨绸缪}这次考试。
bad.en: (meant: we should prepare for this exam in advance)
bad.why: It takes no object; what you prepare for must come before it with a preposition meaning 'for', or use a plain verb meaning 'prepare'.

cards.mean: to alert the target by acting too soon
cards.lit: beat the grass and startle the snake hiding in it

use.how: Predicate, very often after 免得, 以免, 为了不 or 小心: 先别问他，免得打草惊蛇。 Warns against a premature move that tips off someone you are watching.

cards.cue: You suspect a colleague is fiddling the accounts, but if you question him now he will simply destroy the evidence. Why do you wait?

ctx.s: 先别去问他，免得{打草惊蛇}。
ctx.en: Don't ask him yet, or you'll tip him off.

ctx.s: 警方掌握了线索，但为了不{打草惊蛇}，暂时没有行动。
ctx.en: The police have leads, but they are holding back for now so as not to alert the suspects.

ctx.s: 你现在就去质问他，不是{打草惊蛇}吗？
ctx.en: If you confront him now, won't that just warn him?

ctx.s: 想给她一个生日惊喜，就别到处打听，小心{打草惊蛇}。
ctx.en: If you want to surprise her on her birthday, stop asking around, or she'll catch on.

ctx.s: 调查人员悄悄收集证据，生怕{打草惊蛇}。
ctx.en: The investigators gathered evidence quietly, afraid of alerting their target.

ctx.s: 公司早就怀疑他泄露数据，可一次过早的谈话{打草惊蛇}，他第二天就辞职了。
ctx.en: The company had long suspected him of leaking data, but a premature talk tipped him off and he quit the next day.

bad.s: 他突然大叫一声，把孩子们{打草惊蛇}了。
bad.en: (meant: his sudden shout frightened the children)
bad.why: It does not mean to frighten someone; it means to warn a target you are pursuing by moving too early.

bad.s: 这次突击检查{打草惊蛇}，一下子就发现了很多问题。
bad.en: (meant: the surprise inspection shook things up and exposed problems)
bad.why: It names a mistake that lets the target escape, never an effective move that uncovers things.

cards.mean: a lesson from someone else's mistake
cards.lit: the overturned cart ahead serves as a mirror for those behind

story.text: The Han statesman Jia Yi, urging the emperor to reform, quoted a common saying: when the cart in front overturns, the cart behind takes warning. The Qin dynasty had collapsed so quickly, he argued, and if Han did not avoid the road Qin had taken, it would overturn in the same way.

use.how: A noun: 是……的前车之鉴, 有了……的前车之鉴, 以……为前车之鉴. Refers to someone's failure that serves as a warning to others.

near.diff: 前车之鉴 is the warning itself, a noun; 重蹈覆辙 is a verb for ignoring such a warning and repeating the mistake.

cards.cue: Friends ask why you rent instead of buying a huge house on a big loan. You point to your brother, who did exactly that and struggled for years.

ctx.s: 他的失败就是我们的{前车之鉴}。
ctx.en: His failure is a warning to all of us.

ctx.s: 有了上次的{前车之鉴}，这回大家都提前订了票。
ctx.en: After what happened last time, everyone booked their tickets early this time.

ctx.s: 邻居被骗的事就是{前车之鉴}，陌生电话千万别轻信。
ctx.en: What happened to the neighbour who got scammed is a lesson: never trust calls from strangers.

ctx.s: “你为什么不贷款买大房子？”“我哥就是{前车之鉴}啊。”
ctx.en: "Why don't you take out a loan for a big house?" "Look at my brother, that's why."

ctx.s: 那家公司因盲目扩张而倒闭，应当成为同行的{前车之鉴}。
ctx.en: That company went bankrupt through reckless expansion, and it should serve as a warning to others in the industry.

ctx.s: 历史上的许多教训，都是后人的{前车之鉴}。
ctx.en: Many lessons of history are warnings for those who come after.

bad.s: 我{前车之鉴}了他的错误，所以没有犯同样的错。
bad.en: (meant: I learned from his mistake)
bad.why: It is a noun, not a verb: you take someone's mistake as one, you cannot do it to a mistake.

bad.s: 他成功创业的经验是我的{前车之鉴}。
bad.en: (meant: his success is a model for me)
bad.why: It is a warning drawn from someone's failure, never a successful example to copy.

cards.mean: to repeat the same mistake
cards.lit: to tread again in the ruts of a cart that overturned

use.how: Intransitive predicate, often after 以免, 避免, 不要, 又 or 会: 以免重蹈覆辙。 Said of repeating a failure, one's own or someone else's, despite knowing better.

near.diff: 前车之鉴 is the warning a past failure gives; 重蹈覆辙 is failing to heed it and making the same mistake again.

cards.cue: A firm nearly went bankrupt by expanding too fast. Ten years later its new boss starts opening branches everywhere in exactly the same way.

ctx.s: 吸取教训吧，千万别再{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: Learn the lesson, and whatever you do, don't make the same mistake again.

ctx.s: 我们必须改进管理制度，以免{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: We must improve our management system so we don't repeat the same failure.

ctx.s: 他明知上次投资失败的原因，这次却又{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: He knew exactly why his last investment failed, yet this time he made the same mistake.

ctx.s: “这次还按老办法做吗？”“不行，那样只会{重蹈覆辙}。”
ctx.en: "Shall we do it the old way again?" "No, that would only repeat the same failure."

ctx.s: 不少企业没有吸取前人的教训，最终{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: Many companies failed to learn from those before them and ended up going the same way.

ctx.s: 这部纪录片提醒观众，忘记历史就可能{重蹈覆辙}。
ctx.en: The documentary reminds viewers that forgetting history can mean repeating its mistakes.

bad.s: 她每天都{重蹈覆辙}，走同一条路去上班。
bad.en: (meant: she takes the same route to work every day)
bad.why: It means repeating a mistake or failure, not simply doing the same thing as a routine.

bad.s: 老师让我把这道题{重蹈覆辙}一遍。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher made me redo this problem)
bad.why: It takes no object and is not 'to redo'; it criticises repeating a past failure.

cards.mean: caught off guard
cards.lit: too late even to decide where to put one's hands

use.how: Predicate after 让/令 or 一时, or in 打了……一个措手不及. Said when something sudden leaves no time to respond.

near.diff: 惊慌失措 stresses panic and losing one's head; 措手不及 stresses having no time to respond to something sudden.

cards.cue: In the last five minutes the other team suddenly switched tactics, and your side had no time at all to respond.

ctx.s: 突如其来的大雨让我们{措手不及}。
ctx.en: The sudden downpour caught us completely off guard.

ctx.s: 对方在最后几分钟突然改变战术，打了我们一个{措手不及}。
ctx.en: In the last few minutes they suddenly changed tactics and caught us flat-footed.

ctx.s: 面试官的问题出乎意料，他一时{措手不及}，没来得及想好怎么回答。
ctx.en: The interviewer's question was so unexpected that he was caught off guard and had no time to work out an answer.

ctx.s: “怎么连备用方案都没有？”“谁想到系统会突然崩溃，大家都{措手不及}啊。”
ctx.en: "How come there wasn't even a backup plan?" "Who knew the system would crash out of nowhere? Everyone was caught off guard."

ctx.s: 收购价格突然大幅下跌，许多农民{措手不及}，损失惨重。
ctx.en: The purchase price suddenly plunged, catching many farmers unprepared and causing heavy losses.

ctx.s: 提前做好准备，变化来临时才不会{措手不及}。
ctx.en: Prepare in advance, and you won't be caught off guard when change comes.

bad.s: 他做事总是{措手不及}，经常丢三落四。
bad.en: (meant: he is clumsy and careless)
bad.why: It describes being caught by a sudden event, not a careless or clumsy personality.

bad.s: 我们三个月前就知道这件事了，所以大家都{措手不及}。
bad.en: (meant: we knew three months ago, so everyone was ready)
bad.why: It requires suddenness; with months of warning nobody is caught off guard, so the sentence contradicts itself.

cards.mean: producing the opposite of the intended result
cards.lit: to get exactly the reverse

use.how: Predicate, often after 会, 可能, 往往 or 结果: 批评太多会适得其反。 Said of an action or method whose effect is the opposite of what it aimed at.

near.diff: 事与愿违 is any outcome contrary to one's hopes, often from outside causes; 适得其反 says one's own action caused the opposite effect.
弄巧成拙 stresses trying to be clever and spoiling things; 适得其反 is any measure that backfires, clever or not.

cards.cue: A parent nags a teenager to study every single night, and soon the teenager refuses to open a book at all.

ctx.s: 对孩子批评太多，往往会{适得其反}。
ctx.en: Criticising children too much often backfires.

ctx.s: 减肥时一直饿肚子可能{适得其反}，让人更想吃东西。
ctx.en: Starving yourself on a diet can backfire and make you crave food even more.

ctx.s: 他想安慰她，一个劲儿地劝她别哭，结果{适得其反}，她哭得更厉害了。
ctx.en: He wanted to comfort her and kept telling her not to cry, but it had the opposite effect: she cried even harder.

ctx.s: “我天天催他复习，有用吗？”“催得太紧可能{适得其反}。”
ctx.en: "I nag him to revise every day. Does it help?" "Pushing too hard can backfire."

ctx.s: 过度包装本想吸引顾客，却{适得其反}，让人觉得产品不实在。
ctx.en: The lavish packaging was meant to attract customers, but it backfired and made the product seem insubstantial.

ctx.s: 专家提醒，滥用抗生素不但治不好病，还可能{适得其反}。
ctx.en: Experts warn that misusing antibiotics not only fails to cure illness but can make things worse.

bad.s: 他本来想去北京，可是航班取消了，真是{适得其反}。
bad.en: (meant: he wanted to go to Beijing but the flight was cancelled)
bad.why: Nothing he did backfired; an outside event simply spoiled his plan, so the idiom for things going against one's wishes fits instead.

bad.s: 这个方法很{适得其反}，大家都喜欢用。
bad.en: (meant: this method is very suitable)
bad.why: The first character does not mean 'suitable' here; the idiom means backfiring, and it cannot be modified by 'very'.

cards.mean: things turn out contrary to one's wishes
cards.lit: events and wishes go against each other

use.how: A clause on its own, usually after 可惜, 可是, 然而 or 结果: 可惜事与愿违。 Expresses regret that the outcome differed from what was hoped.

near.diff: 适得其反 says one's own action produced the opposite effect; 事与愿违 only says the outcome differed from the hope, whatever the cause.

cards.cue: You had planned a quiet weekend at home, but your boss called and asked you to work both days. How do you sigh about it?

ctx.s: 我想周末好好休息，可惜{事与愿违}，又要加班。
ctx.en: I wanted a good rest at the weekend, but it wasn't to be: I have to work overtime again.

ctx.s: 他们本来打算在海边办婚礼，结果{事与愿违}，连下了一周雨。
ctx.en: They had planned a beach wedding, but things didn't go their way: it rained for a whole week.

ctx.s: 虽然大家都尽了力，但{事与愿违}，球队还是输了。
ctx.en: Everyone gave their all, but it didn't work out, and the team still lost.

ctx.s: “你不是要出国读书吗？”“是啊，可{事与愿违}，签证没批下来。”
ctx.en: "Weren't you going abroad to study?" "Yes, but it didn't work out. My visa was refused."

ctx.s: 人生常常{事与愿违}，重要的是怎样面对。
ctx.en: Life often doesn't go the way we want; what matters is how we face it.

ctx.s: 他希望退休后去各地旅行，然而{事与愿违}，身体一直不好。
ctx.en: He hoped to travel after retiring, but things turned out otherwise: his health has been poor ever since.

bad.s: 这次考试很顺利，一切都{事与愿违}。
bad.en: (meant: everything went as I wished)
bad.why: It means things went against one's wishes, so it cannot describe things going exactly as hoped.

bad.s: 这场大雨{事与愿违}了我们的计划。
bad.en: (meant: the rain ruined our plans)
bad.why: It is a self-contained clause and takes no object; the rain cannot do it to the plans. Use a verb such as 'disrupt' instead.

cards.mean: too far behind ever to catch up
cards.lit: to see only the dust of the one ahead and be unable to reach them

story.text: The Eastern Han official Zhao Zi, on his way to a new post, passed through Xingyang. The local magistrate, a man Zhao had once recommended for office, came out to the road to pay his respects, but Zhao did not stop. The magistrate followed him as far as the post station, yet could only gaze at the dust of his carriage without catching up.

use.how: Predicate, often after 让/令, 只能 or 真是: 他的水平我望尘莫及。 Admires someone far ahead; the subject or speaker is the one left behind.

cards.cue: Your colleague speaks five languages fluently, while you are still struggling with your first. You say how far behind her you are.

ctx.s: 他的中文水平，我真是{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: His Chinese is so good that I can't even come close.

ctx.s: 这家公司的技术实力让竞争对手{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: This company's technical strength leaves its competitors far behind.

ctx.s: “你也能像她那样一天读完一本书吗？”“我哪儿行，只能{望尘莫及}。”
ctx.en: "Can you read a whole book in a day like her?" "Me? No way. I can only admire her from far behind."

ctx.s: 老王退休后开始跑马拉松，连年轻人都{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: Old Wang took up marathons after retiring, and even young people can't keep up with him.

ctx.s: 论经验，我们这些新人对张师傅只能{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: When it comes to experience, we newcomers are nowhere near Master Zhang.

ctx.s: 该市近年的发展速度，令周边地区{望尘莫及}。
ctx.en: The city's pace of development in recent years has left the surrounding regions far behind.

bad.s: 他的成绩比我差远了，我对他{望尘莫及}。
bad.en: (meant: he is far behind me)
bad.why: It is said by or about the one left behind; here the speaker is ahead, so the roles are reversed.

bad.s: 这道数学题太难了，我{望尘莫及}。
bad.en: (meant: this problem is beyond me)
bad.why: It compares you with a person far ahead of you, not with a task that is too hard for you.

cards.mean: longing for one's child to become a great success
cards.lit: to hope that one's son becomes a dragon
