use.how: Predicate or attributive (望子成龙的父母), said only of parents and their own children; often comes with a hint of pressure. For daughters there is also 望女成凤.

cards.cue: A mother signs her seven-year-old son up for piano, maths and English classes, dreaming that he will one day be a famous surgeon.

ctx.s: 天下父母都{望子成龙}。
ctx.en: All parents dream of their children doing great things.

ctx.s: 他父母{望子成龙}，从小就给他报了很多辅导班。
ctx.en: His parents had great hopes for him and signed him up for lots of tutoring classes from an early age.

ctx.s: {望子成龙}的心情可以理解，但不能给孩子太大压力。
ctx.en: Wanting your child to succeed is understandable, but you shouldn't put them under too much pressure.

ctx.s: “你为什么非要孩子学钢琴？”“当妈的谁不{望子成龙}呢？”
ctx.en: "Why do you insist your kid learns the piano?" "What mother doesn't want her child to shine?"

ctx.s: 在一些家庭里，{望子成龙}变成了沉重的负担。
ctx.en: In some families, parents' high hopes for their children have become a heavy burden.

ctx.s: 这部电视剧讲的是一位{望子成龙}的母亲和叛逆儿子的故事。
ctx.en: The TV series tells the story of a mother with sky-high hopes for her son and her rebellious boy.

bad.s: 我{望子成龙}，希望自己将来当上总经理。
bad.en: (meant: I hope to become general manager one day)
bad.why: It is a parent's hope for their child, never a person's ambition for themselves.

bad.s: 老板{望子成龙}，希望新员工快点成长起来。
bad.en: (meant: the boss hopes the new staff grow quickly)
bad.why: It is only used of parents and their own children, never of a boss and employees.

cards.mean: to wait and see
cards.lit: to wipe one's eyes clean and wait (so as to see clearly what happens)

use.how: Usually ends the sentence and rarely takes an object: 让我们拭目以待。 Said of an outcome people are curious or doubtful about.

near.diff: 翘首以待 is eager longing for something hoped for; 拭目以待 is watching to see how an uncertain thing turns out, often with some doubt.

cards.cue: A rival company boasts its new phone will beat everyone. You doubt it, but the launch will show. What do you say?

ctx.s: 新电影下个月上映，到底好不好看，我们{拭目以待}。
ctx.en: The new film comes out next month; whether it's any good, we'll see.

ctx.s: 他说今年一定能考上研究生，大家都在{拭目以待}。
ctx.en: He says he will definitely get into graduate school this year, and everyone is waiting to see.

ctx.s: “这家新餐厅能撑过一年吗？”“不好说，{拭目以待}吧。”
ctx.en: "Will this new restaurant last a year?" "Hard to say. Let's wait and see."

ctx.s: 新市长承诺解决交通问题，市民们正{拭目以待}。
ctx.en: The new mayor has promised to fix the traffic problem, and residents are waiting to see if he delivers.

ctx.s: 这项技术能否真正改变我们的生活，还需要{拭目以待}。
ctx.en: Whether this technology will really change our lives remains to be seen.

ctx.s: 两支球队实力相当，决赛谁能夺冠，让我们{拭目以待}！
ctx.en: The two teams are evenly matched; who will win the final? Let's wait and see!

bad.s: 我饿坏了，正在门口{拭目以待}外卖。
bad.en: (meant: I'm starving and waiting at the door for my takeaway)
bad.why: It is about watching how a notable, uncertain outcome turns out, not waiting for something ordinary, and it normally takes no object.

bad.s: 听到这个坏消息，她伤心得{拭目以待}。
bad.en: (meant: she was so sad she wiped away tears)
bad.why: The eye-wiping here is clearing the eyes to watch closely, not wiping away tears; the idiom has nothing to do with crying.

cards.mean: the one who spoils it for the whole group
cards.lit: the horse that harms the herd

story.text: The Yellow Emperor lost his way and met a boy herding horses who knew the road. Impressed, the emperor asked him how to govern the world. The boy said it was no different from herding horses: simply get rid of whatever harms the herd.

use.how: A noun, usually after 是 or 成了: 他是我们班的害群之马。 Names one member whose behaviour damages the whole group's work or name.

cards.cue: One player keeps breaking team rules, and now the whole squad is punished with extra training. What is he to the team?

ctx.s: 全班同学都很守纪律，只有他是{害群之马}。
ctx.en: The whole class follows the rules; he is the only bad apple.

ctx.s: 一个员工收了回扣，公司马上开除了这个{害群之马}。
ctx.en: One employee took kickbacks, and the company fired the bad apple at once.

ctx.s: 少数无良商家是这个行业的{害群之马}，让顾客失去了信任。
ctx.en: A few dishonest sellers are the black sheep of the trade and have cost it customers' trust.

ctx.s: “为什么大家都被罚？”“还不是因为那个{害群之马}！”
ctx.en: "Why is everyone being punished?" "Because of that one troublemaker, of course!"

ctx.s: 教练说，球队不需要明星，更不需要{害群之马}。
ctx.en: The coach said the team doesn't need stars, and it needs troublemakers even less.

ctx.s: 他总在背后挑拨同事关系，成了部门里的{害群之马}。
ctx.en: He kept stirring up trouble between colleagues behind their backs and became the bad apple of the department.

bad.s: 他是我们队的{害群之马}，每场比赛都进球。
bad.en: (meant: he's our team's star, scoring in every match)
bad.why: It is harsh criticism of someone who harms the group; it can never be praise for a standout member.

bad.s: 这家公司的员工全都是{害群之马}。
bad.en: (meant: every employee of this company is bad)
bad.why: It singles out one or a few who spoil a group; if everyone is bad there is no herd for them to harm.

cards.mean: made even stronger by a new advantage
cards.lit: like a tiger that grows wings

use.how: A predicate, often 真是如虎添翼 or 让……如虎添翼. Said when someone already strong gains a new advantage that makes them stronger still.

near.diff: 锦上添花 adds a pleasant extra to something already good; 如虎添翼 adds strength, making someone already powerful more formidable.

cards.cue: Your debate team, already the champions, has just recruited the best speaker from a rival school. How do you describe the team now?

ctx.s: 球队本来就很强，又来了一位明星前锋，真是{如虎添翼}。
ctx.en: The team was already strong, and now a star striker has joined; it's like giving a tiger wings.

ctx.s: 她英语已经很好，再学会西班牙语，找工作就{如虎添翼}了。
ctx.en: Her English is already excellent; add Spanish and she'll be even stronger on the job market.

ctx.s: 有了新的研发中心，这家公司{如虎添翼}，发展得更快了。
ctx.en: With its new research centre the company, already strong, is growing even faster.

ctx.s: “听说你们组又来了个高手？”“是啊，这下我们{如虎添翼}！”
ctx.en: "I hear another expert has joined your group?" "Yes, now we're unstoppable!"

ctx.s: 这位老将经验丰富，加上年轻助手的帮助，更是{如虎添翼}。
ctx.en: The veteran has plenty of experience, and with a young assistant's help he is stronger than ever.

ctx.s: 对于一个优秀的厨师来说，一套好刀能让他{如虎添翼}。
ctx.en: For a skilled chef, a good set of knives makes him even better.

bad.s: 他从来没学过编程，买了新电脑真是{如虎添翼}。
bad.en: (meant: he has never learned to code, so the new computer is a big help)
bad.why: The tiger must already be strong; it cannot describe a beginner getting basic help.

bad.s: 路上本来就堵，又下起大雨，真是{如虎添翼}。
bad.en: (meant: the roads were jammed, and then heavy rain made it worse)
bad.why: It is praise for gaining strength; for one misfortune piling on another, use the 'snow on top of frost' idiom instead.

cards.mean: in one's element
cards.lit: like a fish that has found water

story.text: Liu Bei grew very close to Zhuge Liang, and his sworn brothers Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were displeased. Liu Bei told them: having Kongming is to me like a fish having water, so I hope you will say no more about it. After that they let the matter drop.

use.how: A predicate, often 在……如鱼得水 or 过得如鱼得水. Said of a person who thrives in a place, job or company that suits them perfectly.

near.diff: 得心应手 is a skill or tool working smoothly in your hands; 如鱼得水 is a person thriving in an environment that suits them.

cards.cue: A shy accountant who loved acting finally joins a theatre company, and there he thrives. How is he doing in his new world?

ctx.s: 他性格外向，做销售工作{如鱼得水}。
ctx.en: He's outgoing, so he is in his element working in sales.

ctx.s: 搬到大城市以后，喜欢热闹的她过得{如鱼得水}。
ctx.en: After moving to the big city, she, who loves bustle, is thriving.

ctx.s: 这位老师在新学校{如鱼得水}，学生们都很喜欢她。
ctx.en: The teacher is in her element at the new school, and the students all love her.

ctx.s: “你在国外习惯吗？”“刚开始不行，现在已经{如鱼得水}了。”
ctx.en: "Have you settled in abroad?" "Not at first, but now I'm completely at home."

ctx.s: 他在原来的公司处处受限，换了工作后反而{如鱼得水}。
ctx.en: He was held back at every turn at his old company, but in his new job he is flourishing.

ctx.s: 在自己擅长的领域里，他{如鱼得水}，很快就成了专家。
ctx.en: In the field he is good at, he was in his element and soon became an expert.

bad.s: 收到生日礼物，他高兴得{如鱼得水}。
bad.en: (meant: he was overjoyed to get a birthday present)
bad.why: It is not a burst of joy at a moment; it describes thriving in a setting or relationship that suits you.

bad.s: 他跑完步口渴极了，喝了一瓶水，{如鱼得水}。
bad.en: (meant: after the run he was thirsty and felt great after drinking water)
bad.why: The water is a figure for a fitting environment; it is never about the relief of drinking.

cards.mean: to pull together to get through a crisis
cards.lit: in the same boat, crossing the river together

story.text: In The Art of War, Sunzi observes that the people of Wu and the people of Yue hate each other. Yet if they are crossing a river in the same boat and a storm strikes, they will help one another like a person's left and right hands.

use.how: A predicate for several people facing one hardship: 大家要同舟共济，共渡难关。 Often an appeal to stick together.

near.diff: 齐心协力 is working together on any task; 同舟共济 stresses people sharing one danger or crisis and helping each other through it.

cards.cue: A storm knocks out power across town, and neighbours share generators, food and medicine until it's over. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 公司遇到困难，老板希望大家{同舟共济}。
ctx.en: The company is in trouble, and the boss hopes everyone will pull together.

ctx.s: 停电那几天，邻居们{同舟共济}，互相送水送药。
ctx.en: During the days without power, the neighbours stuck together and brought each other water and medicine.

ctx.s: 夫妻之间，最重要的是在困难时{同舟共济}。
ctx.en: Between husband and wife, the most important thing is to stand together in hard times.

ctx.s: “这次洪水太严重了。”“是啊，只有{同舟共济}才能渡过难关。”
ctx.en: "This flood is terrible." "Yes, only by pulling together can we get through it."

ctx.s: 那年工厂差点倒闭，全体员工{同舟共济}，硬是撑了过来。
ctx.en: That year the factory nearly went under, but all the workers pulled together and somehow held on.

ctx.s: 球队连续输球，队长说这时候更要{同舟共济}，不能互相埋怨。
ctx.en: After a run of defeats, the captain said this was the time to stick together, not to blame each other.

bad.s: 周末我和朋友{同舟共济}，一起去吃火锅。
bad.en: (meant: at the weekend my friends and I went out for hotpot together)
bad.why: It needs a shared crisis to get through; it cannot mean simply doing something fun together.

bad.s: 他一个人{同舟共济}，熬过了最难的日子。
bad.en: (meant: on his own, he got through his hardest days)
bad.why: It describes several people in one plight helping each other; one person alone cannot do it.

cards.mean: springing up everywhere like bamboo shoots
cards.lit: bamboo shoots after a spring rain, all shooting up at once

use.how: Almost always 像/如雨后春笋般 + 出现/涌现/冒出来. Said of many new things of one kind appearing quickly.

near.diff: 层出不穷 is new ones coming one after another without end; 雨后春笋 is a sudden burst of many at once, like fast growth.

cards.cue: Within two years, electric-scooter rental firms appeared on every corner of the city. How did they appear?

ctx.s: 这几年，奶茶店像{雨后春笋}一样开满了街头。
ctx.en: In the last few years, bubble-tea shops have sprung up all over the streets.

ctx.s: 网上购物流行以后，快递公司如{雨后春笋}般出现。
ctx.en: Once online shopping took off, delivery companies sprang up everywhere.

ctx.s: 城市周边，新的小区如{雨后春笋}般建了起来。
ctx.en: Around the city, new housing estates have been springing up one after another.

ctx.s: “现在怎么到处都是健身房？”“是啊，跟{雨后春笋}似的。”
ctx.en: "How come there are gyms everywhere now?" "I know, they're popping up like mushrooms."

ctx.s: 随着人工智能的发展，相关的创业公司如{雨后春笋}般冒了出来。
ctx.en: With the rise of artificial intelligence, start-ups in the field have mushroomed.

ctx.s: 那个年代，各种文学杂志如{雨后春笋}般涌现，年轻人争相投稿。
ctx.en: In those years literary magazines sprang up everywhere, and young people rushed to send in their writing.

bad.s: 他家门口如{雨后春笋}般开了一家咖啡店。
bad.en: (meant: a café opened right outside his home)
bad.why: It needs many things appearing at once; one new shop cannot spring up like bamboo shoots.

bad.s: 经济不好，小商店如{雨后春笋}般纷纷倒闭。
bad.en: (meant: with the economy bad, small shops closed one after another)
bad.why: Bamboo shoots shoot up; the image is of things appearing, never of them closing or disappearing.

cards.mean: to melt away completely (worries, anger)
cards.lit: the smoke dissipates and the clouds scatter

use.how: A predicate, often with 一下子, 早已 or 都: 误会都烟消云散了。 Said of worries, anger, doubts or past glory vanishing without a trace.

near.diff: 一笔勾销 is deliberately cancelling a debt or grudge; 烟消云散 is a feeling or thing fading away of itself.

cards.cue: You were furious with your friend, but after she explained and apologised, the anger simply dissolved. What happened to it?

ctx.s: 听到孩子平安的消息，她的担心一下子{烟消云散}。
ctx.en: When she heard her child was safe, her worry vanished at once.

ctx.s: 两人把话说开以后，之前的误会都{烟消云散}了。
ctx.en: Once the two of them talked it through, the earlier misunderstandings all melted away.

ctx.s: 考完最后一门，这一学期的压力全都{烟消云散}。
ctx.en: After the last exam, the whole term's stress just evaporated.

ctx.s: “你还生他的气吗？”“早就{烟消云散}了。”
ctx.en: "Are you still angry with him?" "That was gone long ago."

ctx.s: 曾经辉煌的王朝早已{烟消云散}，只留下几段古城墙。
ctx.en: The once-glorious dynasty has long since vanished, leaving only a few stretches of ancient wall.

ctx.s: 看到检查报告一切正常，他心里的疑虑才{烟消云散}。
ctx.en: Only when he saw that the test results were all normal did his doubts disappear.

bad.s: 我的钥匙{烟消云散}了，到处都找不到。
bad.en: (meant: my keys have vanished and I can't find them anywhere)
bad.why: It is for feelings, doubts or past glory fading away, not for an everyday object that has been lost.

bad.s: 他没说再见，就{烟消云散}地离开了。
bad.en: (meant: he left without a trace, not even saying goodbye)
bad.why: It describes feelings or glory fading, not a person walking off without a trace; it is not used as an adverb of leaving.

cards.mean: right by every law of nature, beyond question
cards.lit: the constant course of Heaven and the right order of Earth

story.text: In the Zuo Commentary, the statesman Zi Taishu repeats what Zichan once taught him: the rites are the constant course of Heaven, the right order of Earth, and the conduct of the people. From these words came the phrase for something self-evidently right.

use.how: A predicate, mostly ……是天经地义的（事）. Said of a duty or right so obvious that no one should question it.

near.diff: 理所当然 is simply 'only natural, as expected'; 天经地义 is stronger, a principle beyond all argument.

cards.cue: Your boss asks why you expect pay for the extra hours you worked. To you it needs no argument at all. What is it?

ctx.s: 欠钱还钱，这是{天经地义}的事。
ctx.en: If you owe money, you pay it back; that's simply how it is.

ctx.s: 在很多人看来，父母照顾孩子是{天经地义}的。
ctx.en: To many people, parents looking after their children goes without saying.

ctx.s: “加班凭什么不给钱？”“对，干活拿工资，{天经地义}！”
ctx.en: "Why should overtime be unpaid?" "Exactly. You work, you get paid. It's beyond question!"

ctx.s: 治病救人是医生{天经地义}的职责，不能看病人有没有钱。
ctx.en: Healing the sick is a doctor's unquestionable duty, whether or not the patient has money.

ctx.s: 古人认为尊敬长辈{天经地义}，不需要任何理由。
ctx.en: People in ancient times held that respecting one's elders was self-evidently right and needed no reason.

ctx.s: 顾客付了钱，要求商品质量合格，本来就{天经地义}。
ctx.en: A customer who has paid has every right to expect goods of proper quality.

bad.s: 他从小就{天经地义}地很聪明。
bad.en: (meant: he has been naturally clever since childhood)
bad.why: It is about what is morally right or just, not about innate talent or what someone is like by nature.

bad.s: 这次考试的题目很{天经地义}，大家都会做。
bad.en: (meant: the exam questions were straightforward and everyone could do them)
bad.why: It judges a duty or right as beyond question; it cannot mean simple, easy or obvious.

cards.mean: seamless, with no trace of flaws (a plan, a cover-up)
cards.lit: the clothes of heaven have no seams

story.text: On a summer night a man named Guo Han was lying in his courtyard when a woman came floating down from the sky: the Weaver Girl. He noticed that her clothes had no seams at all. When he asked why, she told him that heavenly clothes are not made with needle and thread.

use.how: A predicate or a complement after 得: 计划天衣无缝, 配合得天衣无缝. Said of plans, teamwork, lies or work so well made that no flaw shows.

near.diff: 完美无缺 is anything perfect; 天衣无缝 stresses that no gap or trace shows, so it suits plans, teamwork and cover stories.

cards.cue: At the surprise party the guests hid, the cake came on time, and the birthday girl suspected nothing at all. How was it all carried out?

ctx.s: 两位舞者配合得{天衣无缝}，观众掌声不断。
ctx.en: The two dancers moved together flawlessly, and the audience kept applauding.

ctx.s: 他以为自己的谎话{天衣无缝}，结果还是被妈妈识破了。
ctx.en: He thought his lie was airtight, but his mother saw through it anyway.

ctx.s: 这部推理小说的情节设计得{天衣无缝}，直到最后才揭晓凶手。
ctx.en: The plot of this mystery novel is seamless, and the killer is revealed only at the very end.

ctx.s: “你的计划真的没问题吗？”“放心，{天衣无缝}！”
ctx.en: "Are you sure your plan has no holes?" "Don't worry, it's watertight!"

ctx.s: 小偷自以为作案{天衣无缝}，却被监控拍得清清楚楚。
ctx.en: The thief thought he had left no trace, but the security camera caught everything clearly.

ctx.s: 修复后的古画和原作衔接得{天衣无缝}，看不出任何痕迹。
ctx.en: The restored parts of the old painting blend seamlessly with the original, without a visible trace.

bad.s: 这个杯子{天衣无缝}，怎么摔都摔不坏。
bad.en: (meant: this cup is unbreakable however you drop it)
bad.why: It means no flaw or gap shows in how something is put together, not that an object is strong or durable.

bad.s: 她长得{天衣无缝}，像明星一样漂亮。
bad.en: (meant: she is flawlessly beautiful, like a film star)
bad.why: It describes plans, teamwork or craftsmanship that show no flaw, never a person's natural looks or beauty.

cards.mean: the truth finally comes to light
cards.lit: the water level falls and the rocks emerge

story.text: In his Second Ode on the Red Cliff, Su Shi describes going back to the cliff in early winter: the mountains high, the moon small, the water low and the rocks standing out of it. The image of rocks revealed as the water falls later came to mean a hidden truth coming to light.

use.how: Often 查个水落石出 or 事情终于水落石出了. Said of an affair or mystery whose truth becomes fully clear, usually after investigation.

near.diff: 真相大白 simply states that the truth is now known; 水落石出 stresses it coming out after digging, and fits 查个水落石出.

cards.cue: Someone keeps taking food from the office fridge. You vow to keep digging until you know exactly who it is. What will you do?

ctx.s: 钱包到底是谁拿的，老师说一定要查个{水落石出}。
ctx.en: The teacher said she would get to the bottom of who took the wallet.

ctx.s: 经过警方三个月的调查，这起案件终于{水落石出}。
ctx.en: After three months of police investigation, the truth of the case finally came out.

ctx.s: “你相信他是清白的吗？”“等事情{水落石出}，大家就知道了。”
ctx.en: "Do you believe he's innocent?" "When the truth comes out, everyone will know."

ctx.s: 这件事不弄个{水落石出}，我睡不着觉。
ctx.en: I won't be able to sleep until I get to the bottom of this.

ctx.s: 记者追查了好几年，那桩丑闻才终于{水落石出}。
ctx.en: Only after journalists dug into it for several years did the truth of the scandal finally come out.

ctx.s: 时间会证明一切，真相总有{水落石出}的一天。
ctx.en: Time will tell; one day the truth will come to light.

bad.s: 我晚饭想吃什么，到现在还没{水落石出}。
bad.en: (meant: I still haven't decided what to have for dinner)
bad.why: It is about a hidden truth being uncovered, not about making up one's mind.

bad.s: 他是一个{水落石出}的人，从来不说谎。
bad.en: (meant: he is an open, honest person who never lies)
bad.why: It describes a hidden matter becoming clear, never a person's character or honesty.

cards.mean: rising along with its surroundings
cards.lit: when the water rises, the boat rises with it

use.how: Predicate, often after 也 or 跟着: one thing goes up because what it depends on went up. 房价涨了，房租也水涨船高。

near.diff: 蒸蒸日上 praises steady, thriving growth of its own; 水涨船高 says something rises only because its base or surroundings rose.

cards.cue: House prices in the area jumped, and within months every landlord nearby had raised the rent too. How do you describe the rents?

ctx.s: 房价涨了，附近的房租也跟着{水涨船高}。
ctx.en: House prices went up, and rents nearby rose right along with them.

ctx.s: 他拿了冠军以后，出场费{水涨船高}。
ctx.en: After he won the championship, his appearance fee went up accordingly.

ctx.s: “这家店的菜怎么又贵了？”“肉价涨了，菜价自然{水涨船高}。”
ctx.en: "Why has this restaurant put its prices up again?" "Meat got dearer, so naturally the dishes did too."

ctx.s: 大家的整体水平提高了，比赛的难度也{水涨船高}。
ctx.en: Everyone's overall level has improved, so the competitions have become harder as well.

ctx.s: 随着城市的发展，这一带的地价{水涨船高}，老居民纷纷卖了房子。
ctx.en: As the city grew, land prices here climbed with it, and the old residents sold up one after another.

ctx.s: 公司业绩越来越好，员工的待遇也{水涨船高}。
ctx.en: The company kept doing better, and the staff's pay and benefits rose along with it.

bad.s: 经济不景气，大家的工资都{水涨船高}，越来越少了。
bad.en: (meant: the economy is bad and everyone's pay keeps shrinking)
bad.why: It only describes something going up with its surroundings; it cannot describe a fall.

bad.s: 老板决定{水涨船高}我们的工资。
bad.en: (meant: the boss decided to raise our pay)
bad.why: It is not a transitive verb meaning 'to raise'; it describes a rise that follows from something else rising.

cards.mean: to drift with the current, having no views of one's own
cards.lit: to follow the waves and chase the current

use.how: Predicate or after 不愿/不能: criticises someone who just goes along with the crowd or circumstances. 他不想随波逐流。

near.diff: 入乡随俗 is sensibly adopting local customs, a good thing; 随波逐流 is having no direction of one's own and letting others decide.
人云亦云 is repeating what others say; 随波逐流 is the broader habit of going wherever the crowd or the times push you.

cards.cue: Everyone in her class chose finance because it pays well, but she wanted to study art and refused to just follow them. What did she refuse to do?

ctx.s: 做人要有自己的想法，不能{随波逐流}。
ctx.en: You need ideas of your own; you can't just drift along with everyone else.

ctx.s: 同学们都去学金融，她却不愿{随波逐流}，选了美术。
ctx.en: Her classmates all went into finance, but she refused to follow the crowd and chose art.

ctx.s: “你为什么也买这个？”“大家都买，我就{随波逐流}了。”
ctx.en: "Why did you buy one too?" "Everyone was buying it, so I just went along with it."

ctx.s: 这几年他一直{随波逐流}，到现在还不知道自己想做什么。
ctx.en: For years he has just drifted along, and he still doesn't know what he wants to do.

ctx.s: 市场上流行什么，这家工厂就生产什么，一味{随波逐流}，始终没有自己的品牌。
ctx.en: The factory makes whatever happens to be in fashion, always just following the market, and has never built a brand of its own.

ctx.s: 这位作家始终坚持自己的风格，从不{随波逐流}。
ctx.en: This writer has always kept her own style and never just gone along with the trend.

bad.s: 他到了国外很快就{随波逐流}，适应得特别好。
bad.en: (meant: abroad he quickly adapted to local ways and settled in well)
bad.why: It criticises having no views of one's own; sensibly adapting to a new place calls for a different idiom, about following local customs.

bad.s: 我决定{随波逐流}大家的意见。
bad.en: (meant: I decided to go along with everyone's opinion)
bad.why: It takes no object: the person who drifts is the subject, and you cannot drift along someone's opinion as an object.

cards.mean: in full swing (a campaign or event)
cards.lit: like fire and like the white flowers of reeds

story.text: At the meeting of the states at Huangchi, King Fuchai of Wu, contending with Jin for leadership, drew up his troops in great square formations during the night. The central army was all in white, with white banners, white armour and white-feathered arrows, and looked like a field of white reed flowers; the left army was all in red and looked like fire; the right was all in black. The display was meant to overawe Jin.

use.how: Adverbial or predicate, typically 正在如火如荼地进行 / 开展: describes a large campaign, contest or season of events at its height.

near.diff: 热火朝天 paints a visible scene of people busily working; 如火如荼 says a large-scale campaign or event is at its height, mostly in writing.

cards.cue: A news report says the city's month-long book fair, with events in every district, is now at its peak. How does the report describe it?

ctx.s: 世界杯正在{如火如荼}地进行。
ctx.en: The World Cup is now in full swing.

ctx.s: 眼下，全市的植树活动开展得{如火如荼}。
ctx.en: At the moment the city-wide tree-planting campaign is in full swing.

ctx.s: 今年的读书节已进入第三周，各区的活动{如火如荼}。
ctx.en: This year's reading festival is in its third week, and events across the districts are at their height.

ctx.s: 在招聘季{如火如荼}的时候，很多学生一天要参加好几场面试。
ctx.en: When the recruitment season is at its peak, many students sit several interviews a day.

ctx.s: 全国人口普查工作目前正{如火如荼}地开展。
ctx.en: The national census is currently in full swing.

ctx.s: 新能源汽车的价格战打得{如火如荼}，消费者成了最大的赢家。
ctx.en: The price war over new-energy cars is raging, and consumers are the biggest winners.

bad.s: 今天三十八度，天气{如火如荼}。
bad.en: (meant: it's thirty-eight degrees, scorching hot today)
bad.why: Despite the fire in it, it never describes hot weather; it describes a campaign or event in full swing.

bad.s: 我一个人在家{如火如荼}地写作业。
bad.en: (meant: I'm at home busily doing my homework)
bad.why: It describes a large collective campaign or event, not one person's small task.

cards.mean: buzzing with enthusiastic activity
cards.lit: hot fire leaping toward the sky

use.how: Complement or attributive: 干得热火朝天, 热火朝天的工地. Describes a lively scene of many people working or busy with enthusiasm.

near.diff: 如火如荼 is mostly written and says a campaign or event is at its height; 热火朝天 paints the visible bustle of people busily at work.

cards.cue: On the day before the school fair, the hall is full of parents and pupils hammering, painting and shouting to each other. How do you describe the scene?

ctx.s: 工地上大家干得{热火朝天}。
ctx.en: On the building site everyone is working away flat out.

ctx.s: 厨房里{热火朝天}，全家人在一起包饺子。
ctx.en: The kitchen is bustling: the whole family is making dumplings together.

ctx.s: “你们在忙什么呢？”“布置晚会的会场，正干得{热火朝天}。”
ctx.en: "What are you all so busy with?" "Setting up the hall for the party; we're right in the thick of it."

ctx.s: 秋收时节，田里到处是{热火朝天}的景象。
ctx.en: At harvest time, the fields are full of busy, lively scenes.

ctx.s: 一进办公室，就看见大家在{热火朝天}地讨论新方案。
ctx.en: As soon as I walked into the office, I saw everyone eagerly debating the new plan.

ctx.s: 比赛前一天，体育馆里彩排得{热火朝天}，没人顾得上吃饭。
ctx.en: The day before the event, the rehearsal in the gym was in full swing and no one had time to eat.

bad.s: 今天{热火朝天}，我们别出门了。
bad.en: (meant: it's boiling hot today, let's stay in)
bad.why: It describes a lively scene of busy activity, not hot weather.

bad.s: 他一个人坐在图书馆里{热火朝天}地看书。
bad.en: (meant: he sat alone in the library reading intently)
bad.why: It paints noisy, bustling activity, usually of a group; quiet solitary study does not fit.

cards.mean: bold and sweeping (reforms, cuts)
cards.lit: a big broadsword and a wide axe

use.how: Adverbial with 地, or predicate: 大刀阔斧地改革 / 裁员 / 删改. Describes decisive, large-scale changes or cuts.

near.diff: 雷厉风行 stresses speed and strictness in carrying out orders; 大刀阔斧 stresses the boldness and scale of the changes made.

cards.cue: A new director arrives at a loss-making firm, closes three departments, scraps half the products and rewrites the rules within a year. How did she reform it?

ctx.s: 新校长上任后{大刀阔斧}地进行改革。
ctx.en: After taking office, the new head carried out bold, sweeping reforms.

ctx.s: 这篇稿子太长，编辑{大刀阔斧}地删掉了一半。
ctx.en: The draft was too long, so the editor boldly cut half of it.

ctx.s: “这么大的问题，慢慢改行吗？”“不行，必须{大刀阔斧}地改。”
ctx.en: "With a problem this big, can we change things gradually?" "No, we have to make bold, sweeping changes."

ctx.s: 面对连年亏损，公司{大刀阔斧}地砍掉了一半产品线。
ctx.en: Facing years of losses, the company made sweeping cuts and dropped half its product lines.

ctx.s: 他做事{大刀阔斧}，不过细节上有时考虑得不够。
ctx.en: He acts boldly and on a large scale, though he sometimes doesn't think through the details.

ctx.s: 这次改造{大刀阔斧}，老街几乎换了一副面貌。
ctx.en: The renovation was sweeping, and the old street looks almost completely different.

bad.s: 他{大刀阔斧}地改了文章里的一个错别字。
bad.en: (meant: he fixed one typo in the article)
bad.why: It describes bold, large-scale changes; correcting one small error is the opposite.

bad.s: 他{大刀阔斧}地骂了我一顿。
bad.en: (meant: he gave me a fierce telling-off)
bad.why: It is about decisive reforms or cuts, not about harsh or violent words.

cards.mean: to go by the facts, realistic
cards.lit: from real things, seek what is right

story.text: Liu De, Prince Xian of Hejian and a son of Emperor Jing of Han, loved learning and old books. When he obtained a good text from the common people, he had a fine copy made and gave it to the owner, keeping the original for himself, so his collection grew to rival the court's. The history of the Han sums him up as one who studied, loved antiquity, and sought what was right from real evidence.

use.how: Predicate, adverbial (实事求是地说 / 评价) or attributive (实事求是的态度): judging or reporting according to the facts, without exaggeration.

near.diff: 脚踏实地 praises working steadily and diligently; 实事求是 is about judging and speaking according to the facts.

cards.cue: Asked whether the project will finish on time, an engineer neither promises the impossible nor panics, but lays out exactly what has been done and what remains. What attitude is she showing?

ctx.s: {实事求是}地说，这次我们做得不够好。
ctx.en: To be honest about it, we didn't do well enough this time.

ctx.s: 写报告要{实事求是}，不能夸大成绩。
ctx.en: A report has to stick to the facts; you mustn't exaggerate the results.

ctx.s: “你觉得他能当选吗？”“{实事求是}地讲，希望不大。”
ctx.en: "Do you think he'll be elected?" "Realistically speaking, his chances aren't good."

ctx.s: 医生{实事求是}地把病情告诉了病人，没有隐瞒。
ctx.en: The doctor told the patient plainly how things stood, hiding nothing.

ctx.s: 评价一个人要{实事求是}，既看到优点，也看到缺点。
ctx.en: When you assess someone you have to go by the facts, seeing both strengths and weaknesses.

ctx.s: 这位记者{实事求是}的报道态度赢得了读者的信任。
ctx.en: The reporter's commitment to sticking to the facts won the readers' trust.

bad.s: 他每天都{实事求是}地工作，从不偷懒。
bad.en: (meant: he works steadily every day and never slacks)
bad.why: It is about judging and speaking according to the facts, not about working steadily and diligently.

bad.s: 我们要{实事求是}这个问题。
bad.en: (meant: we should look at this problem realistically)
bad.why: It takes no object; introduce the problem with a preposition first, or use the idiom adverbially before a verb like 'look at'.

cards.mean: to lump everything together (usually: cannot)
cards.lit: to judge all things by one measure

use.how: Almost always negated: 不能 / 不可 / 很难一概而论. Says cases differ and must not be judged by one general rule.

near.diff: 因人而异 states that something varies from person to person; 一概而论 warns against judging different cases as if they were the same.

cards.cue: Someone says that all online courses are useless. You think some are excellent and some are poor, so a blanket verdict is unfair. What do you reply?

ctx.s: 网课好不好，不能{一概而论}。
ctx.en: Whether online courses are good or not depends; you can't make a blanket judgement.

ctx.s: 每个孩子情况不同，这种事很难{一概而论}。
ctx.en: Every child is different, so it's hard to generalise about this.

ctx.s: “年轻人是不是都不爱读书？”“这可不能{一概而论}。”
ctx.en: "Is it true that young people don't like reading?" "You really can't lump them all together."

ctx.s: 同样是加班，有的出于自愿，有的出于无奈，不可{一概而论}。
ctx.en: Overtime is not all the same: some people choose it and some have no choice, so it can't be judged as one thing.

ctx.s: 有人一提到网红就说是骗子，这种{一概而论}的看法并不客观。
ctx.en: Some people call every influencer a fraud; that kind of sweeping view isn't objective.

ctx.s: 转基因食品是否安全，专家们认为要具体分析，不宜{一概而论}。
ctx.en: On whether GM foods are safe, experts say each case needs analysing and a blanket judgement is unwise.

bad.s: 他{一概而论}地拒绝了所有的邀请。
bad.en: (meant: he turned down every invitation without exception)
bad.why: It means judging different cases as if they were the same, not doing something to all of them; only its first two characters mean 'without exception'.

bad.s: 这本书{一概而论}了中国历史。
bad.en: (meant: this book summarises Chinese history)
bad.why: It does not mean 'to summarise'; it means wrongly treating different cases as one, and it is usually negated.

cards.mean: to adapt measures to local conditions
cards.lit: according to the land, devise what is suitable

story.text: When Helü became king of Wu, he asked Wu Zixu how to make the state secure and powerful. Wu Zixu advised him to build city walls, set up defences, fill the granaries and stock the armoury. In the exchange that follows, the walls and storehouses are to be built to suit the lie of the land, which is where the phrase comes from.

use.how: Predicate or adverbial (因地制宜地发展): fitting plans, farming, building or policy to the conditions of a particular place.

near.diff: 因材施教 fits teaching to each student; 因地制宜 fits plans and measures to the conditions of a place.
入乡随俗 is a person adopting local customs; 因地制宜 is designing measures to suit local conditions.

cards.cue: Planners in a dry northern county grow drought-hardy crops while a wet southern county plants rice, instead of copying one national plan. What principle are they following?

ctx.s: 种什么庄稼，要{因地制宜}。
ctx.en: Which crops to grow depends on the local conditions.

ctx.s: 山区缺水，当地{因地制宜}，发展了果树种植。
ctx.en: The mountain area is short of water, so the locals adapted to it and took up fruit growing.

ctx.s: “别的城市的经验能直接照搬吗？”“不行，还得{因地制宜}。”
ctx.en: "Can we just copy other cities' experience?" "No, we still have to adapt it to our own conditions."

ctx.s: 这家连锁店在各地{因地制宜}，菜单都有当地特色。
ctx.en: The chain adapts to each place, and every menu has local touches.

ctx.s: 老房子改造没有统一模板，只能{因地制宜}地设计。
ctx.en: There's no standard template for renovating old houses; each design has to suit the site.

ctx.s: 各省应当{因地制宜}，制定适合本地的发展计划。
ctx.en: Each province should adapt to its own conditions and draw up a development plan that suits it.

bad.s: 王老师对每个学生都{因地制宜}，教法各不相同。
bad.en: (meant: Ms Wang teaches each student in a way that suits them)
bad.why: It is about adapting measures to the conditions of a place; teaching suited to each student calls for a different idiom.

bad.s: 他到了北京就{因地制宜}，学会了说北京话。
bad.en: (meant: in Beijing he fitted in and picked up the local accent)
bad.why: It is about planning measures to suit a place, not about a person adopting local customs or speech.

cards.mean: varying from person to person
cards.lit: differing according to the person

use.how: Predicate whose subject is a thing (效果、感受、方法): 效果因人而异. States that it depends on the individual.

near.diff: 一概而论 is judging all cases as one, usually negated; 因人而异 simply states that something varies by person.
因材施教 is the act of teaching each student differently; 因人而异 just observes that something differs by person.

cards.cue: A friend asks whether a new sleep app will work for them. It helped you but did nothing for your sister. What do you say about its effect?

ctx.s: 这种药的效果{因人而异}。
ctx.en: How well this medicine works varies from person to person.

ctx.s: “学会游泳要多久？”“这个{因人而异}，有人一周，有人一个月。”
ctx.en: "How long does it take to learn to swim?" "It depends on the person: some take a week, some a month."

ctx.s: 对同一部电影的感受{因人而异}，不必强求一致。
ctx.en: People react differently to the same film; there's no need to insist everyone agree.

ctx.s: 减肥的方法{因人而异}，适合别人的不一定适合你。
ctx.en: Ways of losing weight differ by person; what suits others won't necessarily suit you.

ctx.s: 每天需要睡几个小时，其实{因人而异}。
ctx.en: How many hours of sleep you need each day actually varies from person to person.

ctx.s: 这里的奖金分配{因人而异}，主要看每个人的工作量。
ctx.en: Bonuses here differ from person to person, depending mainly on each one's workload.

bad.s: 他这个人很{因人而异}，你永远猜不透他。
bad.en: (meant: he is unpredictable; you can never figure him out)
bad.why: It describes how a thing varies across people, not a person's character, and it cannot be modified by 'very'.

bad.s: 我和我哥哥{因人而异}，性格完全不同。
bad.en: (meant: my brother and I are completely different in character)
bad.why: Its subject is a thing that varies by person, not the people being compared; it cannot mean 'we are different'.

cards.mean: to learn from others' strengths to fix one's weaknesses
cards.lit: take from the long to make up the short

use.how: Predicate, often with 互相 or 相互: two people or groups learn from each other's strengths. 大家互相取长补短。

near.diff: 扬长避短 is making the most of your own strengths and steering around your weak points; 取长补短 is learning from others' strengths to fix your weak points.
集思广益 gathers many people's ideas to solve one problem; 取长补短 is learning from each other to improve oneself.

cards.cue: One teammate is great at design but weak at coding; the other is the reverse. They sit together every week to teach each other. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 同学之间要互相学习，{取长补短}。
ctx.en: Classmates should learn from each other, each making up for their weak points with the other's strengths.

ctx.s: 他们俩一个擅长设计，一个擅长编程，正好{取长补短}。
ctx.en: One of them is good at design and the other at coding, so they complement each other perfectly.

ctx.s: “为什么要和别的学校交流？”“为了{取长补短}，提高自己。”
ctx.en: "Why do exchanges with other schools?" "To learn from their strengths and improve ourselves."

ctx.s: 两家公司合作以后{取长补短}，产品质量明显提高了。
ctx.en: Once the two companies started working together they learned from each other, and product quality clearly improved.

ctx.s: 中西医如果能{取长补短}，对病人会更有好处。
ctx.en: If Chinese and Western medicine could learn from each other's strengths, patients would benefit more.

ctx.s: 新老员工在一起工作，可以相互{取长补短}。
ctx.en: When new and experienced staff work together, they can each learn from the other's strengths.

bad.s: 面试时要{取长补短}，多谈优点，少谈缺点。
bad.en: (meant: in an interview, talk up your strengths and avoid your weak points)
bad.why: It means learning from others' strengths, not presenting your own strengths and hiding your weak points.

bad.s: 这条裤子太长了，裁缝帮我{取长补短}。
bad.en: (meant: the trousers were too long, so the tailor altered them)
bad.why: It is never used literally for cutting or altering things; it means learning from others' strengths.

cards.mean: to teach each student according to their ability
cards.lit: to give teaching according to the material (each person's talent)

story.text: Two of Confucius's disciples asked him the same question: when I hear something right, should I act on it at once? He told the bold Zilu to consult his father and elder brothers first, but told the hesitant Ran You to act at once. When another disciple asked why the answers differed, Confucius said Ran You holds back, so he pushed him forward, while Zilu rushes ahead, so he held him back.

use.how: Used as a predicate about teachers, parents or coaches: 老师要因材施教。 It takes no object; say 对学生因材施教.

near.diff: 对症下药 fits a remedy to a problem; 因材施教 fits teaching to the person being taught.

cards.cue: A teacher gently encourages the shy pupil and gives the overconfident one harder challenges, each according to who they are.

ctx.s: 好老师懂得{因材施教}，不会用同一种方法教所有学生。
ctx.en: A good teacher knows how to teach each student differently, rather than using one method for everyone.

ctx.s: 这两个孩子性格完全不同，你得{因材施教}才行。
ctx.en: These two children have completely different personalities; you have to teach each in their own way.

ctx.s: 学校推行小班教学，就是为了更好地{因材施教}。
ctx.en: The school introduced small classes precisely so it could better teach each student according to their ability.

ctx.s: “为什么他的作业和我的不一样？”“老师这是在{因材施教}。”
ctx.en: "Why is his homework different from mine?" "The teacher is fitting the work to each of you."

ctx.s: 这位教练{因材施教}，给每个队员定了不同的训练计划。
ctx.en: The coach tailored his teaching to each player and gave everyone a different training plan.

ctx.s: 学习软件根据测试结果给每个人推荐不同的课程，也算是一种{因材施教}。
ctx.en: The learning app recommends different lessons to each user based on their test results, which is a kind of teaching to the individual.

bad.s: 这家餐厅{因材施教}，菜做得很好。
bad.en: (meant: the restaurant makes good use of its ingredients)
bad.why: The 'material' here is a person's talent: the idiom is only about teaching people, never about cooking or using ingredients.

bad.s: 我请了一位家教来{因材施教}我。
bad.en: (meant: I hired a tutor to teach me individually)
bad.why: It takes no direct object. Name the learner with a preposition instead: the tutor teaches 'towards me' (dui wo) according to my ability.

cards.mean: to tailor the remedy to the actual problem
cards.lit: to prescribe medicine that matches the illness

story.text: Two officials came to the physician Hua Tuo with the same complaint: headache and fever. He gave one a medicine to purge him and the other a medicine to make him sweat. When someone questioned the different treatments, Hua Tuo explained that the two illnesses had different causes, so they had to be treated differently. By the next morning both men were well.

use.how: Used as a predicate, often after 要, 才能 or 必须, about solving any problem by first finding its real cause: 找到原因才能对症下药。

near.diff: 因材施教 is about teaching people according to their ability; 对症下药 is about choosing a fix that matches the cause of a problem.

cards.cue: Sales fell because deliveries were slow, not because of price, so the manager fixes delivery instead of cutting prices.

ctx.s: 医生先给病人做了检查，然后{对症下药}。
ctx.en: The doctor examined the patient first and then prescribed the right treatment.

ctx.s: 想解决问题，先要找到原因，才能{对症下药}。
ctx.en: To solve a problem you must find its cause first; only then can you apply the right fix.

ctx.s: 你连问题出在哪儿都不知道，怎么{对症下药}？
ctx.en: You don't even know where the problem lies, so how can you find the right remedy?

ctx.s: 销量下降是因为送货太慢，我们应该{对症下药}，而不是一味打广告。
ctx.en: Sales dropped because delivery is too slow; we should fix that, not just keep advertising.

ctx.s: 市里针对堵车的主要原因{对症下药}，新开了几条公交线路。
ctx.en: The city targeted the main cause of the traffic jams and opened several new bus routes.

ctx.s: 这份报告分析得很透彻，提出的办法也称得上{对症下药}。
ctx.en: The report's analysis is thorough, and the measures it proposes really go to the root of the problem.

bad.s: 我感冒了，去药店{对症下药}了一盒感冒药。
bad.en: (meant: I went to the pharmacy and bought cold medicine)
bad.why: It does not mean buying medicine and takes no object; it means choosing a remedy that fits the cause.

bad.s: 这个方案{对症下药}，根本没解决问题。
bad.en: (meant: the plan missed the point and solved nothing)
bad.why: The idiom says the remedy fits the cause, so it contradicts 'solved nothing'. To say a plan misses the cause, negate it.

cards.mean: to pool everyone's ideas
cards.lit: to gather thoughts and widen the benefit

story.text: Zhuge Liang, chancellor of the state of Shu, wrote to his officials that the reason they shared in running the government was to gather the thoughts of many and widen the benefit of loyal advice. He asked them to speak up and argue with him whenever they disagreed, rather than simply going along.

use.how: Used as a predicate, usually with 大家 as subject, when a group is asked for suggestions: 我们开个会，大家集思广益。

near.diff: 群策群力 is everyone contributing both plans and effort to get something done; 集思广益 is gathering many people's ideas and advice.

cards.cue: The team is stuck on a name for a new product, so the boss calls everyone together to throw out suggestions.

ctx.s: 这个问题我一个人想不出来，大家{集思广益}吧。
ctx.en: I can't figure this out on my own; let's all put our heads together.

ctx.s: 公司开了个会，请员工{集思广益}，给新产品起名字。
ctx.en: The company held a meeting and asked staff to pool their ideas for naming the new product.

ctx.s: 我们设了一个意见箱，目的就是{集思广益}。
ctx.en: We set up a suggestion box precisely to gather everyone's ideas.

ctx.s: “下周的活动怎么安排？”“别急，周一开会，大家{集思广益}。”
ctx.en: "How should we plan next week's event?" "Don't worry, we'll meet on Monday and all chip in ideas."

ctx.s: 这份计划是全组{集思广益}的结果，不是哪一个人的功劳。
ctx.en: This plan came out of the whole group pooling its ideas; it isn't one person's credit.

ctx.s: 遇到难题时，{集思广益}往往比一个人苦想更有效。
ctx.en: When facing a hard problem, pooling ideas often works better than one person racking their brain.

bad.s: 我一个人在家{集思广益}，想了一个好办法。
bad.en: (meant: I thought hard by myself at home and came up with a good idea)
bad.why: It needs many people contributing ideas; one person thinking alone at home has nothing to pool.

bad.s: 他很{集思广益}，什么都知道。
bad.en: (meant: he is very knowledgeable)
bad.why: It is an action a group takes, not an adjective for a well-informed person, and it cannot follow 'very'.

cards.mean: knowing both oneself and one's opponent
cards.lit: know yourself, know the other side

story.text: In the chapter on planning attacks, Sun Tzu writes: if you know the enemy and know yourself, you will not be in danger in a hundred battles; if you know yourself but not the enemy, you will win one and lose one; if you know neither, you will be in danger in every battle. Sun Tzu's order is 'know the other, know yourself'; today the idiom usually puts oneself first and is quoted with 'not in danger in a hundred battles'.

use.how: Used as a predicate or quoted as advice before any contest, exam, negotiation or interview, often as 知己知彼，百战不殆.

near.diff: 有自知之明 is only knowing your own limits; 知己知彼 always involves a rival or opponent as well.

cards.cue: Before the final, the coach makes the team study both their own weak spots and the other side's match videos.

ctx.s: 比赛前先看看对手的录像，{知己知彼}嘛。
ctx.en: Watch the opponent's videos before the match; you need to know them as well as yourself.

ctx.s: {知己知彼}，百战不殆，谈判前一定要做好调查。
ctx.en: Know yourself and your opponent and you'll never be at risk; do your research before negotiating.

ctx.s: “你为什么一直在研究对手的价格？”“{知己知彼}才能赢啊。”
ctx.en: "Why do you keep studying your competitor's prices?" "You can only win if you know them and yourself."

ctx.s: 面试前，他既整理了自己的长处，也研究了这家公司，算是{知己知彼}。
ctx.en: Before the interview he listed his own strengths and researched the company, so he knew both sides.

ctx.s: 教练要求队员既分析自己的弱点，也研究对方的打法，做到{知己知彼}。
ctx.en: The coach had the players analyse their own weaknesses and study the other team's style, so they knew both.

ctx.s: 这本讲商业竞争的书，核心就是{知己知彼}这四个字。
ctx.en: This book on business competition comes down to four characters: know yourself and know your rival.

bad.s: 我们俩是{知己知彼}的好朋友。
bad.en: (meant: we are close friends who understand each other)
bad.why: Here zhiji is not the noun 'close friend' but 'know oneself'; the idiom is about knowing an opponent, not about friendship.

bad.s: 他很{知己知彼}，知道自己适合当老师。
bad.en: (meant: he is self-aware and knows he suits teaching)
bad.why: There is no rival here, and it is not an adjective after 'very'. Knowing only your own limits is a different idiom.

cards.mean: excusable given the circumstances
cards.lit: in the circumstances there is something that can be pardoned

use.how: Used as a predicate about a mistake or wrong act that has a mitigating reason: 迟到是不对，但情有可原。 It admits the act was wrong.

near.diff: 无可厚非 says something hardly deserves criticism at all; 情有可原 admits it was wrong but finds a reason to excuse it.

cards.cue: An employee missed a deadline, but only because his child was in hospital that week. How do you judge the lapse?

ctx.s: 他第一次做这种工作，出点错也{情有可原}。
ctx.en: It's his first time doing this kind of work, so a few mistakes are understandable.

ctx.s: 孩子是饿坏了才偷吃点心的，{情有可原}，别骂他了。
ctx.en: The child only sneaked the snacks because he was starving; it's forgivable, so don't scold him.

ctx.s: 迟到是不对，不过路上出了车祸，这就{情有可原}了。
ctx.en: Being late is wrong, but there was a car accident on the way, so it can be excused.

ctx.s: “她那天为什么发那么大的火？”“她刚失去亲人，{情有可原}。”
ctx.en: "Why did she lose her temper like that?" "She had just lost a family member; it's understandable."

ctx.s: 法官认为被告的行为{情有可原}，判得比较轻。
ctx.en: The judge found the defendant's actions excusable in the circumstances and gave a lighter sentence.

ctx.s: 新手犯错{情有可原}，可同样的错犯三次就说不过去了。
ctx.en: A beginner's mistake can be excused, but making the same one three times can't.

bad.s: 你帮了我这么大的忙，真是{情有可原}。
bad.en: (meant: you have been so kind to me)
bad.why: It excuses a wrong act; helping someone is not wrong and needs no excuse. Just thank the person.

bad.s: 老板{情有可原}了我的错误。
bad.en: (meant: the boss forgave my mistake)
bad.why: It is not a verb meaning 'forgive' and takes no object; it describes the wrong act itself as excusable.

cards.mean: the chief culprit
cards.lit: the chief of the crime, the head of the disaster

use.how: A noun, usually in ……是……的罪魁祸首. Said of a person or of a thing blamed for harm: 熬夜是失眠的罪魁祸首。 Light, joking use is common.

near.diff: 始作俑者 is whoever first started a bad practice that others followed; 罪魁祸首 is the main one to blame for a harm.

cards.cue: Every computer in the office crashed, and it turns out one virus-infected USB stick was behind it all. What was the stick?

ctx.s: 原来，打碎花瓶的{罪魁祸首}是家里的猫。
ctx.en: It turned out the culprit who broke the vase was our cat.

ctx.s: “谁把蛋糕吃光了？”“{罪魁祸首}就站在你面前。”
ctx.en: "Who ate all the cake?" "The guilty party is standing right in front of you."

ctx.s: 长期熬夜是他身体变差的{罪魁祸首}。
ctx.en: Staying up late night after night is the main reason his health got worse.

ctx.s: 专家指出，汽车尾气是城市空气污染的{罪魁祸首}之一。
ctx.en: Experts point out that car exhaust is one of the chief culprits behind urban air pollution.

ctx.s: 警方调查了一个月，终于抓到了这起诈骗案的{罪魁祸首}。
ctx.en: After a month of investigation, the police finally caught the mastermind of the fraud.

ctx.s: 公司亏损，大家都怪市场不好，其实管理混乱才是{罪魁祸首}。
ctx.en: Everyone blames the market for the company's losses, but chaotic management is the real culprit.

bad.s: 他是这次比赛的{罪魁祸首}，帮球队拿了冠军。
bad.en: (meant: he was the key player who won the title)
bad.why: It always assigns blame for harm, never credit. A player who won the title is a hero, not a culprit.

bad.s: 他{罪魁祸首}了这场事故。
bad.en: (meant: he caused this accident)
bad.why: It is a noun, not a verb. Say that he is the chief culprit of the accident, using the pattern shi ... de.

cards.mean: to put the trivial before the essential
cards.lit: to turn the root and the branch tips upside down

use.how: Used as a predicate, often after 就, 有点 or 这不是……吗, to criticise wrong priorities: 只顾装修不管产品，就本末倒置了。

near.diff: 舍本逐末 stresses abandoning the essential to chase the trivial; 本末倒置 stresses getting the order of importance backwards.
因小失大 is about a real loss caused by caring about something small; 本末倒置 is about misjudging what matters most.

cards.cue: A café spends its money on fancy decor and online ads while its coffee keeps getting worse.

ctx.s: 为了减肥连饭都不吃，把身体搞坏了，这就{本末倒置}了。
ctx.en: Skipping meals to lose weight until you ruin your health is getting your priorities backwards.

ctx.s: 他花一晚上装饰笔记本，却一个单词也没背，这不是{本末倒置}吗？
ctx.en: He spent the whole evening decorating his notebook and didn't learn a single word; isn't that backwards?

ctx.s: 开店最重要的是产品，装修只是陪衬，你却把装修当成重点，这就{本末倒置}了。
ctx.en: In running a shop the product matters most and the decor is secondary; treating the decor as the main thing gets it backwards.

ctx.s: 学车是为了安全驾驶，只想着背考题，有点{本末倒置}。
ctx.en: You learn to drive in order to drive safely; just memorising test answers is rather missing the point.

ctx.s: “我加班是为了让家人过得好。”“可你一年见不到孩子几次，不觉得{本末倒置}吗？”
ctx.en: "I work overtime for my family's sake." "But you barely see your kids all year; don't you think that's backwards?"

ctx.s: 这家公司把大部分预算花在宣传上，产品质量却越来越差，可谓{本末倒置}。
ctx.en: The company spends most of its budget on promotion while its products get worse; its priorities are upside down.

bad.s: 他把书架上的书都{本末倒置}了。
bad.en: (meant: he put the books on the shelf upside down)
bad.why: It is not about physically turning objects over; it criticises getting priorities in the wrong order.

bad.s: 这个故事的结局{本末倒置}，非常精彩。
bad.en: (meant: the story's ending had a brilliant twist)
bad.why: It criticises wrong priorities; it is not praise for a surprising plot reversal and cannot be called brilliant.

cards.mean: to lose something big for a small gain
cards.lit: because of the small, to lose the big

use.how: Used as a predicate, often as a warning (别因小失大) or a verdict after the loss (真是因小失大). Said of choices that save a little and cost a lot.

near.diff: 得不偿失 says the gain is worth less than the cost; 因小失大 says caring about a minor thing made you lose an important one.

cards.cue: To save a little on a cheap flight, she booked one that landed after her job interview had already begun.

ctx.s: 为了省一点钱买便宜的头盔，可别{因小失大}。
ctx.en: Don't buy a cheap helmet to save a little money and end up losing far more.

ctx.s: 做生意要看长远，不能为了眼前的小利{因小失大}。
ctx.en: In business you have to think long term, not lose something big for a quick small profit.

ctx.s: “这点小病不用去医院吧？”“拖久了可能更严重，别{因小失大}。”
ctx.en: "It's only a small illness, no need for the hospital, right?" "It could get worse if you wait; don't save a little trouble now and pay for it later."

ctx.s: 为了跟客户争几块钱的运费，他丢了整个订单，真是{因小失大}！
ctx.en: He argued with the client over a few yuan of shipping and lost the whole order. What a false economy!

ctx.s: 考试时他在一道小题上花了半小时，后面的大题都没做完，{因小失大}。
ctx.en: In the exam he spent half an hour on one small question and couldn't finish the big ones after it.

ctx.s: 他为了一点加班费天天熬夜，把最要紧的健康赔了进去，这是典型的{因小失大}。
ctx.en: He stayed up every night for a little overtime pay and sacrificed what matters most, his health: a classic case of losing much for little.

bad.s: 他从小职员一步步做到了总经理，真是{因小失大}。
bad.en: (meant: he rose from a junior clerk to general manager)
bad.why: It describes a loss caused by chasing a small gain, not rising step by step from a small post to a big one.

bad.s: 我们输了一场小组赛，却赢了总冠军，真是{因小失大}。
bad.en: (meant: we lost a small match but won the big title)
bad.why: This reverses it: the idiom means losing the big thing. Here you gained the big thing, so it does not fit.

cards.mean: having nothing to be ashamed of
cards.lit: to question one's heart and find no shame

use.how: Used as a predicate, mostly about oneself: 我问心无愧。 Said of one's conduct when facing doubt or a bad outcome; also 对……问心无愧.

near.diff: 心安理得 is simply feeling at ease, often said critically of someone who should not; 问心无愧 claims one truly did nothing wrong.

cards.cue: Accused of cheating, a student who really earned her grade says her conscience is completely clear.

ctx.s: 我已经尽了全力，结果怎样都{问心无愧}。
ctx.en: I have done my very best, so whatever the result, I have nothing to reproach myself for.

ctx.s: 别人怎么说我不管，我做事{问心无愧}。
ctx.en: I don't care what others say; my conscience is clear about how I act.

ctx.s: “你真的没动过那份文件？”“没有，我{问心无愧}。”
ctx.en: "You really didn't touch that file?" "No. My conscience is clear."

ctx.s: 做生意不骗人，虽然赚得少一点，但{问心无愧}。
ctx.en: If you don't cheat people in business you may earn a bit less, but your conscience is clear.

ctx.s: 当了三十年医生，她说自己对每个病人都{问心无愧}。
ctx.en: After thirty years as a doctor, she says she has nothing to be ashamed of towards any patient.

ctx.s: 项目虽然失败了，可他觉得自己每一步都{问心无愧}，并不后悔。
ctx.en: Although the project failed, he felt he had nothing to be ashamed of at any step and had no regrets.

bad.s: 他做了那么多坏事，却一点也{问心无愧}。
bad.en: (meant: he did so many bad things and felt no shame at all)
bad.why: The idiom means one really did nothing wrong. Someone at ease after doing wrong is shameless, which is a different idea.

bad.s: 这次考试我考了满分，太{问心无愧}了！
bad.en: (meant: I got full marks and I'm so proud!)
bad.why: It is about a clear conscience over one's conduct, not pride in a good result, and it does not take 'so very'.

cards.mean: shocking to see (damage, figures)
cards.lit: what meets the eye startles the heart

use.how: Used as a predicate or attributive (触目惊心的画面) to describe a disturbing sight: wounds, ruins, pollution, alarming figures. It describes the sight, not the person.

near.diff: 惊心动魄 is thrilling and heart-pounding, as in a match or adventure; 触目惊心 is a disturbing sight of damage or harm.

cards.cue: Volunteers arrive at a beach and find it buried under heaps of plastic waste and dead fish.

ctx.s: 地震过后，街道上一片废墟，{触目惊心}。
ctx.en: After the earthquake the streets were in ruins, a shocking sight.

ctx.s: 他腿上的伤口又深又长，看起来{触目惊心}。
ctx.en: The wound on his leg was deep and long, horrifying to look at.

ctx.s: “你看到那段车祸视频了吗？”“看了，真是{触目惊心}。”
ctx.en: "Did you see that car crash video?" "I did. It was really disturbing to watch."

ctx.s: 海滩上堆满了塑料垃圾，那画面让人{触目惊心}。
ctx.en: The beach was piled with plastic waste; the sight was shocking.

ctx.s: 报告中的数据{触目惊心}：每年都有大片森林消失。
ctx.en: The figures in the report are alarming: huge areas of forest disappear every year.

ctx.s: 这些照片记录了洪水过后的村庄，每一张都{触目惊心}。
ctx.en: These photos record the villages after the flood, and every one of them is distressing to see.

bad.s: 烟花太美了，让人{触目惊心}。
bad.en: (meant: the fireworks were stunningly beautiful)
bad.why: It is only for disturbing sights of harm or danger, never for something beautiful.

bad.s: 电话里听到这个消息，我{触目惊心}。
bad.en: (meant: I was shocked to hear the news on the phone)
bad.why: Its first half means 'meeting the eye', so it fits sights, not news heard; and it describes the sight, not the person.

cards.mean: deliberately alarmist talk
cards.lit: alarming words that make the listener start in fright

use.how: Predicate or after 是/不是, about what someone says or writes to scare people: 这不是危言耸听。 Often used to insist a warning is real.

near.diff: 杞人忧天 is worrying yourself about imaginary dangers; 危言耸听 is saying alarming things to frighten others.
大惊小怪 is overreacting to something ordinary; 危言耸听 is exaggerating a danger in words to alarm an audience.

cards.cue: A doctor warns that staying up every night really can damage your heart, and adds that she is not just trying to scare you.

ctx.s: 我说的都是真的，绝对不是{危言耸听}。
ctx.en: Everything I said is true; I'm absolutely not just trying to scare you.

ctx.s: 有些自媒体为了流量，故意{危言耸听}。
ctx.en: Some self-media accounts deliberately spread alarmist talk to get clicks.

ctx.s: 专家说这种说法纯属{危言耸听}，大家不必恐慌。
ctx.en: Experts say the claim is pure scaremongering and there is no need to panic.

ctx.s: “再不保护环境，后果不堪设想。”“你这是不是有点{危言耸听}了？”
ctx.en: "If we don't protect the environment, the consequences will be unthinkable." "Aren't you being a bit alarmist?"

ctx.s: 他的报告并非{危言耸听}，每个数字都有出处。
ctx.en: His report is not scaremongering; every figure has a source.

ctx.s: 那些{危言耸听}的保健广告，让不少老人花了冤枉钱。
ctx.en: Those alarmist health-product ads have made many elderly people waste their money.

bad.s: 老师的讲课很{危言耸听}，同学们都爱听。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher's lectures are gripping and everyone loves them)
bad.why: It is a criticism of scaring people with exaggerated warnings, not praise for exciting or captivating speech.

bad.s: 我一个人在家，越想越{危言耸听}，睡不着觉。
bad.en: (meant: alone at home, the more I thought the more frightened I got)
bad.why: It describes words said to alarm others, not a person's own feeling of fear.

cards.mean: influenced imperceptibly over time
cards.lit: to shift hidden from view and change in silence

story.text: In his family instructions, the sixth-century scholar Yan Zhitui warns his sons to choose their companions with care. A young person's character is not yet settled, he says; spending time with someone, laughing and talking with them, you take on their ways without meaning to learn anything, changing unnoticed until you naturally resemble them. His wording differs by one character from the idiom used today.

use.how: Adverbial with 地 before 影响/改变, or as the attributive 潜移默化的影响/作用. Said of slow influence from environment, people or culture.

near.diff: 耳濡目染 stresses picking something up by constantly seeing and hearing it; 潜移默化 stresses that the change happens unnoticed, and can describe the influence itself.

cards.cue: No one ever lectured her, but after years in a tidy dorm she gradually became tidy herself, without noticing when it happened.

ctx.s: 好的环境会{潜移默化}地影响孩子。
ctx.en: A good environment influences children gradually without their noticing.

ctx.s: 音乐对人的情绪有一种{潜移默化}的作用。
ctx.en: Music has a subtle, gradual effect on people's moods.

ctx.s: 他口音的变化是{潜移默化}的，连他自己都没有察觉。
ctx.en: The change in his accent happened so gradually that even he didn't notice it.

ctx.s: 父母的一言一行，都在{潜移默化}地塑造着孩子的性格。
ctx.en: Everything parents say and do is quietly shaping their child's character.

ctx.s: 你没发现吗？广告正在{潜移默化}地改变我们的消费习惯。
ctx.en: Haven't you noticed? Advertising is quietly changing our spending habits.

ctx.s: 传统文化的教育重在{潜移默化}，而不是死记硬背。
ctx.en: Teaching traditional culture relies on gradual influence, not rote memorisation.

bad.s: 他昨天突然{潜移默化}，变成了另一个人。
bad.en: (meant: yesterday he suddenly changed into a different person)
bad.why: The idiom means slow, unnoticed change over a long time; it cannot describe a sudden change.

bad.s: 我每天{潜移默化}地背五十个单词。
bad.en: (meant: I deliberately memorise fifty words every day)
bad.why: It is influence absorbed without effort or intent, not deliberate study done on purpose.

cards.mean: deep-rooted and hard to change
cards.lit: the roots are deep and the base of the fruit stalk is firm

story.text: The Daodejing speaks of the way to govern a state and keep it long: hold back and conserve, and you build up virtue. This, it says, is called making the roots deep and the base firm, the way of long life and lasting vision. The original has the two halves in a different order and spelling; later writers turned the image into this fixed phrase.

use.how: Predicate or attributive, mostly about ideas, habits, prejudices or traditions: 这种观念根深蒂固. Usually about something one wishes would change.

near.diff: 习以为常 is getting used to something until it seems normal; 根深蒂固 says a belief or habit is so entrenched it resists change.

cards.cue: Laws now treat sons and daughters equally, yet in some villages people still believe a family must have a son, and this view will not budge.

ctx.s: 这种老观念在他心里{根深蒂固}。
ctx.en: This old idea is deeply rooted in his mind.

ctx.s: 要改变{根深蒂固}的偏见，需要很长时间。
ctx.en: Changing deep-rooted prejudices takes a long time.

ctx.s: “重男轻女”的思想在一些地方依然{根深蒂固}。
ctx.en: The idea of valuing sons over daughters is still entrenched in some places.

ctx.s: 他晚睡的习惯已经{根深蒂固}，怎么劝都没用。
ctx.en: His habit of going to bed late is so ingrained that no amount of persuasion helps.

ctx.s: 为什么这些错误的说法会如此{根深蒂固}呢？
ctx.en: Why are these mistaken claims so firmly rooted?

ctx.s: 公司里{根深蒂固}的官僚作风，让新经理很头疼。
ctx.en: The entrenched bureaucratic style in the company gives the new manager a headache.

bad.s: 这棵小树刚种下，就已经{根深蒂固}了。
bad.en: (meant: the sapling has just been planted and its roots are already deep)
bad.why: It is figurative, used for ideas and habits; describing a real young tree this way is wrong, and 'just planted' contradicts 'deep'.

bad.s: 我对这个城市的印象{根深蒂固}，因为我昨天才来。
bad.en: (meant: my impression of the city is strong, because I only arrived yesterday)
bad.why: It needs something built up over a long time; a one-day-old impression cannot be deep-rooted.

cards.mean: so used to it that it seems normal
cards.lit: through habit, to take it as ordinary

use.how: Predicate, often with 早已/已经, or in 对……习以为常. Said of something once surprising or hard that has become routine.

near.diff: 根深蒂固 is an entrenched belief or habit that resists change; 习以为常 is no longer noticing or minding something because it happens so often.

cards.cue: When she first moved to the city the subway crowds shocked her; three years on, being squeezed in every morning no longer bothers her at all.

ctx.s: 他每天加班，家人早已{习以为常}。
ctx.en: He works overtime every day, and his family has long since got used to it.

ctx.s: 刚来时觉得这里太吵，现在已经{习以为常}了。
ctx.en: When I first came I thought it was too noisy here; now I'm used to it.

ctx.s: 对这种小事，大家都{习以为常}，没人在意。
ctx.en: Everyone is so used to such little things that no one cares.

ctx.s: 难道我们要对浪费粮食{习以为常}吗？
ctx.en: Are we really going to accept wasting food as normal?

ctx.s: 刚搬来时她很怕停电，住了半年也就{习以为常}了。
ctx.en: When she first moved there she dreaded the power cuts, but after half a year she got used to them.

ctx.s: “你不觉得冷吗？”“在东北长大，零下二十度我早就{习以为常}了。”
ctx.en: "Aren't you cold?" "I grew up in the Northeast; twenty below has long been normal for me."

bad.s: 他第一次坐飞机，就{习以为常}了。
bad.en: (meant: he took his first flight and found it normal)
bad.why: It needs repeated experience over time; nothing becomes habitual on the very first try.

bad.s: 我{习以为常}每天早上六点起床。
bad.en: (meant: I am in the habit of getting up at six every day)
bad.why: It does not take an object; use a plain verb meaning to be accustomed to, or put the thing before it.

cards.mean: absorbed through constant exposure
cards.lit: the ears are soaked and the eyes are dyed

use.how: Adverbial clause, often 从小耳濡目染, followed by what was learned. Said of skills, tastes or habits picked up from one's surroundings.

near.diff: 潜移默化 stresses unnoticed change and can name the influence itself; 耳濡目染 stresses learning by constantly seeing and hearing, usually from childhood.

cards.cue: Her parents ran a tea shop, and by watching and listening to them every day as a child she can tell good tea from bad without ever being taught.

ctx.s: 他爸爸是厨师，他从小{耳濡目染}，也会做菜。
ctx.en: His father is a chef; having watched him since childhood, he can cook too.

ctx.s: 爷爷天天听京剧，她{耳濡目染}，也成了小戏迷。
ctx.en: Her grandfather listened to Peking opera every day; hearing it all around her, she became a little fan too.

ctx.s: 孩子在父母天天吵架的家里{耳濡目染}，脾气也变得急躁。
ctx.en: Growing up in a home where his parents quarrelled every day, the child absorbed it and became short-tempered too.

ctx.s: 你没学过法律，怎么这么懂？是在家里{耳濡目染}的吧？
ctx.en: You never studied law, so how do you know so much? You must have picked it up at home.

ctx.s: 在茶乡长大的人，{耳濡目染}，个个都懂点茶。
ctx.en: People who grow up in tea country pick it up around them; every one knows something about tea.

ctx.s: 作家在书中回忆，正是童年的{耳濡目染}让他走上了写作之路。
ctx.en: The writer recalls in his book that it was what he absorbed as a child that set him on the path of writing.

bad.s: 我昨天在网上{耳濡目染}了一节语法课。
bad.en: (meant: I watched a grammar lesson online yesterday)
bad.why: It means absorbing something from long, constant exposure, not attending a single lesson; and it takes no object.

bad.s: 我很努力地{耳濡目染}，终于考上了大学。
bad.en: (meant: I studied hard and got into university)
bad.why: It describes learning that happens effortlessly from surroundings, not hard deliberate study.

cards.mean: to be together day in, day out
cards.lit: to be with each other morning and evening

use.how: Predicate or attributive (朝夕相处的同事), about people who live, work or study together for a long period.

near.diff: 形影不离 means always going everywhere together, a sign of closeness; 朝夕相处 just means sharing daily life over time, as roommates or colleagues do.

cards.cue: After four years sharing a dorm room, eating and studying side by side every day, two classmates have to say goodbye at graduation.

ctx.s: 我们在一个宿舍{朝夕相处}了四年。
ctx.en: We lived together in the same dorm, day in, day out, for four years.

ctx.s: 和{朝夕相处}的同事告别，心里很难受。
ctx.en: Saying goodbye to colleagues I saw every day was really hard.

ctx.s: {朝夕相处}久了，难免会有些小矛盾。
ctx.en: When you're together every day for a long time, small conflicts are inevitable.

ctx.s: 在训练营里，队员们{朝夕相处}，感情越来越深。
ctx.en: At the training camp, the team members spent every day together and grew ever closer.

ctx.s: 你跟他{朝夕相处}，怎么会不知道他生病了？
ctx.en: You're with him every single day; how could you not know he was ill?

ctx.s: 多年{朝夕相处}，这条老狗早已成了家里的一员。
ctx.en: After years of sharing our daily lives, the old dog has long since become one of the family.

bad.s: 我们在火车上{朝夕相处}了半个小时。
bad.en: (meant: we sat together on the train for half an hour)
bad.why: It means sharing daily life over a long time; half an hour together is far too short.

bad.s: 我每个月和他{朝夕相处}一次。
bad.en: (meant: I meet up with him once a month)
bad.why: Morning and evening means every day; occasional meetings contradict the idiom.

cards.mean: too eager for quick results
cards.lit: in a hurry to seek success

use.how: Predicate, often in advice: 不要急于求成, 学习不能急于求成. Criticises impatience for results in study, work or reform.

near.diff: 拔苗助长 is the harmful action of forcing growth and spoiling it; 急于求成 is the impatient attitude that may lead to it.
一蹴而就 says something gets done in one go (usually that it can't); 急于求成 criticises the person who wants quick results.

cards.cue: A beginner at the gym tells his coach he wants a six-pack within two weeks and plans to train four hours a day.

ctx.s: 学外语要慢慢来，不能{急于求成}。
ctx.en: Learning a foreign language takes time; you can't expect quick results.

ctx.s: 他太{急于求成}，结果练得受了伤。
ctx.en: He was too impatient for results and ended up injuring himself in training.

ctx.s: “我想一个月就减十公斤。”“别{急于求成}，对身体不好。”
ctx.en: "I want to lose ten kilos in a month." "Don't rush it, it's bad for your health."

ctx.s: 很多创业者失败，就是因为{急于求成}。
ctx.en: Many entrepreneurs fail precisely because they want results too fast.

ctx.s: 改革需要耐心，{急于求成}只会适得其反。
ctx.en: Reform requires patience; rushing for results will only backfire.

ctx.s: 你是不是有点{急于求成}了？才练了三天就想上台演出。
ctx.en: Aren't you rushing things a bit? You've practised for three days and already want to perform on stage.

bad.s: 他{急于求成}，很快就完成了任务，老板很满意。
bad.en: (meant: he worked fast, finished the task quickly and the boss was pleased)
bad.why: It is criticism of impatience, not praise for working efficiently.

bad.s: 火车快开了，我{急于求成}地跑向站台。
bad.en: (meant: the train was about to leave, so I hurried to the platform)
bad.why: It means being impatient for results in a long task, not physically hurrying to catch something.

cards.mean: duty-bound, one cannot refuse
cards.lit: duty does not allow one to decline

use.how: Predicate or in 义不容辞的责任/义务, usually said by someone accepting a task as their duty: 这是我义不容辞的责任。

cards.cue: Asked whether he'd mind helping evacuate flood victims from his own village, a young soldier says it is simply his duty and of course he'll go.

ctx.s: 帮助有困难的同学，是我们{义不容辞}的事。
ctx.en: Helping classmates in difficulty is something we can't refuse to do.

ctx.s: 家乡有难，我{义不容辞}，第一个报名当志愿者。
ctx.en: My hometown is in trouble; it's my duty, so I was the first to sign up as a volunteer.

ctx.s: 保护孩子的安全，是学校{义不容辞}的责任。
ctx.en: Keeping children safe is the school's bounden duty.

ctx.s: “这次救灾你愿意去吗？”“当然，{义不容辞}！”
ctx.en: "Are you willing to join the disaster relief this time?" "Of course, it's my duty!"

ctx.s: 作为医生，抢救病人是{义不容辞}的义务。
ctx.en: As a doctor, saving patients is an obligation you cannot refuse.

ctx.s: 老同学请他做婚礼证婚人，他觉得{义不容辞}，一口答应了。
ctx.en: When an old classmate asked him to officiate at the wedding, he felt it was his duty and agreed at once.

bad.s: 他请我吃饭，我{义不容辞}地拒绝了。
bad.en: (meant: he invited me to dinner and I firmly refused)
bad.why: It means one cannot refuse a duty; it cannot describe refusing anything, and a dinner invitation is not a duty.

bad.s: 老板让我加班，我{义不容辞}这个任务。
bad.en: (meant: the boss asked me to work late and I accepted the task)
bad.why: It takes no object, and it is for a moral duty, not routine overtime ordered by a boss.

cards.mean: wishing to help but unable to
cards.lit: loving him, yet no one can help

story.text: An ode in the Book of Songs praises Zhong Shanfu, a minister of King Xuan of Zhou. It says that virtue is light as a hair, yet few people can lift it; only Zhong Shanfu lifts it. The poet loves him for it but no one can help him. Its wording lacks one character of the idiom; from it comes the idiom, now said when you sympathise but cannot help.

use.how: Predicate, usually said by the speaker about themselves to decline politely: 这件事我爱莫能助。 Often with 实在, 只能.

near.diff: 无能为力 is plain powerlessness, about anything; 爱莫能助 adds that you sympathise and would like to help someone.
力不从心 is your ability failing your own aims; 爱莫能助 is being unable to help another person.

cards.cue: A friend asks you to get her son into your company, but hiring is not your decision, and you tell her, sorry, much as you'd like to, you can't.

ctx.s: 不是我不想帮你，这件事我实在{爱莫能助}。
ctx.en: It's not that I don't want to help; there's really nothing I can do about this.

ctx.s: 他想借钱，可我自己也没钱，只能{爱莫能助}。
ctx.en: He wanted to borrow money, but I'm broke myself, so I can only say I'm sorry I can't help.

ctx.s: “你能帮我改一下成绩吗？”“这不合规定，我{爱莫能助}。”
ctx.en: "Could you change my grade?" "That's against the rules; sorry, I can't help with that."

ctx.s: 我很同情他的遭遇，也很想拉他一把，可惜{爱莫能助}。
ctx.en: I feel for him and would love to give him a hand, but sadly I can't help.

ctx.s: 签证的事归大使馆管，我们学校也{爱莫能助}。
ctx.en: Visas are up to the embassy; much as we sympathise, our school can't help.

ctx.s: 他写信向老同学求助，对方回信说{爱莫能助}。
ctx.en: He wrote to an old classmate for help, and the reply said he regretted he could not help.

bad.s: 他病得很重，医生{爱莫能助}地治好了他。
bad.en: (meant: the doctor helped and cured him)
bad.why: It means one cannot help; it cannot go with actually helping or succeeding.

bad.s: 我自己做作业时，这道数学题太难，我{爱莫能助}。
bad.en: (meant: doing my own homework, this maths problem was too hard for me)
bad.why: It is about being unable to help another person; for your own inability say you cannot solve it.

cards.mean: one's ability falls short of one's wishes
cards.lit: strength does not follow the heart

use.how: Predicate, often with 感到/有些/越来越: 感到力不从心. Said of oneself or another, often because of age, illness or too much work.

near.diff: 爱莫能助 is being unable to help someone else; 力不从心 is your own strength or ability not matching what you want to do.
无能为力 says nothing can be done at all; 力不从心 says you want to and partly try, but your strength falls short.

cards.cue: Your grandmother still wants to tend her big vegetable garden, but at eighty-five her back can no longer manage the digging she loves.

ctx.s: 爷爷年纪大了，爬山时常常{力不从心}。
ctx.en: Grandpa is getting old; when he climbs hills, his body often can't do what he wants.

ctx.s: 一个人管三个部门，她越来越感到{力不从心}。
ctx.en: Managing three departments alone, she feels more and more that she can't cope.

ctx.s: 病好以后他想马上恢复跑步，可还是有些{力不从心}。
ctx.en: After recovering he wanted to start running again right away, but his body still couldn't quite manage it.

ctx.s: 老队长说，每天带队训练，他已经{力不从心}了。
ctx.en: The old captain said that leading training every day was now beyond his strength.

ctx.s: 你是不是觉得工作量太大，有些{力不从心}？
ctx.en: Do you feel the workload is too much and you're struggling to keep up?

ctx.s: 这家小公司想跟大企业竞争，难免{力不从心}。
ctx.en: This small company wants to compete with big firms, so it's bound to find itself out of its depth.

bad.s: 他不想学习，所以考试{力不从心}。
bad.en: (meant: he didn't want to study, so he did badly in the exam)
bad.why: It requires wanting to do something but lacking the ability; with no wish to do it, the idiom does not fit.

bad.s: 他力气很大，一个人就{力不从心}地把箱子搬上楼了。
bad.en: (meant: he is strong and carried the box upstairs effortlessly)
bad.why: It means strength falls short; it cannot describe managing something easily.

cards.mean: within one's power
cards.lit: what one's strength is able to reach

use.how: Mostly a modifier before 的 + noun: 做一些力所能及的事, 在力所能及的范围内. Describes tasks or help that someone can manage.

near.diff: 量力而行 is advice to act only as far as your strength allows; 力所能及 describes the tasks themselves as ones you can manage.

cards.cue: A parent says a seven-year-old is old enough to help with small chores, such as setting the table. What kind of chores are these?

ctx.s: 孩子大了，可以让他做一些{力所能及}的家务。
ctx.en: The child is older now; you can let him do some household chores he can manage.

ctx.s: 退休以后，我想在{力所能及}的范围内帮帮社区。
ctx.en: After I retire, I want to help the community as far as I am able.

ctx.s: 有什么{力所能及}的事，您尽管吩咐。
ctx.en: If there is anything I can do, just tell me.

ctx.s: 志愿者们为受灾群众提供了{力所能及}的帮助。
ctx.en: The volunteers gave the people hit by the disaster whatever help they could.

ctx.s: 老人虽然行动不便，还是坚持做{力所能及}的工作。
ctx.en: Although the old man has trouble getting around, he still insists on doing the work he can manage.

ctx.s: 公司要求每个员工在{力所能及}的前提下参与节能活动。
ctx.en: The company asks every employee to take part in the energy-saving campaign as far as they reasonably can.

bad.s: 这座山太高了，我们{力所能及}，还是别爬了。
bad.en: (meant: this is beyond our ability)
bad.why: It means something IS within your power; for what is beyond it, Chinese says li suo bu ji or li bu cong xin.

bad.s: 他{力所能及}地跑完了全程马拉松。
bad.en: (meant: he ran the whole marathon with all his might)
bad.why: It describes tasks within reach, not an all-out effort; for giving everything you have, use quan li yi fu.

cards.mean: to act within one's means
cards.lit: to measure one's strength and then act

story.text: The phrase comes from a comment in the Zuo Zhuan on Duke Zhuang of Zheng. After Zheng and its allies took the capital of the small state of Xu, the duke did not swallow Xu up but left a member of its ruling house in charge of its people. The chronicle praises him: he weighed his virtue before taking his place and measured his strength before acting.

use.how: A predicate, very often in advice after 要 or 应该: 运动要量力而行。 Said about spending, exercise, commitments and plans.

near.diff: 力所能及 describes tasks within your power; 量力而行 is the act or advice of not going beyond your strength or budget.

cards.cue: A friend just recovering from an injury wants to run ten kilometres on his first day back. What do you advise him?

ctx.s: 刚开始锻炼，一定要{量力而行}。
ctx.en: When you are just starting to exercise, you must not push beyond what your body can take.

ctx.s: 买房是大事，还是{量力而行}吧，别背太多贷款。
ctx.en: Buying a flat is a big deal; stay within your means and don't take on too much debt.

ctx.s: 医生说：“爬山可以，但要{量力而行}，累了就休息。”
ctx.en: The doctor said: "Hiking is fine, but don't overdo it; rest when you get tired."

ctx.s: 捐款完全自愿，大家{量力而行}就好。
ctx.en: Donations are entirely voluntary; everyone should just give what they can afford.

ctx.s: 他没有{量力而行}，一下子接了三个项目，结果都做砸了。
ctx.en: He did not know his limits, took on three projects at once, and botched them all.

ctx.s: 小公司扩张要{量力而行}，不能盲目追求规模。
ctx.en: A small company should expand only as far as its resources allow and not chase size blindly.

bad.s: 这次考试他{量力而行}，考了全班第一。
bad.en: (meant: he gave it everything and came first)
bad.why: It means holding back to stay within your limits; it does not mean trying your hardest.

bad.s: 这件事对我来说是{量力而行}的。
bad.en: (meant: this is within my ability)
bad.why: It is an action or advice, not a description of a task; for a task within your power, use li suo neng ji.

cards.mean: safe and sound
cards.lit: calm and secure, without any illness or harm (yang is an old word for illness or trouble)

use.how: A predicate, often after 都 or 依然: 所有乘客都安然无恙。 Said of people, animals or things that came through danger or a long absence unharmed.

near.diff: 平安无事 is simply that nothing went wrong; 安然无恙 stresses coming out unharmed despite a danger or accident.

cards.cue: A car rolls into a ditch, but the news says the driver climbed out without a scratch. How is the driver described?

ctx.s: 车翻了，幸好司机{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: The car overturned, but luckily the driver was unhurt.

ctx.s: 地震过后，他第一时间打电话确认家人{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: After the earthquake he immediately phoned to make sure his family were safe.

ctx.s: 走失了三天的小狗终于找到了，而且{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: The puppy that had been missing for three days was finally found, safe and sound.

ctx.s: “孩子们都没事吧？”“放心，都{安然无恙}。”
ctx.en: "Are the children all right?" "Don't worry, they're all safe and sound."

ctx.s: 大火烧毁了整栋楼，只有那幅古画{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: The fire destroyed the whole building; only the old painting survived undamaged.

ctx.s: 据报道，飞机紧急迫降，机上乘客全部{安然无恙}。
ctx.en: According to reports, the plane made an emergency landing and all the passengers on board were unharmed.

bad.s: 这家店的生意一直{安然无恙}，越来越红火。
bad.en: (meant: the shop's business has always gone well and keeps growing)
bad.why: It means coming through a danger or accident unharmed; it cannot describe a business doing well.

bad.s: 他今天心情{安然无恙}，一直在笑。
bad.en: (meant: he is in a calm, good mood today)
bad.why: It is about physical safety after danger, not about mood.

cards.mean: drenched in sweat
cards.lit: sweat flows until it soaks the back

story.text: In the Book of the Later Han, the young Emperor Xian, a puppet of the warlord Cao Cao, once told him to his face: if you will support me, be generous; if not, do me the kindness of letting me go. Cao Cao went pale and asked to leave, and when he came out his sweat had soaked through to his back. After that he never again dared to attend court audiences.

use.how: A predicate or after 得: 热得汗流浃背。 Mostly about heat or hard physical work; also, as in the old story, about fear or deep embarrassment.

near.diff: 挥汗如雨 pictures sweat wiped off like rain during hard toil; 汗流浃背 is soaked through, and can also come from fear or shame.

cards.cue: After carrying boxes up six floors in July with no lift, your T-shirt is stuck to your back. How do you look?

ctx.s: 天太热了，走了几步就{汗流浃背}。
