ctx.en: It was so hot that after a few steps I was dripping with sweat.

ctx.s: 搬家工人扛着冰箱上楼，累得{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: The movers carried the fridge upstairs and were soaked in sweat from the effort.

ctx.s: 你怎么{汗流浃背}的？是跑步回来的吗？
ctx.en: Why are you all sweaty? Did you run back?

ctx.s: 农民们顶着烈日在田里收麦子，个个{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: The farmers were harvesting wheat under the blazing sun, every one of them drenched in sweat.

ctx.s: 面试官的问题一个比一个难，他紧张得{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: The interviewer's questions got harder and harder; he was so nervous he broke out in a sweat.

ctx.s: 读完老师的批语，我惭愧得{汗流浃背}。
ctx.en: Reading the teacher's comments, I was so ashamed I broke into a cold sweat.

bad.s: 冬天的早上，他在外面冻得{汗流浃背}。
bad.en: (meant: he was shivering with cold outside on a winter morning)
bad.why: It means soaked in sweat from heat, exertion, fear or shame, never a reaction to cold.

bad.s: 下了一场大雨，他全身{汗流浃背}。
bad.en: (meant: he was soaked by the rain)
bad.why: It means wet with sweat only; being soaked by rain is hun shen shi tou.

cards.mean: the whole range of human emotions
cards.lit: joy, anger, sorrow and happiness

story.text: The four words appear together in the Doctrine of the Mean: when joy, anger, sorrow and happiness have not yet arisen, that is called balance; when they arise and each is in due measure, that is called harmony. From there the phrase came to stand for all human feelings.

use.how: A noun phrase, as subject or object: 人的喜怒哀乐, 分享喜怒哀乐, 喜怒哀乐都写在脸上. Covers all of someone's feelings, good and bad.

near.diff: 悲欢离合 is the ups and downs of life as people meet and part; 喜怒哀乐 is the emotions themselves, including anger.

cards.cue: An actor says his job is to show the audience every feeling a person can have, from rage to delight. What does he show?

ctx.s: 他是个直性子，{喜怒哀乐}全写在脸上。
ctx.en: He is a straightforward person; every feeling he has shows on his face.

ctx.s: 好朋友就是能分享彼此{喜怒哀乐}的人。
ctx.en: Good friends are people who share each other's ups and downs.

ctx.s: 这部小说写尽了普通人的{喜怒哀乐}。
ctx.en: This novel captures every joy and sorrow of ordinary people.

ctx.s: 当演员，就要学会表达各种{喜怒哀乐}。
ctx.en: To be an actor, you have to learn to express every kind of emotion.

ctx.s: 小猫也有自己的{喜怒哀乐}吗？
ctx.en: Do cats have their own emotions too?

ctx.s: 她在日记里记录着这些年的{喜怒哀乐}。
ctx.en: In her diary she recorded all her feelings over these years.

bad.s: 听到这个好消息，大家都很{喜怒哀乐}。
bad.en: (meant: everyone was very happy)
bad.why: It is a noun naming all emotions together, not an adjective, and it does not mean only happy.

bad.s: 他是个{喜怒哀乐}的人，动不动就发脾气。
bad.en: (meant: he is a moody person who flares up easily)
bad.why: It names all feelings as a noun and cannot describe a moody person; for that, Chinese says xi nu wu chang.

cards.mean: the joys and sorrows of meeting and parting
cards.lit: sorrow and joy, parting and reunion

story.text: The phrase is best known from Su Shi's Mid-Autumn poem of 1076, written after a night of drinking while he missed his younger brother Su Zhe, whom he had not seen for years: people have sorrow and joy, parting and reunion; the moon is dim or bright, full or waning; this has never been perfect since ancient times. He ends by wishing they may both live long and share the moon's beauty though a thousand miles apart.
story.source: 苏轼《水调歌头·明月几时有》

use.how: A noun phrase, often object of 经历 or 看尽, or after 人生的: 人生的悲欢离合. Said of lives, families and stories with partings and reunions.

near.diff: 喜怒哀乐 is the feelings themselves; 悲欢离合 is the events of life, separations and reunions, with the sorrow and joy they bring.

cards.cue: A family saga follows relatives scattered by war, some lost for decades, some reunited in old age. What does it portray?

ctx.s: 这部电视剧讲的是一个大家庭的{悲欢离合}。
ctx.en: This TV series tells of the partings and reunions, sorrows and joys, of a big family.

ctx.s: 在火车站工作了三十年，他看尽了人间的{悲欢离合}。
ctx.en: Having worked at the railway station for thirty years, he has seen every kind of farewell and reunion.

ctx.s: 人生总有{悲欢离合}，别太难过了。
ctx.en: Life always has its partings and reunions; don't be too sad.

ctx.s: 奶奶给我讲了她年轻时经历的{悲欢离合}。
ctx.en: Grandma told me about the separations and reunions she went through when she was young.

ctx.s: 中秋夜读苏轼的词，更能体会{悲欢离合}的滋味。
ctx.en: Reading Su Shi's poem on Mid-Autumn night, you feel more deeply what parting and reunion mean.

ctx.s: 这本书通过两兄弟的{悲欢离合}，写出了一个时代的变迁。
ctx.en: Through the separations and reunions of two brothers, the book portrays the changes of an era.

bad.s: 他今天{悲欢离合}，一会儿笑一会儿哭。
bad.en: (meant: his mood keeps swinging today)
bad.why: It is about the course of a life, meetings and partings, not mood swings within a day.

bad.s: 我们公司下午开会讨论了很多{悲欢离合}。
bad.en: (meant: we discussed many ups and downs)
bad.why: It is about people being separated and reunited, out of place for the ups and downs of a business.

cards.mean: still wanting more
cards.lit: the interest has still not run out

use.how: A predicate or adverbial, often with 让人, 觉得 or 大家: 听完还意犹未尽。 Said after something enjoyable ends while people still want more.

near.diff: 流连忘返 is lingering in a pleasant place and not wanting to leave; 意犹未尽 is the feeling, after anything enjoyable ends, of wanting more.

cards.cue: The concert is over and the lights are on, but the audience keeps clapping for another song. How do they feel?

ctx.s: 电影结束了，大家还{意犹未尽}。
ctx.en: The film was over, but everyone still wanted more.

ctx.s: 这本小说太好看了，读完让人{意犹未尽}。
ctx.en: This novel is so good that when you finish it you're left wanting more.

ctx.s: 讲座已经超时了，同学们却{意犹未尽}，围着教授继续提问。
ctx.en: The lecture had already run over, but the students still wanted more and gathered round the professor with questions.

ctx.s: 你看起来还{意犹未尽}啊，要不要再玩一局？
ctx.en: You look like you could keep going. Shall we play another round?

ctx.s: 老朋友聊到半夜，仍然{意犹未尽}，约好周末再聚。
ctx.en: The old friends talked until midnight and still had more to say, so they agreed to meet again at the weekend.

ctx.s: 比赛在高潮中结束，现场观众{意犹未尽}，久久不肯离场。
ctx.en: The match ended at its high point; the crowd wanted more and would not leave for a long time.

bad.s: 这部电影太无聊了，看得我{意犹未尽}。
bad.en: (meant: I couldn't wait for it to end)
bad.why: It means you enjoyed something and wanted more, the opposite of boredom.

bad.s: 他的作业还{意犹未尽}，明天再交。
bad.en: (meant: his homework is not finished yet)
bad.why: It is about lingering enjoyment, not an unfinished task; for that, simply say the homework is not done yet.

cards.mean: love me, love my dog
cards.lit: loving a house extends even to the crows on its roof

story.text: After King Wu of Zhou defeated the last Shang king, he asked Jiang Taigong what to do with the conquered Shang soldiers. Taigong answered that when you love a man you love even the crow on his roof, and when you do not, you hate everything of his, so they should all be killed. The king turned to other advisers and in the end followed the gentler counsel of the Duke of Zhou. The image of the crow became the idiom.

use.how: A predicate, often explaining a reason: 他是爱屋及乌. Said when fondness for a person spreads to things or people connected with them.

near.diff: 情有独钟 is a special love for one thing in itself; 爱屋及乌 is liking something only because it belongs to someone you love.

cards.cue: She never liked football, but since dating a keen fan she follows his team and even wears its scarf. Why?

ctx.s: 他喜欢女朋友，{爱屋及乌}，连她的猫也宠着。
ctx.en: He loves his girlfriend, and that extends even to her cat, which he spoils.

ctx.s: 奶奶疼孙子，{爱屋及乌}，对孙子的同学也特别热情。
ctx.en: Grandma dotes on her grandson, so she is especially warm to his classmates too.

ctx.s: 因为喜欢这位作家，我{爱屋及乌}，去了他的家乡旅游。
ctx.en: Because I love this writer, I even took a trip to his home town.

ctx.s: 你对我弟弟这么好，是不是{爱屋及乌}啊？
ctx.en: You're so nice to my little brother. Is it because of me?

ctx.s: 很多球迷{爱屋及乌}，连球星代言的饮料都买。
ctx.en: Many fans extend their love to everything around their idol, even buying the drinks the star advertises.

ctx.s: 岳父母对女婿好，往往是{爱屋及乌}，因为疼爱女儿。
ctx.en: Parents-in-law who are good to a son-in-law often do it for their daughter's sake.

bad.s: 他特别爱自己的房子，真是{爱屋及乌}。
bad.en: (meant: he really loves his house)
bad.why: The house is only the image; it means love for a person spreading to what is theirs.

bad.s: 我从小就{爱屋及乌}，最喜欢画画。
bad.en: (meant: I have loved painting since childhood)
bad.why: Love for one thing in itself is qing you du zhong; this idiom needs a person whose belongings you love.

cards.mean: to have a special fondness for one thing
cards.lit: one's feelings gather on one thing alone

use.how: Usually 对……情有独钟: 他对老电影情有独钟。 Said of a lasting preference for one thing, place, style or person over others.

near.diff: 爱屋及乌 is liking something because of someone you love; 情有独钟 is loving one thing for itself, more than all others.

cards.cue: Your friend has tried every kind of tea, yet for twenty years she has drunk only one green tea from her home province. How would you put it?

ctx.s: 我对川菜{情有独钟}，每周都要吃一次。
ctx.en: I have a soft spot for Sichuan food; I have to eat it once a week.

ctx.s: 他走过很多城市，却唯独对杭州{情有独钟}。
ctx.en: He has been to many cities, but Hangzhou is the one he loves above all.

ctx.s: 你为什么对这个牌子的手表{情有独钟}？
ctx.en: Why are you so attached to this brand of watch?

ctx.s: 不少年轻人对复古风格的衣服{情有独钟}。
ctx.en: Quite a few young people have a special fondness for vintage-style clothes.

ctx.s: 在所有乐器中，她对钢琴{情有独钟}。
ctx.en: Of all instruments, the piano is the one she loves most.

ctx.s: 这位导演对小人物的故事一直{情有独钟}。
ctx.en: This director has always had a special interest in stories about ordinary people.

bad.s: 他对所有运动都{情有独钟}。
bad.en: (meant: he loves all sports)
bad.why: Du means one alone: it singles out one favourite, so it cannot apply to everything.

bad.s: 我昨天{情有独钟}地吃了一碗面。
bad.en: (meant: I enjoyed a bowl of noodles yesterday)
bad.why: It is a lasting preference, used in the pattern dui ... qing you du zhong, not a way of doing a one-off action.

cards.mean: longing to get home as fast as possible
cards.lit: the heart set on returning is like an arrow

use.how: A predicate, often after 早已 or 个个: 春节快到了，大家都归心似箭。 Said of people away from home, typically before holidays or at the end of a long trip.

near.diff: 迫不及待 is impatience for anything at all; 归心似箭 is specifically the eagerness to get back home.

cards.cue: A migrant worker who has not seen his family all year packs his bag a week before the Spring Festival train leaves. How does he feel?

ctx.s: 快过年了，在外打工的人都{归心似箭}。
ctx.en: New Year is nearly here, and everyone working away from home is longing to get back.

ctx.s: 出差一个月，我早就{归心似箭}了。
ctx.en: I've been on a business trip for a month; I've long been desperate to get home.

ctx.s: 毕业典礼一结束，留学多年的她就{归心似箭}，订了最早的航班。
ctx.en: As soon as the graduation ceremony was over, she, after years of studying abroad, was desperate to get home and booked the earliest flight.

ctx.s: “下班了还不走？”“走！老婆孩子在等我，我{归心似箭}啊。”
ctx.en: "Not leaving yet?" "I'm off! My wife and kids are waiting; I can't get home fast enough."

ctx.s: 春运期间，火车站里挤满了{归心似箭}的旅客。
ctx.en: During the Spring Festival travel rush, the stations are packed with travellers eager to get home.

ctx.s: 战士们完成任务，{归心似箭}，连夜往回赶。
ctx.en: The soldiers finished their mission and, eager to return, hurried back through the night.

bad.s: 他{归心似箭}，想快点出国旅游。
bad.en: (meant: he can't wait to travel abroad)
bad.why: It is eagerness to return home, not to leave for somewhere new.

bad.s: 这支箭飞得{归心似箭}，一下就射中了靶心。
bad.en: (meant: the arrow flew very fast)
bad.why: The arrow is only a comparison for a homesick heart; it does not describe real speed.

cards.mean: forced to leave one's hometown
cards.lit: to turn one's back on the village well and leave one's native place

use.how: Predicate or attributive (背井离乡的打工者). Said with sympathy of people who leave home for a long time out of hardship: work, war, famine.

near.diff: 流离失所 stresses being homeless and drifting with nowhere to live; 背井离乡 stresses having left one's home region far behind.

cards.cue: Floods ruined the farms, and whole families had to leave their native village to look for work in distant cities. What did they have to do?

ctx.s: 为了给家里挣钱，他十八岁就{背井离乡}，到南方打工。
ctx.en: To earn money for his family, he left home at eighteen to work in the south.

ctx.s: 战争让成千上万的人{背井离乡}，失去了家园。
ctx.en: The war drove tens of thousands of people from their homeland and left them without homes.

ctx.s: 奶奶常说：“当年{背井离乡}的滋味，我这辈子都忘不了。”
ctx.en: Grandma often says: "I'll never forget what it felt like to leave home back then."

ctx.s: 这部电影讲的是一群{背井离乡}的年轻人在大城市奋斗的故事。
ctx.en: The film tells the story of a group of young people far from home, struggling to make it in a big city.

ctx.s: 你一个人在外地工作，{背井离乡}的，过年总该回家看看吧？
ctx.en: You're working alone so far from home; surely you'll come back for the New Year?

ctx.s: 那年大旱，村里许多人家不得不{背井离乡}，外出谋生。
ctx.en: That year of the great drought, many families in the village had to leave home to make a living elsewhere.

bad.s: 暑假我们全家{背井离乡}，去海边玩了一个星期。
bad.en: (meant: in the summer holidays our family went to the seaside for a week)
bad.why: It describes leaving one's home region for a long time out of hardship, not a holiday trip.

bad.s: 他从城东搬到城西，算是{背井离乡}了。
bad.en: (meant: he moved from the east of the city to the west)
bad.why: Moving across town is not leaving one's native place; the idiom implies going far away, usually under pressure.

cards.mean: a beloved daughter
cards.lit: a bright pearl held in the palm of the hand

story.text: The image goes back to the poem 'Short Song' by Fu Xuan of the Western Jin dynasty, in which a woman abandoned by the man she loved laments that he once looked on her like a pearl in his palm and has now thrown her away into a ditch. Later the pearl in the palm came to mean a much-loved child, above all a daughter.

use.how: A noun, object of 是, 当作 or 视为: 她是父母的掌上明珠。 Said affectionately of a daughter cherished by her parents.

near.diff: 心肝宝贝 is colloquial and used for any dearly loved person or child; 掌上明珠 is more literary and almost always a daughter.

cards.cue: An only daughter whose parents adore her, keep her photo on every desk and would do anything for her. What is she to them?

ctx.s: 小雨是家里的独生女，从小就是父母的{掌上明珠}。
ctx.en: Xiaoyu is an only daughter and has been her parents' darling since she was little.

ctx.s: 老王把女儿视为{掌上明珠}，什么事都依着她。
ctx.en: Old Wang treasures his daughter and gives in to her on everything.

ctx.s: “你可是我们的{掌上明珠}，出国留学一定要照顾好自己。”妈妈叮嘱道。
ctx.en: "You're our precious girl; take good care of yourself while you study abroad," her mother urged.

ctx.s: 婚礼上，新娘的父亲红着眼眶说：“今天我把{掌上明珠}交给你了。”
ctx.en: At the wedding the bride's father said, eyes red: "Today I'm handing you my precious daughter."

ctx.s: 她虽是富商的{掌上明珠}，却一点也不娇气。
ctx.en: Although she is a rich businessman's beloved daughter, she isn't spoiled at all.

ctx.s: 谁不知道这个小姑娘是全家的{掌上明珠}？
ctx.en: Who doesn't know that this little girl is the darling of the whole family?

bad.s: 我的{掌上明珠}摔坏了，得拿去修。
bad.en: (meant: my treasured phone got broken and needs repairing)
bad.why: It is said of a cherished daughter, not of a prized possession.

bad.s: 父母很{掌上明珠}她。
bad.en: (meant: her parents cherish her very much)
bad.why: It is a noun, not a verb: a daughter can be her parents' pearl, but parents cannot 'pearl' her.

cards.mean: pampered and spoiled since childhood
cards.lit: born delicate and brought up indulged

use.how: Predicate or attributive (娇生惯养的孩子). Said of how a person was raised, criticising the softness or helplessness that results.

near.diff: 养尊处优 is an adult living in comfort thanks to status or wealth; 娇生惯养 is about being spoiled while growing up.

cards.cue: A twenty-year-old has never cooked, washed his own clothes or carried his own bags, because his parents always did everything for him. How was he raised?

ctx.s: 他从小{娇生惯养}，连袜子都没自己洗过。
ctx.en: He was pampered from childhood and has never even washed his own socks.

ctx.s: 别看她是{娇生惯养}长大的，干起活来一点也不怕苦。
ctx.en: She may have been raised pampered, but when she works she doesn't shy away from hardship at all.

ctx.s: 老师对家长说：“孩子不能太{娇生惯养}，该做的家务要让他自己做。”
ctx.en: The teacher told the parents: "Don't spoil the child too much; let him do the chores he should do."

ctx.s: 不少{娇生惯养}的城市孩子，第一次参加夏令营就哭着要回家。
ctx.en: Quite a few pampered city kids cry to go home at their first summer camp.

ctx.s: 你都三十岁了，还这么{娇生惯养}，以后怎么独立生活？
ctx.en: You're thirty and still so spoiled; how will you ever live on your own?

ctx.s: 小说里的大少爷{娇生惯养}，家道中落后吃尽了苦头。
ctx.en: The young master in the novel was raised in luxury, and suffered terribly once the family fortune collapsed.

bad.s: 我奶奶对花草{娇生惯养}，每天浇水三次。
bad.en: (meant: my grandma lovingly cares for her plants)
bad.why: It describes a person who was spoiled growing up, not someone caring for something.

bad.s: 这位老师{娇生惯养}学生，大家都很喜欢他。
bad.en: (meant: this teacher is very kind to his students)
bad.why: It takes no object and is criticism of the spoiled person, not praise of a kind giver.

cards.mean: a platitude, the same old advice
cards.lit: the everyday talk of an old scholar

story.text: In the Three Kingdoms period the powerful minister He Yan asked the diviner Guan Lu to read his fortune. Guan Lu warned him to be humble and cautious if he wished to escape disaster. Deng Yang, who was with them, scoffed that this was only the everyday talk of an old scholar. Not long afterwards both He Yan and Deng Yang were put to death.

use.how: A noun, often after 是 or in 虽然是老生常谈，但…. Said of advice or views everyone has heard many times; often used modestly about one's own reminder.

near.diff: 陈词滥调 is stale, empty phrasing and is harsher; 老生常谈 is familiar, often-repeated advice that may still be true.

cards.cue: Before every exam your father repeats the same advice: sleep early, read each question twice. You have heard it a hundred times. What is his advice?

ctx.s: 妈妈又开始讲“早睡早起身体好”，这都是{老生常谈}了。
ctx.en: Mum is on about "early to bed, early to rise" again; we've heard it all before.

ctx.s: 虽然是{老生常谈}，但我还是要提醒大家：出门注意安全。
ctx.en: It may be the same old advice, but I still have to remind everyone: stay safe when you go out.

ctx.s: “多读书、多练习”听起来像{老生常谈}，其实是学语言最有效的办法。
ctx.en: "Read more, practise more" sounds like a platitude, but it's actually the most effective way to learn a language.

ctx.s: 每次开会，经理强调的都是“注意安全、按时交货”这些{老生常谈}，可大家都知道这很重要。
ctx.en: At every meeting the manager stresses the same familiar points, "safety first, deliver on time", yet everyone knows they matter.

ctx.s: 你说的这些{老生常谈}，我耳朵都快听出茧子了。
ctx.en: I've heard these same old lines of yours so often my ears are practically calloused.

ctx.s: 他的发言都是{老生常谈}吗？不，最后那个建议还挺新鲜的。
ctx.en: Was his speech all platitudes? No, that last suggestion was actually quite fresh.

bad.s: 我们俩是{老生常谈}的朋友，认识二十年了。
bad.en: (meant: we are old friends who often chat; we've known each other twenty years)
bad.why: It means familiar, often-repeated words, not a long friendship or chatting often.

bad.s: 这位老教授讲课很新颖，真是{老生常谈}。
bad.en: (meant: the old professor teaches in a fresh way)
bad.why: It says the words are stale and familiar; it cannot praise an old person's fresh ideas.

cards.mean: ingenious, coming up with something original
cards.lit: to bring out a design of one's own mind, different from everyone else's

use.how: Predicate, or adverbial with 地: 他别出心裁地…. Praises a design, plan or idea that is original and clever.

near.diff: 标新立异 is being different on purpose, often a criticism of showing off; 别出心裁 praises a genuinely clever original idea.

cards.cue: Instead of a normal menu, a café prints its dishes on old record sleeves, and every customer remarks on how clever and unusual the idea is. How is it?

ctx.s: 这家咖啡馆的装修{别出心裁}，墙上挂满了旧唱片。
ctx.en: This café's decor is wonderfully original; the walls are covered with old records.

ctx.s: 他{别出心裁}地用折纸做了一张生日贺卡。
ctx.en: He had the clever idea of making a birthday card out of origami.

ctx.s: “谁想出来的这个包装？真是{别出心裁}！”
ctx.en: "Who came up with this packaging? What an original idea!"

ctx.s: 老师{别出心裁}，让学生用演话剧的方式复习课文。
ctx.en: The teacher had an inventive idea: the students reviewed the lesson by acting it out as a play.

ctx.s: 今年的晚会开场{别出心裁}，观众都很惊喜。
ctx.en: This year's gala opened in a highly original way, and the audience was delighted.

ctx.s: 这次设计比赛，评委最看重的就是作品是否{别出心裁}。
ctx.en: In this design contest, what the judges value most is whether an entry is original.

bad.s: 他{别出心裁}地抄了别人的作业。
bad.en: (meant: he cleverly copied someone else's homework)
bad.why: It praises original creativity; copying is the opposite, and it is never used for cheating.

bad.s: 这个人很{别出心裁}，总想骗别人的钱。
bad.en: (meant: this person is crafty and always trying to cheat people)
bad.why: It praises inventive ideas, not scheming; it can never describe someone out to cheat others.

cards.mean: with an ulterior motive
cards.lit: to have some other purpose in one's mind

use.how: Predicate or attributive (别有用心的人). Accuses someone of hiding a selfish or harmful purpose behind what they say or do.

near.diff: 居心叵测 is darker and more formal: intentions too sinister to fathom; 别有用心 is simply a hidden motive behind an act.

cards.cue: A stranger keeps offering to help you invest your savings and asks for your bank details. You suspect a hidden purpose. How would you describe him?

ctx.s: 他突然对我这么热情，我总觉得他{别有用心}。
ctx.en: He's suddenly so warm towards me; I can't help feeling he's up to something.

ctx.s: 有些{别有用心}的商家，故意夸大产品的效果。
ctx.en: Some unscrupulous sellers deliberately exaggerate what their products can do.

ctx.s: “你别把我想得那么坏，我帮你真的不是{别有用心}。”
ctx.en: "Don't think so badly of me; I'm really not helping you for some ulterior motive."

ctx.s: 这条谣言显然是有人{别有用心}地编造出来的。
ctx.en: This rumour was clearly made up by someone with an agenda.

ctx.s: 她问了我好多公司的事，是好奇，还是{别有用心}？
ctx.en: She asked me so much about the company; was she just curious, or did she have a motive?

ctx.s: 网上那些“免费领奖”的链接，往往是{别有用心}的人设下的陷阱。
ctx.en: Those "claim your free prize" links online are often traps set by people with bad intentions.

bad.s: 妈妈{别有用心}地给我做了一桌好菜，庆祝我考上大学。
bad.en: (meant: mum lovingly cooked a feast to celebrate my getting into university)
bad.why: It implies a hidden selfish motive, which insults a mother's loving effort; it is never used for sincere care.

bad.s: 这个设计{别有用心}，非常有创意。
bad.en: (meant: this design is original and creative)
bad.why: It accuses someone of a hidden motive; it cannot praise a design for being original.

cards.mean: having put much careful thought into it for another's sake
cards.lit: the intention is deep and the care painstaking

use.how: Predicate, often in 真是用心良苦 or 可谓用心良苦, or as a noun (…的用心良苦). Said of someone whose careful, often unnoticed effort was for another's good.

near.diff: 煞费苦心 only says someone went to great pains, for any end, even a bad one; 用心良苦 implies the care was well meant for others.

cards.cue: Your coach was harsh on you all season, and only after you won the final did you realise he had done it all to make you stronger. How were his efforts?

ctx.s: 爸爸不让你玩手机，是怕你耽误学习，真是{用心良苦}。
ctx.en: Dad won't let you play on your phone because he's afraid it'll hurt your studies; he really means well.

ctx.s: 长大以后，我才明白妈妈当年的{用心良苦}。
ctx.en: Only after growing up did I understand how much thought my mother put into everything back then.

ctx.s: 老师故意给他打低分，原来是想激励他，可谓{用心良苦}。
ctx.en: The teacher gave him a low mark on purpose to spur him on; it was all for his sake.

ctx.s: “你知道教练为什么天天骂你吗？他是{用心良苦}啊！”
ctx.en: "Do you know why the coach yells at you every day? It's all for your own good!"

ctx.s: 这本教材故意不给答案，编者{用心良苦}，是想让学生自己思考。
ctx.en: This textbook deliberately gives no answers; the editors mean well: they want the students to think for themselves.

ctx.s: 这部电影的结局让人心酸，导演{用心良苦}，就是想让观众珍惜身边的人。
ctx.en: The film's ending is heartbreaking, but the director meant it for the audience's good: to make them cherish the people around them.

bad.s: 小偷{用心良苦}地研究了这家银行的监控。
bad.en: (meant: the thief carefully studied the bank's cameras)
bad.why: It implies good intentions towards someone else, so it cannot describe a criminal's careful scheming.

bad.s: 我这次考试{用心良苦}，终于考了满分。
bad.en: (meant: I worked hard for this exam and finally got full marks)
bad.why: It is about care taken for another person's sake, not about one's own hard work for one's own goal.

cards.mean: only human, natural for anyone
cards.lit: the ordinary feelings of people

use.how: A noun, usually after 是 or 也是: 紧张是人之常情。 Said to explain or excuse a feeling or reaction anyone would have.

near.diff: 理所当然 is anything that obviously should be so; 人之常情 is specifically a natural human feeling or reaction.

cards.cue: A friend is embarrassed that she cried at her farewell party after ten years at the company. You tell her anyone would feel the same. What is crying, you say?

ctx.s: 第一次上台紧张，这是{人之常情}。
ctx.en: Being nervous the first time you go on stage is only human.

ctx.s: 想家是{人之常情}，你不用不好意思。
ctx.en: Being homesick is perfectly natural; no need to be embarrassed.

ctx.s: “他失业了心情不好，也是{人之常情}，你多体谅他吧。”
ctx.en: "He's lost his job, so of course he's in a bad mood; try to be understanding."

ctx.s: 孩子考砸了，父母一时生气也是{人之常情}，过后好好谈谈就行。
ctx.en: When a child fails an exam, it's only human for the parents to get angry for a moment; just talk it over calmly afterwards.

ctx.s: 喜欢听好话是{人之常情}，但也要听得进批评。
ctx.en: Everyone likes to hear compliments, but you also have to be able to take criticism.

ctx.s: 难道希望家人平安不是{人之常情}吗？
ctx.en: Isn't wanting your family to be safe the most natural thing in the world?

bad.s: 太阳从东边升起是{人之常情}。
bad.en: (meant: it's natural and obvious that the sun rises in the east)
bad.why: It is about human feelings and reactions, not facts of nature like the sunrise.

bad.s: 他是个很{人之常情}的人，大家都喜欢他。
bad.en: (meant: he is a very warm, human person)
bad.why: It names a natural reaction, not a trait; it cannot describe a person's character or be modified by 'very'.

cards.mean: attracting worldwide attention
cards.lit: the whole world fixes its eyes on it

use.how: Mostly attributive (举世瞩目的成就) or predicate. Used in news and formal writing of events and achievements the whole world watches.

near.diff: 举世闻名 is being famous all over the world; 举世瞩目 is drawing the world's attention, usually to an event or achievement now.

cards.cue: Billions of people on every continent are glued to their screens for the first crewed landing on Mars. What kind of event is it?

ctx.s: 奥运会开幕式是一场{举世瞩目}的盛会。
ctx.en: The Olympic opening ceremony is a grand event the whole world watches.

ctx.s: 这项登月计划取得了{举世瞩目}的成功。
ctx.en: The moon-landing programme achieved a success that drew attention around the world.

ctx.s: 世界杯决赛今晚举行，这场{举世瞩目}的比赛将吸引数十亿观众。
ctx.en: The World Cup final is tonight; this match, followed worldwide, will draw billions of viewers.

ctx.s: 这项考古发现一经公布，便成为{举世瞩目}的焦点。
ctx.en: As soon as the archaeological find was announced, it became the focus of worldwide attention.

ctx.s: 她在国际比赛中连夺三枚金牌，成绩{举世瞩目}。
ctx.en: She won three gold medals in a row at the international championships, a result that caught the world's eye.

ctx.s: 这座跨海大桥的建成，被媒体称为{举世瞩目}的工程奇迹。
ctx.en: The media called the completion of the sea-crossing bridge an engineering marvel that captured world attention.

bad.s: 我的新发型在班里{举世瞩目}。
bad.en: (meant: my new haircut got everyone's attention in class)
bad.why: Its first half means the whole world; it cannot be limited to one class, and it is far too grand for a haircut.

bad.s: 全世界都{举世瞩目}这场比赛。
bad.en: (meant: the whole world is watching this match)
bad.why: It already means 'the whole world watches' and takes no object; the match itself should be the subject.

cards.mean: to fly into a thunderous rage at someone
cards.lit: to let loose a great clap of thunder

use.how: Predicate, often 对某人大发雷霆. Describes a sudden, loud outburst of anger, typically by someone with authority over the listener.

near.diff: 暴跳如雷 pictures someone stamping and roaring out of control; 大发雷霆 is a big loud outburst, often a boss or parent scolding.

cards.cue: The manager discovers the report sent to the client was full of errors and starts shouting so loudly that the whole office goes silent. What did the manager do?

ctx.s: 爸爸看到我的成绩单，{大发雷霆}。
ctx.en: When Dad saw my report card, he exploded with rage.

ctx.s: 老板因为一个小错误对他{大发雷霆}，他委屈极了。
ctx.en: The boss blew up at him over a tiny mistake, and he felt terribly wronged.

ctx.s: “别为这点小事{大发雷霆}，先冷静一下。”
ctx.en: "Don't fly into a rage over such a small thing; calm down first."

ctx.s: 项目又推迟了，总经理在会上{大发雷霆}，把大家骂了一顿。
ctx.en: The project was delayed again, and the general manager stormed at everyone in the meeting.

ctx.s: 平时温和的王老师，那天竟然{大发雷霆}，全班都吓坏了。
ctx.en: Mr Wang, usually so gentle, actually erupted in anger that day, and the whole class was terrified.

ctx.s: 你明知道他脾气不好，为什么还要做让他{大发雷霆}的事？
ctx.en: You know he has a temper, so why do things that make him blow up?

bad.s: 今晚{大发雷霆}，我们别出门了。
bad.en: (meant: there's a big thunderstorm tonight, let's stay in)
bad.why: It describes a person's rage only, never real thunder or weather.

bad.s: 听到好消息，他高兴得{大发雷霆}。
bad.en: (meant: hearing the good news, he shouted for joy)
bad.why: It means an outburst of anger; it cannot express joy or excitement.

cards.mean: gnashing one's teeth in hatred
cards.lit: to bite down hard and grind the teeth together

use.how: Describes visible, bitter hatred toward a person: 恨得咬牙切齿, or as an adverbial, 咬牙切齿地说. Not for physical effort or mild annoyance.

near.diff: 恨之入骨 states how deep the hatred goes; 咬牙切齿 paints how it shows on the face and in the voice.

cards.cue: Whenever he mentions the man who cheated his family out of their savings, his jaw clenches and he spits out each word. How does he look?

ctx.s: 一提起那个骗子，他就恨得{咬牙切齿}。
ctx.en: Whenever that swindler is mentioned, he hates him so much he grinds his teeth.

ctx.s: 她{咬牙切齿}地说：“我绝不会原谅他。”
ctx.en: She said through gritted teeth: "I will never forgive him."

ctx.s: 被人当众羞辱以后，他{咬牙切齿}，发誓要讨回公道。
ctx.en: After being humiliated in public, he ground his teeth and swore he would get justice.

ctx.s: 你怎么一说到前老板就{咬牙切齿}的？
ctx.en: Why do you grind your teeth every time your old boss comes up?

ctx.s: 小说里，被夺走家产的少年{咬牙切齿}地望着仇人的背影。
ctx.en: In the novel, the boy robbed of his family's property glares with clenched teeth at his enemy's back.

ctx.s: 球迷们对那个吹黑哨的裁判恨得{咬牙切齿}。
ctx.en: The fans loathe that crooked referee with a teeth-grinding hatred.

bad.s: 他{咬牙切齿}地坚持跑完了全程。
bad.en: (meant: he gritted his teeth and kept running to the finish)
bad.why: It expresses hatred, not endurance or grim determination in the face of pain.

bad.s: 听到考试通过的消息，他高兴得{咬牙切齿}。
bad.en: (meant: he was overjoyed to hear he had passed)
bad.why: It can only describe hatred or fury, never happiness.

cards.mean: to swallow one's anger and say nothing
cards.lit: to hold in one's breath and swallow one's voice

use.how: Predicate for someone who takes an insult or injustice in silence, usually from someone more powerful: 只好忍气吞声. Often said with sympathy or as a call to stop.

near.diff: 逆来顺受 is a lasting habit of accepting any mistreatment; 忍气吞声 is holding back one's anger and protest when wronged.

cards.cue: Her manager mocks her in front of everyone, but she needs the job, so she lowers her eyes and never answers back. What is she doing?

ctx.s: 为了保住工作，他只好{忍气吞声}。
ctx.en: To keep his job, he had no choice but to swallow his anger and say nothing.

ctx.s: 房东无理涨租，她却{忍气吞声}，一句话也没说。
ctx.en: The landlord raised the rent for no reason, yet she held her tongue and said not a word.

ctx.s: 你总是{忍气吞声}，别人只会更欺负你。
ctx.en: If you always just take it in silence, people will only bully you more.

ctx.s: 妈妈对女儿说：“受了委屈就说出来，别再{忍气吞声}了。”
ctx.en: The mother told her daughter: "If you've been wronged, speak up. Stop suffering in silence."

ctx.s: 那些年她在婆家{忍气吞声}，从不敢顶一句嘴。
ctx.en: In those years she bore everything silently in her in-laws' house and never dared answer back.

ctx.s: 有了投诉渠道，受欺负的员工不必再{忍气吞声}。
ctx.en: With a way to file complaints, mistreated employees no longer have to suffer in silence.

bad.s: 排队的时候他很有耐心，一直{忍气吞声}。
bad.en: (meant: he waited patiently in the queue)
bad.why: It needs an insult or injustice to swallow; simply waiting patiently is not that.

bad.s: 老师对调皮的学生总是很{忍气吞声}。
bad.en: (meant: the teacher is always patient with naughty pupils)
bad.why: It is about the weaker side enduring humiliation, not tolerance toward those below you, and it is not modified by an adverb of degree.

cards.mean: wishing one had never done it in the first place
cards.lit: to regret what one did at the very beginning

use.how: Predicate, takes no object: 现在悔不当初. Said of one's own earlier choice once its bad results arrive, or as a warning: 别到时候悔不当初.

near.diff: 后悔莫及 stresses that it is too late to undo; 悔不当初 stresses wishing the original choice had been different.

cards.cue: Years ago he quit a stable job, against everyone's advice, for a get-rich scheme, and lost everything. How does he feel about that decision now?

ctx.s: 他炒股赔光了积蓄，{悔不当初}：要是当年没碰股票就好了。
ctx.en: He lost all his savings on the stock market and bitterly regrets ever starting: if only he had never touched shares.

ctx.s: 当年没听父母的劝，如今想起来真是{悔不当初}。
ctx.en: I didn't listen to my parents back then, and now I truly wish I had.

ctx.s: 别等到身体垮了才{悔不当初}。
ctx.en: Don't wait until your health collapses to regret how you lived.

ctx.s: 签合同前一定要看清条款，不然到时候{悔不当初}也晚了。
ctx.en: Read the terms carefully before you sign, or by the time you regret it, it'll be too late.

ctx.s: 你现在{悔不当初}有什么用？还是想想怎么补救吧。
ctx.en: What good does regretting your choice do now? Think about how to fix it.

ctx.s: 搬到那座城市后，他处处不如意，{悔不当初}。
ctx.en: After moving to that city nothing went right, and he wished he had never gone.

bad.s: 我{悔不当初}刚才多吃了一块蛋糕。
bad.en: (meant: I regret eating an extra piece of cake just now)
bad.why: It takes no object, and it is too heavy for a trivial regret about something a moment ago.

bad.s: 听说你出了车祸，我感到{悔不当初}。
bad.en: (meant: I'm sorry to hear about your accident)
bad.why: It is regret for one's own past choice, not sympathy for someone else's misfortune.

cards.mean: to build up a fortune from nothing
cards.lit: to set up a household with empty hands

use.how: Predicate or attributive (白手起家的企业家), said of people who built a business or family wealth with no capital or inheritance.

near.diff: 自力更生 is relying on one's own strength in general; 白手起家 is specifically building a business or fortune from zero.

cards.cue: She arrived in the city with no money and no connections, sold snacks from a cart, and now owns a chain of restaurants. How did she get where she is?

ctx.s: 他的父母{白手起家}，开起了一家小饭馆。
ctx.en: His parents started with nothing and built up a small restaurant.

ctx.s: 这家公司是她一个人{白手起家}创办的。
ctx.en: She founded this company on her own, starting from nothing.

ctx.s: 很多{白手起家}的企业家都特别节俭。
ctx.en: Many self-made entrepreneurs are especially frugal.

ctx.s: 爷爷常说：“咱们家是{白手起家}的，不能忘本。”
ctx.en: Grandpa often says: "Our family started with nothing; we must never forget where we came from."

ctx.s: 你觉得现在的年轻人还有机会{白手起家}吗？
ctx.en: Do you think young people today still have a chance to make it from nothing?

ctx.s: 他二十岁进城，靠一辆三轮车{白手起家}，如今有了自己的物流公司。
ctx.en: He came to the city at twenty and, starting with just a tricycle, now owns a logistics company.

bad.s: 他继承了父亲的公司，从此{白手起家}。
bad.en: (meant: he took over his father's company and started his career)
bad.why: It means starting with nothing; inheriting a company is the opposite.

bad.s: 我{白手起家}，自学会了弹钢琴。
bad.en: (meant: I taught myself piano from scratch)
bad.why: It is about building a business or fortune, not learning a skill from the beginning.

cards.mean: to cling to a method after circumstances have changed
cards.lit: to notch the boat to look for the sword

story.text: A man of Chu was crossing a river when his sword slipped over the side into the water. He quickly cut a notch in the boat and said: this is where my sword fell. When the boat stopped, he went into the water at the notch to look for it. But the boat had moved on, and the sword had not.

use.how: Predicate or after 是: 这是刻舟求剑. Criticises applying an old rule or method to a situation that has moved on.

near.diff: 守株待兔 is waiting passively for a lucky event to repeat; 刻舟求剑 is failing to see that the conditions have changed.

cards.cue: A shop keeps using the sales tricks that worked twenty years ago, though its customers now buy everything on their phones, and wonders why nothing sells.

ctx.s: 市场早就变了，还用十年前的老办法，这不是{刻舟求剑}吗？
ctx.en: The market changed long ago; isn't using the methods of ten years back just looking for the sword by the notch?

ctx.s: 孩子已经长大了，你还用管小孩的办法管他，未免有点{刻舟求剑}。
ctx.en: Your son is grown up; still handling him like a small child is clinging to what no longer applies.

ctx.s: 经理说：“客户的需求每年都在变，我们不能{刻舟求剑}。”
ctx.en: The manager said: "Customers' needs change every year; we can't stick to what worked before."

ctx.s: 法律修改以后，再按旧条文办事就成了{刻舟求剑}。
ctx.en: Once the law has been revised, going by the old provisions is clinging to a changed situation.

ctx.s: 老师讲了{刻舟求剑}的故事，让学生明白情况变了，方法也要变。
ctx.en: The teacher told the story of the notched boat so the pupils would see that when things change, methods must too.

ctx.s: 拿着老地图在新城区找路，简直是{刻舟求剑}。
ctx.en: Finding your way in the new district with an old map is like notching the boat for the sword.

bad.s: 他每天坚持练习，真是{刻舟求剑}。
bad.en: (meant: he perseveres with practice every day)
bad.why: It mocks rigid thinking in a changed situation; it is never praise for persistence.

bad.s: 为了找回钱包，他{刻舟求剑}，把整条街都找遍了。
bad.en: (meant: he searched the whole street for his wallet)
bad.why: It is not about searching hard for a lost object; it criticises outdated methods.

cards.mean: to cover up a wrong in a way that fools only oneself
cards.lit: to cover one's own ears while stealing a bell

story.text: When the Fan family fell, a commoner found a bell of theirs and wanted to carry it off, but it was too big to carry. He struck it with a hammer to break it up, and it rang out loudly. Afraid that others would hear and take it from him, he quickly covered his own ears. The original speaks of a zhong, a large bronze bell; the idiom later replaced it with ling, a bell.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (掩耳盗铃的做法). Criticises hiding a problem or wrongdoing in a way that everyone else can plainly see through.

near.diff: 自欺欺人 is deceiving oneself and others in general; 掩耳盗铃 stresses a clumsy cover-up of something obvious to all.

cards.cue: After a scandal, an official has every critical post about him deleted and carries on as if nobody knows, though the whole city is talking about it.

ctx.s: 删掉差评就以为产品没问题了，简直是{掩耳盗铃}。
ctx.en: Deleting the bad reviews and thinking the product is fine is just fooling yourself.

ctx.s: 他把车门上的刮痕用贴纸一盖，就当没撞过车，这不是{掩耳盗铃}吗？
ctx.en: He covered the scratch on the car door with a sticker and acts as if he never hit anything. Who does he think he's fooling?

ctx.s: 他以为删了聊天记录，别人就不会知道，真是{掩耳盗铃}。
ctx.en: He thought deleting the chat history would keep people from finding out. How self-deceiving.

ctx.s: 把问题报告锁进抽屉，问题并不会消失，这无异于{掩耳盗铃}。
ctx.en: Locking the report in a drawer won't make the problem go away; it's covering your own ears.

ctx.s: 工厂检查前停产，检查组一走又偷偷排污，这种{掩耳盗铃}的做法瞒不了多久。
ctx.en: The factory stops work before inspections and dumps waste once inspectors leave; a cover-up like that won't fool anyone for long.

ctx.s: 老师早就通知你爸妈了，把成绩单藏起来有什么用？别{掩耳盗铃}了。
ctx.en: Your teacher has already told your parents; what good is hiding the report card? Stop fooling yourself.

bad.s: 小偷{掩耳盗铃}，偷走了邻居的自行车。
bad.en: (meant: the thief quietly stole the neighbour's bicycle)
bad.why: It is figurative, for a self-deceiving cover-up; it does not describe an actual theft.

bad.s: 她怕吵，晚上睡觉总是{掩耳盗铃}。
bad.en: (meant: she covers her ears at night because of the noise)
bad.why: It does not mean literally covering one's ears; it mocks a cover-up that fools no one.

cards.mean: actions that lead away from one's own goal
cards.lit: the cart shafts point south while the wheel tracks run north

story.text: Ji Liang heard that the King of Wei meant to attack Handan and hurried to see him. On the road, he said, he had met a man driving north who told him he was going to Chu, in the south. Told he was going the wrong way, the man answered that his horses were good, he had plenty of money and his driver was skilled. The better these were, said Ji Liang, the farther he would get from Chu, just as each attack took the king farther from his aim of leading the states.

use.how: Predicate, often with 与目标 or after 这是: 做法与目标南辕北辙. Criticises means that work against the very goal they are meant to serve.

near.diff: 背道而驰 is going against a principle or another party; 南辕北辙 is one's own actions defeating one's own goal.

cards.cue: Someone says he is saving hard for a flat, yet every week he spends more on online shopping and wonders why the savings never grow.

ctx.s: 想减肥却天天吃夜宵，这不是{南辕北辙}吗？
ctx.en: You want to lose weight but eat a late-night snack every day. Isn't that working against yourself?

ctx.s: 方向错了，再努力也是{南辕北辙}。
ctx.en: If the direction is wrong, the harder you try, the farther you get from your goal.

ctx.s: 老师对家长说：“想让孩子爱上读书，却天天逼他抄书，这是{南辕北辙}啊。”
ctx.en: The teacher told the parents: "You want him to love reading, yet you make him copy out books every day. That leads the opposite way."

ctx.s: 公司要提高效率，却增加了一堆审批手续，做法与目标{南辕北辙}。
ctx.en: The company wants more efficiency but added a pile of approval steps; the means run counter to the goal.

ctx.s: 他一心想当医生，却把时间都花在打游戏上，真可谓{南辕北辙}。
ctx.en: He is set on becoming a doctor, yet spends all his time on video games: every step takes him further from his goal.

ctx.s: 为了练口语而只背单词表，恐怕是{南辕北辙}。
ctx.en: Only memorising word lists to improve your speaking is probably moving away from what you want.

bad.s: 我家在南边，公司在北边，每天上班{南辕北辙}。
bad.en: (meant: my home and office are far apart, so my commute is long)
bad.why: It is a figure for self-defeating actions, not a literal description of distance or direction.

bad.s: 他{南辕北辙}地跑遍了全国。
bad.en: (meant: he travelled all over the country)
bad.why: It does not mean travelling widely all over the country; it is about self-defeating actions.

cards.mean: professing a love for something one actually fears
cards.lit: Lord Ye loves dragons

story.text: Lord Ye, named Zigao, loved dragons. He had them on his belt hooks and his vessels and carved throughout his house. A real dragon in heaven heard of it and came down. It put its head in at his window and trailed its tail into his hall. Lord Ye saw it, turned and fled, so terrified he lost his wits. What he loved was not dragons, but things that looked like dragons.

use.how: Predicate or after 是: 这是叶公好龙. Said of someone who praises or claims to want something but shrinks from it when it really arrives.

near.diff: 口是心非 is saying one thing and meaning another about anything; 叶公好龙 is claiming to love something and fleeing it once it is real.

cards.cue: For years your friend has talked about wanting a dog, but when you offer him a puppy to keep, he backs away and makes excuses.

ctx.s: 他总说喜欢狗，可朋友的狗一靠近他就躲，真是{叶公好龙}。
ctx.en: He always says he loves dogs, yet he hides whenever a friend's dog comes near. All talk.

ctx.s: 你天天说想去爬雪山，机会来了又不敢去，不会是{叶公好龙}吧？
ctx.en: You keep saying you want to climb a snow mountain, then the chance comes and you won't go. Do you really want it?

ctx.s: 公司口口声声欢迎提意见，真有人提了却不高兴，这不是{叶公好龙}吗？
ctx.en: The company keeps saying it welcomes criticism, then gets annoyed when someone gives it. Isn't that loving the dragon only in pictures?

ctx.s: 他自称热爱大自然，可一到野外就嫌脏嫌累，朋友笑他{叶公好龙}。
ctx.en: He claims to love nature, but outdoors he complains about the dirt and the effort; his friends tease him for it.

ctx.s: 有些人嘴上爱谈创新，真要改变时却百般阻挠，不过是{叶公好龙}。
ctx.en: Some people love to talk about innovation but block every real change; their love is only for show.

ctx.s: 说重视人才不难，能不能容下有主见的人才是关键，否则就是{叶公好龙}。
ctx.en: Saying you value talent is easy; whether you can tolerate people with their own views is what counts. Otherwise it's empty love.

bad.s: 他从小就特别喜欢龙，是个{叶公好龙}的人。
bad.en: (meant: he has genuinely loved dragons since childhood)
bad.why: It mocks a love that is false; it never describes a real fondness.

bad.s: 她{叶公好龙}，一直在默默地学画画。
bad.en: (meant: she quietly loves painting and keeps practising)
bad.why: It means professing a love one backs away from, not a hidden passion one pursues.

cards.mean: to fill a place without the skill for it
cards.lit: to make up the number as a sham player of the yu, a reed mouth organ

story.text: King Xuan of Qi liked to hear the yu, a reed mouth organ, played by three hundred musicians together. A man known as Mr Nanguo, who could not play, asked to join the band and was paid like the others. When King Xuan died, his son King Min preferred to hear the players one at a time, and Mr Nanguo ran away.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (滥竽充数的人). Criticises an unqualified person hidden in a group, or modestly said of oneself: 我只是来滥竽充数的.

near.diff: 鱼目混珠 is passing off fakes as genuine, often goods; 滥竽充数 is an unqualified person filling a place among capable ones.

cards.cue: Asked to join the office choir for a show, you stand at the back and mouth the words because you can't really sing. How do you describe your part?

ctx.s: 我唱歌不好，在合唱团里只是{滥竽充数}。
ctx.en: I'm not a good singer; in the choir I'm just making up the numbers.

ctx.s: “你这次也上台演出？”“别提了，我就是去{滥竽充数}的。”
ctx.en: "You're performing too this time?" "Don't ask. I'm only there to make up the numbers."

ctx.s: 球队人手不够，连不会踢球的人也来{滥竽充数}。
ctx.en: The team was short of players, so even people who can't play football were brought in to fill places.

ctx.s: 招聘一定要严格，不能让{滥竽充数}的人混进来。
ctx.en: Hiring must be strict; we can't let people who aren't up to the job slip in.

ctx.s: 这本论文集里有几篇明显是{滥竽充数}的。
ctx.en: Several papers in this collection are obviously just there to fill it out.

ctx.s: 实行个人考核以后，那些{滥竽充数}的员工就藏不住了。
ctx.en: Once individual assessments began, the employees who were only filling seats had nowhere to hide.

bad.s: 这家店的东西又多又便宜，真是{滥竽充数}。
bad.en: (meant: this shop has lots of cheap things)
bad.why: It is about an unqualified person filling a place, not about a large quantity of goods.

bad.s: 他技术最好，是乐队里{滥竽充数}的主力。
bad.en: (meant: he is the most skilled, key member of the band)
bad.why: It means lacking the skill for one's place, so it contradicts calling him the best.

cards.mean: to imitate others clumsily and look ridiculous
cards.lit: Dong Shi imitates the frown

story.text: The beauty Xi Shi had a pain in her chest and frowned as she walked through her village, and even so she looked lovely. An ugly woman of the village saw this, thought it beautiful, and went about clutching her chest and frowning too. The rich shut their gates and stayed in; the poor took their families and kept away. She saw that the frown was beautiful, but not why. In Zhuangzi she is only an ugly neighbour; the name Dong Shi came later.

use.how: Predicate or attributive (东施效颦之作). Criticises copying someone without the qualities that made it work; also said modestly of one's own imitation.

near.diff: 邯郸学步 is imitating so much that one loses one's own ability; 东施效颦 is imitating badly and looking ridiculous.

cards.cue: A small start-up copies every rule and ritual of a giant tech firm, though it has ten staff, and ends up looking absurd and getting less done.

ctx.s: 他学偶像在台上耍酷，动作却僵硬别扭，简直是{东施效颦}。
ctx.en: He tried to act cool on stage like his idol, but his moves were so stiff it was just a clumsy copy.

ctx.s: 写作要有自己的风格，一味模仿名家只会{东施效颦}。
ctx.en: A writer needs a style of their own; blindly imitating the masters just looks clumsy.

ctx.s: 小公司照搬大公司的管理制度，往往{东施效颦}，反而乱了套。
ctx.en: When small firms copy big companies' management systems wholesale, it often backfires and throws everything into chaos.

ctx.s: 你学他那样说话，不觉得有点{东施效颦}吗？
ctx.en: Copying the way he talks, don't you think you look a bit ridiculous?

ctx.s: 这部电影模仿好莱坞大片，特效却很粗糙，被观众批评为{东施效颦}。
ctx.en: The film imitates Hollywood blockbusters, but its effects are crude, and audiences dismissed it as a clumsy copy.

ctx.s: 他谦虚地说：“我这幅画是{东施效颦}，跟齐白石比还差得远。”
ctx.en: He said modestly: "This painting of mine is a clumsy imitation; it's nowhere near Qi Baishi."

bad.s: 他虚心向老师学习，{东施效颦}，进步很快。
bad.en: (meant: he learned humbly by imitating his teacher and improved fast)
bad.why: It mocks imitation that makes one look foolish; it cannot praise successful learning.

bad.s: 听到坏消息，她{东施效颦}，一脸愁容。
bad.en: (meant: she frowned when she heard the bad news)
bad.why: It is not a description of frowning; it is about copying someone clumsily.

cards.mean: to call black white on purpose, twisting the truth
cards.lit: to point at a deer and call it a horse

story.text: Under the second emperor of Qin, the powerful official Zhao Gao wanted to find out who at court would dare oppose him. He presented a deer to the emperor and called it a horse. The emperor laughed and asked his ministers: some kept silent, some said 'horse' to please Zhao Gao, and some said 'deer'. Zhao Gao later had those who said 'deer' quietly punished.

use.how: Predicate, or 这是指鹿为马: deliberately calling something what it plainly is not, often by someone with power whom others dare not contradict.

near.diff: 颠倒黑白 is any reversal of right and wrong; 指鹿为马 stresses a knowing lie about plain facts, often by the powerful, testing who dares disagree.

cards.cue: In a meeting, the boss calls an obvious flop a big success, and nobody in the room dares to say otherwise.

ctx.s: 明明是他迟到了，却说别人记错了时间，这不是{指鹿为马}吗？
ctx.en: He was the one who was late, yet he says everyone else got the time wrong. Isn't that calling a deer a horse?

ctx.s: 视频拍得清清楚楚，他还在{指鹿为马}，说那辆车没有闯红灯。
ctx.en: The video shows it perfectly clearly, and he still insists the car didn't run the red light.

ctx.s: 数据明摆着下降了，你在报告里写成增长，这就是{指鹿为马}。
ctx.en: The figures obviously went down, and you wrote them up as growth in the report. That's twisting the truth.

ctx.s: 老板把亏损说成“战略投入”，大家明知他在{指鹿为马}，却没人敢反驳。
ctx.en: The boss called the losses a 'strategic investment'; everyone knew he was twisting the facts, but no one dared object.

ctx.s: 在那个部门里，上司{指鹿为马}，下属也只好跟着点头。
ctx.en: In that department, when the boss calls a deer a horse, the staff can only nod along.

ctx.s: 历史上，有些权臣靠{指鹿为马}来试探谁敢跟自己作对。
ctx.en: In history, some powerful ministers used blatant lies to test who would dare stand against them.

bad.s: 他很会说话，经常{指鹿为马}，大家都喜欢听他讲故事。
bad.en: (meant: he is a vivid storyteller and everyone loves his stories)
bad.why: It condemns deliberately distorting facts; it is never praise for imaginative talk.

bad.s: 我把小王认成了小李，真是{指鹿为马}。
bad.en: (meant: I mistook Xiao Wang for Xiao Li)
bad.why: It is a knowing, deliberate lie, not an honest mistake of identification.

cards.mean: to offer a humble, sincere apology
cards.lit: to carry thorny sticks on one's back and ask to be punished

story.text: In the state of Zhao, Lin Xiangru was promoted above the veteran general Lian Po, who swore to humiliate him. Lin kept avoiding Lian Po, explaining that Qin did not dare attack Zhao only because the two of them stood together, and that a quarrel between them would help the enemy. Hearing this, Lian Po was ashamed. Bare-backed and carrying thorny sticks, he went to Lin's gate to beg forgiveness, and the two became close friends.

use.how: Intransitive predicate: 向某人负荆请罪, 上门负荆请罪. Going in person to admit a real fault; among friends often said half-jokingly.

near.diff: 赔礼道歉 is any ordinary apology; 负荆请罪 means humbling yourself, going in person and admitting you were seriously in the wrong.

cards.cue: After insulting a teammate in a meeting, a man goes to her office the next morning, admits he was completely wrong, and asks her to forgive him.

ctx.s: 昨天是我不对，今天特地来向你{负荆请罪}。
ctx.en: I was in the wrong yesterday, so today I've come specially to apologise to you.

ctx.s: 他弄丢了朋友的相机，第二天带着一台新的上门{负荆请罪}。
ctx.en: He lost his friend's camera, and the next day he turned up at the door with a new one to apologise.

ctx.s: “说吧，你打算怎么{负荆请罪}？”妻子笑着问忘了纪念日的丈夫。
ctx.en: 'Well, how are you planning to make amends?' the wife asked, smiling, the husband who had forgotten their anniversary.

ctx.s: 两位老同事吵翻后，年长的那位主动{负荆请罪}，两人重归于好。
ctx.en: After the two old colleagues fell out, the older one went to apologise first, and they made up.

ctx.s: 产品出了严重的质量问题，总经理亲自到客户那里{负荆请罪}。
ctx.en: After a serious quality problem, the general manager went to the client in person to apologise.

ctx.s: 与其在背后找借口，不如痛快地{负荆请罪}，承认自己错了。
ctx.en: Rather than making excuses behind people's backs, you'd do better to apologise frankly and admit you were wrong.

bad.s: 我昨天{负荆请罪}他了。
bad.en: (meant: I apologised to him yesterday)
bad.why: It takes no object; the person you apologise to must come before it, introduced by 'to' (xiang).

bad.s: 法院判他{负荆请罪}三年。
bad.en: (meant: the court sentenced him to three years)
bad.why: It is a voluntary, humble apology, not a punishment that someone else imposes.

cards.mean: to visit again and again to recruit talent
cards.lit: to call three times at the thatched cottage

story.text: At the end of the Han dynasty, the warlord Liu Bei heard of Zhuge Liang, a brilliant young scholar living quietly in a thatched cottage. Liu Bei went in person to invite him; only on the third visit did he see him. Zhuge Liang agreed to serve him, and later wrote in his famous memorial that the late emperor had 'three times visited me in my thatched hut'.
story.source: 诸葛亮《出师表》；《三国志·蜀书·诸葛亮传》

use.how: Predicate, often 经过三顾茅庐 or …三顾茅庐才请来: someone in a higher position repeatedly and sincerely inviting a talented person to join.

near.diff: 礼贤下士 is a general habit of treating talented people with respect; 三顾茅庐 is repeated personal visits to win over one particular person.

cards.cue: A start-up founder flies to another city three times to persuade a famous engineer to join her company, and only succeeds on the last visit.

ctx.s: 为了请这位老师来学校，校长{三顾茅庐}，终于打动了他。
ctx.en: To get this teacher to come to the school, the principal visited him again and again, and finally won him over.

ctx.s: 这位设计师是我们{三顾茅庐}才请来的，你可得好好配合她。
ctx.en: It took us repeated visits to get this designer to join, so make sure you work well with her.

ctx.s: 球队主帅{三顾茅庐}，才把这位退役名将请回来当助理教练。
ctx.en: Only after visiting him several times did the head coach persuade the retired star to come back as assistant coach.

ctx.s: 人家可是大专家，不{三顾茅庐}，怎么请得动？
ctx.en: He's a top expert. If you don't go and ask him in person again and again, how will you ever get him?

ctx.s: 他在回忆录里写道，正是对方的{三顾茅庐}让他下定了决心。
ctx.en: In his memoir he wrote that it was the other man's repeated visits that made up his mind.

ctx.s: 报社总编{三顾茅庐}，终于请这位老作家开了一个专栏。
ctx.en: The newspaper's chief editor called on the old writer time after time and finally got him to write a column.

bad.s: 我上个月{三顾茅庐}了奶奶家，陪她吃饭。
bad.en: (meant: last month I visited Grandma's several times to eat with her)
bad.why: It is about recruiting a talented person, not visiting family; it also takes no object.

bad.s: 他为了找到工作，向那家公司{三顾茅庐}。
bad.en: (meant: he kept applying to that company to get a job)
bad.why: The one who visits is the employer seeking talent, not a job seeker asking for work.

cards.mean: panicked, seeing enemies on every side
cards.lit: every blade of grass and every tree looks like a soldier

story.text: In 383, Fu Jian, ruler of the Former Qin, led a huge army south against the Eastern Jin. After an early setback he climbed the wall of Shouyang and saw the Jin troops drawn up in good order; looking at the grass and trees on Mount Bagong in the distance, he took them for soldiers too, and for the first time grew afraid. His army was soon routed at the Fei River.

use.how: Predicate, often after 弄得 or 吓得: describes people so tense that they take harmless things for threats. 大家草木皆兵。

near.diff: 惊弓之鸟 is a noun naming a person scarred by a past fright; 草木皆兵 describes the state of seeing danger everywhere.

cards.cue: After a burglary on the street, residents think every rustle at night is a thief, and every stranger looks suspicious.

ctx.s: 别这么{草木皆兵}了，门外只是风吹树枝的声音。
ctx.en: Stop being so jumpy. That noise outside is just the wind in the branches.

ctx.s: 小区里刚丢了几辆电动车，大家{草木皆兵}，看谁都像小偷。
ctx.en: A few e-bikes were just stolen in the complex, and now everyone is on edge, seeing a thief in every face.

ctx.s: 流感一来，办公室里{草木皆兵}，谁咳嗽一声都有人躲开。
ctx.en: Once flu season hit, the office was in a panic: if anyone coughed, people moved away.

ctx.s: 公司传出裁员的消息，员工们{草木皆兵}，经理一皱眉就以为轮到自己了。
ctx.en: With rumours of layoffs, the staff are jittery; if the manager frowns they think they're next.

ctx.s: 股市大跌之后，投资者{草木皆兵}，一点小道消息就能引发抛售。
ctx.en: After the crash, investors are so nervous that the slightest rumour sets off a sell-off.

ctx.s: 那段时间他总觉得有人跟踪自己，弄得自己{草木皆兵}，晚上都不敢出门。
ctx.en: For a while he kept feeling he was being followed; he got so jumpy he didn't dare go out at night.

bad.s: 这个公园里{草木皆兵}，到处都是花草树木。
bad.en: (meant: the park is full of plants and trees everywhere)
bad.why: It is never about real vegetation; it describes panic that turns harmless things into imagined enemies.

bad.s: 我们的队伍{草木皆兵}，每个人都非常勇敢。
bad.en: (meant: our side is strong; everyone is brave)
bad.why: It describes fear and nervousness, not strength or courage.

cards.mean: someone so scarred by a past fright they panic at any sign
cards.lit: a bird frightened by the sound of a bow

story.text: The archer Geng Lei told the king of Wei that he could bring down a bird just by plucking his bowstring, with no arrow. A wild goose flew past; he twanged the string and it fell. He explained that the goose flew slowly and cried mournfully because an old wound had not healed and it had lost its flock. At the sound of the string it tried to climb in fright, the wound split open, and it dropped.

use.how: Noun phrase, usually 成了惊弓之鸟 or 像惊弓之鸟一样: a person who, after a bad experience, panics at the slightest hint of it again.

near.diff: 草木皆兵 describes a general state of seeing threats everywhere; 惊弓之鸟 names the person, and stresses the earlier shock behind the fear.

cards.cue: Since being cheated by a phone scammer last year, an old man hangs up in terror whenever an unknown number calls.

ctx.s: 被狗咬过一次以后，他就成了{惊弓之鸟}，听到狗叫就躲。
ctx.en: Ever since he was bitten once, he's been terrified; he hides whenever he hears a dog bark.

ctx.s: 上次被骗了一大笔钱，她现在是{惊弓之鸟}，陌生电话一概不接。
ctx.en: After being cheated out of a lot of money, she's so scarred that she won't answer any unknown call.

ctx.s: 你别吓他了，他刚出过车祸，现在就像{惊弓之鸟}一样。
ctx.en: Don't scare him. He was just in a car accident and he's still jumping at everything.

ctx.s: 经历了那次大地震，很多居民成了{惊弓之鸟}，楼稍微一晃就往外跑。
ctx.en: After that big earthquake, many residents became so jumpy that they run outside at the slightest shake.

ctx.s: 被裁过一次的人，难免像{惊弓之鸟}，一听说公司重组就开始找下家。
ctx.en: People who've been laid off once tend to panic; at the first word of restructuring they start job-hunting.

ctx.s: 那伙劫匪已是{惊弓之鸟}，一听到警笛就四散逃跑。
ctx.en: The robbers were already badly rattled; at the first sound of a siren they scattered.

bad.s: 森林里有很多{惊弓之鸟}，叫声很好听。
bad.en: (meant: there are many birds in the forest with lovely songs)
bad.why: It is a figure for a frightened person, not a word for real birds.

bad.s: 他最近很{惊弓之鸟}。
bad.en: (meant: he has been very jumpy lately)
bad.why: It is a noun phrase and cannot be modified by 'very'; say he has 'become' a startled bird.

cards.mean: to endure hardship while preparing a comeback
cards.lit: to sleep on brushwood and taste bitter gall

story.text: Goujian, king of Yue, was defeated by the king of Wu and forced to submit. Back home, he kept a gall bladder by his seat and tasted its bitterness when sitting, lying down and eating, asking himself: have you forgotten the shame of Kuaiji? He lived plainly and rebuilt his state for many years, and finally destroyed Wu. The gall is in the Shiji; the brushwood bed was added in later retellings.

use.how: Predicate or modifier: 卧薪尝胆多年, 经过多年的卧薪尝胆. After a defeat or humiliation, enduring hardship for years to turn the tables.

near.diff: 破釜沉舟 is one decisive act that cuts off retreat; 卧薪尝胆 is years of quiet hardship after a defeat, waiting to rise again.

cards.cue: After being humiliated in the final, a team spends four hard, quiet years rebuilding, and finally beats the same rival for the title.

ctx.s: 上次比赛惨败以后，他{卧薪尝胆}，苦练了整整三年。
ctx.en: After his crushing defeat last time, he gritted his teeth and trained hard for three whole years.

ctx.s: 落榜以后，他没有抱怨，而是{卧薪尝胆}，第二年考上了理想的大学。
ctx.en: After failing the exam he didn't complain; he buckled down through hard times and got into his dream university the next year.

ctx.s: 你现在需要的不是抱怨，而是{卧薪尝胆}，等待翻身的机会。
ctx.en: What you need now isn't complaining but quietly enduring and preparing until your chance to turn things around comes.

ctx.s: 公司被对手挤出市场后，创始人{卧薪尝胆}，十年后又重回行业前列。
ctx.en: Pushed out of the market by a rival, the founder endured and rebuilt, and ten years later was back among the industry leaders.

ctx.s: 经过多年的{卧薪尝胆}，这支球队终于在决赛中击败了老对手。
ctx.en: After years of hard, patient rebuilding, the team finally beat its old rival in the final.

ctx.s: 那段{卧薪尝胆}的日子虽然辛苦，却让她变得更加坚强。
ctx.en: Those years of enduring hardship to make a comeback were tough, but they made her stronger.

bad.s: 他学习很认真，每天都{卧薪尝胆}地背单词。
bad.en: (meant: he studies hard and memorises words every day)
bad.why: It needs an earlier defeat or humiliation and a long fight back; ordinary daily diligence does not call for it.

bad.s: 度假的时候，我们在海边{卧薪尝胆}，非常舒服。
bad.en: (meant: on holiday we relaxed by the sea, very comfortable)
bad.why: It means enduring deliberate hardship, the opposite of comfort and relaxation.

cards.mean: to cut off all retreat, staking everything on success
cards.lit: to smash the cooking pots and sink the boats

story.text: When a Qin army besieged Julu in the state of Zhao, Xiang Yu led his troops across the river to relieve it. Once across, he had all the boats sunk, the cooking pots smashed and the camp huts burned, and gave each soldier only three days' rations, to show there would be no going back. His men fought desperately and crushed the Qin army.

use.how: Predicate, or in 下定破釜沉舟的决心: making one decisive commitment and deliberately leaving no way back.

near.diff: 背水一战 is fighting a last-ditch battle with no way out; 破釜沉舟 stresses choosing to destroy your own way back beforehand.

cards.cue: A man sells his flat and quits his secure job to put everything into his own restaurant, leaving himself nothing to fall back on.

ctx.s: 为了开这家店，她{破釜沉舟}，卖掉房子，断了自己的后路。
ctx.en: To open this shop she burned her bridges: she sold her flat and left herself no way back.

ctx.s: 他辞掉了稳定的工作，{破釜沉舟}，全力准备考研。
ctx.en: He quit his secure job and burned his bridges to prepare full-time for the graduate entrance exam.

ctx.s: “辞职信一交就收不回了，你真的要{破釜沉舟}吗？”朋友担心地问。
ctx.en: 'Once you hand in your resignation you can't take it back. Are you really going to burn your bridges?' his friend asked anxiously.

ctx.s: 他干脆{破釜沉舟}，把回国的机票退了，留在国外创业。
ctx.en: He simply burned his bridges: he cancelled his ticket home and stayed abroad to start his business.

ctx.s: 为了专心写完论文，她{破釜沉舟}，把所有游戏账号都注销了。
ctx.en: To focus on finishing her thesis, she cut off every escape route and deleted all her gaming accounts.

ctx.s: 下定了{破釜沉舟}的决心之后，他反而不再焦虑了。
ctx.en: Once he had resolved to leave himself no way back, he actually stopped feeling anxious.

bad.s: 我们{破釜沉舟}了很多年，终于把公司做大了。
bad.en: (meant: we struggled for many years and finally grew the company)
bad.why: It is a single decisive act of cutting off retreat, not years of steady effort.

bad.s: 他做饭时不小心{破釜沉舟}，把锅打碎了。
bad.en: (meant: while cooking he accidentally broke the pot)
bad.why: It is never about real pots or boats; it means a deliberate all-or-nothing decision.

cards.mean: dogged perseverance can move mountains
cards.lit: the Foolish Old Man moves the mountains

story.text: An old man of nearly ninety, called the Foolish Old Man, lived behind two great mountains, Taihang and Wangwu, which blocked his way. He set his family to digging them away and carrying the earth to the sea. A man called the Wise Old Man laughed at him. He replied that after him would come his sons and their sons without end, while the mountains would grow no higher. The mountain spirit, afraid he would never stop, told the Heavenly Emperor, who was moved by his sincerity and had the mountains carried away.

use.how: Mostly as a modifier: 愚公移山的精神, 愚公移山式的坚持. Praises patient effort, step by step, against a huge task.

near.diff: 卧薪尝胆 is enduring hardship after a defeat to get even; 愚公移山 is simply persisting at an enormous task, bit by bit, however long it takes.

cards.cue: Villagers spend twenty years cutting a road through a cliff by hand, a little each year, though outsiders said it could never be done.

ctx.s: 老师给大家讲了{愚公移山}的故事，鼓励我们不要怕困难。
ctx.en: The teacher told us the story of the Foolish Old Man who moved the mountains, to encourage us not to fear difficulties.

ctx.s: 要背的单词这么多，只能像{愚公移山}一样，今天背一点，明天再背一点。
ctx.en: With so many words to learn, the only way is like the old man moving the mountains: a few today, a few more tomorrow.

ctx.s: 这些村民用了几十年修通山路，靠的就是{愚公移山}的精神。
ctx.en: These villagers took decades to build the mountain road, and what got them there was sheer perseverance.

ctx.s: 有人笑他们傻，可他们就像{愚公移山}一样，一年一年地在沙漠里种树。
ctx.en: Some laughed at them as fools, but like the old man moving the mountains they planted trees in the desert year after year.

ctx.s: 这么大的工程，难道真要{愚公移山}，一锹一锹地挖？
ctx.en: A project this big, are we really going to do it the Foolish Old Man's way, one shovelful at a time?

ctx.s: 治理这条河靠的不是一时的热情，而是{愚公移山}式的坚持。
ctx.en: Cleaning up this river takes not a burst of enthusiasm but mountain-moving persistence.

bad.s: 他太{愚公移山}了，一点也不聪明。
bad.en: (meant: he is too foolish, not clever at all)
bad.why: 'Foolish' is only the old man's nickname; the idiom praises perseverance and cannot be modified by 'too'.

bad.s: 我们公司明天{愚公移山}，搬到新办公楼去。
bad.en: (meant: our company moves to the new office building tomorrow)
bad.why: It is a figure for long, patient effort, not a word for moving house or office.

cards.mean: to fail to make the list of those who passed an exam
cards.lit: one's name falls below Sun Shan's

story.text: In the Song dynasty, a witty scholar named Sun Shan went to sit the prefectural examination together with the son of a man from his home town. Sun Shan passed, last on the list; the other young man failed. When the father asked how his son had done, Sun Shan answered with a line of verse: the last name on the list is Sun Shan, and your worthy son comes after Sun Shan.

use.how: Predicate, usually in narration: 他高考名落孙山. Failing an entrance exam or a selection; a gentler, bookish way to say someone did not get in.

near.diff: 一败涂地 is a crushing, total defeat; 名落孙山 only says someone did not make the list of those selected.

cards.cue: The admissions list goes up, and a student reads it twice from top to bottom but cannot find his own name.

ctx.s: 他第一次考研{名落孙山}，第二年又考了一次。
ctx.en: He failed the graduate entrance exam the first time and sat it again the following year.

ctx.s: 去年公务员考试她{名落孙山}，今年准备得更充分了。
ctx.en: She didn't pass the civil service exam last year, so this year she has prepared more thoroughly.

ctx.s: “别灰心，一次{名落孙山}不代表什么。”妈妈安慰他。
ctx.en: 'Don't lose heart. Failing once doesn't mean anything,' his mother comforted him.

ctx.s: 这次选拔有一百多人参加，我不幸{名落孙山}。
ctx.en: Over a hundred people took part in the selection, and unfortunately I didn't make the cut.

ctx.s: 听说表哥{名落孙山}，全家都没敢在饭桌上提考试的事。
ctx.en: Hearing that my cousin had failed, no one in the family dared mention exams at the dinner table.

ctx.s: 当年{名落孙山}的少年，后来成了有名的作家。
ctx.en: The boy who once failed the exam later became a famous writer.

bad.s: 他在比赛中{名落孙山}，得了第一名。
bad.en: (meant: he made a name for himself and won first place)
bad.why: It means failing to be selected, the opposite of winning.

bad.s: 这位歌手早已{名落孙山}，大家都不记得他了。
bad.en: (meant: the singer has long faded from fame)
bad.why: It is about failing an exam or selection, not about losing one's fame.

cards.mean: to volunteer oneself for a task
cards.lit: Mao Sui recommends himself

story.text: When Qin besieged the Zhao capital, Lord Pingyuan was sent to Chu to seek an alliance and wanted twenty able retainers to go with him, but found only nineteen. Mao Sui, a retainer who had done nothing notable in three years, put himself forward. The lord said a talented man is like an awl in a bag, whose point soon shows; Mao Sui replied that he was asking to be put in the bag today. In Chu, when talks stalled, Mao Sui stepped up, sword in hand, and argued until the king of Chu agreed.

use.how: Intransitive predicate, often 我毛遂自荐一下 or 他毛遂自荐当…: putting oneself forward as the right person for a role or job.

near.diff: 自告奋勇 is eagerly volunteering for a hard or risky task; 毛遂自荐 is recommending yourself as qualified for a post or role.

cards.cue: A company is looking for someone to lead a new project, and a junior employee nobody had noticed writes to the boss explaining why she is the right person for it.

ctx.s: 我{毛遂自荐}一下，我学过设计，海报可以交给我来做。
ctx.en: Let me put myself forward: I've studied design, so you can leave the poster to me.

ctx.s: “有谁愿意负责这次活动？”“我想{毛遂自荐}。”
ctx.en: 'Who would like to be in charge of this event?' 'I'd like to put my own name forward.'

ctx.s: 班里要选一个主持人，小林{毛遂自荐}，说自己以前主持过晚会。
ctx.en: The class needed a host, and Xiao Lin put himself forward, saying he had hosted parties before.

ctx.s: 公司招人的时候，他主动写信{毛遂自荐}，结果真的被录用了。
ctx.en: When the company was hiring, he wrote in on his own initiative recommending himself, and he actually got the job.

ctx.s: 没想到这次是她{毛遂自荐}，当上了项目负责人。
ctx.en: No one expected that she would put herself forward this time and end up as project lead.

ctx.s: 与其等着别人发现你，不如大胆地{毛遂自荐}。
ctx.en: Rather than waiting for others to discover you, you'd do better to boldly put yourself forward.

bad.s: 我{毛遂自荐}他当班长，因为他很负责。
bad.en: (meant: I recommend him as class monitor because he is responsible)
bad.why: The second half means recommending yourself; it cannot take another person as its object.

bad.s: 他喜欢{毛遂自荐}，到处说自己多么了不起。
bad.en: (meant: he loves to brag about how great he is)
bad.why: It is offering yourself for a specific role, not general boasting about yourself.

cards.mean: surrounded by enemies on all sides
cards.lit: songs of Chu heard on all four sides

story.text: Xiang Yu, king of Chu, was trapped at Gaixia by the Han army of Liu Bang. At night he heard the songs of Chu rising from the Han camps all around him and cried out in alarm: has Han already taken all of Chu? How many men of Chu they have! That night he drank in his tent and sang a lament naming his horse and his consort Yu; then he broke out with some eight hundred horsemen and died soon after at the Wu River.

use.how: Predicate, or in 陷入四面楚歌的境地: 公司四面楚歌。 Said of a person, team or business isolated and attacked from every side at once.

near.diff: 走投无路 is having no way out at all; 四面楚歌 stresses being isolated and pressed by opponents on every side.

cards.cue: In one month a small shop gets new rivals on every side, its supplier drops it and its landlord raises the rent. How would you describe its position?

ctx.s: 那家小店前有大超市，后有网店，真是{四面楚歌}。
ctx.en: That little shop has a big supermarket on one side and online stores on the other; it's besieged on all sides.

ctx.s: 他得罪了老板，又跟同事闹翻，一下子陷入了{四面楚歌}的境地。
ctx.en: He offended the boss and fell out with his colleagues, and suddenly found himself surrounded by enemies.

ctx.s: 产品出了质量问题，投诉、退货、负面新闻一起涌来，公司{四面楚歌}。
ctx.en: The product had a quality problem; complaints, returns and bad press poured in all at once, and the company was beset on every side.

ctx.s: 球队连输几场，球迷骂、媒体批，主教练是不是已经{四面楚歌}了？
ctx.en: After a string of losses, with the fans cursing and the media attacking, isn't the head coach now besieged from all sides?

ctx.s: “你们组的方案还撑得住吗？”“撑不住了，各部门都反对，我们简直是{四面楚歌}。”
ctx.en: "Can your team's plan hold up?" "No. Every department opposes it; we're surrounded."

ctx.s: 到了小说结尾，主人公身边已无一人可信，{四面楚歌}，只好独自离开了那座城市。
ctx.en: By the end of the novel the hero has no one left he can trust, enemies on every side, and he leaves the city alone.

bad.s: 我们的新家四面都是山，风景很好，真是{四面楚歌}。
bad.en: (meant: our new home has mountains on all sides and lovely views)
bad.why: It means being besieged and isolated by opponents; it never describes pleasant surroundings.

bad.s: 生日那天朋友们围着我唱歌，我{四面楚歌}，特别开心。
bad.en: (meant: friends gathered round and sang to me on my birthday)
bad.why: The songs in the idiom are the enemy's; it describes a desperate, isolated position, not happy singing.

cards.mean: an idyllic haven away from the world
cards.lit: a peach-blossom spring outside the world

story.text: A fisherman of Wuling followed a stream lined with blossoming peach trees to its source, squeezed through a narrow opening in a hill and came out into a peaceful village of fields, ponds and houses. The villagers' ancestors had fled the wars of the Qin; they had never heard of the Han, let alone the Wei and Jin. They feasted him, and when he left he marked his way, yet no one could ever find the place again.

use.how: Noun, often after 是 or 像, or as 世外桃源般的: 这里简直是世外桃源。 Said of a quiet, lovely place cut off from the noise of the world, or of such a place as an unreal ideal.

near.diff: 人间天堂 is any very beautiful, rich place, even a busy city; 世外桃源 must be secluded and untouched by the outside world.

cards.cue: After hours on mountain roads you reach a village with no phone signal, clear streams and old people farming as they always have. What do you call it?

ctx.s: 这个小山村没有汽车，也没有高楼，像一个{世外桃源}。
ctx.en: This little mountain village has no cars and no tall buildings; it's like a hidden paradise.

ctx.s: 退休以后，他在山里买了一座小院，过起了{世外桃源}般的生活。
ctx.en: After retiring he bought a small house in the mountains and began living a life apart from the world.

ctx.s: “这里连手机信号都没有？”“没有才好，简直是{世外桃源}。”
ctx.en: "There's not even phone signal here?" "All the better. It's a real haven from the world."

ctx.s: 城市里哪有什么{世外桃源}？想清静，就得学会给自己的心留一块地方。
ctx.en: Where in a city would you find a haven from the world? If you want peace, you have to learn to keep a quiet place in your own heart.

ctx.s: 湖心小岛与世隔绝，居民自给自足，被游客称为现代的{世外桃源}。
ctx.en: The island in the middle of the lake is cut off from the world and its people are self-sufficient; visitors call it a modern Shangri-La.

ctx.s: 他总想逃到一个没有烦恼的{世外桃源}去，可现实问题终究要面对。
ctx.en: He always wants to escape to some untroubled paradise, but sooner or later real problems have to be faced.

bad.s: 上海是个热闹繁华的{世外桃源}，到处都是高楼。
bad.en: (meant: Shanghai is a lively, prosperous paradise full of skyscrapers)
bad.why: It must be a secluded, quiet place cut off from the world; a busy, crowded city is the opposite.

bad.s: 我打算周末{世外桃源}一下，去郊区放松放松。
bad.en: (meant: I plan to get away from it all this weekend)
bad.why: It is a noun naming a place, not a verb meaning to get away from it all.

cards.mean: to offer one's modest view to draw out better ones
cards.lit: to toss out a brick in order to draw out jade

use.how: A modest phrase for one's own contribution, usually when speaking first: 我先说几句，算是抛砖引玉。 Not used to describe other people's input.

near.diff: 班门弄斧 is showing off in front of experts; 抛砖引玉 is offering one's rough view first so that others will offer better ones.

cards.cue: At a meeting nobody wants to speak first, so you offer a rough idea and say you hope others will improve on it. What do you call your opening?

ctx.s: 我先说说我的想法，算是{抛砖引玉}，请大家多提意见。
ctx.en: Let me share my thoughts first, just to get things going; I hope everyone will chip in.

ctx.s: 这篇短文只是{抛砖引玉}，希望能引起更多老师对这个问题的讨论。
ctx.en: This short piece is only meant to start the conversation; I hope more teachers will take up the question.

ctx.s: 会议冷场了，组长只好先讲了一个不成熟的方案来{抛砖引玉}。
ctx.en: The meeting went silent, so the team leader put forward a half-formed plan to get others talking.

ctx.s: “你怎么第一个发言？”“总得有人{抛砖引玉}吧，不然大家都不开口。”
ctx.en: "Why did you speak first?" "Someone has to break the ice, or nobody says anything."

ctx.s: 主持人笑着说：“我先{抛砖引玉}，讲讲我第一次出国时闹的笑话。”
ctx.en: The host smiled: "I'll start us off by telling you about the blunders I made on my first trip abroad."

ctx.s: 本次讲座只介绍几种基本方法，意在{抛砖引玉}，深入的研究还有待各位。
ctx.en: This lecture only introduces a few basic methods, meant to prompt your own ideas; the deeper research is up to you.

bad.s: 专家的报告非常精彩，真是{抛砖引玉}。
bad.en: (meant: the expert's report was excellent)
bad.why: The brick is one's own modest offering; applied to someone else's excellent talk it calls their work a brick and sounds like a slight.

bad.s: 这道题太难了，我{抛砖引玉}了半天也没想出答案。
bad.en: (meant: I racked my brains for ages)
bad.why: It is not about thinking hard; it means offering your own view first so others will contribute theirs.

cards.mean: unshakable determination against impossible odds
cards.lit: the Jingwei bird filling up the sea

story.text: The youngest daughter of the Flame Emperor went to play on the Eastern Sea, drowned and never came back. She turned into a small bird called Jingwei, named for its cry, and ever since it has carried twigs and stones in its beak from the western mountains and dropped them into the Eastern Sea, trying to fill it up.

use.how: Predicate, or in 精卫填海的精神 / 像精卫填海一样. Praises stubborn effort at a task far too big for the one doing it; it can also hint that the task looks hopeless.

near.diff: 愚公移山 says patient effort over generations will finally win; 精卫填海 stresses a small creature's defiant will against a task that seems endless.

cards.cue: A lone young woman picks plastic off the beach every morning, a handful at a time, though everyone says the ocean can never be cleaned. What spirit does she show?

ctx.s: 她一个人坚持清理河里的垃圾，像{精卫填海}一样从不放弃。
ctx.en: She keeps clearing rubbish from the river all on her own, never giving up, like the bird trying to fill the sea.

ctx.s: 面对一望无际的海洋垃圾，几个志愿者每天去捡，凭的就是一股{精卫填海}的精神。
ctx.en: Facing endless rubbish in the ocean, a few volunteers go out to pick it up every day, driven by a will that never yields to impossible odds.

ctx.s: 有人笑他们是{精卫填海}，白费力气，可他们还是一年年干了下去。
ctx.en: Some mocked them as trying to fill the sea, wasting their strength, but they kept at it year after year.

ctx.s: “就凭我们几个人，能改变什么？”“{精卫填海}也是一点一点填的，先做起来再说。”
ctx.en: "What can a few of us change?" "Even the bird filled the sea one stone at a time. Let's just start."

ctx.s: 她失去孩子后，一个人四处奔走推动水上安全教育，这份{精卫填海}般的执着让人感动。
ctx.en: After losing her child she campaigned alone everywhere for water-safety education; her dogged, defiant persistence is moving.

ctx.s: 文章写道，山区教师用一生守护孩子们的读书梦，正是{精卫填海}的写照。
ctx.en: The article says that mountain-village teachers who give their lives to the children's hopes of schooling embody that unyielding spirit.

bad.s: 他熬夜一个小时就把作业写完了，真是{精卫填海}。
bad.en: (meant: he stayed up an hour and got his homework done)
bad.why: It describes long, stubborn effort against an overwhelming task, not finishing a small job quickly.

bad.s: 孩子们在海边用沙子{精卫填海}，玩得很开心。
bad.en: (meant: the children had fun throwing sand into the sea)
bad.why: It is a figure of heroic determination, not a description of literally tossing things into the sea for fun.

cards.mean: so interdependent that one's loss endangers the other
cards.lit: when the lips are gone, the teeth are cold

story.text: The state of Jin asked the small state of Yu to let its army pass through to attack the neighbouring state of Guo. Yu's minister Gong Zhiqi warned his duke that Yu and Guo protected each other: as the saying goes, when the lips are gone the teeth are cold. The duke would not listen and let the army through. Jin destroyed Guo, and on its way home it took Yu as well.

use.how: Predicate, or in 唇亡齿寒的道理/关系: 两家企业唇亡齿寒。 Said of two parties whose fates are so linked that the fall of one exposes the other; often a warning.

near.diff: 息息相关 is any close connection; 唇亡齿寒 warns specifically that one party's ruin will directly endanger the other.

cards.cue: A parts supplier is going bankrupt, and the factory that depends on it realises it must help, or it will be next. Which idiom explains why?

ctx.s: 隔壁的书店关门了，我们咖啡馆的客人也少了，这就叫{唇亡齿寒}。
ctx.en: The bookshop next door closed and our café lost customers too; when one goes down, the other suffers.

ctx.s: 上游供应商要是倒了，我们工厂也撑不住，{唇亡齿寒}啊。
